author: alpcaner
body:
## What

`changelog.d/README.md` documents a fragment filename's leading digits as the join key back to its GitHub issue. Nothing enforced it. This adds `scripts/check_changelog_fragment_issue.py`, which compares those digits against the `(#N)` the fragment's own `### ...` heading cites.

Four fragments on `dev` disagreed, and the mismatch was not cosmetic:

| fragment | heading cites |
|---|---|
| `changelog.d/1909.md` | `(#1700)` |
| `changelog.d/1917.md` | `(#1648)` |
| `changelog.d/1932.md` | `(#1909)` |
| `changelog.d/1940.md` | `(#1848, #1814)` |

`changelog.d/1909.md` holding a `#1700` entry is what *caused* the collision #1941 exists to fix: the 1909 slot was already occupied by another issue's fragment, so the real #1909 fix had nowhere to go and was filed under the PR number instead (`changelog.d/1932.md`).

`changelog.d/1940.md` was invisible to the first cut because it cites two numbers; the multi-citation rule below is what makes it checkable at all.

## What it catches, and what it deliberately does not

**Catches**
- a heading citing exactly one distinct `#N` that is not the filename's leading digits.
- a heading citing several distinct `#N` where the filename falls outside the `[min, max]` span — `1940.md` citing `(#1848, #1814)` is this case.

**Does not catch, on purpose** (the gate is `gate: true`, so it is biased to under-flag rather than hard-fail the merge queue on legitimate prose)
- a heading with no `#N` at all (`813.md`, `853.md`, `1652.md`, `1949.md`), including the `alp-sdk#N` form — `_HEADING_ISSUE_RE` requires a non-word character before `#`.
- a genuine range or multi-issue sweep whose span contains the filename (`1761.md` cites `(#1757-#1783)`, and 1757 <= 1761 <= 1783). Which one is "the" issue is not decidable from the heading.
- anything in the fragment BODY — only the heading is a claim about which slot the file belongs to.
- structurally malformed fragments; `check_changelog_fragments.py` already owns those.

## Verification

- Mutation-proven, not just green: rewriting this PR's own `changelog.d/1957.md` heading from `(#1957)` to `(#9999)` makes the gate exit 1 with `filename leads with issue #1957, but its own heading cites (#9999)`; restoring it returns rc=0.
- Registered in all five places a gate needs: both path-filter blocks and the run step in `.github/workflows/pr-metadata-validate.yml`, plus `metadata/catalog.json` and `metadata/quality-tasks-v1.json` (id `changelog-fragment-issue`).
- Green locally: `check_changelog_fragment_issue`, `check_changelog_fragments`, `check_changelog_citations`, `check_issue_citations`, `check_quality_registry`, `check_local_paths`, `check_cross_platform`, `gen_catalog.py --check`, `gen_verification_status.py --check`, `validate_metadata.py` — all rc=0.

Bench-owed: none. This is a pure-Python text gate.

Closes #1957

author: cj53189
body:
## Audit finding
Addresses F18: after every crawler fails Floor 0, the resolved run can remain `floor: 0` / `joinState: open`, allowing the next Quick Match to join a stranded run with no healthy collapse lifecycle.

## What changed
Quick Match discovery now requires a candidate run to still be in the active `STAGING` status in addition to being an open Floor 0 Quick Match.

Resolved/all-failed runs are therefore no longer eligible matchmaking targets; the next crawler gets a fresh healthy run instead.

## Test added
Reproduces an all-failed Floor 0 collapse, then verifies the next Quick Match selects a different staging run with a future collapse deadline.

## Scope
This PR only changes Quick Match candidate eligibility. It does not implement the separate bounded retained-run cleanup task (F32).

author: binz-collab
body:
### 변경 사항

`#215` 의 **1-3**(지도를 레이아웃 라우트로) 을 **b1 · b2 로 쪼갠 것 중 b1** 이다. 라우트 경계만 세우고 **코드는 옮기지 않는다.** URL 도 동작도 바뀌지 않는다.

```
routes/
  _map.tsx          ← 신설. 지금은 <Outlet /> 만
  _map.index.tsx    ← 기존 index.tsx (이름만 바뀜)
```

### 왜 경계와 이동을 나눴나

한 번에 하면 무언가 깨졌을 때 **라우트가 바뀌어서 깨진 것인지 코드를 옮겨서 깨진 것인지 갈 수 없다.** #217 이 목적지보다 규칙을 먼저 세운 것, #219 가 계약을 먼저 세운 것과 같은 순서다.

b2 에서 지도·마커·컨트롤과 그것들을 움직이는 상태가 `_map.tsx` 로 올라오고, 자식은 시트만 갖는다.

### 바뀌지 않는 것

**`_map` 은 pathless 라우트다.** 경로에 세그먼트를 더하지 않으므로 `/` 는 여전히 `/` 다.

- **프리렌더** — `vite.config.ts` 의 `prerenderRoutes` 는 경로 문자열 기준이라 그대로 맞는다
- **로더와 `head`** — 자식(`_map.index.tsx`)에 그대로 남아 딥링크 메타가 달라지지 않는다
- **`navigate({ to: "/" })`** — 앱 곳곳의 이 호출들은 경로를 가리키므로 그대로다

### 왜 `__root` 가 아닌가

`__root` 는 `settings` · `notices` · `my` · `report` · `login` 까지 감싼다. b2 에서 여기에 위치 추적이 올라오면 **설정 화면에서도 GPS 가 켜진다.** `_map` 은 지도 계열만 감싸므로 범위가 정확히 맞는다.

### 검증

- SSR 응답의 라우트 사슬이 `__root__,/_map,/_map/` 로 바뀌고 `/` 가 200 으로 같은 문서를 준다
- `vitest run` 전체 **1066개 통과**(148 파일)
- `tsc --noEmit` 통과(`routeTree.gen.ts` 재생성 포함), `biome check` 지적 없음, `knip` 통과
- 실제 회귀 판단은 **CI 의 e2e** 가 한다. 홈·검색·지도 컨트롤·히스토리 스펙이 모두 `/` 위에서 돈다

### 관련 이슈

- #215 (1-3)
- #239 · #238

author: khanjal
body:
Groundwork for `check3DShape`, which #71 deliberately left alone.

That method is cognitive complexity **157 across ~470 lines** — the
largest in the plugin — and it had **no test**. The nearest one,
`ShapeMatchPreferenceTest`, covers `beatsBestMatch`, the tie-break helper
beside it, not the detection. Taking it apart in that state would have been
the one change with nothing to catch a mistake.

## What the harness does

Builds a shipped shape into a world of blocks and asserts `checkStargate`
finds it there. The world is a map from coordinate to material, and
anything unplaced reads as `AIR` — which is what an open portal interior
actually is on the server.

The gate is built from the shape's **own** structure material, which lets
`resolveStructureMaterial` short-circuit on its first frame block and keeps
`MaterialGroupRegistry` out of the fixture entirely.

## Five cases

| | |
|---|---|
| a Standard gate built to its own shape | detected |
| the same gate facing north, south, east and west | detected |
| a frame with one block knocked out | refused |
| a frame whose interior is filled solid | refused — the false positive the portal check exists for |
| a ring of dirt | refused |

The positive and negative pair matters: a harness that always returned null
would fail the first two, and one that always returned a gate would fail
the last three.

## I checked the net actually holds

Characterisation tests have an obvious failure mode — they agree with
whatever the code currently does, including its bugs, and can pass while
testing nothing.

So I mutated the production coordinate maths: added one to the row offset
at all nine sites in `check3DShape`. **Both positive cases failed** with
clean assertions (*"a gate built exactly to the Standard shape should be
detected"*), and passed again once restored.

That is the property that matters here — a refactor that gets the
coordinate mapping subtly wrong now gets caught.

## What this unblocks

`check3DShape` can now be pulled apart with something to compare against.
That is the next piece of work, not this one.

764 tests pass.

author: navidemad
body:
## Summary

Follow-through on the 2026-09-06 `/sync-upstream` run's recommended next steps.

**Floor 8875 → 9058, and `MINIMUM_RELEASE` stays 0.4.0.** 9058 is exactly `git rev-list --count 0.4.0`, so both channels now gate the same commit — and that is also the ceiling: the release lockstep means the nightly floor cannot pass 9058 until upstream tags a newer release. Two of the four recommended items were reachable under that cap; the other two are gated/handled as described below.

### Done

- **Backspace/Delete editing pin** (upstream #3298, build 8937) — `test/features/keyboard_editing_test.rb`, 3 examples.
- **Gem bug found by that pin: text-less keys never reached the page.** `Keyboard#raw_dispatch` sent any key without `text` as CDP `rawKeyDown` (Chrome's convention); Lightpanda's `input.zig` drops `rawKeyDown` as Chrome-internal. So Backspace, Delete, Tab, Escape and the arrows were silently swallowed, while Enter/Space (which carry `text`) went as `keyDown` and worked — which is exactly why keyboard *activation* passed and *editing* didn't. Always `keyDown` now. Side effect: the Capybara shared spec `node #send_keys should generate key events` passes.
- **Flag migration** (upstream #3305, build 8946) — `--enable-external-stylesheets` → `--load-resources stylesheet`. The flag is **one comma-separated value, not repeatable** (`cli.zig` tokenizes on `,` into the packed struct — the rules file had this wrong), so `load_images` widens it to `stylesheet,image`. A unit test guards that iframes/workers never go through the CLI value; `Browser#configure_loading` keeps owning those over CDP.

### Gated, not asserted

- **matchMedia `change` on viewport override** (#3378, 9207) — pinned in `viewport_test.rb` behind `skip` below 9207. Nightly serves 9204 today, so it has only been observed *skipping*; the first ≥9207 binary should run it. (A local `main` build for that was attempted; the cached prebuilt V8 was stale and the rebuild is noted in `state/last-sync.md`.)
- **`SELECT_OPTION_JS` detour** (#3375, 9071) — stays.

### Upstream gaps verified along the way (wishlist A54–A56, not filed yet)

- Trusted `beforeinput` is never cancelable — `InputEvent.zig#initWithTrusted` hardcodes `_cancelable = false`, so `preventDefault()` cannot veto a keystroke. Masked-input libraries relying on this don't work yet.
- `<textarea>` `select()`/`setSelectionRange()` reset to 0 until a value has been assigned (`text_entry.zig` reads `_value`, null for child-text-seeded textareas).
- `.value =` does not move the caret to the end (Chrome does), so `fill_in` + `send_keys(:backspace)` deletes nothing.
- B5(2) arrow/Home/End caret movement is now cleanly attributable to upstream (`user_input.zig` has no arm for them) instead of being masked by the gem's `rawKeyDown` drop.

## Test plan

- [x] `bundle exec rubocop` — clean
- [x] `bundle exec rake test:unit` — 235 runs, 0 failures
- [x] `bundle exec rake test:all` on nightly 9204 — **524 runs, 1116 assertions, 0 failures, 1 skip** (the gated matchMedia pin)
- [x] `AUDIT_SKIPS=1 rspec -e "should generate key events"` — passes (was reported as failing in wishlist B5); `-e "should send special characters"` still fails, now for the documented upstream reason (`"Ocean sied"`)
- [x] `viewport_test.rb` matchMedia example against main build 9213 — see comment (cascade half is a documented limitation, pin corrected in `63dcdbf`)

Breaking for users on nightlies < 9058 (2026-08-31 or older): the gem now refuses them with the usual `BinaryError` + update hint.

author: akoita
body:
## Change

Author grounding previously accepted a numeric substring as evidence: a source containing `2020`, `20.5`, or `20%` could support a claimed metric of `20`. Citation completion and factual validation now share whole numeric-value matching, preserving decimal parts, percentage markers, magnitude suffixes, NFKC normalization, and case normalization. Exact years within date ranges remain supported.

Closes #300. This is a deterministic factual-safety correction for the v0.9.0 milestone; it does not resolve or explain the live pilot failures. #75 remains unvalidated and #250 remains blocked. The roadmap records that boundary and splits the affected observation history into readable paragraphs. No CLI, UI, or public contract changes require additional documentation.

## Validation

- Eight partial-number regressions reproduced before the fix.
- Focused application checks: 5 files, 38 tests passed.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm format`, and `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 pnpm validate` on Node 24.5.0 / pnpm 10.18.3.
- The initial full run passed 1,288 tests and timed out in one unrelated storage interruption test; that test passed in isolation (23 seconds), and all 54 release-script tests passed. The complete gate was rerun with reduced worker concurrency and unchanged timeout limits.
- No live providers or private candidate data used.

author: andrewaltimit
body:
Seven-lane wave on the battle system: retail's round order, the Tetsu tutorial, the per-phase HUD, clip-paced damage, the strike camera, impact FX, the results sequencer, casting, and the swing sound. Retail is the measured ground truth throughout; every claim below carries its evidence grade in the lane docs and commit messages.

## What is now retail-faithful

| Area | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Round order | the monster acted before any prompt | command band collects every member's order (`0x14 -> 0x1E`), then the execute band dispatches by initiative (`0x6E -> 0xFE`); ambush skips the command band; Run stamps category 5 on every member |
| Tetsu spar | tutorial never played (`--battle 4` bypassed the arm) | arm replayed from the record's `SET -> 3E FF <row>` pairing; sparring caption (SCUS `0x80078CB4`), paired lesson boxes, forced-command rejections, all disc strings |
| Command UI | pill at Begin/Run, card during strikes, a literal `Magic` chip, invented flat strip on item use | per-phase readout rule decoded from the disc sub-draw table (`PTR_DAT_801F4D34`); Ra-Seru chip off `0x801F4B9E` (`-` when none); AP plate; item target strip is the party bar (record 7) |
| Move labels | none | move-name label (records 76/77, centred on `0xA0`), `N HIT` / `TOTAL` / `DAMAGE` cluster with the record-80 glide, target plaque (record 81) |
| Strike pacing | one damage byte per staged hit, directions folded into the art | damage paced by the clip's hit events (`FUN_801EC3E4` head = `hit_event_admits`, called per anim tick); one HP write per combo; byte-exact arts queue (`0F 0E 19 27` for Up Down Up); one-ahead staging; loop counts read; every art constant `>= 0x1B` at slot `0x11`; art records loaded on both hosts |
| Camera | eye parked inside the acting actor | `DAT_8007BD71 == 0xFE` is the battle-END signal (the port read it as "in battle"); yaw seed keys on action-band entry; the Done band frames per category as retail's `0x50`/`0x51` arms do |
| Impact FX | permanent additive halo on every monster; an invented white hit flash | ghost gate keys on `record[+0x77]`/`[+0x87]` (no idle entry qualifies, census of 1811 entries); `+0x7A` is the impact selector, class 6 = the tint-less Curse arm; retail tint SM `FUN_80050120` ported; render seam `IR0 = blend/0x1000` |
| Battle end | instant teardown | results sequencer (`FUN_8004E568`): load hold, results frame (story flag `0x35`, leader's table-picked win pose, result box), exit fade to BLACK (kind 2 = `B - F`; the port's "white-out" was wrong) |
| Casting | casts bypassed the action SM | every cast runs the SM band: MP charged once at `0x28`, outcome folded at retail's seam; summon route with both flashes, hidden seats, creature seated behind the caster; spell-name label monster-only; enemy specials no longer degrade to strikes (the boot catalog lacked them and its placeholders shadowed real ids) |
| Audio | swing cue produced, never played | per-character `XA30` grunt selected by `_DAT_8007BD84 == 0` plays on native from the CD-XA clip bank; audio duck; level-up jingle staged |

## Corrections to prior beliefs

- The party readout phase rule was inverted; browsing the item window shows the card, the target step the pill.
- `FUN_801DBB8C` registers the arts-list window, not the party readout.
- "Ghosts fire on any non-idle clip tag" and "the disc never carries a `+0x7A` past the table" are falsified.
- The Begin/Run framing does orbit, and its closeness after round one is retail (an attacker stays where its strike ended).
- There is no victory fanfare BGM; `FUN_8003CE08(0x35)` is a story-flag set.
- The ordinary swing sound is the grunt, not the `XA27` sting.
- The play-window never loaded disc art records: every typed art was three swings on both hosts.
- `battle_gimard_tail_fire_a` is the ENEMY Gimard's Tail Fire, not a party summon reference.

Falsified readings are in `docs/reference/re-do-not-re-walk.md`; answered questions with evidence grades in `re-settled-threads.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast`: 720 suites. Twelve tests failed on the integrated tree and every one asserted the behaviour this wave replaced (instant teardown, monster-first rounds, a Cross-only walk parking in the empty item window, a one-arrow Somersault the queue-builder rightly rejects, the pre-battle story-flag bitmap); each was re-derived from retail and passes.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace --release -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- All static gates ok: doc density, md links, ui-host-drift, trait-override-symmetry, shell-observer-traps, site-doc-mirrors, port-catalog ratchet, port-provenance (two reviewed false positives waived), wasm freshness (bundle rebuilt).
- Disc-gated tests ran for real (`extracted/`, `saves/`, `captures/` present): sub-draw table oracle, attack-camera table, afterimage gate census, tutorial arm replay, `+0x7A` census, victory-pose + XA cue tables, cast band, catalog-vs-archive specials.
- Three screenshot sweeps against the integrated binary (Tetsu spar no-input, Tetsu spar driven through the lesson script, map01 Gobu Gobu to the results screen) match the retail frames dumped out of the mednafen states with `mednafen-state vram-dump --display-crop`.

## Residuals (per lane, each with its prerequisite in the source)

- Camera: case-8 dead-target tail; the battle-over arm is ported but no host raises it; cast/capture-band cameras; the summon creature is never framed.
- Pacing: state `0x20` is left immediately so the recover backstep is dropped; empty-event art clips deal nothing; `+0x21C` pause sweep.
- FX: no screenshot of a tinted actor exists yet (needs a class-carrying art or a monster special); `render_flag == 2` additive draw un-cued; `battle_scatter` unreached.
- HUD: empty-bag item window unpinned; heal-item target band lists enemies; bar max pen 146 vs 178 (N=2); the Magic submenu is still debug text on both hosts.
- Logic: round-reset cursor bytes; target-cursor seat window; status-duration writer; confused party member stand-in.
- Audio: extracted-tree boots stage no XA banks; no browser XA lane; monster `0x2A8` runtime bank; win pose plays once; party-wipe hold un-faded.
- Casting: enemy specials draw no visible effect; `< 0x25` anim-pair table unparsed.

## Process notes

Two API rate-limit resets killed all seven lanes twice mid-work. Nothing was lost: every worktree kept its diff and the third round committed early. Integration was cherry-pick from merge-base in completion order; the three semantic merges (F/G on the screen fade + escape path, E/G/F on the command flow, B/E on the arts path) are documented in the integration commit messages.

body:
## 概要
#16 の Part 1（lint 一括整形）。CI の `Lint (Swift)` ジョブが main 由来で常に失敗していた問題を解消し、**このリポジトリで初めて lint ジョブを緑にする** PR です。テスト安定化（#16 Part 2）は別 PR で行います。

## 結果

| チェック | Before (main) | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `swiftformat --lint .` 要整形ファイル | 57 / 91 | **0 / 91** |
| `swiftlint` error | 4 | **0** |
| `swiftlint` warning | 381 | 237（→ #25 で段階解消） |
| `xcodebuild build-for-testing` | — | ✅ TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED |

## コミット構成（レビューしやすいよう分割）
1. `style:` swiftformat をリポジトリ全体に一括適用（51 ファイル、空白・改行のみ）
2. `style:` swiftlint --fix の自動修正（implicit_return / unused_closure_parameter / trailing_closure 等、7 ファイル）
3. `refactor:` LevelProgressionService のレベル定義テーブルを `private static let` に抽出 ← **唯一の非機械的変更**
4. `ci:` `swiftlint --strict` を一時解除

## 判断したこと
- **ローカルツールを CI と同じ最新版に更新**（swiftformat 0.57.2→0.63.0 / swiftlint 0.60.0→0.65.1）。CI は brew で最新を入れるため、古いローカルで整形しても CI が納得しない。
- **`--strict` の一時解除**: warning 237 件は `print()`→Logger 置換など手作業が必要。error 0 件を CI ゲートとし、warning は可視化したまま #25 で段階解消 → 完了後に `--strict` 復活。
- **static let 抽出の理由**: 180 文字超のひらがな配列（error 4 件）を改行したら関数本体が 123 行になり `function_body_length` の error に達したため。関数内ローカル定数の辞書リテラルを型スコープへ移しただけで、値・順序は不変。
- **trailing closure 書き換えの安全確認**: swiftlint --fix が GameView 本体 4 箇所をラベル付き closure → trailing closure に変えたが、呼び先 View はいずれも closure 引数が 1 つだけなので誤束縛は起こり得ない。

## 確認したこと
- `swiftlint --fix` → `swiftformat .` の後、両ツールを再実行しても差分ゼロ（往復しない）
- ビルド warning 7 件はすべて既存（Xcode Run Script の SwiftLint が `app/TestSimpleCheck.swift` に出すもの＋Run Script 自体の outputs 未指定 warning）で本 PR 由来ではない

## 補足
- `claude-review` チェックは `OAuth access token has expired` で失敗中（PR #13 と同じ）。GitHub Secret の再発行が必要で、本 PR のスコープ外。

This PR replaces Discourse’s global embedding configuration with editable **host-to-category relationships**.

### Main changes

- Adds a new **Admin → Customize → Embedding** page.
- Allows staff to:
  - Add an allowed embedding host.
  - Edit its hostname.
  - Assign each host to a specific category.
  - Delete a host.
- Stores these relationships in a new `embeddable_hosts` database table rather than the old:
  - `embeddable_hosts` site setting.
  - Global `embed_category` site setting.
- Migrates existing configured hosts into the new table, assigning them the previous embed category or the uncategorized category as a fallback.
- Normalizes host values by removing `http://`, `https://`, and URL paths.
- Changes embed authorization to check `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`.
- When importing an embedded article, creates its topic in the category associated with that article’s host.
- Adds admin REST endpoints and serializers for listing, creating, updating, and deleting host records.
- Extends the JavaScript store to hydrate plural embedded relationships such as `color_ids`.
- Updates relevant model, controller, and JavaScript tests.

In short, embedding configuration changes from **“a list of allowed hosts sharing one category”** to **“a managed list where every allowed host can post into its own category.”**

One suspicious unrelated change is that the category and embeddable-host fabricator contents appear to have been swapped between their files; that likely deserves correction before merging.

author: venerialduke
body:
## For the player

The garage now has something to offer: six parts, each one upside paid for with
one cost. Four answer a hazard, two buy raw pace. Nothing races them yet —
that's S2.5.

| Part | Gives | Costs | For |
|------|-------|-------|-----|
| Ion Thruster | +0.15 speed | −10 hull | Raw pace on a light frame |
| Ablative Plating | +40 hull | −0.08 speed | Asteroid fields |
| Mirror Shielding | +35 shield capacity | −0.05 speed | Gamma-ray bursts |
| Radiator Fins | +45 heat tolerance | −15 hull | The ringed planet's assist |
| Inertial Anchor | +0.03 acceleration | −0.04 speed | Black holes |
| Overclocked Reactor | +0.10 speed, +0.015 accel | −30 heat tolerance | Going fast and eating the risk |

Intended tension: hull and shields are bought with speed; speed is bought with
fragility or heat. Take every fast part and you reach the stage-3 black hole
quickly and badly equipped for it.

## In code

`src/sim/ship.ts` fixes the five stats and their units — speed **1.0 = one
track-tick per tick**, which is exactly what `track.ts` means by "ticks at base
speed", so the two modules agree by construction.

- `Part` is a set of additive stat deltas plus a name and a garage blurb.
- `resolveBuild(build) → DerivedStats` sums deltas onto base and clamps each
  stat to a floor, so a downside-heavy build still produces a raceable ship.
  Parts stack; order doesn't matter; resolution happens once before the race.
- Every number is a named export in `tuning.ts` — bases, floors, and each
  part's deltas.

## Tests

`tests/sim/ship.test.ts`, 23 cases: **one per part pinning its exact stat
delta** (the acceptance criterion), empty build == base stats, stacking, order
independence, purity, `BASE_STATS` not mutated, parts touching only the stats
they declare, and every floor holding — including a synthetic part for the two
stats no slice part lowers. A doc-pinning test asserts `BASE_STATS` matches the
table in `DESIGN.md`.

66 tests total. `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build`
all pass.

## DESIGN.md

The Ship section now records the stat table with units and bases, how a build
resolves, and the six parts with their numbers.

body:
## Description
**What**: Records a measured decision NOT to add an identifier-length ceiling gate.
**Why**: blueprintx#420 opened with the author's own recommendation not to implement, backed by a measurement; this PR re-runs that measurement, confirms it, and writes the number into `ruff.toml` so the question can't come back without a number.
**How**: One comment block added to `templates/python-common/ruff.toml`, next to the other measured `[lint.pylint]` decision (`max-args = 8`).

---

## Changes Made
**Added**:
- N/A (no new gate).

**Updated**:
- `templates/python-common/ruff.toml`: documented the identifier-length measurement and rejection decision next to `max-args = 8`.

**Fixed**:
- Issue #420: confirmed via re-measurement, no gate warranted.

### Re-measurement (AST-based, `ast.walk` over `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef`/`ClassDef`)

`templates/python-common/{src,bin}` — 493 definitions (issue's own count was 354, drift explained by the repo evolving since the issue was filed; `tests/` is out of scope, same as the issue's own scope):

| range | count |
|---|---|
| > 20 chars | 63 |
| > 30 chars | 4 |
| > 40 chars | **0** |
| longest name | 34 (`assertion_value_or_operator_change`) |

Extended the check across **all 5 Python skeletons' own `src/`** (the issue asked for this before closing definitively) — none come close to python-common's own max:

| tier | longest name |
|---|---|
| ddd-service-native-db | 23 (`PostgresDatabaseHandler`) |
| ddd-service-orm-db | 26 (`SQLAlchemyRecordRepository`) |
| lib-minimal | 0 (no defs in `src/`) |
| mvc-service-native-db | 20 (`PipelineOrchestrator`) |
| mvc-service-orm-db | 21 (`build_session_factory`) |

And the **2 TypeScript skeletons** (`react-spa-webpack` max 17, `ts-lib` max 5; `ts-common` has no `src/`).

**Conclusion confirmed**: a 40-char ceiling finds zero anywhere, ruff has no length-based naming rule to configure, and a length ceiling would fight the repo's type-prefix naming convention by design. Closing without implementing, per the issue's own recommendation — this PR just makes sure the number is written down.

⚠️ **Blocked / not touched**: `templates/python-common/CLAUDE.md` — PR #323 already has an open diff against that file; the natural spot for this note (next to the `max-args = 8` rationale in its "Editing rules" section) was skipped to avoid colliding with #323. The decision is fully recorded in `ruff.toml` itself instead.

---

## Testing
### Manual Testing
**Not Applicable** — docs-only change, no scaffolding behavior touched.

### Automated Testing
- **CI (this PR)**: standard scaffold_checks (spelling, actions, docs build) — no new gate, no `bin/check_*.py`, no pre-commit/CI wiring change.

---

## Documentation
- **CLAUDE.md**: not touched (see blocked note above); the decision itself is the documentation, recorded in `ruff.toml`.
- **README**: not applicable — no new skeleton or user-facing behavior.

---

## Additional Notes
**Follow-up**:
- If `templates/python-common/CLAUDE.md`'s "Editing rules" section ever gets touched again once #323 lands, consider mirroring a one-line pointer to this `ruff.toml` comment there (not required — `ruff.toml` is self-contained).

**Reviewer Focus**:
- The measurement methodology (AST walk vs. the issue's own grep-based count) — numbers differ slightly (493 vs 354 total defs, 4 vs 3 at >30) but the load-bearing conclusion (`0` at >40) is unchanged.

Closes #420

author: ianmcukier
body:
## Summary

Migrates this Neovim config from 0.11 to 0.12, following the runbook in #1. Net **-1892 lines** across 79 files.

**Plugin pruning** (`a0fb276`) — Deleted 24 dead spec files and 17 installed plugins: telescope and its four extensions, noice + nui + nvim-notify, dressing, alpha, mcphub and the avante remnants, mini.nvim, neotest-dart, the bundled fzf, project.nvim, nvim-lsp-file-operations. Plugin count 58 → 41; loaded at startup 38 → 18.

**UI consolidation** — Collapsed three competing notification stacks and two `vim.ui.select` overrides onto snacks.nvim alone (picker, explorer, notifier, input, dashboard, lazygit, gitbrowse, gh). The alpha dashboard's braille header moved across intact.

**Keymap conflicts** — `<leader>hp` was bound twice (gitsigns preview-hunk buffer-local vs. the global PR picker), making the PR picker unreachable in any git buffer; the picker moved to `<leader>hg`. Dropped the `nowait` `gr` binding that made every built-in `gr*` map untypeable, adopting Neovim's defaults (`grn` `gra` `grr` `gri` `grt` `gO` `K`).

**Neovim 0.12 baseline** (`e983b6f`, `a3d8c39`) — Runtime moved to 0.12.5. nvim-treesitter migrated to its `main` branch: highlighting via a `vim.treesitter.start()` FileType autocmd, parsers installed by `install()`. All 27 parsers build and attach. Native `winborder`/`pumborder` replace per-plugin border settings.

**Reorganization** (`5f4046b`) — 27 plugin files named after their plugin repos, `plugins/lsp/` folded in, LSP server settings moved to native `lsp/lua_ls.lua`, `vim.diagnostic.config` moved to `core/diagnostics.lua`, which-key groups centralized in one `opts.spec`, all vimscript-in-Lua removed, `stylua.toml` adopted and the tree reformatted. Also fixes a swapped INFO/HINT diagnostic glyph and two deprecated gitsigns APIs.

**Acceptance checks** (`59c9810`, `0dc80fe`, `fecb454`, `cdf8189`, `88cb71b`) — New `scripts/check.sh`: one command, 12 gates, ~2s. Boots headless Neovim and asserts real runtime state rather than grepping source.

> Note: `68b938a "update plugins to 0.11"` was already on local `main` unpushed, so it rides along in this PR. Pre-existing work, not part of this branch.

## Test Coverage

The test suite for this repo *is* `scripts/check.sh`. Coverage means "does a gate assert the behavior this diff changed", audited at **72%** before this PR's own fixes; the three highest-value gaps were then closed.

```
GATE                                    STRENGTH  NOTE
stylua --check (whole tree)             ***       real tool, real config
headless startup silent                 ***       catches any load error or startup deprecation
startup time <= 150ms budget            ***       measured; currently 58ms
treesitter highlighter + indentexpr     ***       24 filetypes, live runtime state
injection-only parsers installed        ***       markdown_inline, luadoc, regex
checkhealth vim.deprecated              ***       after yank + 24 filetype buffers
diagnostic INFO/HINT glyphs             ***       runtime read-back of vim.diagnostic.config()
global keymap dedup                     ***       nvim_get_keymap, all modes
buffer-local keymap shadowing           ***       ADDED - see below
winborder / pumborder                   ***       ADDED
lua_ls settings merge                   ***       ADDED - asserts the merge, not the file
plugin set identity (27 names)          ***       ADDED - was a bare count
no vimscript / stray which-key.add      ***       exact convention-violation strings
lock has no removed plugins             **        curated name list
```

**The keymap gate was lying.** `nvim_get_keymap` returns *only global* maps, so the dedup probe could not see a plugin shadowing a global lhs inside one buffer — which is exactly the shape of the `<leader>hp` double-bind this PR fixes. The gate would not have caught its own headline defect. It now opens a tracked buffer, waits for gitsigns and LSP to attach, and diffs 21 buffer-local maps against the globals.

Every gate above was negative-tested: each was fed a deliberately broken input and confirmed to fail with a specific message.

```
manifest      rename trouble.lua      -> FAIL: < trouble / > trouble-x
shadow        global <leader>hp       -> FAIL: SHADOW n  hp
borders       winborder = "single"    -> FAIL: winborder=single
lua_ls        globals = { "nope" }    -> FAIL: lua_ls globals not merged
parsers       rm go.so                -> FAIL: NOHIGHLIGHT go
parsers       rm regex.so             -> FAIL: NOPARSER regex
disabled spec enabled = false         -> FAIL: disabled spec present
stylua        binary absent           -> FAIL: stylua not found ... run :MasonToolsInstall
```

### Deferred coverage (documented, not built)

- gitsigns `nav_hunk` maps are asserted present but never invoked — a wrong argument would still register and pass.
- `mason` `automatic_enable` now enables 11 language servers; none are verified.
- `format_on_save` has no runtime verification.
- blink.cmp's capabilities are never confirmed to reach an attached LSP.

## Pre-Landing Review

17 findings from 4 specialists + a red-team pass + the checklist. **9 fixed, 7 accepted, 1 advisory actioned.**

**Critical**

- `scripts/check.sh` — a bad `PHASE` value skipped *every* gate and still printed `ALL CHECKS PASSED` with exit 0. `phase_idx`'s `exit 2` ran inside `$( )`, so it left only the subshell. `PHASE=f` verified nothing and reported success. **Fixed**, then the phase machinery was removed entirely.
- `scripts/check.sh` — the shadow probe skipped insert mode, where blink.cmp binds its completion keys. **Fixed.**
- `conform.lua` — `./node_modules/.bin/prettier` with `format_on_save` means opening and saving a js/ts/json/md file in an untrusted cloned repo executes that repo's binary as you. **Accepted deliberately**: pre-existing, and the runbook lists repo-local prettier under "behavior must not change" so monorepo config and plugins resolve. Documented rather than changed.

**Informational, fixed**

- startup-time gate died with a bare `exit 1` and no message on an unparseable log.
- a discarded `vim.wait` let a missing lua_ls silently skip the LSP half of the shadow check.
- `claudecode.lua` shipped 16 lines of commented-out keymaps referencing `NvimTree` and `oil` — both deleted in this branch's own `a0fb276`.
- fresh-clone runs died on `ENOENT` because mason installs stylua asynchronously; now fails with a diagnosis, and README says so. *(Red team reproduced this in isolated XDG dirs.)*
- the plugin gate counted 27 files without checking which 27. *(Found independently by two reviewers.)*
- `$TMP` was interpolated into a Lua string literal; now passed via `vim.env`.

**Accepted, not changed** — `blink-cmp.lua` naming vs. the `blink.cmp` repo, `lualine`'s empty `disabled_filetypes` tables, and a dated comment on the startup budget. The first two are explicitly prescribed by the runbook (F2 line 869, F8 line 1204).

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Scope Drift

```
Scope Check: CLEAN
Intent:    Migrate this config to 0.12 per the #1 runbook.
Delivered: Exactly that, plus two additions requested during the run (the tree-sitter CLI
           dependency with its doc updates, and the parser-activity gate).
```

## Plan Completion

**36/50 DONE, 0 PARTIAL, 0 NOT DONE, 4 CHANGED, 10 UNVERIFIABLE.** Nothing from the runbook was skipped.

Four deliberate deviations, each confirmed by an independent audit:

1. The `enabled = false` gate is anchored to a leading tab. The runbook's unanchored `grep` matched plugin *option* values — including in content the runbook itself prescribed in step B8. All 18 genuinely-disabled specs are gone.
2. The runbook body lost every Basic-Multilingual-Plane private-use glyph in transit (they arrived as empty strings). Diagnostic signs and 4 dashboard icons were restored from the live config instead.
3. The deprecation probe

author: danbarua
body:
`known` and `known --at` disagreed on the same record. Bonsai's compute-cost question was `established` in one and not the other — a wrong answer whichever half you believe.

```
known                       Established: Q_3 Q_6 Q_8 Q_7 Q_1
known --at 2026-08-12       Established: Q_3 Q_6 Q_8    Q_1
```

## Why, and why the graph settles it

The live survey read `Claim.kind === "confirmatory"`. That was a safe proxy while `is <claim> confirmed` was the only writer of that value — which `ClaimProps.kind`'s own doc still asserts:

> **A closed set, and every value has an act that produces it**: nothing writes `exploratory` …, `confirmatory` comes from `is <claim> confirmed`

`conclude --standing confirmatory` writes it too, to say a finding was **prespecified**. That is a different fact, and not one anybody vouched for. #294 put it on Bonsai's compute-cost claim and the wrong answer became reachable.

**Two comments in this repo argue opposite semantics for `established`**, both deliberately: S-1's fixture said prespecified-at-creation is enough, and `labkit is --help` says *"`confirmed` is for a finding others may build on, which moves a question answered on it from provisional to established."* Neither can settle it, and following one breaks the other.

**The graph settles it.** A promotion is `Decision -PROMOTES-> Claim` — an act, with a date (`standingAsOf` reads `vouching.decided_at`). A standing is a property, with none. So `known --at` can *only* answer from the edge, and any reading that rests on `kind` leaves the two surveys permanently unable to agree. That is a structural fact about the model, not a preference between two doc comments.

## The change

One `OPTIONAL MATCH` on a walk that was already running:

```
OPTIONAL MATCH (cited)-[:SUPPORTS]->(answering:Claim)
OPTIONAL MATCH (answering)<-[:PROMOTES]-(vouching:Decision)
```

Whether anyone vouched is the last hop of the walk that already finds the answering claim — not a value looked up afterwards. No second query, no fold, no `Set`.

**The first attempt did add all three**, and made the two surveys disagree on *four* questions instead of one. That is recorded here because the failure was instructive: reverse-engineering the answer procedurally was both wrong and harder than reading the path.

`whySupported`'s `restsOn` had the same shape and is fixed the same way. `standingAsOf`, which never had the option, was right all along.

## S-1

Its fixture concluded `standing: "confirmatory"` and asserted `established`, arguing in a comment that prespecified-at-creation was enough and `promote()` was for findings whose standing was not knowable at the time. It now does **both** acts, because they are two facts: the design was locked before the run, and somebody stands behind the result.

## Verification

Both surveys now agree exactly — `Q_3 Q_6 Q_8 Q_1` — and Q_7, prespecified but never promoted, correctly leaves `Established`.

`bun run check`: **all 22 passed.**

## Related

#302 — the sweep this came out of found `Artefact.invalidated`, a stored flag nothing writes with four readers, three of them inert. Filed rather than fixed here; its disposition is a decision.

author: quinszouls
body:
## Problem

Tool-call cards intermittently **disappear during a live turn** and only come **back after a page reload**. Thinking/reasoning blocks were unaffected — the asymmetry is the tell.

## Root cause

A session-key asymmetry between the WebSocket event handlers.

- **Backend**: `dispatchOutboundMessage` (`pkg/channels/native.go`) calls `agentLoop.ResolveSessionKey(msg.ChatID)` for **every** outbound event. After `/new` or `/agent`, the key becomes the conversation alias `base:chat:N` (`pkg/agent/loop.go`) — including `tool.executing` / `tool.result` / `subagent.result`.
- **Frontend**: the streaming handlers (`message.stream/.thinking/.ack/.complete`) already re-tagged aliased events back to the current UI key via `effectiveSessionKey()`. **The tool handlers did not** — they stored the raw aliased key on the tool message.
- **Merge**: `useChatHistory` merges streaming state with a **strict** `m.sessionKey === sessionKey` filter, so every live tool message (aliased) was filtered out and vanished. On reload, messages come from REST history tagged with the hook's own key, so cards reappear.

Thinking survived because reasoning lives inside the (re-tagged) assistant placeholder.

**Bonus symptom fixed by the same change:** `handleToolExecuting` marks the preceding assistant `streaming:false` only when `m.sessionKey === toolMsg.sessionKey`; under the alias that never matched, so the assistant bubble kept a stuck streaming spinner during tool calls.

## Fix (two layers)

1. **Single source of truth** — promoted `effectiveSessionKey` to `event-handlers/helpers.ts` and applied it in `handleToolExecuting`. Tool messages are now tagged with the current UI key, matching the streaming handlers.
2. **Defense-in-depth** — `useChatHistory`'s merge filter and poll-scope filter now use `sessionKeysLooselyMatch` (alias-tolerant) instead of `===`, so this class of bug can't silently recur.

The **backend is intentionally unchanged**: emitting the resolved key is the pinned contract (`ack_session_key_test.go`), and frontend re-tagging is the established convention.

## Tests

- `web/src/hooks/event-handlers/toolAliasSessionKeys.test.ts` (16): `effectiveSessionKey` unit + `handleToolExecuting`/`Result`/`SubagentResult` with aliased key; foreign-session drop and cross-session isolation still hold.
- `web/src/hooks/useChatHistory.aliasFilter.test.ts` (4): alias renders, base renders, foreign excluded, non-numeric `:chat:x` excluded.

## Verification (against `origin/main`)

- `bun test` — **390 pass / 0 fail**
- `tsc --noEmit` — **exit 0**
- `biome check` on changed files — **clean**

## Notes / follow-up (out of scope)

`event-handlers/groups.ts` uses the raw alias for `add/removeProcessingSession` symmetrically — no leak, only a cosmetic sidebar-spinner gap when a group turn is aliased. Candidate for a separate small issue.

author: token-boss
body:
## What

An estate's MCP source becomes a declared **machine fact** — `mcp.profiles.<estate>` in the instance lockfile, `kind: hubs` (servers in `~/.claude.json`) or `kind: connector` (a claude.ai connector, which lives in no file) — and every consumer reads the same record: `mcp-profile-config` builds the allow-list or a deny plan, `df-worker` applies it, `lock-verify` L13 verifies it at install, `df-preflight` probes it and **proposes** it when missing.

## Why

Measured: a claude.ai connector (`Scope: claude.ai config`) is in no file, so the name-prefix rule over `mcpServers` could never find it and `df-worker` refused for that estate. Headless `claude -p` without `--mcp-config` sees connectors but loads every server's tools ($3.78 for one turn); with `--strict-mcp-config` it sees none. A connector cannot be allow-listed by file; it is scoped by denying every other server.

Operator rule (2026-09-06): verify each estate's MCP server during install; check what is available and confirm with the user when in doubt. That is L13 (UNKNOWN when it cannot probe, never a silent pass) plus the preflight proposal, applied only by `--apply`.

## Evidence

- `test-mcp-profile-config` 38/38 · `test-df-worker` 97/97 · `test-lock-verify-l13-mcp` 13/13 (new) · `test-preflight-mcp-profiles` 16/16 (new; sanitisation `claude.ai ESO → mcp__claude_ai_ESO__` asserted) · full runner **79/79, 1867 assertions**.
- Gate with the real denylist: CLEAN; `publish-gate/real` posted on `95f4ccf`.
- Absent `mcp.profiles` → byte-for-byte the old behaviour plus one INFO line.

Built by a governed worker launched with `df-dispatch` from a notepad ($14.05, 131 turns); the dispatcher reproduced every suite and the full runner, read the diffs, and committed.

body:
Supersedes #139 by carrying its three runtime fixes onto current `main`. #139 itself is `dirty` — its file set already landed in #136 (+ the SHA-pin hardening in #138) — and its `package.json` predates #137, so merging it directly would **drop the `qs >= 6.15.2` security override**. Nine of its twelve files are byte-identical to main; only these three differ:

**`stryker.config.json`** — `packageManager` was `"npm"` on a pnpm repo, and `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` was never registered in `plugins` (both devDeps are already installed).

**`.github/workflows/mutation.yml`** — Stryker's sandbox preprocessor imports `typescript` whenever a `tsconfig.json` is present, and Astro doesn't ship it as a resolvable dependency; the first nightly run died with `Cannot find package 'typescript'` *after* instrumenting 1,265 mutants. Now installed with `--no-save` when a tsconfig exists. Also `--legacy-peer-deps` on the npm fallback, and a `package-lock.json` branch in the detect step so `cache` is empty only when there is genuinely no lockfile.

**`.quality-gates/security.mjs`** — the gitleaks candidate list put `gitleaks.exe` first on every platform, so a Linux runner over the same mount picked the `.exe` and failed with `ENOEXEC`, reading as a scanner failure instead of a fallthrough. Candidates are now platform-ordered and each must answer `version` before use.

Verified locally: `pnpm run security` passes (gitleaks scanned full history), stryker config parses, pre-push gates green.

author: gbodegas
body:
The framework's own trace of a run is now kept, on this machine and nowhere else. The step records in the drafts file are Blossom's account of a run, one line per node in words a parent reads; this is the other account, what the framework saw, for finding out why a run did what it did.

## The tracer

`blossom/agent/trace.py` subclasses the framework's tracer base, the class that assembles a tree of runs for the graph, each node, and each model call, and hands the finished tree over once the root ends. `LocalRunTracer` writes that tree to the trace store after passing every input, output, and error through a redaction hook: a plain function from text to text, `unredacted` by default, that a household replaces in one place to keep names or dates out of the file. Inputs and outputs are serialized to JSON first, pydantic values by their fields, so the hook always sees text. The gate's pause arrives from the framework as an error carrying the draft, so errors go through the hook as well.

The tracer rides in the run configuration's callbacks, which `run_config` now accepts and which are never saved with the run. The routes attach the application's tracer to every run they start and every thread they resume. A model call made inside a node lands as a child of that node; a check with a runnable standing in for the model shows it under `plan` and `critique`.

## The store

`blossom/stores/traces.py` holds one table, one row per run in the tree, keyed by the framework's run id, with the root's id, the parent's, the thread, the name and type, start and end, the three texts, and when it was recorded. A tree is written in one transaction, and a tree written twice leaves one copy. The file is its own, at `BLOSSOM_TRACE_PATH`, under the same guard as the other two, because it holds the student's schoolwork verbatim and is kept for two weeks rather than the school year. `sweep` deletes rows recorded more than `TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS` ago; it runs at startup and after every recorded run, so a long-lived process needs no timer. The retention policy says why.

## The boundary

The scan in `tests/test_capability_boundaries.py` closes all of `langchain_core.tracers` because the hosted tracer lives there. It now carries `OPENED_PATHS`: the tracer base and its run schema are open to `agent/trace.py` and to no other file, and the package-level re-export stays closed even there. A test holds each of those four cases.

## Elsewhere

`Settings` gains `trace_path`; `ApplicationState` gains the store and the tracer and closes the store at shutdown; `.env.example` documents the variable; the README names the third file, what it holds, and its two-week sweep, and adds it to the synced-folder troubleshooting entry; the architecture doc describes the tracer and drops the gap it closes. No page shows a trace; it is read from the file.

## Tests

`tests/test_trace.py`, 12 cases: a run leaves its whole tree under its thread; inputs, outputs, and the gate's interrupt are kept as text; the redaction hook sees all three; a resumed thread adds a second tree to the same thread; old traces are swept and recent ones kept, by an explicit sweep and by the sweep a run performs; a tree recorded twice leaves one copy; the file is refused where saved state is refused; pydantic values are written by their fields; and the application traces the runs its routes start, into the configured file. The boundary test covers the opened paths.

Checks: ruff check and format clean, mypy clean, 547 passed / 1 skipped.

## Review follow-up

Two changes in the second commit. The tracer read the thread id from the run's metadata, where the framework copies it from the configurable values; that copy is the framework's habit rather than its promise, so `run_config` now states the thread id in the metadata itself, under a named key the tracer reads, and a test builds a run with and without it. And startup opened the drafts file and then the trace file in turn, with nothing closing the first if the second was refused; the stores opened so far are now closed on the way out of a failed startup, and a test refuses the trace path and checks the drafts file was closed.

Four more in the third commit. The framework's tracer base remembers every run's place in its tree for as long as the tracer lives and never forgets on its own, so a tracer kept for the life of the process grew with every run; once a tree is written its ids are dropped, and a test runs two threads and checks both maps are empty. The JSON the redaction hook saw escaped non-ASCII characters, so a hook written against a name never met it; characters now stay as written, and a test redacts a name with an accent. The trace store took the household clock, which is pinned for the fixtures, so every row would carry the same day and the sweep cutoff would never move; the store now runs on the real clock, and a test under a pinned clock checks the rows are stamped later than the pinned day. And no test exercised a model call inside a node, since the scripted callables are plain functions; a test now routes the planner and critic through the framework's fake chat model and checks a run of type `llm` sits under `plan` and under `critique` with its outputs.

## Open

- The redaction hook's default changes nothing. What a household would want redacted is a decision for whoever runs it, and the hook is where that decision goes.
- The trace, the drafts file, and saved graph state now each have a retention rule or an open question about one: two weeks, the school year, and nothing yet. The saved-state question remains.

## Summary by Sourcery

Add local framework run tracing with redaction, bounded retention, and lifecycle-safe application integration.

New Features:
- Keep a local, redaction-aware framework trace for every graph run, node, and model call in a dedicated SQLite store.
- Automatically retain traces for two weeks and sweep expired records at startup and after recorded runs.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure failed application startup closes stores that were opened before a later store refuses its path.
- Prevent long-lived tracers from retaining completed run trees indefinitely and preserve non-ASCII text for redaction hooks.
- Use the real clock for trace timestamps and retention even when the household clock is pinned.

Enhancements:
- Attach the local tracer to newly started and resumed runs through run configuration callbacks.
- Expose the thread identifier explicitly in run metadata and enforce a narrow import boundary for framework tracer APIs.

Documentation:
- Document the dedicated trace file, its contents, retention period, configuration, and synced-folder safeguards.
- Update the architecture documentation to describe the trace store and the observability gap it addresses.

Tests:
- Add coverage for run-tree persistence, nested model calls, redaction, resumed threads, retention, deduplication, startup cleanup, clock behavior, and capability boundaries.

## Summary

Adds the pre-push secret-scan hook for this repo's Pi-side checkout (the Terminal & SSH add-on), designed to survive a container rebuild:

- `tools/install-hooks.sh` — idempotent: installs the gitleaks binary (checksum-verified, arm64) into gitignored `.tools/`, and symlinks the pre-push hook. `--check` reports drift without changing anything.
- `tools/pre-push-gitleaks.sh` — the hook body: scans the outgoing push range with gitleaks' default rules, plus the operator's private-pattern overlay if present at its fixed path on the device — never tracked in this repo, never echoed.
- `tools/deliver-overlay.sh` — runs from the Mini, delivers the overlay to the Pi's fixed path. Same pattern `susuwatari-config`'s `deploy-to-pi.sh` Step 0 already uses: atomic write (temp + mv), sha256-verified, content never echoed.
- README documents the mechanism and the exact `init_commands` line for the Terminal & SSH add-on's configuration, so a rebuild re-applies the hook automatically.

Neither script edits any Home Assistant configuration file. Both are confined to `.git/hooks/` and the newly-gitignored `.tools/`.

## Test plan

- [x] `shellcheck` clean on both scripts.
- [ ] Run `bash tools/install-hooks.sh` from the add-on's own terminal, then `--check` to confirm no drift.
- [ ] Push a planted secret from the Pi — confirm the hook refuses it.
- [ ] Push a clean commit from the Pi — confirm it succeeds.
- [ ] Add the `init_commands` line, restart the add-on, confirm the hook survives.
- [ ] Reboot the house's controller (on your own timing) and confirm the hook survives that too.

## P0-B: Health Check 2.0

Enhances the existing Health Check instead of replacing it.

### What this adds
- measures the real diagnostic call duration for device ping, pairing/fetchUDID, DDI status, and full minimuxer readiness
- does not invent latency for instantaneous state reads such as Wi-Fi or utun flags
- adds a `Last Sign-In Trace` section backed by the persisted P0-A `SideStoreLastAuthSubstageTrace`
- calculates observed sign-in total from wall-clock boundaries rather than summing nested samples
- shows only safe auth metadata: stage, duration, outcome, NSError domain/code, and whitelisted non-secret 2FA mode
- preserves all existing Health Check status mapping and connection/interface details

### Privacy
The Health Check trace does not expose Apple ID, password, verification code, token, DSID/ADSID, Anisette payload, pairing private key, or UDID.

author: alcyedmundo281
body:
`EstadoInfon.VALIDADO` significa «el validador de tres capas lo confirmó»: ontología y lógica coinciden. Es juicio de la máquina, y es un juicio bueno —tiene traza, score y razón— pero **no es una ratificación**. Bajo el principio de potencia y acto sigue siendo potencial hasta que alguien lo actualiza.

## La cuarta vez que aparece la misma forma

| juicio del sistema | ratificación humana |
|---|---|
| `solicitante` (Φ, Bayes) | `prescriptor` |
| `origen` | `procedencia` |
| `estado` (validador) | **`acto` (nuevo)** |

Meterlo dentro de `EstadoInfon` habría hecho que «validado» significara dos cosas distintas según quién leyera.

## «Corregir» no es un tercer botón, es el producto

Aceptar o rechazar mide poco: un contador de aciertos no dice **en qué** falla el sistema. La corrección sí —qué término era el bueno, qué polaridad, qué procedencia— y es la única fuente de esa medida.

Por eso una corrección sin decir qué cambió **se rechaza al construirla**: registrarla vacía sería quedarse con el contador.

`tasa_de_correccion()` la agrega y desglosa por campo. Los infones que nadie miró se cuentan **aparte y no como acierto**: uno sin actuar no dice nada sobre el sistema, y meterlo en el denominador inventaría una tasa. Devuelve `None` y no `0`, porque cero afirmaría que el sistema no se equivocó nunca cuando lo que pasa es que nadie ha mirado — misma decisión que `acuerdo_del_triaje()`.

## Lo que este ciclo NO hace, y por qué

`absorber()` **sigue integrando lo que el validador dio por bueno**, no sólo lo ratificado. Exigir la ratificación antes de que exista una interfaz donde ratificar dejaría el holón vacío: eso llega con el ciclo 15.

Lo que sí se cumple ya es la condición del plan —*un infón que ningún humano actualizó nunca se presenta como real*— porque `es_real` y `describir()` no lo dicen.

## Comprobado

`ruff check` · `ruff format --check` · `mypy` · **590 passed, 3 skipped** (eran 523). El frontend compila.

### Motivation

- Align the POCO F6 Pro Roblox shell profile with the device's real capabilities by focusing on a native-scale 120 FPS/120 Hz request and removing speculative/unsafe OS/kernel/vendor hacks that cannot deliver the claimed 200+ visible FPS or zero touch delay from shell.
- Make state/restore behavior safe and idempotent so repeated `apply` runs do not overwrite the original restore point.
- Provide clear verification/readback and documentation so users understand hardware and software limits.

### Description

- Reworked `poco_f6_pro_roblox_120_low_latency.sh` into a focused v1.1 profile that requests GameManager custom mode at `120` FPS with native render scale and forces standard 120 Hz refresh settings while disabling UI animations and battery saver.
- Removed speculative debug input properties, AppOps/background whitelisting, thermal spoofing, `/sys`/`/proc` writes, and other vendor-level tuning that are either unsafe or ineffective from shell.
- Implemented idempotent state capture with `save_setting_once()` and `state_has()` so the first `apply` preserves original settings and subsequent `apply` runs do not overwrite the restore point, and `restore` deletes the saved state file when complete.
- Simplified and clarified verification output and added a `README.md` and updated `CHANGELOG.md` documenting limits, intended behavior, and testing guidance.

### Testing

- Ran a syntax check with `bash -n poco_f6_pro_roblox_120_low_latency.sh` which succeeded.
- Performed a mocked integration test by creating a temporary `bin` with stubbed `settings`, `pm`, `cmd`, and `dumpsys` commands and ran `sh ./poco_f6_pro_roblox_120_low_latency.sh apply` twice then `restore`; the test confirmed the original `min_refresh_rate` value was saved on first apply, preserved across the second apply, and restored on `restore`, and the state file was removed afterward.
- Executed `git diff --check` which produced no problems; `shellcheck` was not available in the environment so static linting was not run.

## Summary
Implements `mtlkit` per the /office-hours design (kept local per the updated docs/designs/ convention -- not committed to this repo, see CLAUDE.local.md on the author's machine). A seam-based companion library to wavCSE: task/dataset registry, pooling, heads, combine(), compose(), imbalance, and a Hydra-based config/telemetry system, replacing per-branch trainer duplication. upstream/ and downstream/ become thin wrappers; MTRL is migrated onto combine().

This supersedes PR #13, which mixed the (now-local-only) design doc into the same branch/commits as this code. Same code, clean history -- no docs commits.

## Status: 24/25 planned items complete, 1 blocked on missing data

- mtlkit core (registry, tasks, pooling, heads, trainer, combine, compose, experiment/Hydra, imbalance): done, tested.
- downstream/ facade-parity rewrite: done. Tests compare live wrapped code against a git-frozen pre-refactor reference (commit a6b9823). One documented, deliberate deviation: get_pooling_weights's original typo bug (pooling_weights vs position_weights) is fixed, not reproduced -- no consumer could have depended on the crash succeeding.
- MTRL migration onto combine(): done. Numeric-parity test replays pinned batches across a 3-epoch schedule crossing warmup + Omega refresh, matching the pre-migration standalone model exactly.
- PMR/GBC/TSM/NCMTL/FTN verified unmodified: all import, instantiate, and run a synthetic forward+backward pass cleanly. NCMTL's own pre-existing test suite (11 tests, untouched) passes.
- Imbalance seam: done -- pinned mechanical gate + a >=1.5x gradient-ratio assertion.
- Eval perf (issue #11): done -- batch_size/num_workers bumped to match the pattern already established in mtrl/gbc/ncmtl configs.
- FSC-as-3-heads: BLOCKED. Needs real FSC metadata (embedding.tar.gz, DVC-tracked, not pulled in this environment) to derive real action/object/location vocabularies -- the 31-item flattened label list can't be reliably reverse-split without the raw per-field metadata. The underlying many-to-many mask mechanism it needs is already built and tested.

119 mtlkit tests + 11 NCMTL tests passing. Also caught and fixed a real regression during development: an initial model-assembly approach broke NCMTL/FTN (which subclass DownstreamMultiTaskModel and reach into its internal flat attribute layout) -- caught by running the pre-existing NCMTL suite before landing.

## Next
FSC-as-3-heads needs dvc pull (or equivalent real FSC data access) before it can be completed honestly.

author: jobordu
body:
Three of the gate's four UNESTABLISHED instruments are **not uncontrolled**. Nothing told the gate
where to look.

```
check-freshness   test_check_freshness.py   28 controls   PASSES
gh-complete       test_gh_complete.py       18 controls   PASSES
job-log           test_job_log.py           46 controls   PASSES
```

All three suites run in the gating job (`exit-code-gate.sh tools 'test_*.py'` → **56/56 passing**).
Each tool now carries the repo's existing anchored declaration, with the reason it has no
`--self-test` argv surface stated rather than left implicit.

## ⇒ Measured effect: 4 UNESTABLISHED → 3. Only `gh-complete` moved.

## ⛔ And that is the finding

`check-freshness` and `job-log` take **required arguments**, so they hit the gate's
cannot-invoke-bare branch at `:272`, which returns `unest` **without consulting the declaration** —
first consulted at `:340`, sixty-eight lines later. The branch's own message says:

> *"it needs a `# NO-SELF-TEST:` line or an invocation this gate can derive."*

### Two-pole proof, not inference

Same tree, declaration present and then renamed:

```
POLE A   with `# NO-SELF-TEST:`   ->  "CANNOT BE INVOKED BARE ... UNESTABLISHED"
POLE B   declaration removed      ->  IDENTICAL BYTES
```

⇒ **The gate names a remedy it does not honour on the path that prints it.** That is #73's own
doctrine — *an absence report must name a remedy that works* — failing inside the gate. Filed
separately as its own issue; **I am not changing gate semantics in this PR**, because the branch's
comment gives a real reason for existing (*"folding that into 'has no self-test' would be a claim
about the world made from a limit of the invocation"*) and whether a declaration should satisfy it
is the gate author's call, not mine.

## ⚠ What these two declarations buy, stated honestly

**Nothing today.** They are true, they record where the control lives for a human reader, and they
take effect if the gate is fixed. I am not claiming they change the gate's reading, because I
measured that they do not.

## ⚠ Two errors of my own that this work exists to correct

1. Earlier today I published that 8 instruments *"told the gate they HAVE no control."* The
   declaration's own text says the opposite four words in — *"⛔ This is a DECLARATION of where the
   control lives, not a claim that none exists."* I read a label and inferred a state. These three
   now carry that same declaration, for the same reason.
2. My AST probe scored `test_check_freshness` and `test_job_log` at **0 tests / 0 asserts**. Both
   use a module-level `check(name, got, want)` helper — no `def test_*`, no `assert` — so it
   returned a well-formed **0** for suites of 163 and 229 lines carrying **28** and **46** controls.
   Caught only because 0 was implausible.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `test_check_freshness.py` · `test_gh_complete.py` · `test_job_log.py` | exit 0 |
| `scripts/check-tools-index.py` | exit 0 |
| all three tools | compile |
| gate UNESTABLISHED | 4 → 3 |

body:
Superseded. Master fixed the same defect in #191 and #196; nothing here is still needed.

This branch's only remaining delta over master is `!Array.isArray(value)` inside `isRecord`, plus a comment. Master reads the push value through `Object.hasOwn`, which already answers the array case — an array carries `Array.prototype.push`, but never an *own* `push` — so the extra guard is a no-op.

Checked against every shape an `on:` block can take (the string form, both array forms, an empty `push:`, each of the four filters, `paths` alone, a scalar, a sequence, no push key, a null document): master answers all of them correctly, and the extra guard changes none of them.

Closing rather than merging, so the shared action does not carry a redundant guard.

The break itself is unrelated to this branch and still open: `common-checks` resolves `push-excludes-tags#latest`, which is stale, so every repo running common-checks fails to compile that script. `release-composite` republishes that tag only on master and only behind `needs: [checks]`, and `checks` fails on the stale tag — so the fix now on master cannot reach the tag through the normal pipeline. It needs `./orphan-release/orphan-release.sh --source push-excludes-tags` run once from a master checkout with a token that can move the tag.

Closes the operational dead-end created by safe Wave41 reply ambiguity handling and surfaced by #166.

Scope:
- adds explicit human reconciliation for one exact SENDING/AMBIGUOUS Inbox reply attempt

- multiple historical blockers fail closed rather than selecting heuristically
- corrupt reconciliation evidence does not crash Inbox/Today, but sending remains blocked

author: rahlk
body:
Closes #11.

Release run 34004180477 failed at the gate with `create constraint: Neo.TransientError.Transaction.DeadlockDetected`: `BoltStore.createConstraints` used autocommit `session.Run` and returned the first error, so a retryable transient error from two concurrent writers (in CI, `internal/reconcile` and `tests` in parallel against one service; in production, two `caniac --emit neo4j` processes) aborted the generation.

Each `CREATE CONSTRAINT ... IF NOT EXISTS` now runs inside `session.ExecuteWrite`, so the driver retries retryable errors with its bounded jittered backoff (`MaxTransactionRetryTime`, 30 s default). Non-retryable errors are still returned wrapped before any data write; the session close-error handling is unchanged. Neo4j 5 accepts schema commands in a managed transaction (probed live).

Tests: three unit cases through a fake driver/session against the real `createConstraints` (retry after deadlock succeeds with zero autocommit calls; non-retryable error returned once, no retry; cancelled context stops). RED before the fix on the first and third. Five consecutive parallel `go test ./internal/reconcile ./tests` runs and one `go test ./...` green against a live Neo4j 5; `gofmt`, `go vet`, `git diff --check` clean.

Known trade-off: an unreachable server during constraint creation now waits up to the driver's retry window before failing.

## Syfte
Lås current location enligt verksamhetsbeslutet:

**NYBIL baseline → senare legitima verifierade platsobservationer → senaste observation i tid = CURRENT FACT**

Status får skapa en explicit mänskligt verifierad platskorrigering.

## Legitima källor
- NYBIL
- completed CHECK-IN
- ANKOMST
- explicit STATUS-korrigering

- Den skapar inte Check-in.
- Den skapar/ändrar inte RENTAL.
- Den sätter inte AVAILABLE.
- Den ändrar inte SALU, Hjulskifte eller AVVECKLA.
- Tidigare source records och historik skrivs inte om.

## UI
En smal Status-yta `/status/location` för explicit verifiering av fysisk plats, länkad från Status. Befintliga stora Status-formen byggs inte om.

Låser bland annat:
- senare Ankomst slår äldre Check-in,
- senare Status-korrigering slår äldre Ankomst,
- senare completed Check-in slår äldre Status-korrigering,
- incomplete Check-in ignoreras,
- NYBIL är baseline/fallback,
- ort + station sparas som en atomisk observation.

Ingen migration. Ingen generell redesign.

author: vitorpamplona
body:
## What staging showed

The relay inherited a marker naming **139,524 subjects**. Across a 2.75h process the backlog gauge never moved off its starting value, the marker never shrank, and `proj.fetch.derive` logged 665 slices at a **14.4s mean** — 2.6 hours of derive with nothing credited.

That is not a stall. A round derived its entire snapshot and only then retired it, so a ledger this size reads as *completely frozen* for over an hour a pass. And a crash anywhere in that hour discarded every subject already derived and acked, because the marker still named all of them — a ledger that takes longer to drain than the process stays up never finishes.

## The change

**Retire per slice.** Each slice is credited the moment its projection write is acked. Same work, visible when it happens, and a crash now costs the unretired remainder instead of the whole round.

**Shrink the marker with tensor-cell removes.** A round used to end with `persist(pending.get())` — a rewrite of the document to *this process's* whole view. `pending` is process-local and two processes share this marker (the serving relay and the sync mirror each run a store), so either one's rewrite erased the other's write-ahead insurance: the marker stopped naming work that was genuinely unhealed, which is the one thing it exists to do. Removes compose the way `persistDelta`'s adds already did; whole-doc writes do not.

**Skip what another drain retired.** `TrustReconciler` and the background loop both drain this ledger. The pulse caught them as two activity buckets with near-identical search counts — `Drain` 3,477 and `Other` 3,174 — each deriving the same snapshot, splitting one process's derive budget between two passes doing identical work. Retired means written and acked, so skipping is safe and keeps the read-your-writes barrier honest. Deliberately *not* a mutex: an inline drain runs while its caller holds the writer lock, so blocking it on a round that needs that same lock would deadlock.

**Group `removeCells` by document.** A tensor remove takes a list of addresses, and retiring a slice is hundreds of cells leaving one document. Per-cell updates there were not just n round trips but n *concurrent* updates to the same document id, which Vespa serialises. Verified against staging that a multi-address remove drops exactly the named cells and leaves the rest.

## Tests

Two regression tests, both failing on the old ledger:

- `a round retires each slice as it lands, not once at the end` — old: `the marker shrank WHILE the round ran; it only ever read [0, 600]`
