body:
Nine small pieces of work in one round: five things the last two builds left
for the trunk to do, and four of the "small things" the plan set aside for a
shared round. **A fix round followed the review** and is described in its own
section below: nine gaps the review found, and three items decided after the
round had started, two of them the operator's own. Nothing here is a new feature the practice asked for; it is the
tidying and the fixing that the last two rounds put on the shelf, plus two
figures the owner has been asking for.

## What changed, in plain language

**1. A brain map can say which visit it was taken at.** Until now a
measurement recorded the day and the household and nothing else, because the
two halves of the record live in different parts of the database and neither
could reach the other. The trunk can reach both, so it made the link. The
recording form offers that household's completed visits and the measurements
table names the one it was taken at. It stays optional: a questionnaire filled
in at home and an outside provider's export belong to no visit of ours, and the
database refuses a measurement that names another household's visit.

**2. One question about file types, asked in one place.** Three parts of the
app need to know whether a file's first bytes really are a PDF or a photograph.
Only one of them was allowed to hold the answer, so another had written its own
copy. The question moved somewhere everybody may read it, and the copy is gone.

**3. A filed export can no longer name another household's document.** That
rule was kept by a small piece of code; it is now kept by the database itself,
which is harder to switch off and easier to see.

**4. A test that failed at random.** The last build noticed a test that failed
roughly one run in three because of how it waited for an error. Fixed in one
line, and run ten times to be sure.

**5. Three tidying notes** from the last review: a miscount in a document, a
name that had been retired, and one that turned out to need nothing.

**6. The month's takings are now the same figure whoever asks.** They were not.
When a household asks to be erased, its rows are hidden from most of the
practice — quite rightly — but the month's total was being added up from what
the person looking could see, so the bookkeeper saw a smaller month than the
owner and nothing on the screen said why. The total is now added up from the
whole ledger, naming nobody: an amount and a day, no household, no invoice.

**7. The VAT threshold watch.** Settings › Practice now shows what the practice
has supplied over the last twelve months, beside the two figures that matter:
AED 187,500, where registering for VAT becomes a choice, and AED 375,000, where
it becomes a duty within thirty days. Past the second figure the page says so
every time it is opened, until the switch is turned on. Passing the first
figure changes nothing the practice must do, so the page says nothing about it
beyond showing where the practice stands. **Turning it on is
still entirely the practice's own act** — nothing here registers anything, and
an invoice still cannot carry VAT until the authority has issued the number.

**8. The audit screen.** The rail had an "Audit" item marked "Arriving" since
the spring. It arrives: everything that has touched the practice's records,
newest first, in plain sentences, narrowable by who did it, what kind of thing
it was, what happened and which days. Beside it, the report that answers "who
has seen my child's record?" in one press — which is the reason the trail is
kept at all. An erased household's history still opens only for the owner and
the lead practitioner, and reading the trail is itself written into the trail.

**9. A dead column removed.** A column on the invoice table that nothing has
ever written, and nothing could. Three things still mentioned it; all three
were put right first.

## Shared-zone changes

Everything outside the trunk's own paths, file by file. Each is listed again in
`docs/CHANGE-REQUESTS/trunk-notes.md` round 31 and in the widening note in
`docs/SPEC/OWNERSHIP.md`.

**assessment** (items 1, 2, 3)
- `app/api/assessments/routes.ts` — the visit on a recording, the visits list, the check that a named visit is this household's
- `app/api/assessments/rows.ts` — the visit read back with each measurement, and the picker's own query
- `app/api/assessments/schema.ts` — `sessionId` in, the visit out
- `app/api/assessments/file.ts` — one comment, the moved file's new path
- `app/admin/assessments/RecordDrawer.tsx` — the visit picker
- `app/admin/assessments/AssessmentsTab.tsx` — the Visit column
- `app/admin/assessments/AssessmentsTab.test.tsx` — the fixture, and a case for the new column
- `domain/assessment/fileType.ts` and `fileType.test.ts` — the stream's own five-byte copy replaced by the shared check
- `db/migrations/502_assessment_document_key.sql` — new, in the stream's range: the guard trigger of 501 replaced by a foreign key

**client-record** (items 2, 9)
- `domain/client/fileSignature.ts` and `fileSignature.test.ts` — moved to `domain/shared`
- `domain/client/index.ts` — re-exports it, so no caller moved
- `tests/client/db/erasure_act.test.ts` — stops writing the dropped column

**client-portal** (item 4, and the fix round)
- `tests/portal/db/invite.test.ts` — the one-line race fix
- `app/api/portal/reports.ts`, `app/api/portal/household.ts` — the Reports screen narrows to the people this person may read about
- `domain/portal/reports.ts` and its test, `domain/portal/index.ts` — the rule itself, pure

**reports** (item 5, and the fix round)
- `tests/reports/document.test.ts` — the retired name out of a comment
- `db/policies/reports/reports.sql` — the read policy asks for a legal guardian
- `tests/reports/db/rls.test.ts`, `tests/reports/db/portal.test.ts` — the allow and the deny cases

**billing** (items 6, 9)
- `app/api/billing/summary.ts` — reads the practice-wide ledger function
- `tests/billing/db/packages.test.ts` — asserts what holds now the column is gone

**audit-ui** (item 8)
- `app/api/audit/activity.ts` (new), `app/api/audit/schema.ts`
- `app/admin/audit/AuditPage.tsx`, `AuditPage.test.tsx`, `audit.css` (all new)

**The trunk's own and the shared zone** (for completeness)
`domain/shared/fileSignature.ts` (moved in) and its test,
`domain/shared/vat-threshold.ts` (new) and its test, `domain/shared/index.ts`,
`domain/shared/actor.ts` and its test; `app/shell/App.tsx`, `AdminLayout.tsx`,
`adminAccess.ts`, `components/Rail.tsx` and the two shell tests;
`app/admin/settings/PracticePage.tsx` and its test; `app/api/practice/routes.ts`
and `schema.ts`; `app/api/practice/logo.ts` (a comment);
`app/api/create-api.ts`; migrations `911`, `951`, `952`, `953`, `954`, `955`;
`tests/db/**`; `db/runner/plan.ts` (a comment); `.claude/hooks/no-prod-in-dev.sh`;
`docs/SPEC/OWNERSHIP.md`, `docs/SPEC/00-data-model.md`, `docs/SPEC/reports-v1.md`,

author: gentslava
body:
## Зачем

Ключи атрибутов были Title Case (`Payment link`, `Place ID`). Это выглядело прилично только по-английски: **в русском интерфейсе имена атрибутов всё равно показывались английскими**, потому что переводить их Home Assistant умеет исключительно через `state_attributes` в `strings.json`, а привязка идёт по snake_case-ключу.

То есть прежняя схема не давала ни перевода, ни удобного доступа: `state_attr(..., 'Place ID')` — с пробелом и заглавными — не пишет ни одна интеграция.

## Что проверить руками

После деплоя в свойствах замка и сенсора баланса имена атрибутов должны стать русскими («Идентификатор подъезда», «Сумма к оплате»), а не английскими.

Отдельно интересует **дата платежа**: она теперь отдаётся в ISO. Проверить из этого окружения, как её нарисует интерфейс, нельзя — пакет фронтенда в тестовое окружение не ставится. Если ISO покажется сырым, правильное решение не возвращать строку, а завести отдельный сенсор с `device_class: timestamp`: тогда HA форматирует по локали, и сравнение остаётся.

## Исправлено попутно

- `openable` был строкой `"True"`. Непустая строка истинна, поэтому проверка в шаблоне срабатывала всегда — включая `"False"`. Стал булевым.
- дата платежа форматировалась внутри интеграции под русскую локаль и переставала быть сравнимой: как текст `05.09.2026` больше, чем `04.10.2026`, хотя дата раньше.

## Что сохранено и почему

- **`name`** — несёт имя от оператора и с `friendly_name` не совпадает: то составное, собранное самим HA.
- **Идентификаторы адреса, домофона и подъезда** — оставлены на сущности. Перенос в diagnostics рассматривался и отклонён: выгрузка по замыслу безопасна для публикации и хранит только счётчики, поэтому ID пришлось бы отредактировать, то есть обессмыслить.

## BREAKING

`Place ID` → `place_id`, `Access control ID` → `access_control_id`, `Entrance ID` → `entrance_id`, `Name` → `name`, `Openable` → `openable`, `Amount sum` → `amount_sum`, `Target date` → `target_date`, `Payment link` → `payment_link`, `Blocked` → `blocked`.

## Проверки

`841 passed` · pyright `0 errors` · secret-log passed. Новый тест закрепляет оба свойства сразу: ключи snake_case и наличие перевода имени в каждом из трёх файлов переводов.

## Отдельная находка, не в этом PR

`async_lock` — заглушка, которая только пишет в лог «не поддерживается», а `LockEntityFeature.OPEN` не объявлена. То есть в интерфейсе есть кнопка «Закрыть», которая ничего не делает, и нет действия «Открыть» — ровно того, которое описывает домофон. Чинить отдельно.

author: ashsaki
body:
Fixes #91.

 1. Dropped categorizing groups into aa/bb/aaaa/bbbb/aabb buckets because the bucketing is restrictive and incorrect for spinless systems. Also, we do not impose any spin-ordering of alpha and beta orbitals for full-strs subspace mode.
 2. Now, the groups are categorized into two buckets: direct groups (which follow direct matrix element evaluation formula) and standard groups (all others that use `accum_element()`). Direct groups are further divided into paired and unpaired.
    - Direct paired: we split a bitset in an arbitrary middle point (width/2). If two flip positions are in one half and other two in the other half (two-and-two), we qualify the group as direct paired. We have a half-bitset-based prefiltering for these groups: if the low half does not exist in the subspace, we skip evaluation for the group. The split does not assume any spin ordering and only enables the pre-filtering.
    - Direct unpaired: Groups that do not have the two-and-two split. Does not use the pre-filtering. Uses the subspace hashmap lookup and direct formula for matrix element evaluation.
3. The direct vs. standard groups categorization is based solely on the operator terms. There are several checks to prevent the bug like #91. Also, spin ordering assumptions are removed. 
4. Type2 paths (csr2.hpp, csrlike_builder2.hpp, and matvec2.hpp) used same loops duplicated three times in three files to evaluate a matrix element. Only the final write destination differed. The common loops are moved to a single place inside `typ2_group_table.hpp` to avoid duplication.

body:
## Summary

Adds an interactive starfield with cursor gravity well and signup pulse effects, along with a new `/interest` page for an email interest list. The starfield gains optional interactivity that responds to pointer movement and form submissions, while remaining performant in its default non-interactive state.

## Key Changes

- **Interactive starfield enhancements** (`src/components/landing/starfield.tsx`):
  - Added `interactive` prop to enable cursor gravity well and signup pulse effects
  - Stars now track displacement (`ox`, `oy`) and glow state when interactive
  - Implemented gravity well physics: stars lean toward pointer within `WELL_RADIUS` (220px) with smoothstep falloff and asymmetric attack/release rates
  - Added signup pulse system: expanding rings that push nearby stars outward with a wavefront effect
  - Pulse spawns burst shooters (4 streaks) that fan upward from the button location
  - Optimized for idle cost: when settled and no pointer activity, the interactive block is skipped entirely
  - Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` and only enables pointer well on fine-pointer devices (not touch)

- **Starfield event system** (`src/lib/starfield-events.ts`):
  - New `STARFIELD_PULSE_EVENT` custom event for decoupled communication between form and starfield
  - `pulseStarfield()` function dispatches pulse from viewport coordinates
  - No React/Next.js imports to avoid bundling the starfield chunk into unrelated pages

- **Interest list page** (`src/app/(marketing)/interest/page.tsx`):
  - New static page with hero copy, signup form, feature callouts, FAQ, and CTA sections
  - Uses `LandingStarfield` with `interactive={true}` for enhanced visual feedback
  - Mirrors landing page structure and styling with dark theme

- **Interest form component** (`src/components/interest/interest-form.tsx`):
  - Hero-sized form with email input and submit button
  - Orbiting loader animation during submission (respects reduced motion)
  - Success state with animated checkmark and confirmation message
  - Honeypot field and client-side validation before server action
  - Fires starfield pulse on successful submission from button coordinates
  - Error handling with shake animation on validation failures

- **Orbit rings backdrop** (`src/components/interest/orbit-rings-backdrop.tsx`):
  - Decorative SVG with concentric rings and motes
  - Two counter-rotating groups for parallax depth effect
  - Pure CSS animations (no JavaScript), masked to fade behind content

- **Supporting changes**:
  - Added `InterestPageSkeleton` for loading state
  - Updated navigation links across pricing, docs, and footer to include `/interest`
  - Added `/interest` to public routes
  - New CSS animations for orbit spinner and rings rotation
  - Updated `LandingStarfield` to accept and pass through `interactive` prop

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Performance**: Interactive features only activate when needed (pointer movement or pulses). Once settled, the starfield reverts to the plain non-interactive path with zero overhead.
- **Device awareness**: Gravity well only enables on fine-pointer devices (mouse/stylus), not touch, since a finger occludes what it bends.
- **Decoupling**: Starfield and form communicate via DOM events, keeping them in separate code bundles.
- **Motion respect**: All animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, including the pulse, loader, and success state choreography.
- **Pulse physics**: Ring expansion uses cubic easing for a natural wavefront feel; star push force is perpendicular to ring radius for radial displacement.

body:
## Summary

This is a complete architectural refactor of the application from a single-file React component with local state management to a production-grade, cloud-backed assessment platform. The old "Trainito Academy" learning app has been replaced with the "CAIWP MQA Assessment Dashboard" — a real-time, multi-user assessment system with separate candidate and admin interfaces, Firebase authentication, Firestore persistence, and Cloud Functions for secure grading.

## Key Changes

### Architecture & Backend
- **Removed**: Monolithic `App.tsx` (650 lines) with all UI, state, and logic in one file
- **Added**: Modular service layer with pluggable backends:
  - `firebaseBackend.ts`: Production backend using Firebase Auth, Firestore, and Cloud Functions
  - `demoBackend.ts`: Fully in-memory simulation for zero-config demo mode (no Firebase required)
  - `backend.ts`: Abstract interface allowing seamless switching between implementations
- **Added**: Cloud Functions (`functions/src/index.ts`) for secure server-side operations:
  - Auth triggers for user provisioning and admin role sync
  - `startAttempt()` and `submitAttempt()` for attempt lifecycle and grading
  - Answer key validation (never exposed to client)
  - Activity logging and audit trails

### Data Model & Types
- **Removed**: Simple `types.ts` with `Question`, `Participant` interfaces
- **Added**: Comprehensive `src/types.ts` with production data structures:
  - `UserProfile`, `UserSummary` (candidate metadata and progress)
  - `Attempt` (assessment attempt with live progress tracking)
  - `QuestionPublic`, `QuestionReview` (client-safe question types)
  - `ActivityLog`, `ModuleStat` (admin analytics)
  - Constants: `MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`, `PASSING_PERCENTAGE=75`, `TOTAL_QUESTIONS=30`
- **Added**: Server-side question bank (`functions/src/data/questionBank.ts`) with answer keys, never bundled into client code

### UI Components
- **Removed**: Monolithic component with all views (login, quiz, dashboard, HR admin)
- **Added**: Modular component hierarchy:
  - **Auth**: `LoginScreen.tsx` with Google Sign-In + demo mode fallback
  - **Candidate**: `CandidateDashboard.tsx`, `ProfileSetup.tsx`, `AssessmentRunner.tsx`, `ResultsScreen.tsx`
  - **Admin**: `AdminLayout.tsx` with tabs for `OverviewTab.tsx`, `LiveMonitorTab.tsx`, `CandidatesTab.tsx`, `AuditLogTab.tsx`, `SetupTab.tsx`
  - **Shared**: `Logo.tsx`, `DemoModeBanner.tsx`, `ConnectionStatus.tsx`

### State Management & Context
- **Removed**: Local `useState` hooks scattered throughout monolithic component
- **Added**: `AuthProvider.tsx` context for centralized auth state and user profile/summary subscriptions
- **Added**: `ReactiveStore.ts` — minimal in-memory pub/sub for demo mode to mimic Firestore's `onSnapshot()` semantics

### Security & Validation
- **Added**: Firestore security rules (`firestore.rules`) enforcing:
  - Candidates cannot write to `users`, `user_summaries`, `answer_keys`, or `activity_logs`
  - Candidates can only update live progress fields in `attempts`
  - Answer keys are server-only; grading happens exclusively in Cloud Functions
- **Added**: Firestore indexes (`firestore.indexes.json`) for efficient queries on attempts, summaries, and audit logs

### Configuration & Deployment
- **Added**: `.env.example` for Firebase config (public, client-safe values)
- **Added**: `firebase.json` for Hosting + Firestore deployment
- **Added**: `SETUP.md` — comprehensive setup guide for Firebase project creation, OAuth credentials, and deployment
- **Added**: `tailwind.config.js`, `postcss.config.js` for styling

# Release: zylos-core 0.7.2-rc.29

Publishes the 8 commits accumulated since rc.28. Version bump + CHANGELOG only; no code change beyond the already-merged PRs (#67 #68 #69 #70 #75 #76 #80).

## Added
- **Feishu task lifecycle streaming** — Commitment Core task events (created → started → submitted for review → accepted/cancelled) fan into the originating conversation as a task status card with completion re-notifications (#67).
- **Repository-linked resident Agent upgrades** — upgrade from one repository link, preserving newer installed sources during latest resolution (#69).
- **Single-component repository upgrades** — explicitly scoped single-component updates with the installed baseline normalized for the deployment ledger (#70).

## Fixed
- **Failed assistant runs preserve the drafted reply** — FailRun persists the accumulated output into the failed outbound row instead of empty content; `queryFailedRuns()` exposes the recovery listing (#79, #80).
- Task-stream worker defaults to the supervise loop under pm2 instead of usage-error restart-looping (#68).
- Evidenced local candidate promotion through the deployment gate (#75).
- Native upgrade reports bound to release evidence without rewriting execution identities (#76).

author: hannoeru
body:
## Problem

The postbuild dist checker (`scripts/dist-verify.ts`) could report success while a forbidden import was present. Its forbidden-`require()` rule was skipped for any file containing `as default`, so a declaration like:

```ts
import uno = require("@unocss/core")
export { uno as default }
```

passed validation. The script also carried obsolete commented-out checks, misleading `cjsFiles` naming, and had no test coverage.

## Changes

- Forbidden `require()` of `@unocss/*` in CJS declaration output (`.d.ts` / `.d.cts`) now always fails the build — the `as default` exemption is removed.
- Scope intentionally limited to **declaration outputs**: runtime `.cjs` may `require()` ESM-only packages because Node ≥ 22.12 (the minimum engine) supports `require(esm)`. The nuxt and webpack integrations rely on this; an earlier draft that scanned runtime output produced false positives in CI.
- Removed obsolete commented-out implementation; renamed `cjsFiles` → `cjsDeclarationFiles` so logs match what is scanned.
- Direct-execution guard now compares via `pathToFileURL()`, fixing a silent no-op on Windows (`argv[1]` is `C:\...`, never equal to a `/C:/` URL pathname).
- Added `test/dist-verify.test.ts`: spawns the real checker against temporary fixtures and asserts pass/fail exit codes, including the default-export case.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run test/dist-verify.test.ts` — 3/3 passed
- Full checker run against a complete local build: `Dist files verify passed`
- CI green across ubuntu/macos/windows matrices

author: truhojunbot-tech
body:
Closes #262. Reported by Quota, following up on my own note in PR #261.

⚠️ **Stacked on `fix/260-claude-codex-session-cap` (PR #261)**, not on `main` — it modifies the policy-aware codex branch that PR introduces. Retarget to `main` once #261 merges.

## Reproduced against the live store — no fixtures needed

9,894 sessions on this host:

```
globally newest : worktrees/alpha_engine/codex   (09-04 05:52)
agent_crew's    : 019e0cf9                        (09-02 23:53)
=> a resume dispatched for agent_crew would have attached alpha_engine's
```

The store is dominated by non-crew directories (metaculus 3,982; ht-8004 2,422), so the odds of `--last` belonging to the dispatching worktree were low in general.

Attribution would still have recorded the *dispatching* project's `context_id`: token cost against the wrong logical context, another project's history in the prompt — and a successful task either way, which is what made it invisible.

## The binding

Each rollout's first record is a `session_meta` carrying `cwd` and `id` — the per-worktree binding the CLI doesn't expose — and `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` targets it exactly.

- `codex_session_for_cwd()` finds the newest session for a worktree, newest-first under a **read budget** (the store is unbounded and this runs on every dispatch).
- A resume uses that id; an unbound worktree starts **fresh**. Never `--last`, which is a guess dressed as continuity.
- The resolved id is written to `provider_session_id` **at dispatch**, before the provider runs, so a task that crashes mid-run is still joinable to the session it resumed.
- After each codex run the binding is recorded, so the next resume needs no search.
- #261's rule is untouched: fresh/reset resumes nothing, binding or not.

## Verification

16 tests, including the A/B interleaving the issue asks for (B written last, A still resumed) and an isolation test proving the dispatch-time record is the source rather than the post-run capture.

Five mutations, each failing exactly the intended test. **One initially survived**: removing the read budget passed, because the bound test put the target in an *older day* directory and the day-level break already excluded it. The test now puts thirty rollouts and the target in **one** day — the case the read bound actually protects.

One #260 assertion is updated rather than kept: it asserted `resume --last`, which this change removes.

Suite: **1116 passed / 10 failed**, the same 10 that fail on `main`.

author: revarbat
body:
`-T` renders nothing, so this job needs no display libraries and the runner is a free choice. Free for *correctness* — not free for *time*.

| | durations |
|---|---|
| **ubuntu**, `-Tmf`, no images | 30, 36, 45, 45, 46, 47 min |
| **macOS**, `-f`, **all** images | 35, 38, 40 min |

The mac does strictly more work and still finishes sooner.

## Why

Rendering the images costs about **11%** — measured at 34.9s → 38.9s over one file on one machine. The runner gap is bigger than that.

What dominates both jobs is parsing every script and evaluating every example, which `-T` does not avoid. Geometry — the part `-T` *does* skip — is only 1.4–6%.

## The spread matters as much as the median

ubuntu ranged **30 to 47 minutes for identical work**, a 57% swing. macOS varied 14%. Shared Linux VMs against near-dedicated mac hardware.

That variance is why one ubuntu run beat every macOS run while another took 47 minutes — and why the median is the wrong thing to look at alone.

## Effect

Roughly 7 minutes off every PR, and a far more predictable wait. The 75-minute limit stays until a few mac runs have been timed here.

body:
## Summary

Adds a per-job "decision timeline": an unconditional, retained record of when each job actually fired, why, and at what carbon-intensity value (when known) - answering "why was this job shifted" without opting in to anything.

- Introduces `DecisionStrategy` (`FIXED_WINDOW`/`SUCCESSIVE`) and `DecisionReason` (a greenest-available-slot outcome, plus two fallback reasons) to classify how and why a job fired.
- Every `@GreenScheduled` or programmatic job now records this automatically, independent of the separate (opt-in) carbon-impact feature.
- The recorded history is queryable, and also published as an event so it can be exported or persisted beyond the default in-memory store.
- The scheduler's "job fired" logging is now consistent and enabled at a sensible level across all trigger types (closes #117), with the job's identity/strategy/zone attached to every log line for the duration of its execution.
- The carbon-intensity value the scheduler already computes when picking a green execution slot is no longer discarded.

Quarkus/Spring/Micronaut extension support and the public docs page are intentionally out of scope here and blocked on this PR merging first.

Note: this branch is based on a clean `main`, not on the still-open #280 - the two touch overlapping files but are independent; a merge conflict between them is expected and should be resolved at merge time by whichever lands second.

## Documentation

The public docs page for this feature (tracked separately) leads with how to quickly check "is my job actually running" via logging, before explaining the timeline itself, how it relates to the separate carbon-impact feature, and how to plug in a custom store.

## Test plan

- [x] `./mvnw -pl core test` and `./mvnw -pl execution-planner test` - all green
- [x] `./mvnw -DskipTests install` - full multi-module build compiles cleanly against the changed planner contract

author: huaicheng
body:
`init_dram_backend()` calls `abort()` when `mlock()` fails, and it fails for any
run whose `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` does not cover the backend, which is the default on
most machines. On such a host FEMU currently dies at startup in every mode:

```
[FEMU] Err: Failed to pin the memory backend to the host DRAM
Aborted (core dumped)
```

Pinning exists to keep page faults out of the emulated latency, not to make the
device work at all. Warn with the size and the reason, say what it costs, and
carry on.

The device is unaffected otherwise; only its timing is then subject to page
faults, which the message says.

### Testing
- Built at `-Werror`, release and with the address and undefined-behaviour
  sanitizers.
- Every mode (0-5) instantiated on a host with an 8 MiB memlock limit: aborts
  before the change, comes up after it.
- Guest regression matrix on a 128-core host: black-box with page, hybrid and
  fast mapping, zoned with ZRWA, three heterogeneous namespaces, key-value, and
  black-box with FDP. All pass, no change to write amplification.

Noticed while tightening the CI step that instantiates each mode, which used
`|| true` and so had never reported that the runner could not start the device.

author: yananix
body:
Chinese era parsing is inconsistent with the strings produced by format in zh-CN, zh-HK, and zh-TW.

For example, parsing "公元前 2026" with "GGGG y" currently returns CE 2026 (year 2026), instead of BCE 2026 (year -2025). Parsing "公元 2026" with "G y" or "GGGGG y" returns Invalid Date.

The narrow and abbreviated matchers only accept 前, although the localizer emits 公元 for CE. The wide matcher accepts 公元前, but the BCE parser only recognizes strings starting with 前, so the CE prefix incorrectly wins.

This change accepts the localized CE form at every width and distinguishes the full BCE form from the CE prefix in all three locales. Formatting output stays the same.

Validation (run from pkgs/core):
- pnpm exec vitest run src/locale src/parse/test.ts src/format/test.ts: 699 tests passed.
- The new regression cases failed 18 tests before the fix and pass after it. They cover all five era tokens, BCE/CE, years 0 and 1, and the unconsumed input suffix.
- Oxfmt, Oxlint, and git diff --check passed for the changed files.
- Ran the locale snapshot generator. It does not cover era tokens; it only produced pre-existing month snapshot updates, which are excluded from this PR.

author: take-cheeze
body:
This PR adds three new opt-in graph-rewriting passes that decompose mmdeploy/mmcv's custom operators into subgraphs built from standard ONNX ops, enabling onnxsim to simplify graphs containing these custom ops that otherwise have no ONNX Runtime kernels.

## Summary

Three custom operators from mmdeploy/mmcv detection pipelines are decomposed:
1. **`MMCVDeformConv2d` / `MMCVModulatedDeformConv2d`** (deformable convolution v1/v2) → standard ops (`Gather`, `GatherND`, `Reshape`, `Transpose`, `Concat`, `MatMul`, etc.)
2. **`MMCVMultiScaleDeformableAttention`** (deformable attention for BEVFormer/Deformable DETR) → `Split`, `Reshape`, `Transpose`, `Gather`, `Concat`, `GridSample`, `ReduceSum`
3. **`TRTBatchedNMS`** (TensorRT-plugin post-processing NMS) → `NonMaxSuppression`, `TopK`, `GatherND`, `Pad`, `Compress`, etc.

These are `PassType::Other` rewrites (not run by default) that must be explicitly enabled via `extra_optimizers=["rewrite_deform_conv_to_gather"]` (Python) or `--enable-optimization rewrite_deform_conv_to_gather` (CLI).

## Key Changes

- **`onnxsim/passes/rewrite_deform_conv_to_gather.h`** (~813 lines): Decomposes deformable convolution (DCNv1/DCNv2) using 4-corner bilinear sampling with zeros padding via `GatherND`, matching the algorithm in mmcv's CUDA kernel and torchvision's `deform_conv2d`. Scope limited to `groups=1` for correctness; `deform_groups` and kernel size are unrolled at pass-build time.

- **`onnxsim/passes/rewrite_msdeformattn_to_gridsample.h`** (~630 lines): Decomposes multi-scale deformable attention by splitting input values per feature-map level, reshaping/transposing for `GridSample` (with `[0,1]`→`[-1,1]` coordinate normalization), and applying per-level attention weights. Reuses the bilinear-sampling infrastructure from the deformable-conv pass.

- **`onnxsim/passes/rewrite_trt_batched_nms.h`** (~698 lines): Decomposes TensorRT's batched NMS plugin into a standard "per-class greedy NMS via `NonMaxSuppression`, then per-batch global top-K merge" algorithm. Handles background-class exclusion, score thresholding, and per-batch padding/counting.

- **`onnxsim/custom_optimizer_passes.cpp`**: Registers the three new passes in the optimizer pipeline.

- **Test files** (`tests/test_deform_conv_to_gather.py`, `tests/test_msdeformattn_to_gridsample.py`, `tests/test_trt_batched_nms.py`): Comprehensive test suites with NumPy reference implementations of each algorithm. Since the custom ops have no ONNX Runtime kernels, tests use `check_n=0` (onnx.checker only, no execution of original) and independently verify the simplified graph's output against the reference.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Bilinear sampling with zeros padding**: Reuses the `GatherND`-based technique from `rewrite_gridsample_to_gather.h` (4-corner validity masking, clamped indices, weighted sum). Deformable conv uses absolute pixel coordinates (no denormalize step); deformable attention converts `[0,1]` to `[-1,1]` for `GridSample`.

- **Dynamic shape handling**: All three passes read dynamic dimensions (`N`, `H`,

author: tymonius
yongjohnlee80
body:
Asked for directly: *"let's create a utility error function that automatically wraps into our conventional structure"*, and *"so all error wrapping to be structured exactly the same format"*.

Until now the shape lived only in prose and every call site retyped `fmt.Errorf("... (%w)", errs.X)`. **A format retyped at every call site is a format that drifts** — this sweep has already found one condition spelled two different ways inside a single package.

| helper | for | produces |
|---|---|---|
| `Wrap(base, format, args…)` | a call site reporting a failure | `where, specifically (what)` |
| `WrapCause(base, cause, format, args…)` | the same, keeping an underlying error recoverable | `where (what): cause` |
| `Sentinel(base, detail)` | declaring a package's layered condition | `what: detail` |

`WrapCause` is the one that earns its place beyond convenience: it's the shape the auth rung needed, where a first-party identity **and** an underlying cause must both stay recoverable. Formatting the cause with `%v` is the mistake it exists to make hard.

## Two things the tests changed, not the design

**`Sentinel` carries no brackets of its own.** This fell out of writing the test, not planning: wrapping a self-bracketed sentinel produced `"term: write to /dev/tty ((closed: backend is stopped))"`. The bracket belongs to `Wrap`, which puts exactly **one** pair around the identity a call site reports, at any depth. The test asserts the bracket *count*, so a sentinel that starts bracketing itself again fails here.

**A nil base is reported, not panicked** — and the panic budget is why. It refused the three new panic sites and demanded a category, which was the right question rather than paperwork: I couldn't honestly call them `invariant`, since a caller *can* pass a runtime error variable that happens to be nil. Registering three new violations in a budget that only falls was the wrong answer to a design I hadn't finished thinking about.

Panicking was disproportionate. Building an error shouldn't be able to take a process down, nothing is corrupted by getting there, and a helper this widely used would turn a logging mistake into an outage. So a nil base returns an error carrying `errs.ErrFatal` that still delivers the caller's message — unmissable and catchable, without the blast radius.

## Wrapping is not required

The other half of the ruling, now in both convention copies:

```go
return ErrNoIdentity                            // yes
return errs.Wrap(ErrNoIdentity, "no identity")  // no — says it twice
```

The message-level form of *one layer is a real answer*. Either return the upstream error, or add something.

`Wrap` is asserted **byte-identical** to the `fmt` spelling it replaces, so adopting it is not a behaviour change anywhere it's applied.

Suite, vet, gofmt, comment budget and panic budget all green.

A twelfth deduped onto #1259. The swept-path record is `docs/audits/security-sweep-1220-setup-cli.md`. Closes #1220. The two fixed here are both on the macOS LaunchAgent plist — the OS-level persistence descriptor that carries `GH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in plaintext — plus the sibling credential writer that copied its pattern: **SEC-1220-10 — plist markup injection.** `generatePlist` escaped only its three `EnvironmentVariables` values and interpolated the path fields raw. `logsDir` resolves from `log_dir` in `.config.json`, then `LAUNCH_LOG_DIR` / `LOG_DIR` / `VIBE_LOGS_DIR`, and `lib/log_dir.ts` checks only that the value is absolute or `~`-anchored — `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` all pass. A value carrying `` closed the enclosing element and could add a `ProgramArguments` entry, or a `Program` replacing the executable outright, in a descriptor launchd runs at every login. A path containing a plain `&` produced a plist `launchctl` refuses while setup still reported success. The Windows twin (`setup/scheduled_task.ts`) already escaped every value; the two private `escapeXml` copies had **drifted**, which is the root cause of the class rather than of the instance. The escape now lives in `worker/deno/lib/xml_escape.ts` with one owner and both descriptors import it. **SEC-1220-11 — permissions on the two files that hold tokens.** `Deno.writeTextFile(path, secret, { mode })` + a late `Deno.chmod` applies `mode` only when *creating* a file, so a pre-existing 0o644 copy is truncated and filled with the secret **before** the mode is narrowed, and both calls follow a symlink pre-positioned at the path. That pattern was on `writeSecurePlist` (`setup/launchagent.ts`) and on `writeConfigFile` (`setup/config_setup.ts`, `.config.json` — the ImgBB key, the GitHub App identifiers, the private-key path), whose docstring named `writeSecurePlist` as its model. Both now use `lib/file_utils.ts` `atomicWrite` (`O_EXCL` at 0o600, then rename) and both fail loud. Separately, `setupLaunchAgent` returned early when the rendered plist matched the file on disk, skipping the chmod entirely — the one case the tightening exists for, a plist an older worker wrote 0o644, re-renders to *identical* content, so re-running `./setup.sh` to pick up the fix did nothing. ### Filed, not fixed here Per the issue's definition of done, surviving findings are filed one per finding with a `` marker and `severity:*` / `confidence:*` labels: | Finding | Issue | Severity | Where | | ------- | ----- | -------- | ----- | | SEC-1220-01 | #1288 | high | `screenshot.ts:334-343` — `--deny-env` is a Deno permission check, not an environment scrub, so `--allow-run` on the next line hands every "denied" secret to any child. author: abdelrazzaq19
body:
Phase 3 of the modernization: making the catalogue usable once it holds more than a handful of cars, and finishing the map work that the flutter_map v8 migration left half done.

What this adds:

- CarQuery value object holding search, price range, seats, transmission, fuel type, availability and sort order. Filtering lives in the domain layer rather than the bloc so it is unit testable and so every screen agrees on what "matching" means.
- Debounced search bar and a filter sheet. The sheet edits a local draft and only reports it on Apply, so backing out leaves the list untouched.
- Favourites, stored at users/{uid}/favourites/{carId}. The toggle is optimistic and rolls back if the write fails. A favourites read failure degrades to "nothing saved" rather than failing the whole car list.
- Distance sorting and a user-location pin via geolocator, wrapped behind a LocationService interface so nothing else imports the plugin and tests need no platform channel. Denial is explained in the UI instead of silently doing nothing, and a permanent block offers no pointless retry.
- Every nearby car as a map marker, plus an "open in maps" hand-off using a geo: URI with a web fallback.
- A connectivity banner over the existing Firestore offline persistence.

Three defects fixed along the way:

- The car card's Semantics label was swallowing the favourite button, so a screen reader could not reach the heart at all. The heart is now a sibling of the tappable card rather than a descendant.
- FilterSheet could not clear a price filter: copyWith(minPrice: null) falls back to the existing value, so the draft is cleared first.
- Sorting by distance with no known position produced an arbitrary order. Cars without a location now sink to the bottom instead of floating up.

Tests go from 114 to 162. Android and iOS permission declarations are included, along with the <queries> entries Android 11+ needs before url_launcher can see a maps app.

author: fishdan
body:
Closes Spec 016. All 15 tasks accepted.

## Why

Spec 009 could not make GNOME's on-screen keyboard appear in a Chromium browser. A captured `WAYLAND_DEBUG` trace proved Brave sent a protocol-correct `text-input-v3` focus handshake that GNOME Shell simply did not act on, and the browser was changed to Firefox to work around it.

Remote input sidesteps that entire class of problem. GSConnect injects events at the **input layer**, exactly as a physical keyboard does, so it no longer matters whether the focused application cooperates with the compositor's text-input protocol.

## What's here

- `scripts/install-gsconnect.sh` — Ubuntu repository only, idempotent, and it handles the Wayland constraint that a newly installed extension is invisible to the running session until logout.
- `scripts/configure-gsconnect.sh` — `--apply` restricts to remote input, `--status` reads settings back, `--harden` stops LAN advertising.
- `docs/phone-input.md` — install, plugin policy with rationale, pairing, daily use, network exposure, credentials, removal, limitations.

The Plasma `kdeconnect` package is deliberately **not** used; it would pull Qt and KDE libraries onto a GNOME appliance for no benefit.

## Corrections made during the work

Three assumptions turned out to be wrong, each caught by checking rather than trusting:

1. **The plan's ordering was impossible.** It said the plugin policy would be applied before pairing. GSConnect stores plugin state per device, and no device exists until pairing. The plan was corrected rather than quietly worked around.
2. **The first policy script did nothing.** It set an `enabled` key on the per-plugin schemas. Those schemas have no such key — the real control is the Device schema's `disabled-plugins` list. It would have reported success while changing nothing.
3. **The documented removal path was wrong.** `gnome-extensions disable` does not stop GSConnect: the daemon is D-Bus activated and parented to systemd, so it kept running with **port 1716 still listening**. Anyone following the original docs would have left a network listener on a firewall-less machine believing the feature was removed. The path now includes an explicit daemon stop and a port check.

## Security posture

Only `mousepad` is enabled. All fourteen other plugins are in `disabled-plugins`, verified by reading settings back, and each risky plugin's own switch is cleared as defence in depth — `share.receive-files`, `sftp.automount`, `notification.send-notifications` and `contacts.contacts-source` all ship **enabled** and are now `false`.

`discoverable` is `false`, so the appliance no longer advertises. Recorded rather than glossed over: there is **no host firewall**, so port 1716 is LAN-reachable; this is acceptable only because pairing requires confirmation at both ends.

**A secret-hygiene failure was caught by the pre-PR scan.** The DualSense's Bluetooth address and the paired device's identifier had been written into `progress.ai` and `handoff.ai`, violating the constitution and this spec's own criteria, on a public repository. Neither was in `main` and the branch was unpushed, so nothing was published; both were purged from all branch commits before push, with the justification for the history rewrite recorded in `progress.ai`.

## Acceptance

Owner-accepted from the couch with no keyboard or mouse: pointer and typing work, **including in Brave** — the Chromium engine whose behaviour defeated Spec 009 — and a streaming password was entered with the session persisting across close and relaunch, retiring the last of Spec 009's deferred acceptance.

Reboot-validated: extension enabled, daemon relistening, device still paired, full plugin policy intact, `discoverable` still `false`, tablet reconnected unaided.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The paired device is a **Galaxy Tab A11 (type `tablet`)**, not a phone. No functional difference; recorded because the spec says "phone" throughout.
- **GNOME 51 will break this package** (`gnome-shell (<< 51~)`); the appliance runs 50.1. Logged as a Spec 013 maintenance risk.
- Installation pulled **39 packages** including `folks`, `telepathy` and `evolution-data-server`, leaving three D-Bus-activated services resident at roughly 46 MiB. Recorded under the constitution's explicit-dependencies principle.
- Brave was restored to the dock, which T008 required in order to test a Chromium browser from the couch.

## Summary

`moon ide analyze agent_review` listed several exports with zero cross-package usage plus 20 promoted trait methods. This trims the package to the surface `cmd/openseek` actually reaches.

- **`ReviewError` → `priv`.** No cross-package code names it; `run_review` raises it as a plain `Error` and the CLI catches generically.
- **`current_schema_version` / `severities` → package-private.** Only `validate` reads them. `exports.mbt` is removed; `parse` / `validate` (real consumers in `cmd/openseek/gate.mbt`) move back into `types.mbt`.

`ReviewScope` / `ReviewStats` remain as opaque `type` lines in the `.mbti` (with no methods now); the derived impl is public even on a private struct, so that is the floor.

author: rajkaria
body:
## Why

Nineteen of the twenty-one published Plays sit at one download and two sit at zero, and every one of those is the run that verified it. The board holds one row, from this machine.

Discovery inside the registry is **not** the gap. Registry search already ranks them first or second on their own queries (`browser tabs` returns `tab-debt` first, `decode a string` returns `whatis` first). For scale, the leading Play in comped's own category, `sidships/token-tab`, is at 34 downloads.

Two things actually were the gap:

1. Nothing has ever been posted to any channel. `docs/context/comped-plays.md` has said "Not done: launch posts" since 05 Sep.
2. gotcomped.com was comped-only, so eighteen Plays had no web presence at all. A person who liked one had no way to reach the other twenty, and twenty-one registry links is not a link you can share.

## What this adds

**`site/plays.html`** is that link. Generated by `tools/build_site.py` from one table: three families, the question each Play answers, a paste-ready run line under each, and a cold `demo=true` line wherever the Play has one. Linked from the landing page nav, the footer, a new `#more` section, and `llms.txt`, so an agent asked to run comped learns the other twenty exist.

A test asserts the table and `plays/` hold exactly the same slugs, so a published Play cannot go missing from the page, and a second test asserts the landing page reaches it.

**`docs/launch/POSTS.md`** is the other half: Discord (three staggered posts), X, LinkedIn, Show HN with its first comment, Reddit, prepared answers to the questions that actually come back, and the reason the pitch splits in two. Everyone with rote can run all twenty-one in one paste; everyone else needs the door that takes no account, so leading with the Plays off-Discord converts nobody.

## Layout bugs found while checking it

Two were pre-existing on `docs.html` and `developers.html`:

- The doc grid track defaulted to `min-width: auto`, so one wide command block widened the whole page (42px of horizontal body scroll at 1280).
- The nav overflowed a 375px phone by 61px.

One was new to the pattern: the Copy button sat inside the `overflow-x: auto` region, so a long command scrolled it out of reach. It now sits outside the scroller.

## Verification

- 518 tests pass, 6 skipped.
- Page checked in the browser at 1280 and at 375: no horizontal overflow at either, 21 play entries, 29 copy buttons, no console errors.
- No em dashes on any reader-facing page (house style, enforced by test).

body:
> *A green mechanical check below shows this change conforms to the engine's rules — not that it is correct. What covers correctness is the behavioural steps in **Review** you can run yourself and the change's honest self-report — not a reading of the diff for defects; a green check is never a substitute for that. **Your merge is the binding gate.***
>
> *About those checks: only the one that runs when the change is proposed for merge can stop a risky merge — a check that ran while the change was still being written is early advice. The engine's checks are proven against deliberately broken examples they must catch — the custom ones each against their own, the standard kinds against one shared example — so a passing check can't be one that quietly did nothing; a few are openly-noted exceptions where that kind of proof doesn't apply. Either way that speaks to the check, not to whether this change is right. And a check that could not run leaves its area unverified.*

Closes #807
Part of #806

## Purpose

**Four engine tools answered `--help` by doing their real work or blocking as a server; each now prints usage and exits before its own main() reads anything or acts.**

An AI or a person probing a tool with --help is asking to be told what it does. overlay_disclosure.py posted or edited a pull-request comment, issue_conformance_ci.py wrote to GitHub issues, and the two MCP servers blocked serving stdio — the #594 class of footgun, already fired in real sessions. #807's fifth tool, audit_soft_promote.py, was removed by PR #1224.

- The #594 guard first in each main(): `--help` / `-h` anywhere in argv prints a usage text naming the tool's real launcher and what a bare run does, and returns 0 before any environment variable, token, event or server is touched by the tool's own code.
- Any other argument, a dash flag or a bare word such as `help`, prints the usage to stderr and returns 2 without acting; the verb set is closed (`demo` where it exists).
- overlay_disclosure.main() and knowledge_mcp_server.main() take argv, where None means no arguments (never sys.argv); the entry blocks pass sys.argv[1:]; knowledge_mcp_server.main() returns an int and its entry block exits with it.
- Tests in each tool's existing module patch the outermost seams (boot.gh_token, _load_event, reconcile; _run; server.run), assert the launcher line in the usage, and prove the seams are never entered; a subprocess case per tool with a bounded wait proves the real exit status (0 for --help, 2 for an unknown argument).

*Impact: Probing any of the four tools is now safe; nothing changes for the workflows and MCP entries that launch them bare.*

## Scope

**Four tools, their four test modules, the regenerated knowledge graph, and one integration-repair commit.**

- W1 (a3d80fc1): overlay_disclosure.py and issue_conformance_ci.py guards, usage texts naming engine-overlay-disclosure.yml and engine-issue-conformance.yml, tests in test_overlay_disclosure.py and test_issue_conformance_ci.py.
- W2 (6a48c9c6): memory/mcp_server.py and knowledge_mcp_server.py guards; the memory server's usage and module docstring name the engine-memory entry through accepted_hook_dispatch.py under attended-memory-mcp and call a direct run the unqualified lane; the knowledge server's usage names the engine-knowledge-graph entry; tests in memory/test_mcp_server.py and test_knowledge_query.py.
- W3 (94a6a54b): knowledge graph regenerated; ci-assurance.md unchanged (no test docstring changed); derived_state.py verify in-sync.
- Integration repair (1fe53a0a): the four guard comments qualify their `#594` reference as StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#594, which engine/check/shipped-issue-references requires; graph regenerated again.
- Repair after the deliverable review (92b19c6a): the rejection names the first unrecognised word (never the valid verb) in issue_conformance_ci.py and memory/mcp_server.py, with the four tools' tests asserting the named word; a no-op environment patch is removed from test_overlay_disclosure.py; the four test modules' opening docstrings record the --help guard and ci-assurance.md and the graph are regenerated.
- Repair round 2 (057f449e): `demo demo` on the two verb tools exits 2 naming the second word instead of raising StopIteration; tests cover it in-process and as a subprocess; three docstrings wrap so the knowledge graph's summaries read whole.
- Merge of origin/main after review (the final head): PR #1229's memory-server changes beside the guard; the knowledge graph regenerated; no other conflict.

**Change profile** — the shape of this pull request at a glance:

- **Size:** 10 files changed, +341 / −23 lines.
- **Kinds of thing touched:** 8 tools, 1 doc, 1 other file (not in the engine's map).
- **Where:** .engine/tools, .engine/docs, .engine/knowledge.
- **Shape:** 8 commits on this branch — a standalone change unless a `Part of #N` line below says it is one slice of a larger effort.

_This is a description, not a gate — it never blocks a merge. It is here so you can weigh the change by what it touches, not by its line count._

*Impact: No launcher file (workflows, .mcp.json, .codex/config.toml, manifests) is edited; the no-argument path of every tool is unchanged.*

### Behaviors

**The capabilities this change delivers, each with the test that exercises it.**

- overlay_disclosure.py --help prints usage naming its workflow and exits 0; --bogus and a bare word exit 2; boot.gh_token, _load_event and reconcile are never entered. — `test_overlay_disclosure.TestHelpNeverActs`
- issue_conformance_ci.py --help exits 0 naming its workflow; only `demo` is accepted; _run is never entered on a probe. — `test_issue_conformance_ci.TestHelpNeverActs`
- memory/mcp_server.py --help exits 0 naming the accepted-hook launch chain; --bogus, help, serve and `demo extra` exit 2; server.run is never entered on a probe; bare and None argv still serve. — `memory.test_mcp_server (test_help_prints_usage_names_the_launch_chain_and_never_serves and three siblings)`
- knowledge_mcp_server.py --help exits 0 naming the engine-knowledge-graph entry; unknown arguments exit 2 at the process level because main() now returns an int that the entry block exits with. — `test_knowledge_query.TestMcpServerHelpNeverServes`
- The four existing bare od.main() calls in test_overlay_disclosure.py keep the no-argument path even when sys.argv carries flags. — `test_overlay_disclosure.TestHelpNeverActs.test_none_means_no_arguments_not_the_process_flags`

## Out of scope

**The general --help contract, import-time work, and the fifth tool.**

- A shared help helper in validate.py, the emit() consolidation, the retrofit of the ~68 read-only tools, and the enforcing help-contract check — #806's arc; designing its seam inside the urgent slice would pre-empt the census-driven design (tracked as StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#806)
- Environment reads and server-object construction that happen at module import (boot.py's PROTECTED_BRANCH read, the MCP server objects, the SDK's own reads) — they precede main() and no guard inside main() can reach them; the plan bounds its promise to the tool's own main() (tracked as StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#806)
- audit_soft_promote.py, #807's fifth tool — deleted by PR #1224 with the promotion lane; engine/check/lane-removed keeps it gone
- An argparse migration of the four tools — it would change the no-argument path's exit codes and messages that the launchers rely on

*Impact: Each boundary is the sealed plan's, not a forgotten piece.*

## Risk

**5 risks, ranked, each with the bound that contains it.**

- **A guard placed after an existing environment read inside main() would leave the footgun half-open (the most safety-sensitive edit).** The guard is main()'s first statement in all four (diff read in each node's evidence); the tests patch the outermost seams and set no environment; subprocess probes with dummy GITHUB_REPOSITORY/GITHUB_TOKEN exit 0 printing usage.

author: hyuntohoon
body:
`{"job": "youtube_ref_refresh"}` on a daily EventBridge cron.

## This is a compliance mechanism, not a cache warmer

YouTube Developer Policy III.E.4.c/.d caps stored API data at 30 calendar days, and III.E.4.d extends that ceiling to a videoId obtained from a plain public `search.list` — there is **no resource-id exception**. So "once mapped, never look again" is not implementable: the mapping survives only as a *refreshed* one, and a row this job cannot refresh is **deleted** rather than kept.

## Two passes, and the order is load-bearing

**1. EXPIRE** — delete every row past the window, whatever its `verify_state`. Runs **first** so a quota exhaustion, a network failure or a bad deploy in pass 2 can never postpone a deletion the policy requires. *A sweep that only runs when the enrichment succeeds is not a sweep.*

This is also why `idx_tpr_stale` is unconditional: a `'gone'` row still **stores** API-derived data — the videoId, `privacy_status`, `made_for_kids` — so the clock applies to it in full, and marking a row `'gone'` must not become a way to opt it out of retention.

**2. REFRESH** — oldest `'live'` rows first, 50 ids per 1-unit `videos.list` call.

### Why pass 2 refreshes only `'live'` rows

A row already known `'gone'` or `'not_embeddable'` is a settled fact the member has to act on (re-pick), not something to poll. Refreshing it would move `last_verified_at` forward every day and keep a dead row alive **forever** — technically compliant, permanently useless, and spending an id slot daily.

Left unrefreshed it ages out and pass 1 deletes it. That gives the member up to 30 days of the useful `410 Gone` "your video died, pick another" signal and then reclaims the row. If a video's owner re-enables embedding, the member re-picks and A3's write path re-verifies — no polling needed.

## Fails loudly, unlike the request-path clients

The music and backend clients fail **closed and quiet** on a missing key, which is right for a request path. This job logs and **re-raises** instead: a retention sweep that silently does nothing is the exact failure the policy exists to prevent, and it looks identical to a healthy run. Re-raising surfaces it on the rule's `FailedInvocations` alarm (which the workspace `worker_crons` module wires automatically).

## Session lifecycle

fetch ids → materialise → **close** → HTTP → fresh short write session. The recurring bug class that produced the Neon `ProtocolViolation`.

## Two shared-db pins, different values

This repo has **two**, and only one moves here:

| pin | value | why |
|---|---|---|
| CI canonical schema (`deploy.yml`) | → **V56** | Had to move, or the new integration tests **skip** — they guard on the V56 columns, and a skip reads as green. |
| installed package (`requirements.txt`/`.lock`) | unchanged | This job uses raw SQL and imports no new model. Bumping the runtime ORM would be an unrelated deploy change riding along in a compliance PR. |

The asymmetry is now commented at the pin site, because it is the kind of thing that looks like an oversight to the next reader.

## Verification

- `pytest`: **553 passed, 52 skipped**. The skips are `TEST_DB_URL` / live-API gated; CI runs the integration suite against a real Postgres service container bootstrapped from the pinned canonical schema.
- **18 new unit tests + 8 new real-engine integration tests.**
- The integration file uses a real engine because **both** load-bearing behaviours *are* WHERE clauses. A mutant that filtered the retention DELETE on `verify_state='live'` — the exact defect the Step-A1 review caught in `idx_tpr_stale` — passes a mocked suite while letting every `'gone'` row escape the policy forever.
- **10 mutations, 9 caught.** Two survived first pass and exposed real test weaknesses:
  - the session-lifecycle harness keyed "a session is open" on `execute` rather than on **construction**, so a mutant that merely opened a connection around the HTTP call was invisible to it;
  - the expiry-ordering test checked "DELETE before HTTP" when the consequence that matters is "DELETE before the refresh **writes**" — otherwise a 31-day row is refreshed first, its clock reset, and it survives the very sweep meant to delete it.

  Both rewritten; both mutants now die. The tenth is an equivalent mutant (moving `expire_stale()` after the work SELECT preserves both invariants).

## Not in this repo

The EventBridge rule, the `YOUTUBE_SECRETS_PARAM` env var and the `/myblog/youtube` IAM grant. They are in the workspace PR; until it is applied this job has no trigger and no credential — and it fails loudly rather than pretending to run.

Refs: `docs/rfcs/FEAT-youtube-playback-provider.md` Step A5

author: rahulparmar311197
body:
## Summary
- `CandleWorker._derive_timeframe` (`backend/app/workers/candle_worker.py`) picked the base-timeframe candles to aggregate into a higher timeframe by slicing the last `window` rows *positionally* (`recent[-window:]`), assuming the base timeframe has no gaps.
- A single dropped tick, worker restart, or feed hiccup leaves the current bucket short of base candles — but the *next* bucket's closing candle still satisfies `_completes_bucket` by wall-clock arithmetic and still triggers derivation. The positional slice then pads the missing count out with rows from the *previous*, already-derived bucket, deriving that bucket's timestamp from the wrong row and silently overwriting its already-correct, already-persisted candle with data spanning two different periods — while the true current (incomplete) bucket is never derived at all.
- Fixed by computing the target bucket's timestamp directly from `as_of` and filtering fetched base candles to actual bucket *membership* (`compute_bucket_start(c.timestamp, target_minutes) == target_bucket_ts`) rather than position, matching the approach already used correctly in `app/market/aggregation.py`'s `resample_candles`.
- Documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` under a new section before "Multi-leg options execution (§37-40)".

## Test plan
- New `tests/workers/test_candle_worker.py::test_derive_timeframe_skips_an_incomplete_bucket_instead_of_corrupting_the_prior_one`: derives a first 5m bucket normally from five 1m candles, then feeds a second 5m bucket's worth of ticks with one minute deliberately missing, and asserts the first bucket's derived candle is untouched (no corruption, no second row for the incomplete bucket).
- Verified the new test fails against the pre-fix code (first bucket's derived candle gets silently overwritten with the wrong `open`) via `git stash`, then passes once the fix is restored.
- `python -m pyflakes app tests` clean.
- `python -m pytest tests -q` run twice: 275 passed both times.

author: rmusser01
body: ## Summary Fixes a P1 screen-reuse regression (TASK-31808): warm revisits of the reused ChatScreen never consumed CHAT or VLLM_CONSOLE handoffs. ChatScreen is `reusable=True`, so `on_mount` — which schedules `_consume_pending_chat_handoff` and `consume_pending_vllm_console_intent` — fires once per app run; every later visit runs only `on_screen_resume`. The resume-path timer list `_console_resume_handoff_timers` (introduced in the Console screen-reuse arc, fed0b7257a / af82ac9630) re-armed only four of the six handoff consumers. Chat is the default initial screen, so it is warm on essentially every real navigation: - vLLM setup's "Use in Console" navigated to Console but never applied the target (the `VLLM_CONSOLE` claim sat pending forever). - Every `open_chat_with_handoff` caller (Library conversations, Library screen, Media, Skills, Study) staged a `CHAT` payload that was never consumed — silently, no error. PR #2421's verification doc had already recorded the failing assertion as an "unrelated route-reuse failure ... not fixed here". ## Fix Add the two missing consumers to `_console_resume_handoff_timers` in `on_screen_resume`, with the identical `set_timer(0.15, ...)` idiom `on_mount` uses (Textual timers accept the async `_consume_pending_chat_handoff` directly, exactly as `on_mount` schedules it). Because they join the tracked list, `on_screen_suspend`'s existing timer-cancel covers them — a switch-away inside the 0.15s window cannot consume handoffs against the hidden screen (preserving Qodo #2420 finding 4's guarantee). Both consumers are claim-based and self-guarding, so the pre-existing first-visit double-schedule (on_mount + the mount's own resume) stays harmless, matching the four consumers already in both lists. ## Red → green evidence - `Tests/UI/test_vllm_lab_workflow.py::test_navigation_to_fresh_models_screen_preserves_exact_ready_handoff` - RED on unfixed origin/dev (`2b4973971e`): `AssertionError: assert not True` at the `has_pending(HandoffChannel.VLLM_CONSOLE)` check — every baseline run that got past test setup (3/5; the other 2 hit the pre-existing setup flake below). - GREEN with the fix (repeated runs; the handoff assertion never failed post-fix). - NEW `Tests/UI/test_console_native_chat_flow.py::test_warm_console_resume_consumes_staged_chat_handoff` — drives the production router end-to-end (Chat → Settings → `open_chat_with_handoff` → warm Chat), asserting the same reused instance comes back, the CHAT claim drains, and the payload lands in the staged-context lane (`_pending_console_launch_context`). RED on unfixed code at the `has_pending(HandoffChannel.CHAT)` assert; GREEN with the fix. Existing CHAT-handoff tests mock `open_chat_with_handoff` and never exercised warm-resume consumption. ## Neighbor suites (paired-arm verified under a load-32 box) - `test_chat_screen_suspend.py` (owns the suspend timer-cancel contract): 2/2 passed. - `test_product_maturity_phase3_knowledge_entry.py`, `test_study_quizzes_screen.py`: passed. - `test_settings_raw_cli.py`: 40/41; `test_pending_raw_cli_save_vetoes_real_navigation_until_arrival` fails IDENTICALLY with this fix reverted (splash runs 7.0s vs the test's 3s boot budget; ChatScreen never mounts before the failing wait) — pre-existing on dev. - `test_console_controller_wiring.py` + `test_console_session_settings.py`: 454 passed, 6 failed; the named session-settings failures reproduce IDENTICALLY on the reverted pristine arm (fork-transition cleanup asserts + notify-once IndexError) — pre-existing on dev; the resume-repair test passed on both arms. - Pre-existing flake: the vLLM workflow test also flakes in its SETUP phase (`NoMatches: 'VllmSetupView'`), before the behavior under test — measured 2/5 on the UNFIXED baseline, similar rate post-fix; filed as TASK-31809 (wait-loop exit predicate does not match the assert that follows it). ## Residual risk (release-eve wrap-up; not run locally) Curtailed by the wrap-up directive under machine saturation — CI should cover: full-file sweeps of `Tests/UI/test_vllm_lab_workflow.py` and `Tests/UI/test_console_native_chat_flow.py`, plus `Tests/UI/test_product_maturity_phase1_core_loop.py`, `Tests/UI/test_console_fleet_lifecycle_controller.py`, `Tests/UI/test_uat_first_time_character_chat.py`, `Tests/UI/test_console_roleplay_resume_navigation.py`. ## Admin Control Center
- dedicated `/admin/users` Users & Auth console
- server-only Supabase Auth email/ban/unban/hard-delete controls
- staged deletion jobs + protected self/super-admin accounts
- immutable admin audit and governed account status lifecycle
- active-session account control gate (pre-migration fail-open compatibility)
- `/admin/regions` using the existing Alsamos Map Engine (`AlsamosMapSurface`), not an external map
- `/admin/system` database/mail/governance health view
- RBAC-compatible server checks and least-privilege RPCs
- internal mailbox alias lifecycle RPCs
- pre-migration graceful profile fallback

## Security
- no login/password is required or stored
- service-role key is only read inside `admin-user-control` Edge Function
- no service key or arbitrary SQL console is exposed to the browser
- dangerous actions require reasons and are audited
- hard delete is staged before Supabase Auth identity deletion
- self + super-admin destructive controls are protected
- Auth email updates keep Alsamos `identity_accounts.login_email` synchronized with rollback on sync failure
- user details RPC returns only a whitelisted profile payload after hardening

## Deploy order
1. run migrations `20260906090000`, `20260906091500`, `20260906092000` in order
2. deploy `admin-user-control` with JWT verification enabled and normal Supabase server env vars
3. deploy frontend

Supabase project is currently inactive from the available connector, so production DB/Auth mutation testing is intentionally deferred to the Lovable run/deploy step.

body:
## 问题

`readings.sh` §③ 的 `unit` 列直接回显 `status.json` 的 `active_unit` 字符串。
那是个**标签**，不是读数——它既不保证同名 unit 存在，也不保证在跑。

2026-09-06 11:03 值守 wf-194310 时实际踩到：S3 单 `dev-fg-80c109d9ea04` 报
`unit fleet-graph-dd-dev-fg-80c109d9ea04-r1`，`systemctl is-active` 回 `inactive`，
`list-units --all 'fleet-graph-dd-*'` 一行都没有。差一步就把一张健康的单判成死单——
真实情况是 dd runner (pid 3247725) 在跑，`final_review` 的 `claude-opus-5`
子进程也在跑，`opencode.db` mtime 距读数 46 秒。

## 改法

`unit` 列换成两个实测值：

- `live=<pid>`：`pgrep -f "dd run --development <dev>"` 命中的进程号，没有则 `-`
- `db_age_s`：该单最新 `opencode.db` 的 mtime 年龄（含 `g<N>` 层），说明在飞的那一段是否还在写

## 验证

```
dev-fg-80c109d9ea04 | state running | ... | live 3247725 | db_age_s 46    | last_event 02:56Z g1 continuous_review APPROVE
dev-fg-8bca5bc0e6fe | state failed  | ... | live -       | db_age_s 46802 | last_event 14:07Z g1 implement failed
```

活单一眼可见在写，死单一眼可见早停。

author: ladical13
body:
## The canvasser has been a blank screen since August 19

`window.syncToCRM = syncToCRM` sits at the bottom of `canvasser/static/app.js`, referencing a function deleted in 396236b when the Den sync became the Pipeline handoff. It is a **top-level statement one line above `boot()`**, so the ReferenceError it throws stops `boot()` from ever running — and `boot()` is the only caller of `showApp()`, which is the only thing that removes `hidden` from `<div id="app">` (index.html:43).

Every rep opening the canvasser got a blank dark screen. The cache-buster moved to `v=3` in 32f7d4f, *after* the break, so the service worker invalidated everyone's cached copy and pulled the broken bundle down.

Reproduced by loading the bundle with browser stubs:

```
THREW AT TOP LEVEL: ReferenceError: syncToCRM is not defined
```

## Why 19 green tests didn't catch it

`test_app_bundle_is_syntactically_valid` runs `node --check`, which **parses and does not execute**. It cannot see a reference to a name that no longer exists.

## Changes

- **`window.syncToCRM` → `window.addToPipeline`.** The dead name is gone, replaced by the function the Add to Pipeline button actually calls — which was never exported and only worked because a top-level function declaration is global in a classic script.
- **Sign Out fixed**, broken the same way and for the same reason: it called `/api/logout` (gone since identity moved to the portal), then `showLogin()` (deleted with the login screen). It now hands off to the portal's `/logout` like the CRM does, stopping the GPS timers first so the last thing the tab does on the way out is not a location push.
- **`tests/boot_runner.js`** loads `app.js` the way a browser does. `runInThisContext`, not `require()`: in a CommonJS module a top-level `function foo(){}` is module-scoped, but in a browser classic script it is a global — which is what the inline `onclick=` handlers resolve against, so only the former reproduces the failure.
- **`test_the_bundle_boots_and_every_inline_handler_resolves`** asserts two things this bundle could not have survived: nothing throws while loading, and every name an inline handler calls is really defined. The handler list is scraped from `index.html` and `app.js` rather than written down, so a new handler is covered the day it is written instead of the day someone remembers this test.
- **Cache-buster v3 → v4** across all 11 spots, or PWA clients keep the broken bundle.

## Verification

Fails on the old code, passes on the new:

```
old: {"ok":false,"threw":"ReferenceError: syncToCRM is not defined","missing":[...]}
new: {"ok":true,"missing":[],"rejections":[]}
```

All six suites green on Python 3.12 (the version CI uses): salescrm 116, portal 145, estimator 1105, prospector 27, agents 264, canvasser 20 — **1,677 passed**.

> Note for anyone running locally: a default `python` of 3.11 fails `portal` and `estimator` before any test runs. `estimator/app.py:9185` uses a nested `'''` inside an f-string, which is PEP 701 syntax requiring 3.12. Unrelated to this change and reproduces on a clean tree.

## Not included

Everything else from the canvasser review — the GPS toggle that doesn't stop broadcasting, the 2,000-pin silent truncation, the all-time leaderboard, the doorstep `closed → won` mapping, Nominatim rate limits, offline pin saves — is deliberately out of scope here. This PR is the outage and the test that catches its whole class.

author: btcson66-rgb
body:
Full audit first, then consolidation only: **no new calculators, no new guides, no new languages, and no page deleted.** Sitemap goes 1,207 → 1,229 URLs — the 22 additions are the new directories and hubs, nothing was removed, so **no redirect is required.**

## The problem

The site had no layer between a 1,207-URL sitemap and a single calculator page. The homepage carried the whole catalogue: 15 `<h2>` sections and **304 internal links** on English, including `guideIndex[locale]` rendered in full — because that index was the only inbound link **131 editorial pages** had. Two consequences: the homepage's own topic was unreadable from the markup (its H1 was a keyword list, "Costco membership, annual-fee card, commute cost, and debt-to-income calculators"), and Google got no signal about which pages belong together.

## Four layers now

| Layer | Route | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| Homepage | `/`, `/{locale}/` | Hero, what the site is for, four decision clusters, ten calculators, links to both directories, six guides, method and limits, FAQ. Nine sections; nothing exhaustive. |
| Topic hub | `/{locale}/topics/{topic}/` | One decision area: its calculators, up to twelve guides, how to read the pages. **`en` + `zh` only** — `es`/`fr`/`de` are frozen for new routes per the README i18n policy, and get the same grouping as anchored sections of their own directories. |
| Directory | `/{locale}/tools/`, `/{locale}/guides/` | The complete catalogue, grouped by topic, all five core locales. Where the 131 homepage-only pages now get their inbound link. |
| Leaf | calculator and guide pages | A topic strip linking the page's hub, both directories, and any page sharing its slug at another URL prefix. |

Six topics: `housing`, `debt-credit`, `transportation`, `everyday`, `memberships`, `income-savings`. The first four are the clusters the homepage leads with. Assignment is **derived, not registered** — `classifyTopic()` runs ordered rules over hyphen-separated slug tokens plus an override table for the slugs that mislead them, so a new page needs no bookkeeping.

## Homepage reduction

`<main>` bytes, before → after:

| Locale | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| en | 67,506 | 16,541 | −75.5% |
| zh | 50,502 | 8,806 | −82.6% |
| es | 42,059 | 14,179 | −66.3% |
| fr | 19,590 | 14,553 | −25.7% |
| de | 19,176 | 14,378 | −25.0% |

English internal links 304 → 25; `<h2>` 15 → 8. `fr`/`de` shrink least because they *gained* the trust block they were missing.

## Stale numbers, fixed at the source

`/en/about/` said "we currently publish eight calculators" against eighteen served. The Spanish, French and German About pages each claimed eight calculators and 29 decision guides against 17 and ~196. `src/lib/catalog.ts` now counts the real catalogue at build time; `getLibraryCounts(locale)` is what a page calls when it needs a number, and the README says not to type one by hand again.

## Also in this change

- **Homepage keyword de-stuffing.** All five locales' titles and H1s state what the site is instead of stacking per-tool keywords. Single-calculator keywords stay on the calculator pages.
- **YMYL trust parity.** `es`/`fr`/`de` homepages gain the method / sources / limits block `en`/`zh` already had, citing the CNMV, AMF and BaFin pages already used on those locales' own legal pages. No source was invented.
- **Three calculators had no outbound guide link at all** (`ev-vs-gas`, `cost-per-mile`, `latte-factor`, en + zh). Fixed — every calculator page now links at least one guide.
- **A same-slug duplicate.** `/{locale}/gym-membership-cost-per-visit/` and `/{locale}/guides/gym-membership-cost-per-visit/` are the same slug, the same intent, and both indexable. They now link to each other automatically (the mechanism is generic, so a future collision is caught too). Deciding which URL should survive needs Search Console data — see below.
- **404 page** stops advertising `hreflang="x-default"` to `/en/404/`, a URL that has never existed.
- **`llms.txt`** leads with the six topic hubs and is generated from the same catalogue as the pages.

## Deliberately untouched

GA4 events, AdSense code, `ads.txt`, the affiliate components, permalink rules, and every existing slug. No new frontend dependency, no animation, no UI library — the calculator bundles are unchanged.

## Verification

`npm run verify` exits 0: build, `astro check` (0 errors), lint, growth tests, and 123 checks.

- `check:guide-index` — 1,152 editorial pages, **zero orphans**
- `check:links` — 33,043 internal links resolve, all page links end in a slash (no sitemap 404s, no redirect hops)
- `check:all-locales` — 347 logical routes, 969 localized pages, canonical / hreflang / sitemap coverage complete
- `check:shell`, `check:multilingual`, `check:growth-release`, `check:og-images` — pass
- Duplicate indexable titles/H1s: 1, and it is `/` vs `/en/` — the existing compatibility design (`/en/` canonicalizes to `/` and is excluded from the sitemap)
- hreflang pointing at a non-existent page: 1 → **0**; FAQPage schema without a visible FAQ: 0

## Not done, and why

These need GSC data this build does not have, and the first three need a redirect mechanism the host does not provide:

1. **The `gym-membership-cost-per-visit` pair.** Both URLs are pinned by existing check scripts; choosing a survivor needs their impression split.
2. **Four other overlapping-intent groups:** `annual-vs-monthly-billing` / `monthly-vs-annual-subscription`; `extended-warranty-math` / `is-an-extended-warranty-worth-it`; `average-commuting-cost` / `full-commute-cost-including-time`; `costco-math` / `is-costco-executive-membership-worth-it`.
3. **GitHub Pages cannot issue a 301.** Actually merging pages needs a decision first: a Cloudflare proxy layer, or the existing `deindexed-urls.json` soft-deindex mechanism (noindex,follow + out of sitemap + hreflang removal). That decision is the prerequisite, which is why nothing was merged here.
4. **Three en↔zh same-topic pairs use different slugs** (`loan-term`, `net-worth`, `savings-rate`). Their hreflang is currently correct but single-locale. Pairing them means changing both `resolveSeo()` and `check-all-localized-routes.mjs`, which assume hreflang always maps to the same path.
