body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - This PR changes the task-coordination service and its database contract.
> - The existing v1 presentation can turn missing evidence into positive-looking facts.
> - Issue #53 requires an additive, observation-only contract that fails closed.
> - This pull request adds persisted generation, a pinned schema, and a separate v2 route without changing v1.
> - The benefit is truthful coordination output that cannot act as unsupported authorization evidence.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Fixes #53
Refs #52
Refs #82

## Agent / Author

- Agent: OpenAI Codex
- Human reviewer: iMelki

## Scope

- Allowed files/directories: coordination loader/projector/routes, DB migration/schema, deterministic test selection, tracking, and evidence.
- Out-of-scope files/directories: v1 response behavior, control execution, delivery mutation, schedulers, factory pin/start, and preserved PR #45 WIP.

## What Changed

- Added migration `0213_coordination_generation.sql` and persisted positive `issues.coordination_generation`.
- Vendored the canonical Projects Ops `task-coordination.v2` schema and enforced its SHA-256 digest.
- Added presentation-only `GET /api/issues/:rootIssueId/coordination/v2` with empty controls and delivery.
- Kept process/output evidence false and confidence zero without independent persisted proof.
- Limited placements to board, assigned, or participating same-company agents.
- Added real HTTP isolation, projector, route, schema, and deterministic test-selection coverage.
- Recorded deliberate negative-proof failures and restored passes under `doc/evidence/coordination-v2/`.

## Verification

- Focused v2 projector: 5/5.
- Existing v1 projector: 31/31.
- Route tests: 8/8.
- Real DB/HTTP company isolation: 4/4.

- Real pre-push: pass, including full workspace typecheck and 12 exact suites.
- Negative-proof receipt: `doc/evidence/coordination-v2/2026-09-06-issue53-receipt.json`.

## Risks

- The migration adds one non-null column with a safe default and a positive-value check.
- The new route is additive and observation-only; v1 remains unchanged.
- Unknown, malformed, stale, future, or ownership-mismatched facts are represented as non-positive or rejected.
- Hosted CI and independent exact-head review remain required before merge.

## Model Used

- OpenAI Codex, GPT-5 (current desktop deployment; tool use, code execution, and medium reasoning).

body:
<!-- sms-operational-split -->
Implementation continues in **#4000 (private-profile capture)** and **#4016 (gated commitment follow-up and staff controls)**. This original draft preserves the fifth-round review history and remains unmerged; its outstanding fixes are carried in the split. Both new parts remain disabled while their final review and CI complete.

---

The SMS drafter can suggest actions, but customer requests and staff promises do not become durable operational work. This initial extension records grounded requests/promises, fills clear empty private-profile fields through a shared audited writer, and checks explicitly timed obligations against later outcomes before raising an existing admin notification linked directly to the customer profile.

It extends the existing SMS intake, extraction receipts, commitment ledger and watcher. SMS work does not enter Owed, Agent Ops, Triage or a new review queue. The existing reply/delivery policy is unchanged. Profile changes, critical audits, obligations and source receipts commit atomically; retries and owner edits are guarded. Estimate fulfillment reuses the call agent's actual delivery witnesses, and unavailable customers cannot block intake.

Activation requires `GATE_SMS_OPERATIONAL_ACTIONS=true` plus `GATE_SMS_OPERATIONAL_ACTIONS_SINCE` set to an explicit offset timestamp. Unsetting the gate revokes the lane. Historical discovery records are not imported. The migration preserves recorded evidence on rollback by refusing destructive removal after activation.

This remains a draft while owner decisions are pending on recurring-date changes, callback times, no-deadline response windows and family-property account relationships. Undated obligations are recorded without guessed due times. Automatic scheduling/cancellation, account changes, overwriting existing profile values, consent changes and money movement are outside this initial change. Report/paperwork delivery needs an exact artifact/recipient link before automatic closure; prose claims remain verification exceptions.

Still-open work uses the existing rolling 24-hour admin-bell dedupe window, so reading a bell cannot permanently hide an unfinished request. New profile rows preserve logical empty fields across fact batches while compare-and-set checks use actual stored defaults. Obligation descriptions are quoted phrases naming their typed deliverable. SMS/email answers need confirmed delivery; initial sent states and Gmail SENT labels are context only.

Validation: 230 focused local tests passed, with lint and domain checks clean. All 22 PostgreSQL cases passed in CI's isolated synthetic database, including merge/undo/race handling, post-request visits, profile-fact ordering, repeat reminders, retried emails, persisted evidence caching and archive/restore races. All seven [CI jobs](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/actions/runs/34015586759) passed on `57890eac6`; the Railway PR preview also succeeded. Local migrations and PostgreSQL tests were not run because no dedicated dev/preview database is configured. No customer communications, live customer updates, merge or gate activation were performed.

Access codes require an explicit quoted code type matching the selected profile field. Retried email delivery is selected by event timestamps. Fulfillment caches verdicts against the obligation, quoted evidence, current owner, model/contract and witness records; provider/schema failures retry after one hour. Archived accounts retain their obligations without processing or new bells until restoration, with an active-owner check under the write lock. This extends the existing SMS commitment context; no additional schema or queue is introduced.

The current and historical SMS prompt inputs use the existing PAN/CVV scrubber, including split readbacks; fulfillment prompt strings are scrubbed too, and detected payment data in model output is rejected before operational persistence. Controller-location values retain full sentence context. Negated or mixed action requests become review exceptions. Prior bell links follow merges across the rolling dedupe boundary. The original call watchdog again owns its independent 7:20 ET timer.

Review status: seventeen findings across the first four GitHub review rounds are fixed; one P2 is deferred below. Round five on `57890eac6` surfaced new P1s, so remediation stops at the repository's round cap. This draft is **not merge-ready** despite green CI.

## Open for Adam

- P1 — `server/services/sms-operational-extractor.js:140`: explicit date/clock wording can lose follow-up entirely when the model omits both timing fields. Detect timing from the source quote or raise a timing exception. [Finding](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/3970#discussion_r3943165021)
- P1 — `server/services/sms-commitment-fulfillment.js:106`: delivered automatic appointment confirmations are excluded by the human-message allowlist. Admit the specific confirmation witness for that obligation kind. [Finding](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/3970#discussion_r3943165022)
- P1 — `server/services/sms-commitment-fulfillment.js:57`: directly linked estimates omit commercial proposals associated through guarded lead ownership. Reuse the call lane's ownership resolution. [Finding](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/3970#discussion_r3943165024)
- P1 — `server/services/sms-commitment-fulfillment.js:26`: report/paperwork obligations have neither an admissible automatic witness nor an exposed human closure action, so verified completion cannot stop the daily bell. Add a closure path through the existing customer/bell workflow. [Finding](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/3970#discussion_r3943165025)

## Review history and proposed split

author: choiceoh
body:
## Summary

메일 첨부로 들어온 **이미지**를 비전 모델이 먼저 읽게 배선한다. 캡처 경로(`miniapp.capture.*`)는 #4100부터 이미지를 비전 체인(main → vision 롤)으로 이해해 왔는데, **추출기(`AttachmentExtractFn`)로 들어오는 메일 첨부는 곧장 PaddleOCR로 갔다.** 그래서 같은 사진 견적서가 챗에서는 읽히고 메일에서는 글자만 납작하게 나왔고, 의미가 글자가 아닌 첨부(현장 사진·도장 찍힌 도면·손글씨 메모)는 메일 경로에서 사실상 빈 결과였다.

폴백 방향은 **비전 → OCR 한 방향**이라, OCR이 실패해도 비전으로 올라가지 않는다는 구조가 이 구멍을 오래 보이지 않게 했다.

## Changes

- `chat.WithImageVision(extract)` — 추출기를 감싸 이미지면 비전 체인을 먼저 태우고, **비이미지 · 작은 이미지 · 비전 실패는 감싼 추출기로 흘려보낸다.** 그 추출기가 이미 이미지를 OCR하므로 이 변경은 이해를 더할 뿐 뺄 수 없다. 그래서 describer에 OCR 폴백을 넘기지 않는다 — 넘기면 같은 이미지를 두 번 읽는다.
- **40KB 바닥** (`visionAttachmentMinBytes`) — 메일은 무인·대량 유입이라 서명 로고·푸터 배너마다 프론티어 비전 호출이 붙으면 안 된다. 사진 찍은 견적서·스캔본은 수백 KB~수 MB이고 로고는 그 아래다. 바닥 아래 이미지도 **여전히 읽힌다** — 로컬 OCR이 읽을 뿐. 메일 게이트의 기존 2KB 트래커 픽셀 컷과 같은 발상의 한 단계 위.
- MIME이 `image/*`면 그것으로 판정하고, `application/octet-stream`으로 오는 발신자를 위해 파일명 확장자도 본다.
- 배선 3곳: 메일 분석 파이프라인(`method_registry_late.go`) + 폴링/프로액티브 mailanalysis 설정 2곳(`server_chat_config.go`).
- **관측 가능하게**: 비전이 실제로 읽으면 저널에 `attachment image described by vision file=… bytes=… chars=…` 한 줄. 이 경로는 성공하면 "메일 분석이 그냥 좋아지는" 형태라 로그가 없으면 판정이 불가능하다.
- `WithImageVision(nil)`은 nil을 유지한다 — mailanalysis는 nil을 "첨부 비활성"으로 읽으므로 감싸다가 켜버리면 안 된다(테스트로 고정).

## Verification

- `make ci/fast` — 9/9 PASS (109.9s). `make check` — All checks passed(Go 게이트 + python 61 tests).
- 신규 테이블 테스트 `TestWithImageVisionRoutesAttachments` — 6케이스: 큰 이미지→비전 · 비전 빈 응답→추출기 · 40KB 미만→비전 호출 안 함 · PDF→비전 호출 안 함 · octet-stream+`.JPEG`→비전 · 확장자 없는 octet-stream→추출기. `TestWithImageVisionKeepsNilExtractorNil`.
- `gofumpt -l` 무출력 · 라이브: `scripts/dev/live-test.sh restart && smoke` → `/health`·`/ready` OK, 로그 에러/경고 0.
- ⚠️ **메일 파이프라인 자체는 라이브로 돌리지 않았다** — 실제 `miniapp.mail.analyze`는 프로덕션 상태(분석 캐시·피드)에 쓰기가 발생하는 실행이라 검증 목적으로 트리거하지 않았다. 라우팅은 유닛 테스트로, 배선은 컴파일과 기동으로 덮었고, 실제 첫 발화는 위 저널 한 줄로 확인된다.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds frontier vision calls on qualifying mail attachments (cost/latency) and changes attachment text fed into mail analysis; fallbacks preserve prior OCR behavior when vision is skipped or fails.
> 
> **Overview**
> Mail and related **attachment extractors** now try the same vision chain used for capture-path images before falling back to the existing `ExtractAttachmentText` OCR path, so photos, drawings, and non-glyph images are described instead of coming back nearly empty.
> 
> **`chat.WithImageVision`** wraps the extractor: large enough image attachments (≥ **40KB**, MIME `image/*` or common extensions including octet-stream by filename) call `describeCapturedImage` with **no inline OCR** so the wrapper’s extractor remains the single fallback; smaller images, non-images, empty vision results, and nil extractors behave as before. Successful vision reads log **`attachment image described by vision`** for observability.
> 
> Wiring updates **`AttachmentExtractFn`** in interactive mail analyze, Gmail poll, and LMTP mail-analysis configs. Table tests cover routing, size/MIME gates, and nil-preservation.
>

author: leshchenko1979
body:
**Stacked on #1415 + #1416** (md-plane foundation + md-plane pick redraw — carries both until they merge).

## What

The markdown-plane merge and pick redraws re-sent the host body as raw markdown. When that body contained a mermaid fence, the edit **replaced the rendered diagram with raw fence text** — a successfully delivered diagram died the moment a keyboard merged onto it or a pick redrew the bubble.

This PR ports the send path's own proven mechanism to edits: fences are resolved **once at payload build** into a `media` array (`resolve_markdown_media`, the same helper `sendRichMessage` uses), and the edit carries `rich_message: { markdown, media }`. Tables stay native; diagrams re-render server-side; the keyboard lands.

## Details

- `edit_rich_markdown_media` + body builder in `rich/api.rs`: same wire convention as the send path — byte media entries upload via `attach://` multipart, url entries ride server-side.
- **`multipart_scalar_fields` carries `message_id`** — required by #1414; without that part the server rejects every media-bearing edit with `400 message to edit not found` (live-probe evidence in #1414).
- `edit_rich_md_fencesafe` chokepoint: no fence → byte-identical plain edit (zero HTTP overhead); fence → resolve once, media edit. **429 propagates with no fallback** (retry re-sends byte-identical content); any other rejection → warn + plain markdown edit so the keyboard always lands.
- All four redraw sites ride the chokepoint: keyboard merge, tap pick redraw, shared redraw helper, stale-shell strip.
- Body-shape tests (message_id, media array, `attach://` refs, no-key null check) + mockito JSON-path edit test.

Port of leshchenko1979/opencrabs#98 (owner-verified on our fork: diagram + buttons merged onto one message, tap redraw kept both, image survived both edits).

Original issue: https://github.com/leshchenko1979/opencrabs/issues/98

새 테스트 9건 전부 통과, 콘솔 오류 0건:

- 카드마다 체크가 있고 기본은 꺼짐

- 완료함에서 다시 체크하면 목록으로 복귀
- 모두 지우기(확인창 포함)
- 새로고침 후에도 완료 상태 유지
- 완료해도 캘린더에는 남음

## 함께 고친 것 — 날짜에 의존하던 테스트

기간 막대 검사도 첫 조각만 보던 것을 **모든 조각**으로 넓혔습니다. 주 경계에서 나뉘어도 정확히 검사합니다.

기존 107건도 전부 통과합니다.

author: tjworks
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #240 — the execution issue for this line. The design is written up in a private repository; the user-facing contract it decided is `docs/first-run/README.md` on this branch, and every step below is held to that page.

## Live verification scenario

A person who has not worked on this line, on a clean non-development machine with Docker installed, with only the published first-run page: install the CLI from the root URL, run `tapstate new`, accept the default server (the local development stack starts), pick "Mirror one table, as it changes" against a MySQL they have, run `tapstate up`, and then say where the workspace is and what they can do next without reading YAML. The scenario needs the published CLI and the republished install site, so it runs after this merges and is recorded on #240; it is not a CI assertion.

## What changed

A new user can go from a clean machine to a running pipeline without reading resource YAML or sequencing apply / discover / apply / start by hand.

- `tapstate new` (bare, or `new <recipe>`) is the guided entry: it says it is building a workspace, asks which Tapstate server to use (the default `http://127.0.0.1:8080` starts a pinned local development stack in Docker when nothing is listening — `mongo` + `server` + `bootstrap`, no sample data, the published connectors pre-registered, admin created and signed in; a typed URL asks to sign in), then asks what the workspace is for from a six-entry catalog (`sample`, `mirrored-table`, `reshaped-table`, `nested-json`, `consolidated-table`, `blank`), asks only that recipe's questions, and writes an ordinary workspace. Secrets are never written into the files: `${NAME}` references plus a `.env` and a `.gitignore`. `new --list [-o json]` prints the catalog; `--yes` with flags is deterministic and never starts containers without `--start-local`. `new --kind …` and `tapstate demo` are unchanged (`demo` writes byte-identical files to `new sample --yes`).
- `tapstate up` brings the bound workspace to running through the same calls the individual verbs use: preflight (server, version, connectors registered, every source reachable, workspace readable with a pipeline), apply sources, discover schema per source, apply the rest, start — stopping at the first failing stage with a coded diagnostic naming the stage and the next action. Running it again converges (`State: running (nothing to do)`). `.env` is read before the process environment. The reserved `run` placeholder is gone; `up` is the composite verb.
- Both commands end with the same summary shape: the files and what each is for (`ls`'s wording), the state, the next commands, and one line that an AI assistant can take it from here.
- Install site: `/` now installs the CLI only, `/demo` is the full demo, `/cli` stays as an alias. README, `docs/README.md`, `docs/quickstart-online.md` and `docs/demo.md` point readers accordingly; the demo walkthrough printed by `tapstate demo --print-steps` names `/demo`.
- Three new error codes, each with catalog text and a golden line: `cli.docker-unavailable`, `cli.workspace-unreadable`, `cli.workspace-has-no-pipeline`.
- Two architecture gates in `arch-tests`: `up` reaches the control plane only through `Repl`'s shared cores, and the guided path reaches saved servers and sign-ins only through `ContextManager` / `ContextResolver` / `AuthService` (`FirstRunAuthorityRulesTest`); and the first-run wording gates (`FirstRunWordingGatesTest`: "Tapstate server" never "context" on this surface, the entry modes do not impersonate each other, the demo is never sold as a one-command installer).

## End-to-end case

`e2e/src/test/java/io/tapstate/e2e/GuidedFirstRunIT.java` — written and run locally against an in-process server, a real MySQL and the real connector jar: `new mirrored-table --yes …` writes the workspace and `up` (no credentials on the line) reaches preflight through the saved session, and then fails on #247 — the bundled catalog types `port` as `string`, so every generated workspace is refused by the connector's Number cast. That defect predates this branch (`new --kind source --set port=…` fails the same way on `main`); this is the first end-to-end test to run into it. **The IT is not on this branch yet**: a red test is not committed. It lands once #247 is fixed, with no change to the test itself. The specification vocabulary cannot express it: there is no word for invoking the CLI or reading what a process returned, so it is Java, as the admission rule provides for.

Until then the change is covered by module tests: `cli` 1141 tests green (goldens for every recipe's files and both summaries, `UpCmdTest` for every stage and the converged run, `LocalStackTest` for the stack), `arch-tests` 74 green including the two new gates, install-site `verify-smoke.sh` 9/9.

## Documentation impact

- [x] This change needs documentation follow-up (add the `docs-needed` label)
- **Draft in this repository:** docs/first-run/README.md
- **Public page it is headed for:** https://tapstate.dev/docs/first-run

## Checks

- [ ] `mvn verify` is green locally — `cli` and `arch-tests` are green offline; the `e2e` module's new IT is red on #247 and therefore not committed; `ARestartedServerKeepsCarryingIT` failed once on CI for a timing reason unrelated to this branch (#246).
- [ ] An end-to-end case covers this change, and is named above — named, blocked by #247.
- [x] New or changed e2e assertions carry mutation evidence: the mutation applied,
      the red observed, and that only it went red — every new gate was planted red once and reverted (assertion lines are in the commit-by-commit record on #240).

### Release note

**Kind:** new

As a new user, I can install the CLI, pick what I want from a short catalog in `tapstate new` -- which writes a readable workspace without reaching a server, so it works with none in existence -- and then run `tapstate up`, which asks which server to bring it up against and takes it all the way to running, so that I never have to read resource YAML or sequence apply, discover, apply and start by hand before the first result.

Two changes to released behaviour ship with it, both called out for the notes: bare `tapstate new` now enters the starter-outcome picker instead of the single-resource wizard (`new --kind <kind>` is unchanged), and `--server`, `--user` and `--start-local` moved from `new` to `up` along with everything that reaches a server.

---

**Issues filed while working this line** -- a live query, so it includes
any filed after this body was written:
https://github.com/tapstate/tapstate/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+%22Refs+%23240%22

One a maintainer accepts is labelled `known-issue`: shipped with knowingly,
to be improved later. The rest want a decision before this line closes out.

Merging this does not close the execution issue for `beta-guided-first-run`. That happens at
the closeout, once **every** repository this workstream declares has merged.

**Maintainer: run the closeout for `beta-guided-first-run` after merging.** Whoever merges owes
the closeout, because it is work in a repository the author may not have.

author: aletuan
body:
## What

Expo Go on iOS ships one SDK at a time and cannot install an older one. It moved to 57, and the app pinned to 54 now opens to "Project is incompatible with this version of Expo Go". This moves the project to SDK 57 so the published EAS Update lands on the runtime Expo Go is asking for (`runtimeVersion` follows the SDK by policy, so no other change is needed there).

## How

- `app/package.json` / `package-lock.json` — every package moved to the version SDK 57 bundles, via `expo install`: react-native 0.81 → 0.86, react and react-dom 19.1 → 19.2 (kept on one version, per the white-screen note in `checks.yml`), all `expo-*` modules to their 57.x lines, `eslint-config-expo` 10 → 57, `@types/react` to 19.2.
- `app/app.json` — `expo install` added the config plugins SDK 57 lists for datetimepicker, font, image, sharing and status-bar.
- `StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject` → `StyleSheet.absoluteFill` in 14 files: React Native 0.86 removed the former, and the latter is now the same plain object.
- `app/eslint.config.js` — `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 7 turns on the React Compiler rules. The app does not run the compiler, and the existing tree produced 192 findings under them (164 `react-hooks/refs`, all the deliberate read-a-ref-during-render idiom). The four rules that fire are off with the reason written beside them; `rules-of-hooks` and `exhaustive-deps` stay on.
- `app/README.md` — the "why SDK 54" note becomes a "why SDK 57" note with the upgrade steps for next time.

## Checks

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `eslint . --max-warnings=0` clean
- `vitest run --coverage`: 94 files, 1718 tests, 100% coverage
- `expo export --platform all` bundles iOS and Android (run offline; `expo install --check` needs the Expo API, which CI has)

## Not done here

The 192 React Compiler findings are left as-is rather than refactored, since the compiler is not enabled and the patterns are intentional. If the compiler is ever switched on, the rules come back with it.

body:
## Summary
The dependabot dev-dependencies group update (#245) fails at the typecheck step because TypeScript 7 removed two options this config used:

```
types/tests/tsconfig.json(8,5): error TS5102: Option 'baseUrl' has been removed.
types/tests/tsconfig.json(12,25): error TS5108: Option 'moduleResolution=node10' has been removed.
```

- Removed `baseUrl`. It served no purpose here — every import in `types/tests/` is either a bare package specifier resolved through `node_modules` (`chart.js`, `@kurkle/color`) or a relative `include` path, neither of which depends on `baseUrl`. No `paths` mapping was needed to replace it.
- Changed `moduleResolution` from `"Node"` (the removed `node10` alias) to `"Bundler"`, matching what `chartjs-chart-matrix`, `chartjs-chart-sankey`, and `chartjs-chart-treemap` already use for their equivalent type-test configs.

Unlike the other kurkle repos that block on TypeScript 7 for other reasons (typedoc, `@astrojs/check`), this repo has no such blocker, so this is a real fix rather than a workaround.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes with the pinned TypeScript (5.9.3, current lockfile)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes with TypeScript 7.0.2 (the dependabot group's target), installed temporarily with `npm install --no-save` and reverted with `npm ci` before committing — lockfile is unchanged

author: allenfbyrd
body:
## Summary

Batch 3 of the v0.13 cycle: the correctness debt surfaced by the 2026-09-06 stateful DAST run, the FedRAMP upstream re-sync, and the disclosure follow-through.

1. **Published schema and runtime agree on non-blank strings.** `NonBlankStr` in `evidentia_core.models.common` carries `minLength: 1` plus the full Python whitespace class. Every stripping core model uses it, and the six plain request payloads that carried a bare `minLength: 1` now reject whitespace-only values with the standard 422 instead of failing later inside a core model. The ai-gov register, update and acquisition requests keep their documented 400 `invalid_body` and publish the same pattern as documentation only. A regression gate (`tests/unit/test_openapi_non_blank_gate.py`) fails if a new `minLength: 1` string ships without the pattern. `openapi.json` and the generated TypeScript types are regenerated (17 properties gain a pattern; no type changes).
2. **Stateful DAST harness isolation.** Each Hypothesis example starts with fresh registry and catalog stores. State left behind by earlier examples changed which link-derived rules were available when Hypothesis replayed a sequence while shrinking, which surfaced as `FlakyStrategyDefinition` in CI run 34004542188. Two local runs pass after the change.
3. **FedRAMP CR26 pins re-verified.** Closes #275. The vendored `common-definitions` (0.3.0) and `security-decision-record` (1.1.1) schemas are byte-identical to `FedRAMP/schemas@c3ed146` again (blob SHAs verified), `UPSTREAM.json` carries the new pins, and the SDR emitter writes `metadata.updateSource`, the key schema 1.1.0 now requires (the status file's operator-facing field is still `source`). `FedRAMP/rules` did not move, so the KSI and FRR catalogs are unchanged. The live drift sentinel reports the new pins match.
4. **Disclosure follow-through.** `docs/ai-assistance.md` links the organisation policy at polycentriclabs.com/ai-policy and its GitHub mirror; the CHANGELOG's Unreleased section records the batch.
5. **Design draft for V13-01 and V13-05** at `docs/designs/cadence-assertion-layer-design.md`, for design review: day-granular cadences, a `CadenceSeries` assertion over the evidence store, one new `conmon series` leaf, and Nessus and Greenbone file ingest as the first consumer.

## Checks

Ruff, mypy (all seven packages), the full pytest suite, docs health (strict), version consistency, doc counts, parity, public surface and the wiki mirror sync pass locally; the 17-check pre-push gate passed on push.

author: fedormilovanov
reel
body:
Two of the seven issues left open since 2018 and 2019, closed with code rather than with a comment.

## #40, from 2018: suggest a renderer that is installed but not configured

`config.renderer` defaults to handlebars. That is right for an application with no view engine, and confusing for one that installed `@usehenri/inertia`, wrote pages and wonders why they are not the ones being rendered. Nothing fails, so nothing said anything.

```text
  view ✏  @usehenri/inertia is installed but "renderer" is not set, so pages are rendered with handlebars => add "renderer": "inertia" to your configuration
```

Only when the key is absent. An explicit `"renderer": "template"` is a decision and is left alone. The suggestion lives in `base/renderer.js` so it can be tested on its own, and one of its tests asserts every renderer it can suggest is one the view module accepts, which is how this goes wrong a year from now.

## #65, from 2019: "failed to deserialized user on logout"

The report has no body and the user module has been rewritten since. Rather than close it as stale, this pins the behaviour it was about: the deserializer answers `done(null, false)` for a row that is no longer there, so a session whose user was deleted reads as anonymous rather than as an error, and signing out of it works. The test creates the account, signs in, deletes the row and then asks for a page and signs out.

## Verification

`pnpm test`, `pnpm lint --max-warnings 0`, `pnpm format:check`, and `scripts/smoke.sh` on a scaffolded application.

Closes #40. Closes #65.

author: otchealth-fleet-bot[bot]
body:
Closes a real gap the auto critic flagged on #556, which I merged before reading because that check is **report-only** and therefore reported `success` while its verdict was `revise`. Worth recording as its own lesson: a report-only check that says success is indistinguishable from a check that found nothing.

## The gap

The fourth case in `tests/installed-skill-shared-modules.test.mjs` asserts that shared setup modules only reach into `setup/` or `skills/`, so that installing two directories stays sufficient. It scanned only static `from "..."` specifiers.

That means a module could acquire a dependency on a third sibling directory through a dynamic `import(...)` or an `export ... from` re-export, and the test would keep passing while the installed layout broke. The test was more confident than its own method.

**Not hypothetical.** `setup/drift-recon.mjs` and `setup/image-drift.mjs` already use `await import("../skills/kb-memory/azure-secret.mjs")` today, and the original scanner could not see either of them.

## The change

Both scanners in the file now share one specifier extractor covering from-specifiers, dynamic `import()`, and `require()`. Template literals are included, since a static prefix before any `${` is still a real path, which `setup/model-routing.test.mjs` relies on.

## Proof

Injected a third-sibling dynamic import into `drift-recon.mjs`:

```
=== BROADENED test ===
not ok 4 - the shared setup modules only reach back into setup/ or skills/
    drift-recon.mjs -> ../vendor/azure-secret.mjs

=== OLD (static-only) scanner, same injection ===
old scanner offenders: [] -> would have PASSED
```

Restored, 4 pass / 0 fail. Full gate: `run-tests.sh` **ALL GREEN (231 test targets)**.

author: henryvn2004-arch
body:
Đợt 3 track visual, tool thứ hai: **Số Đẹp**. Hai việc: một cái vành, và một lỗi đo được ở chỉ số đồng thuận — **Henry đã duyệt luật thay thế nên đã sửa luôn** (mục 2).

## 1. Vành ngũ hành

Dựng trong `ketQuaHTML` của module dùng chung `tools-shared/so-dep.js` → một nguồn, không chép sang trang.

Tầng T3 trước giờ chỉ có một hàng chữ `Kim 2 · Mộc 3 · Thủy 0 · Hỏa 1 · Thổ 2`. Hàng chữ đó nói đúng **con số** nhưng không nói được **dáng**: dãy nghiêng hành nào, hụt hành nào. Vành nói đúng phần đó — hành thiếu tụt về tâm thành một vết lõm nhìn phát thấy. Giữ nguyên hàng chữ: hình chở DÁNG, chữ chở SỐ.

**⚠️ Thang chuẩn hoá theo CHÍNH dãy** (max = hành nhiều chữ số nhất), không theo độ dài dãy. Đây là dữ liệu **thành phần**: 9 chữ số chia 5 hành nên hành trội thường chỉ 3 — đo 500 dãy: `p10=2 · median=3 · p90=5 · max=7`. Lấy độ dài (10) làm trần thì dãy nào cũng co lại còn ~1/3 vành, hết đọc được hình.

**Cố ý không nạp `hook-charts.js` ở `/tools/so-dep.html`.** Trang standalone đó dùng `tools.css`, thiếu `--line-2` / `--sans` / `--gold-soft`. Biến hụt thì `stroke:var(--line-2)` rơi về `none` (mất sạch lưới) và nhãn rớt về font mặc định — **hỏng im lặng, không lỗi nào bắn ra**. `_vanhNguHanhHTML` tự trả rỗng khi không có `HookCharts`, nên trang đó giữ nguyên như cũ.

## 2. 🔴 T3 gần như luôn bỏ phiếu "tốt" — đã sửa

Luật cũ ở cuối `tinhNguHanh()`:

```js
out.verdict = hopMenh.length > 0 ? 'tot' : 'trung';
```

`hopMenh` chỉ cần dãy **chứa ít nhất MỘT chữ số** thuộc hành nạp âm hoặc hành cung phi. Với 9-10 chữ số rải trên 5 hành thì điều đó gần như chắc chắn xảy ra. Nhánh `'xau'` **không tồn tại trong biểu thức**.

Đo 500 số ngẫu nhiên (PRNG deterministic):

| tầng | phân bố verdict |
|---|---|
| T1 Bát Tinh | xấu 193 · tốt 183 · trung 122 — cân |
| T2 Quẻ Dịch | xấu 157 · tốt 201 · trung 142 — cân |
| **T3 Ngũ Hành** | **xấu 0 · tốt 484 · trung 16** |

T3 chiếm **1/3 phiếu đồng thuận** — dòng chữ to nhất màn hình — nên tool bị kê thêm một phiếu "tốt" gần như miễn phí: `0/3 nói tốt` chỉ ra **4/500 lần (0,8%)**. `0888888888` (thiếu 4/5 hành) vẫn hiện **"3/3 trường phái cổ pháp nói tốt"**.

Đây đúng loại lỗi im lặng và luôn nghiêng về phía thổi phồng — và nó cãi lại chính cam kết mà header `so-dep.js` tự viết ra: *"hiện điểm RIÊNG từng trường phái + chỉ số ĐỒNG THUẬN … không có điểm tổng giả khoa học"*.

### Luật mới

Xét **tỉ trọng** chứ không xét **sự có mặt**: hành nào chiếm nhiều chữ số nhất mới là hành dãy này mang, rồi so sinh/khắc với hành nạp âm bản mệnh.

- trội **khắc** bản mệnh → `xấu`
- trội **đồng hành** hoặc **sinh** bản mệnh → `tốt`
- còn lại → `trung`
- **hoà** (từ 2 hành cùng đỉnh, 27% số dãy) → `trung` — không có hành trội thì không kết luận, **không bốc đại một hành**

Cùng 500 số đó, sau khi sửa:

| | tốt | trung | xấu |
|---|---|---|---|
| luật cũ | 484 | 16 | **0** |
| luật mới | 151 | 279 | **70** |

Đồng thuận `3/3` rơi **14,4% → 4,4%**; `0/3` lên **0,8% → 25,8%**. **T1/T2 không đổi một số nào** — đúng như mong, luật này chỉ đụng T3.

**Đối chứng độc lập:** script đo tự tính lại verdict từ `phanBo` bằng bảng ngũ hành gõ riêng trong chính nó, **không gọi hàm vừa sửa** — 500/500 khớp, 0 lệch. (Đo hai đường rồi so, chứ không hỏi hàm "mày có đúng không".)

### Hai chi tiết đáng nói

**`NapAmTool` được thêm trường `hanhMe`.** Quan hệ sinh/khắc lấy từ `NapAmTool.ungDung()` — bảng DUY NHẤT trong repo, không chép bản thứ hai. Nhưng trường sẵn có `hanhHop` là **chuỗi để HIỆN** (`'Mộc · Hỏa'`); bóc nó bằng `.split(' · ')` là lấy chuỗi hiển thị làm API — đổi câu chữ một phát là hỏng im lặng. Nên thêm `hanhMe` (trần, chỉ tên hành). Additive, consumer cũ không đụng gì.

**UI nói RA vì sao tầng này bỏ phiếu như vậy:** *"Hành trội của dãy là **Thổ** — khắc bản mệnh (Thủy). Phiếu của tầng này tính theo hành trội."* Nếu không nói thì người đọc thấy phiếu đổi mà không biết vì đâu.

Và câu ngay trên đổi *"Dãy số có chứa hành hợp mệnh"* → *"Trong dãy có mặt hành hợp mệnh"*. Câu đó nói về **sự có mặt**, đứng cạnh dòng *"hành trội — khắc bản mệnh (Thủy)"* mà vẫn giữ chữ "hợp mệnh" thì hai câu đọc ra như cãi nhau (cả hai đều đúng: dãy có 1 chữ số Thủy, nhưng Thổ mới trội). Chỉ thấy được lỗi này bằng cách dựng ảnh ra rồi đọc như người dùng đọc.

## Đã chạy

- Dựng ảnh thật trong Chromium, **light + dark**, ba dãy chọn cho **đủ ba nhánh verdict** (khắc mệnh · đồng hành · sinh mệnh — chọn theo nhánh, không phải chọn cho đẹp): câu giải thích đúng nội dung, màu phân giải đúng ở cả hai theme (đỏ `192,57,43` sáng / `240,138,122` tối), **0 ngoại lệ JS**
- Vành: 5 trục đúng nhãn tiếng Việt, **0 nhãn tràn khỏi hộp SVG** (`getBoundingClientRect`), `--line-2` phân giải được ở cả hai theme
- Trường hợp biên `0888888888` (chỉ một hành) ra đa giác suy biến — một đường từ tâm ra Thổ. Vẫn đọc được, nhưng mảnh. Muốn chắc hơn thì thêm chấm ở đỉnh trục — sửa đó nằm trong `hexRadar` dùng chung, ảnh hưởng cả vành 12 cung lẫn vành 8 chiều, nên không gộp vào đây.
- Bump `nap-am.js?v=2 → v=3` ở cả 4 trang nạp nó; `so-dep.js?v=1 → v=2` ở cả 2 trang
- `check:hooktag` (cả luật 2 về `?v=`) · `check:shellboot` · prettier · eslint (0 error; 2 warning ở `so-dep.js` có sẵn từ trước, không phải của diff này)

## Chưa có trong PR này

- Hai tool free còn lại: Bát Trạch (bảng tra, không hợp radar) · Kim Lâu (nhị phân)
- Ba câu vẫn để ngỏ: ô lưới 12 tháng có nền màu nhạt không · lá số B engine chấm phẳng · chỗ đặt nút tải ảnh 9:16 cho Tương Hợp

author: hathawayandrx105
body:
## 背景
PR #13 修完 OCR 的 33 findings 里成立的部分后，剩下一批被归类为「死代码 / 未使用变量」的编译警告（19 条）。逐条查证时，**从中挖出两个功能性缺陷** —— 这批警告不是噪音，是缺陷的外在症状。

## 真 Bug

### 1. popup 候选窗的 buffer 与 mmap 指向两块不同内存
`new_popup` 调用了两个 helper：
- `ensure_buffer_static` — 建 memfd A，mmap 后**丢弃指针**（整块映射泄漏），用 A 建 `wl_buffer`
- `ensure_mmap_static` — 另建 memfd B，返回 B 的指针

结果：`show()` 里 render 写进 B，合成器从 A 读 —— **popup 路径候选窗必然空白**。`show()` 里的 `ensure_buffer` 因 `buffer.is_some()` 早退，也不会纠正。

`new_popup` 是 `Activate` 事件的主路径（`main.rs:129`），每次激活输入法都走。

**修复**：把实例方法 `ensure_buffer` 的正确实现抽为 `create_buffer(shm, qh, w, h) -> (WlBuffer, (fd, ptr, size))`，两条路径共用，buffer 与 mmap 保证同源；`ftruncate`/`mmap` 失败时关闭 fd。删掉两个破损 helper。

### 2. 边框颜色字节序错位
`draw_border` 按 `0xAARRGGBB` 解包，调用点传 `0x4C566AFFu32`（即 `RRGGBBAA` 排布）。实际画出的是 `(0x56, 0x6A, 0xFF)` 亮蓝，而非 PR #9 设计的 `#4C566A` 灰蓝。

**修复**：调用点改 `0xFF4C566A`，并在 `draw_border` 文档注明约定。新测试断言四边中点精确等于 `#4C566A`。

## 顺带发现：PR #9 的核心交付从未接入生产
`draw_candidates_compact` 是 #9 的主要产物（紧凑布局 + 高对比边框），但 `window.rs:299` 生产路径一直调旧的 `draw_candidates` —— `_compact` 只被自己的两个单测调用。

对比两者：90% 代码相同，唯一实质差异是 `_compact` 用**全透明背景**，而 `draw_candidates` 有不透明深色底 `0x1E1E26E8`。透明背景让文字直接叠在桌面上，可读性更差 —— 生产在用的那个才是对的。`_compact` 声称的边框改进 `draw_candidates` 也有。

**决定**：删 `_compact`，保留 `draw_candidates`。原两个测试改为对生产路径断言。

其中 `test_renderer_highlight_border` 是假测试：它检查第 1 行像素是否等于高亮色，但第 1 行就是边框，断言与函数名（验证高亮项）无关。改为真断言四边边框色。

## 清理（均确认无调用点或语义等价）
| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `render.rs` | 删死函数 `update_metrics`（算完 `required_h` 就丢弃，全参数带 `_`） |
| `builder.rs` | 删调试残留 `tables` 查询 —— 含 4 个 `unwrap()`，词库损坏会 panic |
| `window.rs` | 删冗余 `conn` 字段（`EventQueue` 已持连接，`main` 中 `conn` 活到进程退出） |
| `store.rs` | `increment_prefix` 去掉多余 `clone`；`FstStore::open` 补错误上下文 + **新增 `fst_len` 越界校验**（损坏 dict.bin 此前直接 panic 在切片） |
| `bin/kime` | 删未使用的 `KEY_SPACE` 常量、`Path` 导入；收敛多余 `args` 中间绑定 |
| Dispatch 空实现 | `state`/`conn` 参数加下划线（trait 必需签名，不可删） |

## 验证
- `cargo build --workspace`：**19 warnings → 0**
- 92 测试全绿（kime-core 54+11 / kime-pinyin 9 / kime-shuangpin 12 / platform-wayland 4+2）
- 新增 `crates/platform-wayland/tests/buffer_identity.rs`：断言同 memfd 的 mmap 写入可从 fd 读回，并反向锁定「两个独立 memfd 不共享像素」这一修复前形态
- 新增 `test_renderer_draws_border_around_candidates`：**该测试首次运行即失败**，抓出上述颜色错位
- CRG risk 0.40，0 affected flows

author: drewstone
body:
Learning could reuse results after an experiment changed, accept malformed observations, and lose the errors needed for later learning.
This change binds results to exact inputs and preserves failures through code improvement, persistent lessons, and Knowledge research.

- Bind strategy checkpoints to profiles, tasks, settings, external execution identity, and authored source bytes.
- Create reflective proposal sources from the active checkout, signal, and cost account; reject invalid or partial patch batches.
- Preserve Git status columns, validate observations, expose storage failures, and serialize immutable Corpus writes across processes.
- Run the supplied Knowledge profile unchanged and align with released Eval 0.174.0 and Knowledge 14.0.0.
- Replace obsolete transfer-only architecture verdicts with separate specialist, domain-learning, evaluation-quality, and meta-learning claims.

Runtime 0.195.0 requires `checkpoint.executionRef` for strategy resume and `createImprovementProposalSource(context)` for reflective generators.
Bench 0.8.32 carries the matching dependency ranges.
The existing methods and package boundaries remain; this repair does not introduce another learning API or establish a capability gain.

Validation:

- Prior full Runtime integration: 3,561 passed, nine skipped on Node 24.11.1 with four workers.
  Later main integrations change instructions and skills only.
- Fresh typechecks, 701-file lint, package export/install/edge execution checks, version checks, release workflow checks, and documentation freshness passed.
- Clean exact-archive check passed 128 public imports and measured proposal creation with Sandbox 0.36.4 and 0.37.0.
- PrimeIntellect package integration passed.
- Built public-package smoke: eight malformed observations rejected, a valid empty response accepted, persistence failures retained, immutable Corpus values, and two exact Knowledge profiles preserved.
- Eval [PR 738](https://github.com/tangle-network/agent-eval/pull/738) and Knowledge [PR 190](https://github.com/tangle-network/agent-knowledge/pull/190) are merged and published.

The [learning audit](docs/research/learning-system-audit-2026-09-05.md) and retained findings distinguish implementation proof from unmeasured domain-learning and meta-learning claims.

Adds the original 1.08-second “Pocket Victory” completion cue, reproducible synthesis source and provenance, and native WAV resources for iOS and Android. The shared one-shot adapter coalesces repeated callbacks and uses ordinary OS notification sound delivery without permission prompts, volume overrides, loops, or DND bypass.

The session/notification coordinator owns durable completion intent, scheduling, and relaunch deduplication; the documented adapter contract prevents foreground and scheduled paths from both playing a completion. Synthetic screens remain inert.

Validation: native audio checks passed before main integration. Integrated head a5d160e7dfd761f11e247b6c7c45f87be0ded984 passes 44 tests and analysis locally; [integrated CI](https://github.com/vanzeph/minutrove/actions/runs/34015121424) verifies the same head. Includes deterministic PCM verification, Flutter format/analysis and 44 tests, Android debug APK and iOS simulator builds, and 2 native tests on each platform verifying packaged audio decode, one playback completion, and normal notification configuration. Android 10 emulator; iOS 18.5 simulator / Xcode 16.4. Exact WAV preview and license details are in assets/audio/README.md. These tests do not certify physical-device audibility or Focus behavior; that remains native acceptance work. No binaries are publicly uploaded.

author: sj0618
body:
## 문제
실서버(job_d4267b1043a5 / trace a5b5bb219863d8db)에서 "RSI(14) 30 이하 매수, 70 이상 매도" 요청의 첫 리서치 응답은 `rsi lte 30 / rsi gte 70`으로 컴파일 가능했지만 규칙 밖의 사유(산문 길이)로 거절됐고, repair 턴이 같은 규칙에 `window=14, aggregate="last"`를 덧붙여 실행 불가 → need_clarification으로 끝났다. #116의 산문 클램프는 이 사례를 막았지만 출처 부족·반증조건 누락 등 다른 사유로 repair가 돌 때 모델이 규칙을 바꾸는 문제는 남아 있었다.

## 변경
- `strategy_research.py`: repair 응답의 전략 필드(entry/exit 조건, holding/rebalance 일수, required_metrics, backtest_years, sector)가 첫 응답과 다르면 **첫 응답의 규칙 + repair 응답의 근거·산문**으로 먼저 봉인한다. 그 조합도 실행 불가(첫 규칙 자체가 결함)일 때만 종전대로 repair 응답을 단독 판정. 조건 `description` 차이는 규칙 변경으로 보지 않음.
- repair 프롬프트에 "지적된 필드만 고치고 규칙 조건·기간은 그대로, window/aggregate 등을 덧붙이지 말라" 지시 추가.
- 컴파일러 `aggregate="last"`는 손대지 않음: 두 평가기(`condition_compiler._series_value`, `PreparedFeatureStore._rolling_metric`) 모두 "직전 봉 값"(lookback) 의미라 no-op으로 바꾸면 기존 의미가 바뀐다. 별도 결정 사항으로 보고.

## 검증

author: adarshyadav428
body:
Stacked on #82 — base is `ci/run-five-gates`, so review that one first. GitHub will retarget this to `main` automatically when #82 merges.

## Why

`docs/refactor-safety-contract.md` claims that a change confined to `components/` and page JSX **cannot** alter what gets stored or computed. The claim is true. It was also only *prose*: the contract asked a reader to re-run two greps by hand, and the call-site count in it went stale twice while the invariant never actually broke — which is worse than a wrong number, because it invites the conclusion that the rule lapsed.

This is the layer that makes UI changes safe by construction. It should fail a test, not require a careful reader.

## The four invariants

`tests/architectureInvariants.test.ts`:

1. **No DB writes in `components/`/`hooks/`.** Excludes `URLSearchParams.delete()` by matching the *receiver*, not by filtering the word `searchParams` out of the file — so a real `.delete(` in a file that also touches query params is still caught. Also asserts `app/api` still holds >30 writers, so the check can never pass because the walk silently found nothing.
2. **No direct Supabase table reads** outside two documented exemptions (`useUser`, `useSubscription` — both own-row, neither tier-gated), and those two must still read what the allowlist claims.
3. **Every `getAuthedUser` page redirects an un-onboarded user**, one structural exception (`app/onboarding/page.tsx`, inverse guard).
4. **`middleware.ts`'s `isPublic`** holds exactly the expected ten routes.

## Two real gaps this found

`/welcome` and `/wrapped` had gone **their whole lives with no onboarding guard**. `/upgrade` is a public route, so signing up and paying before finishing the wizard reached `/welcome` with no `height_cm` — where `computeWrappedStats` would narrate a plan the user had never seen.

Both now carry it, at no extra cost: `/welcome` adds `height_cm` to a `profiles` select it was already making; `/wrapped` adds the read to its existing `Promise.all`.

**No allowlist.** CLAUDE.md called this "8 sites" when it was really 9 carrying the guard and 2 without. Counting the sites was the mistake — the rule is "all of them", and only a test can say that.

## Docs corrected in the same pass

- The public-route list said **7** entries for months while the code said **10** (missing `/refunds`, `/contact`, `/pricing`).
- Test counts were stale in three places — `90 files / 1,379` and `89 files / 1,334` against a real **120 / 1,589**.
- The safety contract's by-hand grep instructions are replaced by the test; its pinning table and verification-gates block now cover CI.

## Verification

Each invariant was made to fail for its own reason before being trusted — a `.insert(` added to a component, the guard removed from `app/log/page.tsx`, and a route added to `isPublic` produced **exactly three distinct failures**, then were reverted:

```
× no component or hook writes to the database
× every authenticated page redirects an un-onboarded user
× exposes exactly the expected exact-match routes
```

All five gates green: **120 files / 1,589 tests**, `check:tokens` PASS, lint clean, build and `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

The course required beginners to paste long namespaced skill commands and introduced programming before they could comfortably use Claude. It also lacked a concrete multi-file consolidation exercise.

Rebuild the course around ordinary conversation: install once, ask for work, answer a short question, review the saved result, and ask Claude to save or improve the procedure.

- Five lessons cover setup, automatic skill use, spreadsheet comparison/consolidation/Excel dashboards, sourced tax research, and reusable work procedures.
- Remove the Node.js lesson and explicit workbench commands from the learner workflow.
- Replace process diagrams with 25 labeled interface illustrations and three unchanged, attributed Anthropic extension screenshots. Illustrated replies are explicitly examples, not execution evidence.
- Add a consolidation skill and two invented Excel sources: four bill records, Ohio $300 plus Texas $700. The practice download is pinned to the matching fixture commit.
- Keep copyable global instructions and click-by-click open/reload/restart help.

Validation: repository checks pass (67 local links, six discoverable skills, 25 accessible illustrations); all six skills pass the skill validator; all illustrations render; workbook checks verify text IDs, formulas/stored values, totals, reconciliation cases, and consolidation inputs. Reviewed the rendered lesson in Chrome. No secrets or employer material found in intended public content.

Limits: this does not establish live Claude skill selection or end-to-end execution on a managed Windows connection. The illustrations are not screenshots of those tasks running. Native Excel calculation and the learner's approved environment still need the in-app checks documented in the lessons. Plugin installation from the default marketplace will receive the new kit after this PR is merged.

author: wellthaifounder
body:
## What this fixes

Two separate small things that both made the app feel less trustworthy than it actually is.

**1. The "needs review" number lied.** After deciding a batch of transactions in the Review tab (marking them medical or not), the little red number on the Review tab and the number on the sidebar and top bar wouldn't go down — they'd sit there showing the old count until you happened to leave the page and come back. It looked like the app hadn't actually done what you asked. It had; the number just didn't know it.

**2. That same number was flat-out wrong everywhere except the Expenses page.** Go anywhere else in the app — Dashboard, Settings, Documents — and the sidebar badge always showed nothing, even with 27 things waiting for you. It only ever showed the real number while you happened to be standing on the one page that number is about.

**3. "We found $0" was a dead end.** If you connect a bank and Reclaim finds zero medical transactions on it — which happens to anyone who actually pays for care with a credit card instead of that account — the screen offered "review them now" (there's nothing to review) or "I'll do it later." Neither helps. There was no way to just connect the account that *does* have your medical spending.

## What changed for you

- The review count is now one number, computed one way, used everywhere — the sidebar, the top bar, the Expenses page's own tab and summary card. Deciding a batch of transactions updates all of them immediately, everywhere in the app, with no refresh needed.
- That number is also now correct on every page from the moment you land on it, not just after visiting Expenses first.
- The sidebar's second badge (visible next to Expenses) is now a real count of expenses ready to submit for reimbursement, instead of a number that was always zero.
- When a bank connection finds zero medical transactions, the screen now leads with a "Connect Bank Account" button to link the account you actually use for medical spending, with the old "review them now" option demoted underneath. If you're still mid-setup, this still doesn't offer an "I'll do it later" escape hatch — that stayed intentional.

## What proves it works

- Confirmed directly against the database that the underlying counts behave as expected.
- Walked through it in the real running app: decided a review item through the Review tab and watched the sidebar badge, top bar badge, stat card, and tab badge all drop together instantly, with no page reload. Then jumped straight to the Dashboard — without ever visiting the Expenses page first — and confirmed the sidebar showed the same correct, live number there too.
- Checked the "we found 0" screen in both the first-time-setup version and the "connecting a second bank" version, confirmed the ordinary non-zero case still looks exactly as it did before, and checked light mode, dark mode, and a phone-sized screen.
- The app builds and passes its type and lint checks with zero new errors or warnings.

## What I chose not to do

Didn't touch the other stat cards on the Expenses page (Total, Medical confirmed) that share the same "doesn't use live data" limitation — those are a separate, larger rework of that page that's better done once, not patched card by card.

author: senaviacorp
body:
Tres defectos del modal «Sync Errors» que escondían el daño real, medidos en
producción el 5-sep-2026.

1. **El contador cuenta filas, no ficheros.** La fila 19 arrastra cinco
   `file_ids` en una sola cadena: el panel decía 5 y faltaban 8. El endpoint de
   lista ya devuelve `file_ids_pendientes` y el botón ya instanciaba
   `useFailedSyncs()` descartando `data`, así que sumarlos no cuesta ninguna
   petición extra. Se muestra como suelo («N filas (M ficheros)»), porque
   `file_ids_pendientes` es `null` si la comprobación falló.
2. **Los pendientes solo se pintaban en las resueltas-en-falso.** Una fila
   abierta con cinco ficheros perdidos se veía igual que una con uno; sus ids
   solo asomaban en el Payload Preview crudo.
3. **`Delete` avisaba pero no impedía.** El DELETE del backend no comprueba los
   adjuntos, así que un clic confirmado destruía el único inventario de lo que
   falta. Mientras el fichero siga perdido el botón desaparece y queda Resync.

Y un cuarto en el hook: `useResyncFailedSync` invalidaba solo en `onSuccess`,
pero el resync es idempotente y va fichero a fichero — un 502 es recuperación
**parcial**, no nula. Pasa a `onSettled`.

**No era un defecto**, comprobado: el badge «Fichero AUSENTE» sí parte `file_ids`
por comas y comprueba todos, y contempla el `file_id` singular.

Requiere el PR de la API (Senavia-Corp/gqm-api#146) para que la recuperación
funcione de punta a punta.

author: mokume-agent[bot]
body:
## 目的

静止画 (`FrameWriter`) と動画 (`MovieWriter`) が背圧を別々に持ち、**どちらの待ちにも期限が無かった**。外の何かが永久に用意できないと待ちが永久に終わらず、待つのは main actor の上なので**絵も観測も入力も一緒に黙り、プロセスを殺すしかなくなる**。

## 畳んだもの / 畳まなかったもの (ADR-0008 決定 6)

**畳んだ — 背圧の数え方。** 取り込みの 5 行が逐語同文だったが、**それは畳む理由ではない**。畳んだのは「終わりの合図を先に、枠を後に」という**順序が不変条件**だからである。片方だけ入れ替わると抱えている数を数え損ない、`drain()` が**書き終わる前に返る** — ファイルが欠けたまま「書けた」ことになり、コンパイルも検査も通る。順序は `Backpressure.Release` の 1 箇所に閉じ込めた。

**畳まなかった — 待ちの意味。** `drain()` は「頼んだ全部がファイルになった」、`finish()` は「ファイルが閉じた」で、保証しているものが違う。**静止画は finalize 前は「まだ無い」だけだが、mp4 は「あるが壊れている」**（末尾のメタデータが要る）。Issue 本文が「背圧の実装を畳む」とだけ書いて待ちの意味を畳んでいないのは、正しい線の引き方だった。

## 期限は 2 段で、測り方が違う

| 待ち | 期限 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 枚を符号化しきる (`drain()`、`finish()` の前半) | **進捗ベース** — 1 つも進まなくなって 5 秒 | `finished` が 1 枚ごとに signal される。**新しい合図を足さずに測れる**。総時間で測ると、長く撮った動画の符号化を進んでいるのに諦める |
| ファイルを閉じる (`finish()` の後半) | 平らな 30 秒 | 合図が 1 回きりで進捗が見えない |

**越えても殺さない。** mp4 は末尾のメタデータが要るので途中で止めると再生できないファイルになる。**待つのをやめても仕事は走り続ける**ので、失うのは「返ってきた時点で出来ている」という保証だけである。取引はこう並ぶ:

- いま: 永久に固まる (プロセスを殺すしかなく、そのときもファイルは未完成)
- 期限あり: N 秒で諦めて警告 (N+1 秒で終わるはずだった場合だけ損をする)

`take()` には期限を置かない。そこに期限を置くことは「上限に達したらフレームを落とす」という意味になり、このパッケージが選んでいる「待たせる」の反対側になる (ADR-0025 決定 2)。

## 期限を入れて初めて通れるようになった道

`drain()` が諦めると `outstanding` が残るので、**抱えたまま手放される経路ができる**。`DispatchSemaphore` は作ったときの値より小さいまま解放すると落ちるので (libdispatch が「Semaphore object deallocated while in use」で止める)、`isolated deinit` で枠を戻す。

**最初の検査を書いた時点で実際に signal 5 で落ちた** — 固まりを直した代わりに落ちるところだった。

## 他の環境を調べた

期限の形を決める前に Processing (Java)・Unity・openFrameworks・TouchDesigner・p5.js と AVFoundation 自身の契約を調べた ([全文](https://github.com/mokume-metal/mokume/issues/958#issuecomment-5557032484))。規約どおり**根拠には使っていない** (ADR-0008 決定 1「業界の標準であることは、このリポジトリでの実需の証明にならない」)。分かったこと:

- **期限を持っている環境が 1 つも無かった。** Unity Recorder は `timeout` の grep が 0 件で `WaitForCompletion()` に引数すら無い。Processing の唯一の期限は `awaitTermination(5000, **SECONDS**)` = 83 分。`ofxVideoRecorder` は `// TODO: kill ffmpeg process if its taking too long` と自認して未実装
- **停止でブロックするのは通り相場**で、守らない側の痛みが 3 環境で実証されている (TouchDesigner は開発元スタッフがフォーラムで「実験したら 2 フレーム待てば足りた」と案内、p5.js は自分のテストが `sleep` を挟んでいる、Unity `CaptureScreenshot` は 2013 年から `File.Exists` ポーリングの回避策が積み上がっている)
- **TouchDesigner が「上限を持たない設計の帰結」を実演していた** — 上限を撤廃した結果、上限が消えたのではなく **Windows の `TdrDelay` レジストリとして利用者の手に押し出された**

期限の根拠は 3 つとも内側にある: AGENTS.md 自身の「固まりうる待ちには、待つ側が期限を持たせて越えたら殺す」/ `RenderDevice` だけが `waitLimitSeconds` を持つ非対称 / Apple 自身が `isReadyForMoreMediaData` について「remain that way for **extended periods**」と書いていること。

## 確認方法

`Backpressure` は GPU もファイルも要らない素の型なので、**期限そのものを決定論的に固定できる** — 期限を短くして構成し、誰も枠を返さない状態で待たせればよい。書き出しの経路ごと動かして測ろうとすると「遅いディスクを用意する」話になって再現しなくなる。

6 本を足し、**3 通りに壊して赤くなることを確かめた**:

| 壊し方 | 赤くなった検査 |
| --- | --- |
| 諦めたとき `nil` を返す | 2 件 |
| 諦めたとき `outstanding` を 0 に戻す | 1 件 |
| 期限を総時間で測る | 3 件 |

復元して 0 件。

### Closes #958 の完了条件

| 完了条件 | 何でどう確かめたか |
| --- | --- |
| 背圧の実装が 1 つ | `Output/Backpressure.swift`。`slots` / `finished` / `limit` / `outstanding` / `peak` / 取り込み / signal の順を持つ。2 つの writer は転送するだけになった (`limit` / `outstanding` / `peakOutstanding` は計算プロパティ) |
| `drain()` / `finish()` の待ちに期限がある | 上の表の 2 段。`FrameWriter.drain()` と `MovieWriter.finish()` の両方 |
| 期限を越えたときの振る舞いが検査で固定されている | `BackpressureTests` 6 本。**諦めた数を名乗ること**・**`outstanding` を 0 に戻さないこと**・**総時間ではなく進捗で測ること**を、それぞれ壊して赤くなるのを見た |
| ~~`MovieFile` の二重背圧~~ | **#979 へ切り出した** (本文も更新済み)。前者は写しを畳む話、あちらは AVFoundation の使い方の話で、説明の筋が違う |
| `make ci-check` が緑 | `.build` を消してから回した |

**既存の検査は 1 行も変えていない** — `SaveFramesTests` と `RecordMovieTests` が `outstanding <= limit` / `peakOutstanding == limit` / drain 後に 0 を見ており、畳み方を間違えれば落ちる。

## 行数は減っていない

`FrameWriter` 142 → 124、`MovieWriter` 165 → 173、`Backpressure` 143 (新規) で、計 307 → 440。#812 で測ったとおり、**畳んだ理由を書く doc が畳みで浮いた分を食う**。

## 別に起票したもの

- **#978** — 終了の後始末が main を塞ぐ。`AVAssetWriter.finishWriting()` の同期版は 2013 年に非推奨で、理由が「should not be called from the main thread. Doing so can **cause the finishWriting operation to fail**」。`MovieFile` は正しく `await` 版を使っているが、`MovieWriter.finish()` の `closed.wait()` が main を塞ぐので**合成すると Apple が畳んだ形に戻っている**。`applicationShouldTerminate` → `.terminateLater` が正規の口で未実装
- **#979** — `MovieFile` の二重背圧 (1ms ポーリング)。Apple の答えは `requestMediaDataWhenReady` か macOS 26 の `SampleBufferReceiver.append(_:) async`

**`endRecord()` の側は非同期にできない** — 利用者が同期の `draw()` から呼ぶ public API なので、`await` を持ち込むと ADR-0010 決定 1 (利用者のコードに並行性の注釈が現れない) に反する。だから期限はどちらにせよ要る。

Closes #958

## FII/DII production freshness recovery

Closes the code-level gap between a successful fetch/write and a trustworthy production freshness verdict.

### Changes
- adds a fail-closed production readiness evaluator over stored FII/DII rows
- compares latest stored official institutional session against the latest recorded market session rather than wall-clock age, avoiding weekend false-stale states
- adds a one-way daily-job guard: official FII/DII data older than the recorded market session is rejected, while valid official data newer than a lagging market recorder is still allowed
- preserves exact official NSE provenance and 1D/3D/5D/20D window readiness
- registers focused tests in Canonical Live Adapters CI

### Safety
- no estimates or fabricated missing values
- no direct directional vote
- no verdict/candidate/Telegram/execution authority
- no manual Railway config/deploy changes
- no claim that cron runtime is proven merely because code or deployment passes

### Completion boundary
This PR hardens freshness and creates the read-only production readiness evaluator. A real scheduled Railway cron run + DB readback remains a separate runtime proof boundary and will not be marked DONE until observed.

author: natea
body:
# Run-lifecycle stability: stop the platform from killing its own agent runs

This branch is one night's work on a single theme: **Paperclip's development server was destroying the agent runs it was supposed to host, and then blaming the agents for it.** Twenty commits, 55 files, +5,860/-220.

If you have never seen this codebase: Paperclip runs autonomous agents as child processes. Each agent wake is a *heartbeat run* — a row in `heartbeat_runs` plus an OS process running a coding-agent CLI. A supervisor (`server/scripts/dev-watch.ts` → `tsx watch`) restarts the server whenever a source file changes. That restart was the problem.

---

## The headline bug, and how it compounded

Editing any file under `server/src/**` restarted the server. On restart, `drainRunningRunsForShutdown` walked every `running` row and SIGTERMed its process group. In development, the agent editing the file was itself running as one of those rows — **so every source save killed the editing agent's own run, plus every other agent's run on the instance**, surfacing as `Claude exited with code 143`.

The originally filed mechanism was wrong. Adapter children are spawned detached, so `tsx watch`'s own kill never reaches them. The drain was doing it *deliberately* — it could not tell a restart from an operator stop.

That single defect then compounded through four downstream layers, each of which is a commit here:

1. The adapter read the truncated stdout of a signal-killed process through its login/upstream heuristics and reported an **auth or upstream fault** — a provider problem that never happened.
2. `server_shutdown_interrupted` and `process_signal_terminated` were absent from the transient-infrastructure retry set, so the interrupted run got one attempt with no backoff, and the next sweep demoted the issue to **`blocked` with an empty `blockedBy`** — a blocker with no owner and nothing to unblock.
3. The productivity reviewer counted those platform-killed, zero-cost runs as an agent **spinning on its own work** (`high_churn`).
4. Separately, agents whose every comment was refused by a mis-scoped write guard looked *silent* to the same reviewer, because a refused comment leaves no trace — producing false-positive underperformance reviews against agents that spoke on every single heartbeat.

Measured cost before the fix: **19 runs terminated with `server_shutdown_interrupted`**, 18 of them in one night, 17 belonging to a single agent.

---

## The fixes

### Run preservation

**`a58ad2ee6` — leave detached agent runs alive across a dev-watch restart (AND-18)**
*Symptom:* every `server/src/**` save SIGTERMed every in-flight agent run.
*Cause:* the shutdown drain could not distinguish a watcher restart from an operator stop.
*Change:* `dev-watch.ts` sets `PAPERCLIP_DEV_WATCH=1` on the watched child; the drain reads it and preserves runs that lead their own process group and are still alive. Ctrl-C arrives as SIGINT and still drains normally, so agent processes are never kept past an operator stop. A preserved run keeps its `running` row for boot reconciliation to adopt.
*Evidence:* see **Did it work?** below — one real restart post-fix, `interrupted: 0, preserved: 1`.

**`82ca70257` — record the execution lane at the spawn site (AND-20)**
*Symptom:* the discriminator deciding whether a run could survive a restart was silently disabled.
*Cause:* `isServerStdioBoundHotRestartRun` read `executionEngine`/`processTopology` from `contextSnapshot`. **Nothing ever wrote those keys.** Every call fell through to a last-resort `adapterConfig.engine !== "cli"` check, which does not determine the lane — so every run took one branch regardless of how it was spawned.
*Change:* each spawn site now records its own lane (CLI / ACP / remote / native) and the topology actually achieved — Windows cannot detach, so it honestly reports `server_stdio`. Read-back prefers a recorded lane, then the observed process shape (`pid === pgid` means detached), which is the same signal AND-18's preservation gate uses, so both restart paths now agree. The legacy heuristic stays as a deliberately-unflipped last resort: draining an adoptable run costs an optimisation, adopting a server-bound run loses the run.

### Stop misattributing infrastructure failures

**`6b5b6efa3` — classify a signal-killed provider process as infrastructure (AND-17)**
*Symptom:* a process-group SIGTERM was reported as a provider auth or upstream fault.
*Cause:* the login/transient-upstream heuristics ran over the truncated output of a killed process.
*Change:* `isProcessSignalTerminated` recognises both shapes a signal arrives in — a real `signal`, and the 128+N exit codes a shell wrapper reports instead (130/137/143) — and short-circuits the provider heuristics with a typed `process_signal_terminated`. Timeouts are deliberately excluded; the runner already reports a richer typed disposition for those.

**`985d2cb87` — retry restart-interrupted runs instead of demoting the issue (AND-17)**
*Symptom:* a restart left the issue `blocked` with an empty `blockedBy`.
*Cause:* `server_shutdown_interrupted` and `process_signal_terminated` were missing from `TRANSIENT_INFRA_CONTINUATION_ERROR_CODES`, so both hit the `default` branch — one attempt, no backoff.
*Change:* both retry with backoff. `process_lost` deliberately stays out: it is the signal the stranded-recovery paths are built on, and reclassifying it would suppress escalations owed to the board.
*Evidence:* `heartbeat-retry-scheduling` (31 tests), `service.pause-durability` (9 tests).

**`c268ddaf4` — stop productivity review blaming agents for platform failures (AND-17, AND-29)**
*Symptom:* agents flagged `high_churn` for runs the platform killed, and flagged silent while every comment they made was being refused.
*Cause:* two blind spots in one evidence-gathering block. A burst of platform-killed runs with **zero billable usage** is contention, not churn. And refused comments never reach `issueComments`, so a silenced agent and a silent one were indistinguishable.
*Change:* two platform-killed zero-cost runs now mark contention; refused-write activity rows are attributed to sampled runs, and one refused attempt proves the agent demonstrably spoke. The reviewer labels and files but never holds the assignee — suppressing the review would hide the platform failure, and stopping the agent would punish it for something it did not do.
*Evidence:* `productivity-review-service` (22 tests).

### Fix the write guard that silenced agents

**`36c4dfa76` — bind a checkout run to the issue it checked out (AND-22)**
*Symptom:* a scheduler-driven run could check an issue out and then be refused every comment and status update **on that same issue** — leaving the agent having moved an issue to `in_progress` with no way to explain or undo it.
*Cause:* not the request header the denial copy blamed. `readRunSourceIssueId` found no `issueId` in the run's `contextSnapshot`; scheduler heartbeats wake with none, so every write looks cross-issue.
*Change:* checking an issue out *is* the run declaring its task, so `POST /checkout` now binds the run to the issue. The binding is one-way — a bound run cannot be re-pointed, so it cannot be used to walk a run across targets and evade the cross-issue influence cap. A binding failure never fails an otherwise-successful checkout.
*Evidence:* `unassigned-run-issue-trap` (19), `scheduler-run-owned-issue-write` (3).

**`1f8ec5848` — scope the write guard to the run, stop prescribing a header (AND-25)**
*Symptom:* an unbound run was refused PATCH and comments while checkout, issue-create and document-write all succeeded — take the issue, then cannot speak on it. Denial copy told callers to send a header **they were already sending correctly**, and emitted the literal string `$PAPERCLIP_RUN_ID` verbatim to callers.
*Change:* a run may write to an issue whose `checkoutRunId`/`executionRunId` is that run. The two failure shapes get distinct codes with distinct sanctioned pa

author: andyou007
body:
jsFn.show/hide scheduled a 3s auto-hide timer and a one-shot transitionend listener per call, but never cancelled the previous cycle's timer/listener when a slot was reused before it finished. With only two toast slots shared across every demo button, firing toasts faster than the animation cycle stacked cycles on the same element: the old timer could hide a freshly reused toast almost immediately, and orphaned transitionend listeners (waiting on a transition that no longer happens) never got cleaned up, eventually wedging slots so no toast could show at all.

Track each element's pending timer/listener in a WeakMap and cancel it whenever show() or hide() runs again on that element.

author: jsun-m
body:
## The defect

`warn-already-triaged.py` answers one question: is this health-check warn ALREADY triaged? Health-check warns are chronic by construction — they re-fire every pass until an owner decision lands — so the ones that survive are precisely the ones already investigated. `NONE FOUND` is the verdict that sends an agent to re-derive a decision that was already taken.

It searched two files: `pending-questions.md` and `current-track.md`.

But a warn whose decision is **settled** is not written to a file that waits on a human. It is written to core memory. Those warns therefore came back `NONE FOUND` — indistinguishable from genuinely untriaged.

## Evidence, at the parent commit

Live host, 9 warns, `python3 src/health-check.py | python3 skills/proactive-loop/scripts/warn-already-triaged.py`:

```
5 with candidate parkings, 4 with none: screen-capture, live-checkout-branch, engine-revision-drift, daily-cron-punctuality
```

All four of those have their triage in core memory. Probe name alone, on that host's memory corpus:

```
  screen-capture         -> 3 file(s)
  live-checkout-branch   -> 2 file(s)
  engine-revision-drift  -> 5 file(s)
  daily-cron-punctuality -> 6 file(s)
```

So 4 of 9 were reported untriaged while the decision was on disk the whole time. (Corpus contents are personal, so the reproducible before/after below uses a fixture instead.)

## Before / after, hermetic fixture

Fixture memory dir holding one file, `zz-fixture-probe-parked.md`, whose first line is `## zz-fixture-probe is parked`. Same input both runs.

**Parent commit `958ca777`:**

```
searching 1 parking file(s) for 1 warn(s)

  NONE FOUND zz-fixture-probe          — no heading, no body mention; genuinely untriaged, OR every token missed (try one from the warn text)

0 with candidate parkings, 1 with none: zz-fixture-probe
```

**This branch:**

```
searching 4 parking file(s) for 1 warn(s)

  CANDIDATES zz-fixture-probe          (1) — verify the CONDITION matches, not just the probe
             via 'zz-fixture-probe' -> memory/zz-fixture-probe-parked.md:1  ## zz-fixture-probe is parked

1 with candidate parkings, 0 with none
```

## The change

1. **`parking_files()` includes the core-memory corpus.**
2. **The memory-dir composition gets one owner.** `_default_memory_dir()` was private to `health-check.py`. Rather than adding a second copy in the script, it moves to `util_paths` as `default_memory_dir()` / `memory_dir()`, and health-check delegates — so the corpus reader and health-check's own divergence check cannot drift apart.
3. **Memory hits are labelled `memory/<name>`.** A pending question waits on a human; a memory records a decision already taken. Same word "parked", opposite next action, so the reader must be able to tell which one a hit is.
4. **Reads are cached.** The corpus went from 2 files to dozens, scanned per token per warn.

## The legacy memory-dir alias — CHANGED after review

**This section previously said the opposite.** It claimed `memory_dir()` deliberately did not honor
the legacy `SUTANDO_PRIVATE_DIR` alias, preserving health-check's behavior. @yixuan-ag2 pointed out
that this reproduces *this PR's own bug* for a different cohort: a host still on the legacy alias
resolves the default path, finds no corpus, and gets `NONE FOUND` — silently.

Fixed in `f66b729d`. `memory_dir()` now resolves through `_memory_dir_env()`, exactly as
`personal_path()` and `shared_personal_path()` already do. Consistency with its siblings in the same
module is the defensible position; mirroring health-check was not, because health-check opts out of
that lookup deliberately and for a probe-specific reason.

**health-check keeps its own env policy and is unchanged.** `MEMORY_DIR` is restored to its original
expression byte-for-byte, so this PR changes no path health-check resolves. It still delegates the
*composition* to `default_memory_dir()` — that is the part that was duplicated.

Legacy-alias host, same input:

```
before   NONE FOUND zz-legacy-probe    0 with candidate parkings, 1 with none
after    via 'zz-legacy-probe' -> memory/parked.md:1
         1 with candidate parkings, 0 with none
```

A canonical-var host is unaffected (control run, unchanged).

## Tests

`tests/util-paths-memory-dir.test.py` 13 -> 20, `tests/proactive-loop-warn-already-triaged.test.py` 22 -> 29.

Mutations, each run on a restored copy, each red on a NAMED arm:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| `parking_files()` drops the memory extension | `FAIL: test_memory_files_join_the_parking_corpus` |
| `display()` always returns the bare name | `FAIL: test_a_memory_hit_is_labelled_so_it_is_not_read_as_a_pending_question` |
| caching removed (read per token) | `FAIL: test_each_file_is_read_once_however_many_tokens_are_searched` |
| health-check re-composes the path itself | `FAIL: test_default_memory_dir_delegates` |
| `memory_dir()` stops honoring the legacy alias | `FAIL: test_legacy_alias_is_honored_like_its_siblings` |
| `memory_dir()` consults the legacy alias FIRST | `FAIL: test_canonical_var_still_wins_over_the_legacy_alias` |

author: jasonkoopmans
body:
`czlonkowski/n8n-mcp` — lets a client search the n8n node catalog, read existing workflows, and author or validate new ones. **Do not merge until the two secret values are filled.**

## The credential picks the tier

| | Tools | Reach |
|---|---|---|
| No `N8N_API_KEY` | **7** | Bundled node/template reference. Never contacts the instance |
| With `N8N_API_KEY` | **28** | Real workflows, credentials, folders, datatables, executions — including deletes |

Your n8n Public API is enabled (`/api/v1/workflows` returns 401, not 404), so the second tier is available.

## Shipped in a middle tier

`DISABLED_TOOLS` removes two whole tools:
- `n8n_delete_workflow` — does nothing but delete
- `n8n_manage_credentials` — reaches the stored Telegram bot token, SMTP, and the rest

That flag is too blunt for the others, because the deletes are **buried inside multi-operation tools** — dropping `n8n_manage_folders` outright would also lose folder listing. So `DISABLED_TOOL_OPERATIONS` strips only the delete operations:

```
n8n_executions:delete;n8n_manage_folders:delete;n8n_manage_datatable:deletetable,deleterows,deletecolumn;n8n_manage_agents:delete
```

**Verified against 2.82.1, not assumed.** With the policy applied the count drops 28 → 26, both named tools disappear, and exactly the named operations vanish from each remaining tool's `action` enum — `deleteTable`/`deleteRows`/`deleteColumn` included, which also confirms the lowercase env form matches the camelCase operations.

Two things left enabled on purpose, both noted in the manifest: `n8n_update_full_workflow` can overwrite an existing workflow, and `n8n_test_workflow` genuinely executes one — so it can send a real Telegram message or write to Obsidian.

## Why the standard warning lands harder here

Upstream's README opens with *"NEVER edit your production workflows directly with AI — export backups first."* In a repo-backed n8n that's advice. Here, workflows exist **only** in the SQLite DB on n8n's PVC with no copy in Git, so an unwanted edit has no `git revert`. The PVC is on the backed-up `longhorn` class, which makes recovery a Longhorn restore to the last recurring backup — real, but not reconcilable.

## Findings from running the image

- **`N8N_API_URL` is plain `http` on port 443** — looks wrong, isn't. n8n sets `N8N_PROTOCOL=https` but no `N8N_SSL_KEY`/`N8N_SSL_CERT`, so that only shapes generated URLs; it serves cleartext. n8n's own servicemonitor scrapes it with `scheme: http` for the same reason.
- **Telemetry is ON by default** and, per upstream's `PRIVACY.md`, feeds *"datasets and machine learning models for workflow generation."* These are personal workflows — `N8N_MCP_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true`. It also stops a `$HOME` mkdir that fails under `readOnlyRootFilesystem`.
- `uid=34242(nodejs)`; **no host allow-list** (a foreign `Host` header still returns 200, so Envoy's hostname matching is the enforcement point); serves fine with a wholly read-only root filesystem and **no tmpfs**, hence no persistence block; ~64Mi under load.
- `AUTH_TOKEN` gives native bearer auth — 401 without it. Auth-ladder step 2, no Envoy `SecurityPolicy` needed. The image warns (but keeps serving) if the token is under 32 characters.

## Before merging

`app/secret.sops.yaml`, then `sops --encrypt --in-place`:

- `AUTH_TOKEN` — `openssl rand -hex 32`
- `N8N_API_KEY` — n8n UI → Settings → n8n API → Create an API key

Omit `N8N_API_KEY` entirely and the app still runs, just in the 7-tool reference tier.

## Docs

Added a catalog row, and disambiguated the existing **n8n** client-wiring section — that one is n8n *calling* our servers, the opposite direction from this app. Also recorded there that it has never actually been wired: the n8n database contains zero `mcpClientTool` / `mcpClient` / `mcpTrigger` nodes.
