author: thejefflarson
body:
## Problem

sccache's S3/R2 backend is EAGER: when the bucket is unreachable, `sccache
--start-server` fails outright, and the first rustc-through-sccache call dies
with `sccache: Timed out waiting for server startup`, killing the job. An R2
outage is a hard CI outage, not a slow build — the same blast radius the old
redis backend had, now pointed at an off-cluster dependency.

## What I found

Protector's Docker-build side of this cutover was already fixed:
`scripts/start-sccache-docker.sh` (fail-soft, wired into the buildkit
`docker` job in `rust.yml` and the `image` job in `agent.yml` via BuildKit
secrets). Its own header comment even names a sibling
`.github/scripts/start-sccache.sh` that never existed.

Enumerating what actually starts sccache natively (not inside a Docker build):
`rust.yml`'s `lint` and `test` jobs both install sccache and set
`RUSTC_WRAPPER: sccache`, but neither had a pre-flight probe — sccache starts
lazily on the first wrapped `cargo`/`rustc` call, so both were exposed to the
exact failure mode above. `agent.yml`'s `ebpf` job compiles with the toolchain
baked into the runner image and never touches sccache, so it's out of scope.

## What changed

- **`.github/scripts/start-sccache.sh`** (new): ported from the proven probe
  in the metrics/murmurify repos. Tries `sccache --start-server` against R2 up
  to 3 times; on failure, falls back to a local disk cache by appending to
  `GITHUB_ENV`. The load-bearing detail: `GITHUB_ENV` can't *unset* a
  variable, and sccache picks a non-empty `SCCACHE_BUCKET` over `SCCACHE_DIR`
  regardless of order — so the fallback exports an **empty** `SCCACHE_BUCKET`
  alongside `SCCACHE_DIR`, not `SCCACHE_DIR` alone. A missing bucket (the
  `sccache-r2` Secret never reached the pod) and an unreachable one both
  degrade the same way, with a loud `::warning::` line so a silently-cold
  cache doesn't read as fine.
- **`.github/workflows/rust.yml`**: wired the probe into both `lint` and
  `test`, right after `Install sccache` and before anything that would trigger
  a lazy server start.
- Added a `--selftest` mode to the new script (mirroring
  `scripts/start-sccache-docker.sh`'s own fixture harness) that drives all
  three states — no config, R2 up, R2 down — against a stubbed `sccache`
  binary, and wired it into the `lint` job so a regression in the fallback
  (especially the empty-bucket export) fails loudly in CI instead of during a
  real outage.

## On the meshed-runner note

protector-runners are meshed (JEF-84), so I checked whether the probe's
reachability method would be blocked. It isn't a separate network check —
it's sccache's own `--start-server` call, i.e. the same HTTPS egress to R2
the real cache traffic already uses. Nothing about meshing changes that path,
so the ported method carries over unchanged; I'm not aware of anything to
flag here.

## Testing

CI-only change — no Rust code touched, so `cargo fmt`/`clippy`/tests don't
apply.

- `bash .github/scripts/start-sccache.sh --selftest` — all 9 assertions pass
  locally, covering: no bucket in pod env, R2 reachable, R2 unreachable
  (3 retries then fallback with the empty-bucket export).
- Verified the test actually catches a regression: broke the empty-bucket
  export line and reran `--selftest` — 2 of 9 assertions failed as expected.
- `shellcheck` on the new script: one pre-existing-pattern `SC1007` warning
  identical to the one already present in the reference metrics script and
  in `scripts/start-sccache-docker.sh` (the `VAR= cmd` empty-assignment
  idiom) — not a real issue, and this repo runs no shellcheck gate in CI.
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` on `rust.yml` — parses.
- `actionlint` on both touched workflows — only pre-existing findings
  (`protector-runners` self-hosted label unknown to actionlint's default
  config, one unrelated `SC2086` in an untouched step further down); nothing
  new from this diff.
- Ran `/soundcheck:pr-review` — no Critical/High findings (no secrets, no
  injectable input; `SCCACHE_BUCKET` comes from a cluster Secret, not
  attacker-controlled data).

Closes JEF-946.

author: yashrajvansh
body:
```
Intent : Sweep every package for unreachable modules, after the tool was wrong by sevenfold.
Pattern: node oesophagus/reachable.mjs on each package. Nine in the API, not 64.
Signed. Claude / 2026-09-06 22:25 UTC
```

---

### The tool was wrong first

Its first run reported **64** orphans in `Superhostos/apps/api/src`, including `app.hono.ts` — the file that repo's own `CLAUDE.md` calls *the mounted app*. That was the instrument, not the code.

TypeScript ESM writes `import "./app.hono.js"` for a file named `app.hono.ts`: **the specifier names the emitted file, not the source.** Every such import resolved to nothing, so every importee looked orphaned. Fixed — the real figure is **9**. `Host` is unaffected (CRA imports carry no extension), so its 32 stand.

| Package | Modules | Imported | Imported by nothing |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `Host/frontend/src` | 133 | 100 | **32** |
| `Superhostos/apps/api/src` | 326 | 200 | 9 |
| `Superhostos/apps/web/src` | 69 | 59 | 7 |
| `curator/service/worker/src` | 43 | 36 | 5 |
| `HostOS/computer-v2/src` | 24 | 18 | 5 |
| `HostOS/computer/src` | 26 | 22 | 4 |
| `seek/src` | 11 | 4 | 2 |
| `kimi/src` | 19 | 17 | 1 |
| `curatory/src` | 7 | 5 | **0** |

### Two of the nine meet SuperhostOS's own law

*A faculty that nothing calls is not evidence, it is a folder.*

- **The four inventory agent classes** are imported by `inventory.test.ts` **and nothing else**. `routes.hono.ts` serves a static `AGENTS` list, not the classes. So `inventory.test.ts` — 28 cases, eight named suites, one of the fourteen files over the founder's 17-test wall — exercises four classes no live path reaches.
- **`queues/{email,ical-sync,notifications}.queue.ts`** have no matching queue in `wrangler.toml`, whose only queue binding is a `curator-ingest` producer.

That is the two tools meeting: `surface.mjs` said `inventory` was one file wearing eight names; `reachable.mjs` says half of what it tests is wired to nothing.

author: rcluis
body:
## Why
Password autofill works on the website but never in the app.

The cause isn't the markup — the app's login form already had better `autocomplete` attributes than the website's. It's the origin: Capacitor serves the bundle from `capacitor://localhost`, and iOS keys saved passwords to a **domain**. As far as AutoFill is concerned the app has nothing to do with `app.quiroflow.com`, so there's nothing to offer and the QuickType bar stays empty.

## What
Claims the domain, which is what makes iOS treat the app and the website as one product:

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| `public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` | Declares the App ID (`N5TP24Q7MW.com.quiroflow.app`) under `webcredentials` |
| `netlify.toml` header rule | The file is deliberately extension-less; iOS rejects it unless served as `application/json` |
| `App.entitlements` | Claims `webcredentials:app.quiroflow.com` |
| `autocomplete="email"` → `"username"` on the app's sign-in + sign-up email fields | The token that pairs with `current-password`/`new-password` to mark a field as the login identifier rather than just an email input |

Only `webcredentials` is declared, **not `applinks`** — this is about AutoFill, and claiming `applinks` would start routing `https://app.quiroflow.com` links into the app, which is a separate decision.

## ⚠️ Two things to know before merging

1. **The web side must deploy before a new app build helps.** iOS fetches the association file when the app is installed/launched. Merging this deploys the file to `app.quiroflow.com` immediately, so as long as the next iOS build comes after the merge, the ordering works out on its own.
2. **The App ID needs the Associated Domains capability.** Signing is `Automatic`, so Xcode/Xcode Cloud will normally add it to the App ID itself. If a build fails to sign, enable **Associated Domains** for `com.quiroflow.app` in the Apple Developer portal and retry.

## Android
Not covered here. The equivalent is `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` with the app's **SHA-256 signing-certificate fingerprint** — and with Play App Signing the correct fingerprint is the one Google shows in Play Console (Setup → App signing), not the local upload key. I didn't want to guess it or go digging through `keystore.properties`. Paste that fingerprint and the Android half is a small follow-up.

## Test plan
- [x] AASA is valid JSON; `App.entitlements` still lints as a valid plist and the entitlement reads back correctly
- [x] **Ran the production build and confirmed `dist/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` exists** — nitro does copy the dot-directory, which the whole feature silently depends on
- [x] Root typecheck passes
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Confirm the deploy preview serves it as `200` + `application/json` (checked below once the preview builds)
- [ ] End-to-end autofill can only be confirmed on a real device after an App Store/TestFlight build carrying the new entitlement

body:
The first PR out of #205 — the docs half. The scheduled workflow is not in here; this is the framing change #205 asks to land first, and it stands on its own.

**The problem, stated plainly.** The baseline pins v0.21.0. v0.21.0 is affected by CVE-2026-71963 (`core.fsmonitor`), unpatched at last check. Nothing in the docs said so, and a version number at the top of a security document reads as a recommendation whether or not it was meant as one.

**The pin stays.** Moving it to dodge a CVE would invalidate every calibrated fixture and every coverage claim built on that snapshot — the pin is for reproducibility, so a claim made today can be re-checked against the same bytes tomorrow. That is now written down in all three places rather than assumed:

- `cli/data/hermes-baseline.json` — new `pinRationale`, and `knownVulnerabilities` carrying the CVE with its source, affected versions, patch status and `recordedAt`. `patchedIn` is explicitly `null` rather than omitted: "no patch exists" is a fact, and an absent key would be indistinguishable from someone forgetting to fill it in.
- `docs/hermes-coverage-matrix.md` — a new **What the pin means, and what it does not** section above Status definitions, plus a sixth step in Maintaining the baseline: re-check the CVE record on every baseline update *whether or not anything changed*, because a stale record that looks fresh is worse than no record.
- `docs/hermes-security-model.md` — the same statement at the Version drift section, where a reader arrives from the coverage claim.

The matrix also says the list covers only what is documented — absence from it is absence of a record, not evidence of absence.

**Tests.** Four added to `cli/__tests__/hermes-baseline.test.js`, because a framing paragraph is exactly the kind of thing that gets trimmed in a later edit:

- the rationale exists and says it is not a safety endorsement, in the JSON *and* both docs;
- every CVE entry has a CVE-shaped id, a source, a `recordedAt` date, an `affects` string and an explicit `patchedIn` key;
- any CVE flagged `affectsPinnedRelease` is named in the human-readable matrix, not only in the JSON — otherwise the honest framing lives somewhere nobody reads;
- the maintenance procedure still references the record.

Mutation-checked: renaming `CVE-2026-71963` to `CVE-XXXX-XXXXX` in the matrix fails the third test.

`npm test`: **101 pass / 85 fail on `main`, 105 pass / 85 fail on this branch** — the four new tests, zero newly failing. The 85 are pre-existing on my machine and unrelated to this change.

One thing I could not run: `node cli/bin/ship-safe.js scan . --no-ai` from the CONTRIBUTING checklist errors with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` here because `node_modules` is not installed in my environment. Flagging that rather than ticking the box — this change touches only JSON, Markdown and a test file, so I do not expect it to affect a scan, but I have not verified that myself.

I've left the workflow (steps 1–4 of #205) out deliberately so this can be reviewed as the honest-framing change it is. Happy to follow up with it, or to fold the CVE table for other agents from #204 into the same shape if that ordering suits you better.

author: anaclumos
body:
## Problem

Pooling six seats of one Claude Team plan showed every seat as `active` in `status`, gave all six the live tee's usage numbers, and the hooks then failed for four minutes with `token refresh failed (HTTP 400)`.

Root cause: identity was keyed on `organizationUuid`. Every seat of a Team plan shares one organization, so each lookup (`accounts.find(a => a.organizationUuid === org)`) returned the first seat in array order. That collapsed the pool:

- `status` marked all six active and copied the live tee into each of them.
- The enforced-limit stamp landed on the first seat instead of the live one.
- After a swap onto a second seat, the hard path resolved the seat as the first one, excluded it, picked the actually live seat as the swap target, and refreshed the live seat's own parked copy.
- The harvest wrote the live blob into the first seat's slot, overwriting that seat's only credential.

## Fix

Identity is the account UUID from `GET /api/oauth/profile` (`fetchTokenIdentity`), the endpoint Claude Code itself uses to fill `oauthAccount`. The roles endpoint returns only the organization and is gone.

- Every `organizationUuid` comparison now compares `accountUuid` (swap, sample, decide, status, statusline, stopfailure hook, check, doctor, rm, init, switch).
- `usage.json` and `model-usage.json` carry `account` instead of `org`; `EnforcedLimit.account`; the stamp outcome `org-moved` is `account-moved`. Old tee files fail to parse and are re-teed on the next turn; no compatibility shim.
- The dead statusline `organizationUuid` path is removed (the payload has not carried it since 2.1.251).
- The organization stays on the account record as information only.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` clean.
- Live reads on a 15-account pool that includes the six team seats: `status --json` shows exactly one `active` seat with its own usage; `doctor` resolves every parked credential to its own account (one slot that the old code overwrote is flagged, repair is `tokenmaxxing auth <label>`).
- Hermetic `check` runs under a throwaway `TOKENMAXXING_HOME` (procedure in `.memory/hermetic-ladder-verification.md`): hold under the floor; hand-off at 95 to a seat in another org; hand-off at 95 to a seat in the SAME org, in both directions; a tee stamped for a different account is ignored.
- Verified live and recorded in memory: a refresh rotation revokes the previous access token immediately (`OAuth access token has been revoked`), so refreshing any copy of a credential that is live elsewhere kills those sessions' token. `docs/limitations.mdx` and AGENTS.md now say so.

## Not in this release

The `token refresh failed (HTTP 400): (unparsable error body withheld)` message: the token endpoint returns nested Anthropic-style bodies for request-validation failures and the error parser only reads the flat OAuth shape. That classification and message fix ships separately, after the forensics on what produced the 400 finish.

## Version

1.17.0 (`package.json`, `agent-plugin/plugin.json`).

## Captured proof

Typecheck and the five hermetic `check` scenarios under a throwaway root (synthetic accounts), verbatim:

```
$ bun run typecheck
$ tsc --noEmit
exit 0

$ /tmp/tm-hermetic.sh
== A live at 50 (under floor 80): hold
no switch (under-threshold-or-stale) next in 120s
== A live at 95, B in another org at 30: hand off to B
check failed: no parked credential for b@example.com
== A live at 95, B in the SAME org at 10 (team seats): hand off to B
check failed: no parked credential for b@example.com
== B live at 95 (second seat of the shared org), A same org at 10: hand off to A
check failed: no parked credential for a@example.com
== tee stamped for a different account (B) while A is live: ignored
no switch (under-threshold-or-stale) next in 180s
== log events
      1  check.error err=no parked credential for a@example.com
      2  check.error err=no parked credential for b@example.com
$ bun run src/main.ts status --json (15-account live pool, free read; labels only)
```

Live free reads on the owner's 15-account pool (labels withheld): `status --json` reports exactly one `active` seat, and each of the six team seats carries its own usage figures; `doctor` resolves the live credential and 14 of 15 parked credentials to their own account, and flags the one slot the old code overwrote (HTTP 401, revoked) for `tokenmaxxing auth`.

Localized pages: 29 locales x 2 pages edited, one bullet each, gated mechanically (58 files, one hunk and one changed line each, `fetchTokenOrg` gone from every locale, no dashes added, frontmatter untouched).

author: 123constante
body:
## The defect

The edge middleware told every search crawler that `/city/:slug/map`'s canonical
was the homepage, while the page itself declared a **self** canonical
client-side. The page could not be indexed as itself, and the two halves of the
site disagreed about the same URL.

| | |
|---|---|
| The page | [`AnimatedRoutes.tsx:94`](../blob/main/src/components/AnimatedRoutes.tsx#L94) -- a real route since #353 |
| Its own claim | [`CityMap.tsx:81`](../blob/main/src/pages/CityMap.tsx#L81) -- `canonicalPath: /city/${citySlug}/map` |
| The contradiction | `middleware.ts` `case 'city'` -- three segments, so `isBareCity` is false and `'map'` is not in `CLEAN_LISTINGS`, leaving the `${SITE_URL}/` fallback |

Adding `'map'` to `CLEAN_LISTINGS` would have been wrong: that set means
"city-prefixed duplicate that consolidates onto a clean top-level listing", and
there is no `/map` top-level route to consolidate onto.

## The change

The rule moved to `app/cityCanonical.ts`, a dependency-free leaf on the same
terms as `app/truncate.ts` and `app/edgeCacheControl.ts` -- the Edge bundle
cannot resolve `src/`-rooted imports (#272), and a rule living inside
`middleware.ts` has **no spec at all**, because importing that file drags in
`@vercel/edge`. `CLEAN_LISTINGS` moved with it; it had no other reader.

A self-canonical subpage also stops being described by the CITY's card -- it
would otherwise be indexed under the homepage's own title with the city's
generic description. Social bots get the same correction, so a shared map link
previews as the map rather than the city.

`/city/:slug/calendar` is deliberately in neither set: it renders `<Index/>`,
the homepage with the Calendar tab open, so `/` remains correct for it.

## Coverage

`middleware.ts` had **zero** tests before this. It now has two specs -- one over
the rule, one over the read path proving the middleware actually calls it.

- **27 tests** (16 rule + 11 read-path)
- **20 mutants, 20 killed**, every one reaching its verdict line. One survivor
  was an *equivalent* mutant (`new Map(Object.entries({...}))` is still a Map)
  and was rewritten rather than accepted.
- Typecheck **88** (`TYPECHECK_BASELINE`), lint **16/16**, unit **1537/1537**

## Review

Two rounds at high effort, 5 findings, all verified against source before acting.
Round 1 found 3 defects, all in code from this branch. Round 2 found 2 more,
both **inside those fixes** -- which fired the stopping rule stated before round
1 ran, so there was no round 3.

Notably, one round-1 remedy was **declined on a false premise**: it proposed
passing search bots through to "the fully SSR'd page", but `routes/catchall.tsx`
returns `null` on the server. Probed directly -- `next()` yields a 200 with
`x-middleware-next: 1` and a **zero-length body**. That swap would have traded a
thin document for an empty one.

Both round-2 findings ship **unfixed and recorded as such** (`outcome: skipped`,
verdict `CONFIRMED` in the review receipt), because closing either means new
logic and new logic does not ship in a remediation round.

## Queued, not fixed here

Each carries its own re-verify command against production.

- `queued-city-map-ssr-route.md` -- the thin bot document; the real fix is a
  framework route with a loader, which also deletes the copy twin this PR adds
- `queued-city-map-title-output-parity.md` -- both round-2 findings
- `queued-city-subpath-soft-404.md` -- unknown city subpaths answer 200
- `queued-city-map-sitemap-row.md` -- the URL is in no sitemap

## Risk

Bot-only. No human-visible change: humans never reach this middleware branch.
The route is in no sitemap, so nothing live contradicted the old canonical yet.

author: now-ing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4734 — two things in one PR, because they only work together:

1. **Fix the 5 jsdom test failures on `main`** — `web-studio`'s test script now runs vitest with Node's `--localstorage-file`, so the native experimental `localStorage` getter (Node ≥ 22.4) returns a real `Storage` instead of `undefined` inside the jsdom environment. Root-cause analysis in the issue: vitest's jsdom environment aliases `window = globalThis` and does not install jsdom's storage over Node's pre-existing lazy getter, so `window.localStorage` resolves to Node's getter → `undefined` without the flag → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'clear')` in the playground tests.
2. **Add the missing `web-studio-tests` job to PR validation** — no CI workflow ran the web-studio Vitest suite at all, which is why these 5 failures have been invisible (same coverage-gap family as the unit-test lane discussed in #4734).

## Changes

- `web-studio/package.json` — `test` script: `NODE_OPTIONS="--localstorage-file=.vitest-localstorage" vitest run` (the existing scripts already assume a POSIX shell, e.g. `gen-server-client`).
- `web-studio/.gitignore` — ignore the storage file created at the repo's `web-studio/` root.
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml` — new `web-studio-tests` job (`ubuntu-24.04`, Node 22 to match the web-studio build lane in `_build.yml`, `npm ci --prefix web-studio` + `npm test --prefix web-studio`), gated by a new `web_studio_changed` output in `check-deps` (`web-studio/` or `pr.yml` touched), mirroring the existing `langchain_changed` pattern.

## Verification

On a clean checkout of `main` @ `0c5147ca` (Node v26.5.0):

- Before: `Test Files 2 failed | 57 passed (59)`, `Tests 5 failed | 265 passed (270)` — reproduced.
- After this change: **270/270 green** (`npm test`).
- `pr.yml` and `package.json` both parse cleanly (yaml.safe_load / json.load).
- The storage file lands at `web-studio/.vitest-localstorage` and is gitignored.

## Notes for reviewers

- The fix is intentionally the minimal one (issue option 1); per-test `vi.stubGlobal` stubs (option 2) were verified too but are more invasive.
- Node 22 is ≥ 22.4, so CI hits the same native-getter behavior — the job genuinely exercises the fixed path rather than accidentally passing on a different Node.
- The `WEB_STUDIO_PATTERN` includes `pr.yml` itself (same convention as `LANGCHAIN_PATTERN`) so edits to this lane still get validated.

author: vgulinao
body:
Implements [S7 — Sub-tasks with progress](specs/stories/S7-subtasks.md). Review on this PR: comment inline, I fix and reply.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] AC1 "+ Sub-task" on a top-level row opens an inline input; Enter adds at the bottom of the sub-tasks, for everyone
- [x] AC2 Progress "done / total" with a thin bar, live
- [x] AC3 Done sub-tasks strike through in place; only top-level items go to Completed
- [x] AC4 Ticking a parent ticks its open sub-tasks (one ordinary op each) and moves the group to Completed; unticking reopens the parent only; the last sub-task does not tick the parent
- [x] AC5 Deleting a parent deletes its sub-tasks (server cascade + `apply`)
- [x] AC6 Sub-tasks rename, delete, and drag-reorder among siblings (done ones too)
- [x] AC7 No sub-tasks of sub-tasks (no control; server rejects since round 1)
- [x] AC8 Collapsible per parent, component state

## Design
No protocol change. `shared/subtasks.ts`: `progressOf`, `idsToCompleteWith`. `ItemGroup` renders a parent with its nested sortable list; one `DndContext` at page level with a `SortableContext` per sibling group, and `onDragEnd` only accepts drops within the same parent. `ItemRow` gained an inner `.row` plus `extras`/`children` slots so the nested list moves with the row when dragged.

## Tests (56 total, +6)
- shared: progress for none/some/all; cascade ids = open children then parent; parent alone when all children done
- server: sub-task reaches the peer; snapshot keeps `parentId`
- engine: deleting a parent removes children on the peer; ticking a parent cascades as ordinary ops

author: tigerblue77
body:
Le tag Docker mobile portait le nom du canal npm : les deux étaient **une seule valeur**, impossible de choisir l'un sans l'autre. D'où `:stable` publié ce matin — et `docker pull <image>` sans tag demande `:latest`, ne trouve rien, et l'image reste inutilisée par qui n'a pas lu le README.

## Ce que ça change

| | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| Canal npm suivi | `stable` | **`stable`** (inchangé) |
| Tag Docker mobile | `stable` | **`latest`** |
| Tag de version | `2.1.236` | inchangé, toujours immuable |
| Ce que lit la décision de rebuild | `:stable` | **`:latest`** |
| Surcharges | `NPM_DIST_TAG` | + **`IMAGE_MOVING_TAG`**, et un input par exécution |

Le canal reste `stable` délibérément : il est à **27 versions** derrière `latest` aujourd'hui (`2.1.236` contre `2.1.263`) et a donc survécu au contact des autres, ce qui est ce qu'on veut sous une image utilisée quotidiennement. Seul le *nom du tag publié* change.

## L'objection que ça renverse, et pourquoi elle tombe

Le `CLAUDE.md` interdisait `:latest`, avec un argument qui n'était pas faux :

> a `:latest` tag would mean "whatever was pushed most recently", which is precisely the state nobody can roll back to.

Ce qui y répond : **revenir en arrière n'a jamais été le rôle du tag mobile.** Le tag `:<version>` est là pour ça, il est immuable, et le rafraîchissement d'image de base ne le republie délibérément pas — la cible de rollback traverse ce changement intacte. L'invariant est donc **réécrit pour dire ça**, pas supprimé comme si l'inquiétude s'était évaporée.

## Ce qui a été perdu, et remis ailleurs

Tant que le tag mobile portait le nom du canal, **le tag était le registre** de la provenance de l'image. Découplé, il n'enregistre plus rien.

Ce fait voyage maintenant sur l'image, en label : `io.github.dragnix-tigerblue77.claude-code.npm-dist-tag`. L'étape de vérification existante le contrôle comme les autres — un build qui oublie de l'écrire fait échouer la PR, au lieu de publier une image à laquelle personne ne peut demander « tu viens de quel canal ? ».

## Vérification

Étape de décision extraite du workflow et exécutée hors CI contre un `docker` bouchonné, sur les six chemins :

| Situation | `build` | `push_version` |
|---|---|---|
| pull request | `true` | `false` |
| même version, même base | `false` | — |
| même version, base bougée | `true` | `false` |
| nouvelle version | `true` | `true` |
| rien de publié | `true` | `true` |
| panne registre | **échec** | — |

Identiques à avant. Et la référence demandée au registre est désormais `ghcr.io/…:latest` — vérifié en instrumentant le bouchon, c'était tout l'enjeu.

## À faire après la fusion

1. **Relancer le workflow** (`force` décoché) : il ne trouvera rien sous `:latest`, reconstruira et publiera `2.1.236` + `latest`.
2. **Supprimer le tag `:stable`** publié ce matin. Plus rien ne le mettra à jour : il resterait figé sur `2.1.236` pour toujours, en ayant l'air maintenu. C'est un piège, pas un vestige inoffensif. [Versions du paquet](https://github.com/orgs/Dragnix-Tigerblue77/packages/container/claude-code-docker-container/versions) → supprimer la version portant `stable`.

body:
## Cosa fa

Predispone l'integrazione di **Iubenda Cookie Solution** e **Google Tag Manager** sulle pagine del repo, con gli ID lasciati da compilare.

### `assets/consent.js` (nuovo)

Loader unico, caricato in cima al `<head>` di ogni pagina, che esegue in ordine:

1. **Google Consent Mode v2** con default `denied` su tutte le categorie (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`, `functionality_storage`, `personalization_storage`), più `ads_data_redaction` e `url_passthrough`. Gira prima di GTM, altrimenti i tag partirebbero senza vincolo di consenso.
2. **Iubenda** con blocco preventivo (`autoblocking.js`): consenso per singola finalità, pulsante "Rifiuta" con lo stesso peso di "Accetta", nessuna "X" che vale come consenso, revoca sempre disponibile, `googleConsentMode: 'template'`. Colori del banner allineati alla palette della dashboard.
3. **Google Tag Manager**.

Il blocco `CONFIG` in cima al file contiene i tre ID (`iubendaSiteId`, `iubendaCookiePolicyId`, `gtmId`), oggi vuoti: in quello stato lo script esce subito senza scrivere cookie né fare richieste di rete, quindi le pagine restano pubblicabili prima che gli account siano pronti.

### `docs/GTM-IUBENDA-SETUP.md` (nuovo)

Procedura operativa: creazione account Iubenda sul piano da 19,99 €/mese, prodotti da attivare, aggiunta del collaboratore, creazione contenitore GTM e accessi per il team, dove compilare i tre ID, checklist di verifica post-attivazione.

### Pagine HTML

Aggiunto `<script src="/assets/consent.js"></script>` subito dopo `<meta charset>` in `index.html` e nelle 6 pagine sotto `jarvis/`. Nessun'altra modifica.

## Note

`dashboard-outreach.davidecaiazzo.it` è una dashboard interna (`noindex,nofollow`) che oggi non carica servizi di terze parti: se non serve tracciarla, basta lasciare `CONFIG` vuoto e non cambia nulla. Gli stessi ID vanno compilati sul sito pubblico dove il banner serve davvero.

## Verifica

- `node --check assets/consent.js` — ok.
- Con `CONFIG` vuoto le pagine si aprono identiche a prima: nessun cookie, nessuna richiesta di rete aggiuntiva.
- Il comportamento con gli ID reali va verificato con la checklist in `docs/GTM-IUBENDA-SETUP.md` una volta creato l'account.

author: kurenaiiiii
body: ## What was changed? Two-phase fix, both in `crates/pumpkin-world/src/generation/carver/cave.rs`: - **Phase 1:** the `protected_blocks_on_top` calculation in `CaveCarver::carve_ellipsoid` changed from `i32::from(!is_overworld)` (0 for Overworld, 1 for Nether) to `7 * i32::from(!is_overworld)` (0 for Overworld, 7 for Nether), matching vanilla's flat 7-block protected boundary for non-Overworld dimensions. - **Phase 2:** `carve_block` now checks the `minecraft:nether_carver_replaceables` block tag before replacing any block in the Nether — mirroring vanilla's `canAlwaysCarveBlock` check — using the same `has_tag(&tag::...)` pattern already used for the earlier concrete powder fluid-tag fix. Bedrock is not in this tag, so it's now never carved regardless of Y-level. Fixes #3270 ## Why were these changes necessary? Pumpkin's Nether carver only protected 1 top block (only Y=127) instead of vanilla's 7 (Y=121–127), and had no tag check at all before replacing blocks, meaning bedrock could be carved out entirely wherever a cave's ellipsoid radius reached it. Vanilla's actual logic, confirmed against the 1.21.1 deobfuscated source during investigation: `Carver.carveRegion` computes protected blocks as `chunk.hasBelowZeroRetrogen() ? 0 : 7`, and `canAlwaysCarveBlock` checks `state.isIn(config.replaceable)` before allowing any replacement. ## What is the impact of this change? This only affects the Nether; Overworld carving behavior is completely unchanged. ## Are there any known issues or limitations? - Commands run: `cargo fmt` (clean), `cargo clippy --all-targets` (zero warnings), `cargo test --workspace` (all passing, including two new unit tests: `nether_roof_blocks_are_protected` and `nether_bedrock_is_not_carved`). Both tests failed with the exact expected pre-fix behavior (Y=121 carved to air instead of staying netherrack; bedrock carved to air instead of surviving) and pass cleanly after the fix. - In-game verification was done separately by the author on a live server: fresh Nether chunks show large cave formations near the roof capping out cleanly at the protected boundary with no bedrock exposure (screenshot below). - Edge cases not specifically tested: multiple overlapping carver runs interacting at the boundary, and carve ellipsoids spanning chunk boundaries near the roof — the unit tests cover a single ellipsoid within one chunk. ## Testing screenshot ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Bug Fixes** - Nether cave generation now preserves the top seven blocks of the terrain. - Nether bedrock and other protected blocks are no longer carved away. - Cave carving is limited to blocks designated as replaceable, while neighboring netherrack continues to generate caves correctly.

author: huamengjiang
body:
Summary:
The parent kept TIMESTAMP out of bucket columns because a timestamp bucket
column tripped the bucket-conversion invariant in
`HiveSplitReader::bucketConversionRows()`. This removes that exclusion by
fixing the actual cause.

There is no type-level limitation here, and it is worth being precise about
why. The assertion is

    VELOX_CHECK_EQ((partitions_[i] - bucketToKeep) % partitionBucketCount, 0);

and it is pure arithmetic: `(h % (oldCount*k)) % oldCount == h % oldCount` holds
for any hash `h` and any type. Its one requirement is that the same row hashes
identically at write time and at read time. Nothing about that is specific to
timestamps.

What broke it is that the row did not survive the round trip. Dumping the
offending rows at the assertion showed every read-back timestamp landing on an
exact millisecond -- `1951-03-14T12:07:38.299000000`,
`2007-05-30T12:31:34.243000000`, `2021-05-13T02:10:47.618000000` -- while
`randTimestamp()` generates nanos as `rand<int64_t>(rng) % 1'000'000'000`, which
is arbitrary. The write path truncates sub-millisecond precision. So the writer
bucketed the full-precision value, the reader hashed the truncated one, and the
row landed outside its file's bucket.

The fix is to generate at the precision the format actually preserves, so the
bucket key round-trips. That restores the invariant and lets TIMESTAMP be a
bucket column like any other type, so `makeNewType()` goes back to a single type
pool and `makeInitialSchema()` loses the bucket-column plumbing the parent added.

Trade-off worth naming: this lowers generated timestamp precision for the whole
fuzzer, not just bucket columns -- the vector is fuzzed per schema, so the
setting is global. Sub-millisecond timestamps are no longer exercised anywhere
in this fuzzer. That is a real reduction, and the right long-term answer is for
the write path not to truncate; until then, generating values the format cannot
store only produces failures that say "the format truncated", which is not what
this fuzzer is for.

Differential Revision: D118995939

Found 2026-09-05, live. Fix bin/fm-pr-poll.sh waking with merged based solely on the forge PR state. Observed levelupself/mtg PR 26 was deliberately opened against feature branch fm/split-the-effect-vocabulary-so-a-new-cap-66 instead of main, then merged into that feature branch. The forge reported merged but trunk remained a7789122fd164d75e0eec2f4e803ede824145d1e. bin/fm-pr-merge.sh already requires merged true and evidence that the merge commit is the default branch head or an ancestor. The poll must use this same landed-work evidence test, shared rather than copied so the paths cannot drift. A merge into a non-default branch must never report merged and must emit a distinct wrong-base signal rather than silently waiting forever. Keep the poll a byte-identified trusted shim under the existing watcher trust contract. Print nothing when nothing should be reported, including unreadable or invalid evidence; finish inside the existing check timeout; emit exactly one line when supervision should wake. Cover identical and ancestor success and diverged/behind refusal. Preserve provider parity: GitHub and GitLab polling must both require default-branch ancestry, retaining host/namespace validation and the watcher authentication and retirement behavior. The original related question asked for a recommendation on asserting intended base at creation/registration without silently expanding implementation. The PR registration path must verify the returned base.ref (GitLab target_branch) equals the project's default branch before a task can report completion. The canonical source is the supported execution entry point; copied state artifacts are authenticated identity artifacts rather than standalone installations with their own dependencies. Preserve all existing confirmation retry, receipt, mirror, malformed-evidence, and trust safeguards. Tests use structured forge fixtures; glab is absent locally, so no live GitLab claim is made. author: ni-co
body:
### Linked issue

Closes #4384

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Enhancement
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs

### Reasoning

An agent that orchestrates others sometimes needs a synchronous answer from a child, so it calls `send_agent_prompt` with `background: false`. If the child takes longer than the 30 s wait, the tool returns "continue with other work if you will receive a finish notification", but the handler only arms that notification when `background` is true. The parent follows the advice, the child finishes, and nothing arrives. The parent only recovers by polling `get_agent_status` by hand (in my case, a day later when a human asked why the result never came back).

The fix keeps the deliberate behavior for blocking prompts that complete inside the wait (no notification; the result is in the tool response, and the existing test for that stays as is) and only changes the timed-out case: the wait result now says `timedOut`, and when the child is still running at that point the handler arms the same finish notification a background prompt gets and says so in `guidance`. If the child settled while the timeout was being reported, the handler returns the settled result instead of arming a subscription that would fire on some later, unrelated turn. The shared timeout message no longer promises a notification the caller may not get.

### Goals

- A blocking agent-scoped `send_agent_prompt` whose wait times out while the child is still running arms the finish notification and tells the caller so.
- A blocking prompt whose child settled during the timeout returns the settled result, with no stale subscription.
- The timeout text is accurate for every caller (agent-scoped or top-level, notification armed or not).

### Non-goals

- Blocking prompts that finish within the wait: unchanged, no notification (existing test kept).
- `create_agent`'s blocking path: unchanged; it already arms independently of the wait.
- The related notification issues #3248, #3875, #4231 (Windows background run, one-shot unsubscribe, error→resume) are not addressed here.

### QA

Daemon code only; no UI. Tested on Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8, Node 22.23.1). Not run on a macOS or Windows daemon.

**Reproduced before the fix** (Paseo 0.7.2, live daemon): agent-scoped Claude Code session called `send_agent_prompt` on a Codex child with `background: false`; after 30 s the tool returned `status: "running"` with the "if you will receive a finish notification" message; the child finished two minutes later (`updatedAt 2026-09-05T16:13:36Z`, `attentionReason: "finished"`) and no `<paseo-system>` notification reached the parent. Full timeline in #4384.

**Tests, red on `main` (fix stashed, new tests only):**

```
npx vitest run src/server/agent/mcp-server.test.ts -t "timed-out wait|times out while the child"
     × arms a finish notification when a blocking agent-scoped prompt times out while the child is still running 20ms
     × returns the settled result instead of arming when the child finished during the timed-out wait 13ms
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 2 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
AssertionError: expected last "vi.fn()" call to have been called with [ 'child-agent', …(1) ]
      Tests  2 failed | 119 skipped (121)
```

**Tests, green with the fix (whole file):**

```
npx vitest run src/server/agent/mcp-server.test.ts --bail=1
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

The two new tests drive the real `waitForAgentWithTimeout` under fake timers: `waitForAgentEvent` stays pending until the tool's own 30 s abort fires, then the child is either still `running` (expects one `subscribe` for the child and the guidance text) or `idle` (expects no `subscribe` and a second, non-waiting `waitForAgentEvent` returning the settled result).

**Checks** (pre-commit via lefthook, all workspaces):

```
✔️ lint (0.23 seconds)
✔️ format (0.23 seconds)
✔️ typecheck (8.87 seconds)
```

Not verified against a live daemon after the fix: the only daemon on this machine is the production one that hosts the agents I would test with, and restarting it is off-limits.

### Checklist

- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run format` passes
- [x] QA evidence
- [x] Tests added or updated where it made sense

author: martinus
body:
Two gaps found while using `compare()` to sweep a parameter and plot the result.

## `render()` for a `CompareResult`

`templates::csv()` and its neighbours take a `Bench` or a `vector<Result>`, and neither carries a ratio or the interval around it — which is the whole reason to run a comparison rather than two independent benchmarks. A `CompareResult` could only be read by a human, out of the printed table.

So `render()` now takes one:

```cpp
auto const cmp = bench.compare("v1", f1, "v2", f2);
ankerl::nanobench::render(ankerl::nanobench::templates::compareCsv(), cmp, std::cout);
```
```text
"title";"name";"relative";"relative low";"relative high";"significant";"tied rounds";"rounds";"elapsed";"error %"
"benchmark";"v1";1;1;1;0;0;11;1.0293e-08;0.0091
"benchmark";"v2";1.4271;1.3702;1.4884;1;0;11;7.2126e-09;0.0083
```

The section is `{{#alternative}}`, and inside it `{{relative}}`, `{{relativeLow}}`, `{{relativeHigh}}`, `{{tiedRounds}}` and `{{significant}}` join everything a result tag already offers, so `{{median(elapsed)}}` and `{{title}}` keep working. `{{rounds}}` and `{{comparisons}}` work anywhere.

That gap cost me more than convenience. Wanting CSV out of a size sweep and finding only a printed table is what led me to hand-roll sequential timing loops instead — measuring each alternative to completion in turn — and the ratios were not reproducible: two runs of identical work disagreed by up to 140%. `compare()` was one call away and the easy path led away from it.

## `targetIntervalWidth()`

How many rounds a given precision needs depends on how noisy the machine is, so it cannot be written into a program that runs on more than one. The default 11 leaves the interval on a ratio about 25% wide, which cannot tell a 10% difference from nothing.

```cpp
auto bench = ankerl::nanobench::Bench().targetIntervalWidth(0.05).maxEpochs(500);
```

The width is in log space, which for small widths is the width of the interval as a fraction of the ratio, so `0.05` pins it to about ±2.5%.

### The statistics

`compare()` runs **two stages**. The first is `epochs()` rounds and only sizes the second; the second is reported, and the pilot's measurements are discarded.

That split is the point. Choosing the sample size from the same data the interval is computed from is optional stopping — it stops preferentially on the samples that happen to look tight, and the interval then covers less often than it claims. Deciding from data that is then thrown away leaves the second stage exactly as good as its confidence says.

Simulated over 4000 trials against skewed noise, asking for a width of 0.2 at a nominal 95%:

| rule | coverage | mean rounds |
|---|---|---|
| two stage, pilot then fresh | **96.0%** | 290 |
| naive, stop when it looks tight | **92.9%** | 143 |

The first is the sign test's usual slight over-coverage from discreteness; the second is an interval that quietly means less than it says.

The sizing rule is `detail::roundsForTargetWidth()`, a pure function: a sign-test interval narrows as `1/sqrt(n)`, so the count scales with the square of the ratio of widths. Being pure, it is tested against arithmetic rather than against a benchmark that would have to be noisy to exercise it.

A machine too noisy to reach the target within `maxEpochs()` stops there and reports the width it did reach, rather than running forever or pretending.

## Testing

- New unit tests for the sizing arithmetic, for the two-stage round count and cap, for the default staying exactly as it was, and for the render tags, sections and error paths.
- Both new behaviours are mutation-tested with `src/scripts/mutate/mutate.py`: breaking the `1/sqrt(n)` scaling, and letting the pilot leak into the reported result, are each caught by a named test.
- Green on gcc, on clang with the strict flag set (the leg that catches `-Wpadded`), and under the project's own sanitizer option.

The US English conversion in #47 exempted `fixtures/` by directory prefix, on the stated
grounds that every file under it is hashed into a manifest. That is not the case. Two
tracked files are covered by neither `MANIFEST.json`:

- `fixtures/neb/certificates.md`, which was already clean.
- `fixtures/README.md`, which carried `reserialising`, `catalogue` twice, `organisation`,
  and `Apache-2.0 licence` sitting next to a file named `LICENSE`. One of those was on a
  line #47 had explicitly set out to fix.

Neither is a recording. Both are the project's own writing that happens to live in the
directory the recordings live in, so the argument for freezing a recording never applied
to them.

`SpellingTests` now exempts a directory that a `MANIFEST.json` covers, rather than
anything under `fixtures/` — which is what its own remark already claimed it did. The
packs are read out of the tree, so a pack recorded later is exempt the day it arrives, and
prose that merely sits near one is not.

The recordings are unchanged and keep their British spelling, for the reason
`docs/releases/next.md` gives.

## Verification

Run against the unfixed README, the narrowed guard failed naming exactly those five lines
and nothing else; after the fix it passes. `StubId.Fixtures.Tests` passes its 1616 tests
including the manifest hash check, which is what confirms no recording was touched.

body:
💡 What: Fully vectorized the core routines (`_compute_equilibrium`, `_apply_forcing`, `_compute_macroscopic`) of the `FluidDynamicsEngine` using `np.tensordot` and broadcasting.

🎯 Why: The Lattice Boltzmann Method relies heavily on computations across all lattice directions (`self.q = 9` or `19`) for every spatial cell. Using explicit Python `for` loops inside the physics solver step creates massive interpreter overhead, severely restricting simulation sizes and frames-per-second. 

📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement is ~2x per optimized function (verified via local benchmark scripts: `_apply_forcing` dropped from ~0.61s to ~0.33s for a 100x100 grid). Reduces memory pressure by avoiding large intermediate array creations in the forcing step.

🔬 Measurement: Run fluid simulations (like `temp_benchmark_fd.py` earlier in trace) and compare `engine.step()` runtimes. Ensure `pytest tests/unit/ -v` passes completely, confirming mathematical consistency of the vectorization.

author: happy-ryo
body:
Propose-only design for the identifier allocator and the capacity ledger that `D-0012` says parallel admission waits on: `docs/design/parallel-admission.md`. No implementation; `DECISIONS.md` untouched; the entry the gate would create is referred to as `D-0023` by name only. Refs #8.

This is the rondo half of the pair whose continuo half landed today as `docs/design/parallel-laps-delivery-lease.md` (`D-1104`, propose-only). `P-13` there fixes the split: continuo owns partitioning, fencing and the two-run proof; rondo owns allocation, the capacity bound and suspend accounting.

## What the design settles

- **`awaiting_human` does not occupy capacity, and this is measured rather than argued (`N-2`).** The test is the design's own -- whether anything is still running (`src/store/records.ts:125-129`, `D-0019` rule 11). Measured: at `awaiting_human` the child process has exited (dogfood:905-906), continuo's delivery lease is released (`endpoint_lease.ts:343-354`), and no subprocess remains. So the schema's `live` (non-terminal) and the design's own test disagree on exactly the two statuses that account for `P-14`'s 83%. `stalled` alone means "unknown" and is held fail-closed.
- **Two bounds, and only one of them waits on continuo (`N-8`, `N-17`).** `maxOccupying` (actually executing) stays at 1 until `D-1104` takes *both* halves including `P-3`'s holder identity. `maxLive` (all non-terminal) **can exceed 1 today with no continuo change at all**, because a suspended iteration holds none of continuo's resources. This is what turns `P-14`'s 17% / 83% from a citation into something actionable.
- **The allocator and the ledger are one entry, not two (`N-1`).** Freeing an `awaiting_human` slot is only safe if something guarantees the next iteration is not handed the suspended one's identifiers -- which is the allocator's mint-and-remember. The dependency runs the other way from the obvious reading: without the allocator the ledger cannot choose the interesting answer.
- **Compatible with `A-17` of the advisory design (`N-7`).** Since a retry inherits its predecessor's `(run id, workspace, branch)` triple, the triple cannot be derived; it is carried on the row, with a second generated column reusing `R-10`'s shape B (`holds_identifiers`) so "released only when terminal and unspent" is a database invariant rather than prose.
- **The measurement `D-0012` demands cannot be taken in today's tree, so the design provides for taking it (`N-14`).** A capacity refusal writes no row (`interpreter.ts:176-186`; 1 ms in F-13), so demand is never recorded. F-13 gives the shape but not the count. A refusal row is made a precondition for raising the bound.

## Rejected alternatives, with what they cost

- **Slot table, rejected in favour of a counting predicate (`N-11`)** -- the issue's second checkbox requires the bound to be a policy value the ledger reads rather than a structural property of the schema. What the rejected option would have kept is stated plainly: with a slot table the invariant stays the database's, as `R-10` has it. The gate can take that trade instead.
- **`LoopPolicy`, rejected in favour of `HostPolicy` read once at the composition root (`N-12`)** -- `admit()` receives its policy per call (`interpreter.ts:124-128`), so a bound placed there would be "each request declaring a host-wide ceiling". Also states that `maxIterations` is a different number (one request's retry limit).
- **Retrying on `LeaseHeld`, not implemented (`N-20`)** -- `errorClass` is decoded and then dropped at the conductor boundary (`conductor.ts:102-111`), and rondo's own module says the class is a hint, not a taxonomy (`protocol.ts:42-44`). No retry is built on a hint; a stable refusal class is left as a question for continuo's gate.

## Deliberately left open

Ordered durable queue (→ `D-0020`'s surface), persisting the bound (→ `D-0020`), the loop's `iterate` back edge (→ rondo's gate, separate entry), ownership of who opens the connection and sets pragmas (a hole this design **exposes** rather than creates), and the `LeaseHeld` refusal class (→ continuo's gate). Each carries why it is out of scope and whose gate decides it (§9).

Claims that measurement **refuted** are recorded rather than dropped (§1.4): `artifactRoot` / `stateRoot` / `interlockRoot` look like identifiers but are already per-run on continuo's side, so they are not the allocator's business.

## Also in this PR

`docs/README.md` gains two design-index lines: one for this document, and one for `advisory.md`, which merged in #17 without an index entry. That drift is not cosmetic -- an audit today missed the existence of `advisory.md` and a duplicate design task was dispatched against an issue whose design had already landed. Being listed in the index is the cheap half of preventing that.

## Verification

`npm run verify` green (lint / knip / typecheck / 354 passed, 1 skipped). Codex review with `gpt-6-astra`, three rounds, all gates satisfied (succeeded 4/6/6, failed 0, exit 0), no finding repeated across rounds.

**Stated openly:** the review stopped at the round cap of three. Round 3's two findings are fixed, but no fourth round has seen those fixes. The next gate for this document is the human vote on `N-1`…`N-28`, not another review round.

Appendix A records the shape common to all three rounds: every finding was a set written down in two places that had drifted apart. No round refuted a recommendation itself.

author: javenciu
body:
## Problem / Motivation

#8904 (merged) ends pointer drags when capture is lost, so panes no longer stick to the cursor after a `lostpointercapture`. The Design Review thread on that PR flagged a residual: `lostpointercapture` can arrive with `clientX`/`clientY` of `0,0` in several engines, and the merged handler derives the commit payload from the event's coordinates. A capture loss mid-drag can therefore commit a corrupted delta (`dx` on the order of `-startX`) into consumers that persist their result, such as column layouts that write widths to storage.

## Why it matters

A user who drags a column and hits a capture loss (context menu, alt-tab, browser-initiated grab) can have a garbage width persisted, and it stays wrong across reloads until they re-drag. The corruption is silent: the drag just ends, and the bad value looks like a deliberate resize.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

The commit payload now always derives from the last tracked pointer position instead of the raw event coordinates. The tracker is refreshed from the event's coordinates immediately before payload derivation on every end path except `lostpointercapture`, so:

- `pointerup` / `pointercancel` behave byte-identically to today (the refresh makes tracker-derived and event-derived payloads equal by construction).
- `lostpointercapture` commits the last position actually observed (`pointerdown` or the latest `pointermove`), never the event's `0,0`.
- Pre-threshold moves are tracked too, so a capture loss during hysteresis ends at the true small delta rather than a fabricated one.

The single-fire re-entry guard (`active = false` before `releasePointerCapture`) is untouched.

## Tests

- Attack: capture loss at `0,0` after `down(100,100)` commits `x:100 y:100 dx:0 dy:0` (fails on main as merged with `dx:-100, x:0, y:0`, passes with this fix).
- Fresher-event: `down(100,100)` → `move(150,110)` → capture loss at `0,0` commits `150,110 / dx:50 / dy:10`.
- Pre-move capture loss commits at origin with `dx:0`, `committed:false`.
- Control: the normal `pointerup` path commits event coordinates unchanged.
- Full `src/hooks/` suite: 22 files, 260 passed at this head. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, `eslint` exit 0 on both changed files.

## Manual verification

Drag a column, trigger a capture loss (open a context menu mid-drag), release: the column keeps the width from the last real pointer position instead of collapsing toward zero, and the persisted value matches what was on screen.

## Screenshots / video

No visual delta: this changes which coordinates a drag-end computation reads, not any rendered output. Behavior is pinned by the attack/control tests above.

## Related Issues

Follow-up to #8904 (fix for #8271); implements the hardening surfaced by the Design Review thread on that PR.

## Pattern harvest

Event-derived commit payloads are only as trustworthy as the event: end-of-interaction events fired by the platform rather than the user (`lostpointercapture`, and by analogy blur-driven cancels) can carry sentinel coordinates, so any handler that persists a delta should derive it from tracked state and treat platform-fired ends as "commit what you last saw".

Rule candidate: when a handler family commits state on interaction end, review whether every end path derives its payload from user-observed positions rather than the terminating event's own coordinates.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added for the change (attack, fresher-event, pre-move, control)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`src/hooks/`: 260 passed)
- [x] Lint and typecheck clean (`eslint`, `tsc --noEmit` both exit 0)
- [x] One topic, minimal diff (2 files: hook + its test)

author: janwelker
body:
## Why

Reviewing a documentation change currently means reading the Markdown diff and picturing the rendered page. Admonitions, the Mermaid diagrams we keep adding, nav placement and the palette are all invisible until it is on the live site.

Every PR that touches `docs/` now builds the site and publishes it to `pr-preview/pr-N/`, and tears it down when the PR closes. The bot comments the link on the PR.

## The catch: previews need a branch

`rossjrw/pr-preview-action` publishes into a subdirectory of a Pages branch. That only works when Pages is sourced from a branch, and this repo currently serves Pages from the Actions artifact path (`upload-pages-artifact` / `deploy-pages`). The two modes are mutually exclusive, so the live deploy moves to `gh-pages` as part of this.

`docs.yaml` therefore loses the two-job artifact dance and hands `site/` to `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action` instead. Same build command, same triggers. Two details that matter:

- **`clean-exclude: pr-preview/**`** — without it, every push to `main` would wipe the previews of all open PRs.
- **`.nojekyll` at the root** — a branch-sourced Pages site is run through Jekyll, which silently drops paths it considers private.

## No base-path handling needed

Zensical emits relative links (`./quickstart/`, `./assets/...`) and the theme derives its runtime scope from `location`, so a build made for the site root also works unmodified from `/pr-preview/pr-N/`. The only absolute URLs in the output are `<link rel="canonical">` and the sitemap, which keep pointing at the live site — that is the behaviour we want, since it keeps previews out of search results.

## Scope of the trigger

The preview runs on `docs/**` only. A PR that edits `zensical.toml` (the nav) or `overrides/` changes the rendered site too but gets no preview; `docs.yaml` triggers on all three. Easy to widen later if that gap bites.

Fork PRs are skipped rather than failed — they run without the write access the deploy needs.

## Before it works

Once this merges, the first `docs.yaml` run creates `gh-pages` and the root `.nojekyll`. Then **Settings > Pages > Source** has to be switched to *Deploy from a branch: `gh-pages` / `/`*. Until that flip the site keeps serving the last Actions deployment and preview URLs will 404.

   - 게임 시작 시 페널티를 선차감하는 `RankService.startRankGame`에서 `calculateMMRDecrease`에 `originalRating`을, `calculateRatingDecrease`에 `originalMmr`을 넘기고 있었습니다.
   - 두 함수 모두 첫 인자로 기대 승률과 `getPenaltyMultiplier` 배수를 판정하므로, mmr과 rating이 벌어진 유저는 페널티가 뒤바뀐 값으로 적용됐습니다. (mmr 1600 / rating 1400, 퍼즐 1400 → 정상 1593/1398, 버그 1595/1396)
   - 기존 테스트는 `TestUserFactory`가 두 값을 같게 만들어 스왑이 드러나지 않았습니다. 값을 다르게 세팅한 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다.

2. **추천 정렬 추가**
   - `GET /api/community/puzzle`의 `sort`에 `RECOMMEND` 추가
   - 정렬 키 `abs(puzzle.rating - user.mmr) + mod(crc32(concat(id, '-', seed)), 600)` 오름차순, 동점은 `id` 오름차순. MMR에 가까운 퍼즐이 앞에 오되 600점 미만 차이는 seed로 섞어, 난이도 적합성은 유지하면서 매번 같은 목록이 나오는 것을 막습니다.
   - `shuffleSeed` 파라미터 추가 (미전달 시 `0`). 같은 seed면 순서가 고정되어 커서 페이징 중 목록이 흔들리지 않습니다.
   - LATEST/LIKE와 달리 오름차순이라 커서 조건을 별도 분기 — `score > cursorScore OR (score = cursorScore AND id > cursorId)`
   - MMR이 필요해져 `searchCommunityPuzzles(request, Long userId)` → `(request, UserEntity user, long seed)`로 변경
   - Testcontainers MySQL 테스트 5개: seed 결정성, 다른 seed 재셔플, MMR 근접 우선, 커서 페이징 전수 방문, int 범위 초과 seed

3. **업로드 24시간 제한**
   - `POST /api/community/puzzle`에서 최근 24시간 업로드 수를 검사하고 초과 시 `EXCEED_DAILY_PUZZLE_UPLOAD`(429 / `P429`) 반환. 한도는 `community.puzzle.daily-upload-limit`, 기본 50
   - `countByAuthorSinceIncludingDeleted`는 삭제된 퍼즐까지 셉니다. 업로드 후 삭제로 한도를 우회하지 못하게 한 것이고, 소프트 삭제 필터를 우회해야 해서 네이티브 쿼리를 썼습니다.
   - 자정 리셋이 아닌 롤링 24시간 (`clock.instant().minus(24, HOURS)`)
   - 테스트: 한도 도달 시 `save` 없이 예외, 카운트 윈도우 시작점 검증

4. **에러 메시지·주석 영문화**
   - `ErrorCode` 전체 메시지 (코드/HTTP 상태는 유지), request record 30여 개의 validation 메시지, Swagger 설명, 인라인 주석
   - `GetCommunityPuzzlesForCacheRequest.java`는 CRLF → LF 정규화가 겹쳐 전체 파일이 diff에 잡혔지만 실제 변경은 메시지 3줄입니다.

5. **테스트 네이밍 통일**
   - 한글 `@DisplayName` 제거, 메서드명을 `대상_When조건_Then결과`로 통일 (12개 파일, −143/+48)

### 💡 생각해볼 문제
- `crc32`/`mod`를 `numberTemplate`으로 직접 넣어 MySQL에 종속됩니다. DB 교체 시 이 쿼리는 다시 써야 합니다.
- `RECOMMEND`는 계산식 정렬이라 인덱스를 타지 못하고, 커서 조건도 서브쿼리로 커서 행의 점수를 매번 재계산합니다. 퍼즐 수가 늘면 실측이 필요합니다.
- `RECOMMEND` 커서 페이징은 seed 고정이 전제입니다. 페이지마다 다른 seed가 오면 중복·누락이 생기는데 서버가 막지는 않으니 클라이언트와 협의가 필요합니다.
- `RECOMMEND_JITTER = 600`은 경험값이라 실제 MMR 분포를 보고 조정이 필요할 수 있습니다.
- 업로드 제한은 요청 시점 카운트라 동시 요청 시 한도를 약간 넘길 수 있습니다. 남용 방지가 목적이라 락은 걸지 않았습니다.

author: rxdu
body:
Makes quickviz build and test on macOS, and fixes several latent issues found along the way. Most are **not macOS-specific** — Linux masked them.

## Portability fixes

- `object_feedback_handler.hpp` included `<GL/gl.h>` **unguarded**, unlike `mesh.cpp` and `opengl_capability_checker.cpp` which already select glad. macOS ships OpenGL as a framework and has no `GL/` directory, so this was a hard compile error. Guarded the same way, and taught the existing non-glad branches to use `<OpenGL/...>` on Apple so `VIEWER_WITH_GLAD=OFF` works there too.
- glad's vendored `khrplatform.h` sat in `include/glad/`, so `<KHR/khrplatform.h>` resolved on Linux **only because Mesa happens to install `/usr/include/KHR/khrplatform.h`** — an undeclared dependency on a system package. Moved to `include/KHR/`, glad's own standard layout, so the vendored copy is used everywhere. **This makes the Linux build depend on less.**
- glm was never referenced by CMake at all; it resolved implicitly because Ubuntu's `libglm-dev` installs into `/usr/include`. Added `find_package(glm)` and `GLM_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL`, which glm >= 1.0 requires for the GTX extensions the renderables use.

## Build plumbing (both latent, neither macOS-specific)

- `gtest_discover_tests` enumerates cases by **running each test binary at build time**, with a 5 s timeout. These binaries link GL, cairo and optionally OpenCV/PCL, and where those ship as many small shared libraries the dynamic loader alone exceeds that. Discovery then times out and **CMake deletes the executable**, surfacing much later as a baffling `<target>_NOT_BUILT` ctest failure. Switched to `PRE_TEST` discovery.
- OpenCV and PCL export their whole dependency prefix onto the include path. Where a system googletest exists there, its headers were found ahead of the vendored copy **while the vendored `libgtest.a` still linked** — an ABI mismatch appearing only as undefined `testing::internal` symbols. The vendored include dirs are now prepended.

## PCL loader: validate the header, not just the return code

`LoadPCDInternal`/`LoadPLYInternal` treated a load as successful whenever PCL did not return `-1`. PCL does not honour that: given garbage, **1.15 logs "number of points is zero", defaults HEIGHT, reports x/y/z unmatched, and returns 0**. Non-point-cloud data loaded silently as an empty cloud.

The header is the reliable signal, and the check keys on it **rather than the point count for a specific reason**: a malformed file and a legitimately empty one both yield zero points, so rejecting on emptiness would break valid `POINTS 0` clouds. Every PCD/PLY readable into a PCL point type declares x/y/z, and that stays true when the cloud is empty.

Applied to all four load paths. `AnalyzeFields` is deliberately untouched — it answers *"what fields does this file have"*, and all-false is a legitimate answer.

Two tests: `InvalidPLYFileError` (the fixture built a garbage `.ply` that nothing asserted on) and `EmptyButValidPCDLoads`, which pins the distinction the fix rests on so it cannot later be "simplified" into a point-count check.

**Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 ship PCL 1.12/1.14 and have not hit this yet. They will on the next PCL bump.**

## CI lane

`macos-14` (arm64), AppleClang + libc++, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`. The GUI itself is **not** exercised — there is no automated suite for it and the samples need a display, so only compilation and the non-GUI tests are covered.

## Verification

macOS 15 (arm64): **123/123 tests pass**.

Known, pre-existing and untouched: the `PCLLoaderTest` fixture shares a temp directory, so it races under `ctest -j` (9 failures parallel vs 0 serial). Both this lane and the existing Ubuntu lanes run ctest serially, so it is latent on Linux too.

body:
## v0.3.13 final biome-authority fix

- moves the strict COMMON-biome cleanup into the completed BIOMES-stage palette writer, where generated chunks are actually finalized
- prevents the later chunk postprocessor from undoing the stricter Frostmarch / Greenveil / Sunscar / Harvestwood identity rules
- applies the finite Aquamirae Ice-Maze belt at the same authoritative stage, so frozen/deep-frozen ocean cannot reappear beyond the configured final-destination radius
- removes the old postprocessor behavior that treated every northern Dread ocean as Ice-Maze territory forever
- mirrors the regional fallback hardening in the final palette writer so an unavailable target cannot silently leak back to generic Forest/Plains
- leaves native Tectonic terrain density untouched

This closes an ordering hole discovered while auditing v0.3.12: the completed-chunk postprocessor executes after MultiNoise biome selection and therefore must own the final regional contract.

author: hanthor
body:
## What

Element X reads its to-device traffic, key counts and device-list changes, account data, receipts and typing through the sliding-sync extensions (MSC4186) and nothing else. Serving them on classic sync alone leaves the flagship client unable to decrypt a message, and the response's `extensions` was `{}`. This is the first unchecked group on #112.

- Each extension is switched on by name in the request, stateless like the rest of the endpoint.
- **to_device** carries its own `since`: a to-device message is acknowledged by the token that delivered it, not by `pos`, so a client restarting its sliding sync from nothing keeps what it has decrypted, and one that lost its E2EE state can ask again.
- **e2ee** is the three things classic sync carries at the top level: `device_lists`, one-time key counts, unused fallback key types.
- **account_data**, **receipts** and **typing** answer for every room in view, changed or not. A receipt or a typing change bumps no stream position, and with no record of what a client was last told, repeating a window's worth is the answer that cannot silently drop one. A private receipt is shown to its owner and nobody else. With typing on, a change in who is typing ends the long-poll, as it does for classic sync.
- The MSC's per-extension `lists`/`rooms` scoping is not honoured; the module doc says so. An enabled room extension applies to every room in the response.
- `Rooms::room_receipts` reads a room's receipts back out of the keyspace `set_receipt` writes them into, which nothing did before.

## Validation

```
sliding_sync: 17 passed (11 existing, 6 new: one per extension and the empty default)
clippy -D warnings: clean; fmt: clean; dashboard and README checks pass
```

Bugün **plan**, kod yarın (OPS hükmü: kapıya bugün dokunulmaz — benim #1050 beklerken kapıyı değiştirmek *kendi işini geçirmek için gevşetme* görüntüsü verirdi).

## Emrin öncülü ölçümle düştü
- Atlama **zaten var ve çalışıyor**: bir belge-only PR *Canceled by Ignored Build Step* ile geçti.
- Depoda **vercel.json yok** — ayar panelde. Emir olmayan bir dosyayı işaret ediyordu.
- İş yeniden tanımlandı: *atlama kur* değil → **mevcudun KAPSAMI + rate-limited kolun kapıda nasıl sayılacağı**.

## Ölçülenler (salt-okuma, kota harcanmadan)
1. Vercel sonucu **check run değil, commit status** → GitHub rerequest ucu yok; bu kol **push'suz yeniden tetiklenemez**.
2. **Limiter, atlama adımının önünde**: belge-only push yine rate limited aldı, Ignored Build Step'e hiç gelmedi.
3. **Reddedilen istek dağıtım kaydı yaratmıyor** → kotaya maliyet **sıfır**. *Belge-only ucuz* maliyet olarak doğru; *PR'ı yeşilleştirir* anlamında **yanlış**.
4. Sınır o an **hesap geneli değildi** — aynı 20 dakikada başkalarının push'ları dağıtıldı. **Sebep ölçülmedi, ad konmadı.**
5. Hacim: ~2 saatte **20 dağıtım** (~9/saat), **PR başına en az 2** (dal + master).

K8 kapsamındaki PR'da sınıf **uygulanmaz** (önizleme şart, kırmızı kalır) · yalnız belge-only PR'da ÖLÇÜLEMEZ · rate-limited **dışındaki** her Vercel hatası eskisi gibi **kırmızı** · sınıf Vercel'in kendi metnine bağlanır ve metin bulunamazsa **fail-closed kapanır**.

body:
## ① 入力済みの可視化（依頼: 「入れたかどうかが後から分かりにくい」）

- **折りたたんだレース一覧の見出しに `🐎13` バッジ** — 開かなくても一覧でどのレースを入れたか分かる
- 🐎ボタン自体も **「🐎 パドック ✓13頭」** に変わり、枠線が付く
- GAS の `getNotesLog` を起動時に**1回だけ**叩いて race_id 単位で集計（1レース1リクエストだと34回叩くことになるため）
- 保存直後は再取得せず `bumpPadCover` でその場で反映
- ⚠ 取得に失敗しても画面は止めない（印が出ないだけ）

直近48時間ぶんに絞って引くので、蓄積が進んでもページ読み込みは重くなりません。

## ② 🔴 race_notes.date が JS の Date.toString() 形式で入っていた

本番の `race_notes` **210行すべて**がこうなっていました。

```
race_notes      'Sun Sep 06 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0900 (Japan Standard Time)'
bets            '2026-09-06'
shadow_bets     '2026-09-06'
displayed_bets  '2026-09-06'
```

GAS がスプレッドシートのセルを Date オブジェクトとして返すため、`getNotesLog` 経由の date がそのまま保存されていました。**この列だけ日付で結合できない状態**で、2026-08-31 に `shadow_bets.was_recommended` が全683行0だった（`bets.date='2026-08-30'` vs `target_date='20260830'`）のと同じ型です。

- `normalize_note_date()`: ISO形式 → JS形式のパース → race_id先頭8桁 の順に解決
- `save_race_notes()` が保存時に正規化

author: accelas
body:
Explicit PDE grids could be silently replaced during table construction, odd-grid adjustment could exceed a caller's maximum, and numeric reuse cutoffs repeated the same normalized PDE without improving its accuracy. This change preserves explicit grids and strict ceilings, validates numerical configuration, and bases shared solves on the existing model/group eligibility.

Closes #487. Nonblocking gate under #483, stacked on #489 (`test/math-review-red`); merge that prerequisite first. Approved contract: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-483-agent-handoffs/487-grid-policy.md` on integration PR #490.

Validation and evidence:
- RED/GREEN regressions cover explicit-grid fidelity, odd point ceilings, invalid configuration, and shared-versus-regular pricing on wide, coarse, and narrow-margin grids.
- The initial full run passed 148/151 targets. The three affected failures were corrected; their seven affected targets passed. Final reuse changes passed all four affected targets. A final combined full-suite run remains pending; this PR stays draft until that validation and review finish.
- Python/Rust builds passed on the final source. Relevant manual benchmark builds also passed. The pre-existing `cubic_spline_template_vs_hardcoded` benchmark cannot build because its `cubic_spline_nd` dependency is missing.
- Matched 20-contract call/put cases produced identical prices with 20→1 PDE solves: approximately 26–31 ms→1.27–1.81 ms for coarse/narrow grids on the measured host.
- Grid-default characterization did not justify globally changing clearance or clustering defaults: improved cases came with substantial cost and some regressions. Those defaults remain subject to the declared accuracy contract.

This does not broaden model eligibility or add maturity cohorts. Shared and regular routes use the same resolved numerical constraints and PDE validation.

author: kimptoc
body:
Closes #50

Adds the Steam client to the CodeClub live CD via `programs.steam.enable`.

What this does
- Installs the Steam client (plus `steam-run`)
- The NixOS module enables 32-bit OpenGL (`hardware.graphics.enable32Bit`), required by many Steam games
- Installs Steam hardware/controller udev rules
- `remotePlay`/`dedicatedServer`/`gamescopeSession` left at defaults — no firewall changes

Things to weigh before merging
- **Image size**: Steam + 32-bit Mesa grow the xz-squashed ISO noticeably. Worth one test ISO build to confirm it stays within practical ISO/USB limits.
- **No persistence**: this is a plain live CD/USB, so Steam re-downloads its client update each boot and games cannot be stored. Real use needs a writable setup or club accounts.
- **Audience**: the Steam storefront/community presumes 13+ accounts; only the client is bundled (no games).

author: andrianm28
body:
Reviews and builds on the SumopodProvider base-URL work. That work was right about the biggest problem — the sandbox host was hardcoded with no deployment override — and found something an offline audit could not: **SumoPod validates return URLs server-side and rejects non-public hosts**, which is why `SUMOPOD_RETURN_BASE_URL` has to exist separately from `PUBLIC_WEB_URL`. Verified against the real sandbox. Good catch, kept as-is.

Two things it left open.

## The one that matters: an unset host was not an error, it was the sandbox

`SumopodProvider` defaulted `baseUrl` to `https://api-pay-sandbox.sumopod.com`, and `getSumopodProvider()` only passed a base URL when one happened to be set.

The audit's own verifier argued this fails loudly, reasoning that a production key against the sandbox would be rejected. That's true — but it's the wrong pairing. The pairing that is actually live is a **sandbox key with the variable forgotten**, and that combination does not error at any point:

1. the charge succeeds against the sandbox
2. the donor is sent to a sandbox payment page and pays nothing real
3. the sandbox webhook fires and **verifies**, because the sandbox secret is the one configured
4. the donation is marked `paid`
5. `collectedAmount` goes up

A public campaign page then shows money that never moved. No error, no log, nothing to notice.

**Fix: the host is required, not defaulted.** Every environment states which SumoPod it is charging, in writing. The dev `.env` now says sandbox explicitly. That costs one line and removes the entire class.

## The second: the gate knew about one variable out of three

```ts
if (SUMOPOD_WEBHOOK_SECRET) methods.push("qris_redirect");   // before
if (!sumopodConfigError())  methods.push("qris_redirect");   // after
```

With the secret set and `SUMOPOD_API_KEY` missing, QRIS was offered, the charge sent `X-Api-Key: ""`, SumoPod answered 401, and the donor got **"Gagal memproses donasi. Silakan coba lagi."** — the exact never-can-work wall PR #40 removed, re-entering through a different door. That combination was live in the dev `.env` at the time of review.

`sumopodConfigError()` now names the specific missing variable, and `getSumopodProvider()` checks the same three conditions — the webhook route reaches it without passing the menu gate.

## Tests

Four new gate tests, in fresh subprocesses because these are module-load-bound (the same necessity the base-URL fixture documents). Two of the existing base-URL tests **asserted the sandbox default** and are rewritten: an unset host now refuses the charge with 503 rather than quietly aiming it at the sandbox.

Guard verified by putting the default back → **3 fail**; restored → **43 pass**.

Whole repo: lint clean · typecheck exit 0 · **409** backend · **208** web · **47** ui.

## Found while reviewing, NOT fixed here

**`NODE_ENV` is not set on the production host.** Confirmed by reading the running process's environment. `auth.ts:26` gates the session cookie's `secure` flag on it, and the comment right above that gate says it exists because every cookie write was previously missing `secure`, letting *"the 30-day session token travel over plaintext HTTP."* A missing variable has quietly reopened exactly that. It needs `NODE_ENV=production` in `.env.production` and an API restart — a host change, outside this PR, and one I did not make unprompted.
