author: evengul
body:
Closes MCO-490. The last step of the switchover: the additive scorer has decided nothing in production since #451, so it goes, along with everything that existed only to measure it.

**−1481 lines, +169.**

## The eight constants, and why each is now redundant

| constant | why it is gone |
| -- | -- |
| `RECIPROCAL_PENALTY` (13) | Pack/unpack loses arithmetically: an ingot from a block costs `effort/9 + (1/9)·c(block)`, the block costs `effort + 9·c(ingot)`. Its hand-swept **[11,15]** admissible window — the clearest sign the model had run out of room — goes with it. |
| `SELF_BLOCK_LOOT_PENALTY` (200) | `selfCost` makes breaking what you placed cost the item *plus* the breaking, which is strictly worse than any other route. |
| `LOW_YIELD_PENALTY_WEIGHT` + `_CAP` | Dividing by expected yield **is** the penalty — 0.33 sticks per witch kill costs three kills. Both were measured **unpinned by any test**: 0 and 200, 5 and 500, all passed. |
| `DEPTH_PENALTY` (5), `REQUIREMENT_PENALTY` (10) | Proxies for the summed chain cost the model sums directly. Depth was a flat `d1` on **96 of 98** real candidates — a constant wearing a metric's clothes. |
| `RECIPE_THRESHOLD_BONUS` + `PlanContext.recipeThreshold` (100) | MCO-522 measured it: 0 losses on 1.21.4, 0 movers on 26.2.0. |
| `EFFICIENCY_WEIGHT` (20), `SUPPLIED_BONUS` (30) | Output/input ratio with its two carve-outs; supply is now simply cost 0. |

## Deleted with it

`ScorerMutation`, `ScoreDiagnostics` (engine + CLI), the `score-diagnostics` exec entry, and `cost-diagnostics`' `factors`, `demands=` and comparison modes.

`RankingModel.LEGACY_SCORE` and `PlanSelector.legacyRank` go too. They were added in #451 for exactly one purpose — keeping the comparison honest across the switchover — and that purpose is spent.

**`cost-diagnostics`' default mode is now `why`.** There is no second model left to diff against, so every mode measures the one model on its own terms — the shape MCO-520 already had to give `sweep` for the same reason. `DEFAULT_WHY` was already the item set written for it.

## What survives, deliberately

**`isSelfBlockLoot`** — moved to its own file in the first commit. MCO-490's audit turned on separating tuning from *knowledge about the game*, and this is the knowledge: costing self-block loot as circular unconditionally priced `acacia_log` at 25.7 min and lost it to a chest, because breaking an acacia log is how you get one. `PlanSelector.acquirable` still needs it, and a class named for a scoring model was always the wrong address.

## Tests

- Two pure-scorer expectations go with the bonus they pinned (MCO-496's firing/withheld pair).
- Two were coupled to `ScoreDiagnostics` but had substance worth keeping, so they were **rewritten, not dropped**. The notable one is the zero-margin stick tie: crafting and breaking leaves used to score *identically*, and the planner picked crafting only on the recipe-first tie-break. Under a cost model that is no longer a tie — four sticks from two planks beats a leaf block outright — so the test now asserts crafting wins **on cost**, which is a stronger claim than the one it replaces.

mc-engine **225** (was 227: −2, 2 rewritten) · mc-web **1201** · mc-data **368** · mc-nbt **48** · database tier **609**. `mvn clean compile` clean, and the CLI verified end to end against world 3 and 26.2.0.

## Docs

Both `CLAUDE.md` files updated — the restricted-area rule now names `UnitCostModel` and `EffortTable` rather than `SelectionScorer`, and mc-engine's tool section documents `cost-diagnostics`' modes with the MCO-524 warning attached: **an `INERT` or "no plateau" verdict is a claim about the version, not the constant.**

The third commit is docs only, and worth a glance: `UnitCostModel`'s header still opened *"A sketch… **Nothing calls this in production.**"* — true when written, the exact opposite of true now that it is the only thing deciding where anything comes from. Plus the KDoc links the deletion left dangling, which Kotlin does not fail a build on and nothing else would have caught.

author: cargopete
body:
Last of four batches for nuthatch#1160, following #92, #93 and #94. After this, `rg GRAPH_API_KEY src scripts` finds two comments saying a module does not use it, and nothing else.

## What goes

- `lib/subgraph.ts` (`subgraphQuery`, `delegationEventsQuery`, `hasSubgraphAccess`) and its test. Nothing imported it any more.
- `lib/graph-network.ts` keeps the subgraph id and the explorer link the payments page renders; the gateway origin and the two URL builders go, with their tests.
- `api/feed`'s epoch summaries came from the nest behind `NUTHATCH_FEED` or from the Graph Network subgraph through a client of its own. Nest only now; without a nest the feed simply has no epoch items. `feed-epochs.ts` loses `SubgraphEpoch` and `fromSubgraphEpoch`; the parity test that compared the two shapings now pins the nest shaping to the summary it always produced.
- `nuthatchEnabled(flag)` is gone from `lib/nuthatch.ts`. The routes that were still behind a plain flag with no gateway behind it (`dips`, `dips/agreements`, `check-dips`, `check-dips-chain`, `warm-ipfs`) ask `hasNuthatch()` instead, which is the question the flag was standing in for.
- `.env.example` and the README's variable table drop the key; `docs/nuthatch-migration.md`'s last checkbox is ticked and rewritten, because the board's 2026-09-05 decision superseded its "the key stays configured" position.

## What happens in Vercel after this deploys

Once production is serving on this commit: `GRAPH_API_KEY` is removed from every environment, and so are the eighteen `NUTHATCH_*` per-surface flags (nothing reads them any more; `NUTHATCH_URL`, `NUTHATCH_USER` and `NUTHATCH_PASSWORD` stay). That is the proof #1160's done-state asks for - the dashboard serving with the variable absent - and it is recorded on the issue when it has been done.

## Tests

171 files, 2,234 tests, `tsc` clean, the coverage gate met. Several test files still carry a `vi.mock('@/lib/subgraph', …)` factory for a module that no longer exists; vitest tolerates it and they are inert. They can go in a tidy-up, not here.

author: murlockwarlock
body:
## Summary

Implements Plan v1.2.0: **"Welcome vs Resume UX + Immediate AI Kickoff"** across Telegram and MAX messengers.

### Key Changes
1. **Welcome vs. Resume UX**:
   - **First Entry**: Displays the topic welcome message (if configured), sets durable technical marker `DBMessage(role="topic_welcome", content="shown")`, and triggers kickoff if `auto_start_dialogue` is true.
   - **Resume**: Re-entering a topic never repeats the welcome message; instead, it immediately triggers the hidden AI resume kickoff (`build_topic_resume_system_message(topic_name)`).
2. **Return to Main UX**:
   - Idempotent if already in Main dialogue.
   - Outputs exactly `✅ Мы вернулись в общий режим диалога.` (no static `start_message`).
   - Immediately triggers hidden AI kickoff (`build_main_dialogue_resume_system_message()`).
3. **Technical Role Isolation**:
   - Technical marker `topic_welcome` is strictly filtered out from:
     - AI dialogue context history across all memory modes (TOPIC, GLOBAL, RESET).
     - Admin client history views in Telegram and MAX.
     - Single client exports (TXT/JSON) and mass exports (TXT/JSON).
     - Client activity metrics and outer join calculations.
4. **Scope Validation**:
   - Pre-call and post-call scope validation across Telegram and MAX: validates `(dialogue_id, topic_id)` matches user's active state before calling AI provider and after provider returns.
   - Stale/interrupted navigation cleanly drops discarded turns with zero DB or UI contamination.
5. **Kickoff Persistence**:
   - Hidden AI kickoffs are never persisted as `DBMessage(role="user")`.
   - Assistant responses are saved under captured `(dialogue_id, topic_id)` scope.

### Test Coverage
- `tests/test_welcome_resume_journey.py`: 25 comprehensive tests covering all 12 user journeys.
- Full regression test suite (181 tests) passing cleanly.

author: lucasruan1618
body:
# What does this PR do?

This PR adds **video-to-video support for Wan2.1** through the Diffusers modular pipeline.

The new `WanVideoToVideoBlocks` workflow:

- encodes an input video into Wan VAE latents;
- selects the denoising schedule from `strength`;
- adds noise to the encoded video at the selected timestep;
- denoises with a Wan2.1 T2V transformer; and
- decodes the result back into video frames.

The implementation supports both official Wan2.1 T2V checkpoints:

- `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`
- `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-14B-Diffusers`

Wan2.1 I2V checkpoints are not compatible because their transformers use a different image-conditioning input interface.

## Example

```python
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from diffusers import UniPCMultistepScheduler, WanVideoToVideoBlocks
from diffusers.utils import export_to_video, load_video


MODEL_ID = "Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-14B-Diffusers"
INPUT_VIDEO_URL = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/diffusers/hiker.mp4"
OUTPUT_PATH = Path("wan_modular_video_to_video_14b.mp4")

pipe = WanVideoToVideoBlocks().init_pipeline(MODEL_ID)
pipe.load_components(dtype={"vae": torch.float32, "default": torch.bfloat16})
pipe.update_components(
    scheduler=UniPCMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config, flow_shift=3.0)
)
pipe.to("cuda")

video = load_video(INPUT_VIDEO_URL)
videos = pipe(
    video=video,
    prompt="Change the video style to anime, with hand-drawn cel shading, expressive details, and vivid colors",
    negative_prompt="Bright tones, overexposed, static, blurred details, subtitles, low quality",
    height=480,
    width=720,
    strength=0.7,
    num_inference_steps=25,
    generator=torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(42),
    output="videos",
)

export_to_video(videos[0], str(OUTPUT_PATH), fps=8)
```

For lower-memory GPUs, replace `pipe.to("cuda")` with `pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload()`.

## Testing

- Adds modular pipeline loading and memory tests.
- Adds output parity coverage against the native `WanVideoToVideoPipeline`.
- Manually validated `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-14B-Diffusers` at 480x720 on a 48 GB RTX 6000 Ada GPU.
- The manual run produced 49 frames at 8 FPS without CPU offloading.

## Self-review

**Verdict: READY**

### Resolved blocking issues

1. **CUDA batch consistency.** `WanVideoVaeEncoderStep` now forwards the pipeline generator to `encode_vae_image`, preserving per-sample VAE encoding when a generator list is supplied. The intermediate `video_latents` are now identical between single and batched execution. The test uses the existing Wan-specific `2e-3` tolerance for small CUDA differences introduced by later model and decoder operations. (`src/diffusers/modular_pipelines/wan/encoders.py:621`)
2. **Invalid spatial dimensions.** The VAE encoder now rejects heights and widths that are not divisible by 16 before preprocessing or denoising. Regression coverage checks invalid height and invalid width independently. (`src/diffusers/modular_pipelines/wan/encoders.py:604`)

### Non-blocking issues

1. **Clarify the pre-generated `latents` API.** The assembled pipeline advertises optional `latents`, but `video` and `video_latents` remain required. A latent-only call fails with `Required input 'video' is missing`, while passing both performs an unnecessary VAE encode before ignoring `video_latents`. Confirm the intended modular API with the reviewer. (`src/diffusers/modular_pipelines/wan/before_denoise.py:645`)
2. **Add user-facing documentation.** This introduces public `WanVideoToVideoBlocks` and `WanVideoToVideoModularPipeline` APIs without a corresponding usage page or example under `docs/` or `examples/`. Per `.ai/review-rules.md`, new public behavior should update usage documentation.
3. **Use the standard mapping helper.** `_wan_v2v_map_fn` always returns one class and can use `_create_default_map_fn("WanVideoToVideoModularPipeline")`, as prescribed for checkpoint variants in `.ai/modular.md`. (`src/diffusers/modular_pipelines/modular_pipeline.py:110`)

### Dead-code analysis

| Path | Status | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wan/encoders.py`: `WanVideoVaeEncoderStep` | Used | Included by `WanVideoToVideoBlocks`; produces `video_latents`. |
| `wan/before_denoise.py`: video-to-video timestep and latent steps | Used | Included by `WanVideoToVideoCoreDenoiseStep`; their outputs feed the Wan denoising loop. |
| `wan/modular_blocks_wan_v2v.py`: blocksets | Used | Exported publicly and selected by `WanVideoToVideoModularPipeline`. |
| `modular_pipeline.py`: `_wan_v2v_map_fn` | Used but redundant | Referenced by `MODULAR_PIPELINE_MAPPING`; the standard constant mapping helper can replace it. |

No likely-dead inference path was found. This PR adds pipeline blocks rather than a new model, so there is no new model `forward` path to trace.

### Validation performed

- `pytest tests/modular_pipelines/wan/test_modular_pipeline_wan.py -k VideoToVideo -q`: **22 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Ruff on all ten changed source and test files: passed.
- `utils/check_forward_call_docstrings.py`: passed.
- `utils/modular_auto_docstring.py` on the new blockset: up to date.
- Public import smoke test and `git diff --check`: passed.

**Fix before submitting:** none. **Leave for the actual review:** agree on latent-only behavior and documentation scope.

## Before submitting

- [x] Did you use an AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) to help with this PR? If so:
  - [x] Did you read the [Coding with AI agents](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/conceptual/contribution#coding-with-ai-agents) guide?
  - [x] Did you run the [`self-review`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/.ai/skills/self-review/SKILL.md) skill on the diff?

author: yeroo
body:
The agliteterm half of parity batch **P4** (agwinterm #238, contract #240). Plan: `docs/plans/completed/2026-09-06-p4-lite-mirror.md`. Four verbs on one subsystem — a session's two panes — and the rule that ties them together. **The swap is implemented, not deferred** (the batch index and `lite-parity.md` had left that to this plan).

## The vocabulary (agwinterm's, copied not re-decided)

`vertical` = left/right panes (lite's only layout until now, the default of a session never split); `horizontal` = top/bottom. **A slot is a position, an id is a shell**: slot 0 is the left/top box, slot 1 the right/bottom; `primary|left|top` name slot 0, `split|right|bottom` slot 1. **A swap moves panes, never ids.** The session-id rule, by condition: a session id names the session's own shell while it exists; **whenever that shell is the one that closes** — whatever closed it (`split close` on it, the close chord on it, any slot-1 close after a swap, its process exiting) — the surviving shell **becomes the session** (same id, name, workspace, flag, context, sidebar row; its own pane id kept) and the id names it. The one thing a promotion does not survive is a kill-and-relaunch: the `D` line records shells, so the survivor is adopted by its shell's id and comes back under it (revmux r1). A promoted session's node carries `paneIds` (`[<its shell's id>]`) so the shell's own agent can find its session (revmux r2).

## What changed

- **`session split [on|off|toggle] [--axis vertical|horizontal] [--target ID]`** — every reply is a pane id: `on` = slot 1's id (also when already split — after a swap that is the session's own shell), `off` = the survivor's (also when already single), `toggle` = whichever it produced. `--target` is honoured for the first time (a session id, either pane's id, a prefix, a name; a cover refused); a non-displayed session can be split without moving focus (#230); an unknown op is refused, not a toggle; `--axis` on a split session re-orients it live.
- **An axis per session**, consulted in one place for geometry (`paneRect`) and one for paint (the divider); `hitTest`, the grid sizes and the caret follow through `paneRect`.
- **The tree's split block**: `paneCount`, `paneIds` (slot order), `focusedPane` (a slot), `axis` — agwinterm's keys. `paneCount`, `focusedPane` and `axis` are present exactly when split; `paneIds` is present exactly when the session's pane ids are not simply `[id]` — split, or a promoted single session, whose node carries `paneIds` alone (`[<its shell's id>]`, no `paneCount`; revmux r2 — `paneCount` is the split discriminator in both products). A node is `active` when the displayed session is it whichever pane has focus, and the sidebar row highlights the same way (with the split focused, nothing read active or highlighted before).
- **`session split close [--target ID]`** — closes EITHER side. Closing the session's own shell is a **promotion**: the hidden shell's object takes the session's identity and place in the list; its pane id stays (`Session::paneId`, set once in `attachSession`, never written again). No `ClosedSpec`, no `session closed` event — the session is still there — a `tree` event. One primitive, `closeSplitSide(owner, closeOwner)`, behind `split off`, `toggle`, the close chord (now the focused PANE, either side), `session close` on the split shell's id, and a split side's process exit (`WM_APP_PANEEXIT`; a one-pane session's exit still shows `(exited)`). Refusals: unknown target, cover, one-pane session naming `session close` — agwinterm's sentences.
- **`session swap [--target ID]`** — one flag on the owner, read where the panes are laid out and hit-tested; reply `{session, paneIds, focusedPane, axis}` from the same builder the tree uses. `g_focus` indexes owner/split, so the focus follows the pane with no code.
- **`session focus [primary|split|left|right|top|bottom|other]`** — new verb; the wrong pair refused naming the axis; a one-pane session refused. The two focus keys and palette rows are slot-based ("Focus Left / Top Pane").
- **The `L` line** — `L <S-idx> <axis> <0|1>` after the `P` lines, written only when a split's layout is off the default (so a vertical unswapped tree writes the P3 bytes), validated per field (a bad word restores vertical / order 0, named in the log), dropped without its `P`, refused wholesale with the `P` guard. A 0.17.14 reader ignores it (unknown line types are ignored), so a downgrade loses the layout, not the split. `K` stays by role.
- Every structural change emits `tree` — including the unsplit path, which emitted nothing before.
- Because the pty-host knows a shell by its pane id, resize and kill now key on `paneId` (after a promotion `id` names another shell).
- Contract refreshed with `-Update` (51 steps, 11 errors — #240's file); `check-contract` in step. README (48 verbs), the shipped skill (the splits section is the vocabulary + the rule + the four verbs), `docs/state-file.md`, `qa/panes.md` (three new cases + `qa/fixtures/layout-restart.ps1`).

## Deliberate divergences (for agwinterm's `docs/lite-parity.md`, a docs PR after this merges)

- agwinterm's session id names the FOCUSED pane while no pane carries it; lite's always names the session's own shell (no per-session pane resolution) — the split's shell is reached only by its own id.
- `session close <split shell's id>` closes that shell (an unsplit) in lite; agwinterm answers `session not found` for a pane id. Pre-P4, in lite's favour, unchanged.
- Ids are fresh after a graceful restart (as everything in lite); the `L` line puts axis and order back onto the recreated pair.
- A promoted session's node carries `paneIds` alone, with no `paneCount` — so in lite the presence of `paneIds` does not imply a split (`paneCount` does, in both products). agwinterm reaches the same state (closing the carrier pane keeps the session; its env vars are per pane too) and emits nothing for it; lite's key exists so the survivor's own agent, whose `AGWINTERM_SESSION_ID` is no node's `id`, can find its session's node — a lookup agwinterm's skill has no recipe for.
- After a kill-and-relaunch a promoted session comes back under its SHELL's id (the `D` line records shells, not promotions; adoption re-mints `id = paneId`). The one exception to the session-id rule; a graceful restart has no promoted sessions to keep (ids are fresh).

## Validation

- `test/run-all.ps1 -Strict` with the dev `agwintermctl` (agwinterm `main` at `dc0a2c6`): **twelve suites green** — 693 PASS at `57d4abc`, 699 after the r1 fix, **706 PASS, 0 SKIP, 0 FAIL** after the r2 fix (`5089ae9`); the matrix's 56 cells pass (54 + `promote-killed`, `axis-relive-killed`).
- With the released CLI every P4 step SKIPs (the `$cliHasP4` probe: `session swap x` → "Nothing sent" client-side, no pipe) — **this PR's CI is red by construction until agwinterm tags the release that carries #238 + #240** (0.17.13), the P3-lite gate again.
- `qa/fixtures/layout-restart.ps1`: horizontal split, a ping in each shell, `restore capture`, `swap`, the file read (`P 1` / `L 1 horizontal 1` / `K 1 <own> <split>`), the window **killed** and relaunched — block `horizontal`, `paneIds:[<fresh split>, <own>]`, each captured slot on the shell that ran it, both ids answer `session text`, the file re-written the same. 20/20 killed, 20/20 `-Graceful`.

![restored horizontal swapped split](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yeroo/agliteterm/feat/p4-lite-mirror/docs/img/qa-p4-layout-restart.png)

Harness fix along the way: `restore-matrix.ps1` now scrubs `AGWINTERM_SESSION_ID` / `AGWINTERM_PANE_ID` / `AGWINTERM_PIPE` like conformance does — run from inside an agwinterm pane its untargeted split calls aimed at the developer's own pane.

## Review rounds (revmux, `--min-confidence 60`; a fix commit gets its own narrow round)

- **r1** (`01-initial`, the whole branch at `57d4abc`): 2 Major, 8 Minor, 1 Pre-existing, 1 Immaterial. Both Majors the same shape — a pre-P4 site using `id` where the shell's id (`pa

body:
The broader HYGD audit found reproducible weighted-loss aggregation, segmentation-target encoding, clinical-import and temperature-optimizer defects. Add separately identified v6 checkpoint selection using global weighted CE, strict PAPILA parsing, 0/1 mask normalization, hash-bound inference/parity, a bounded positive temperature fit and fresh-output guards. Clarify BatchNorm adaptation, upstream anatomy exposure, contour unions and the distinct LEACE fitting maps.

A complete fixed v6 run selected the same epochs and produced byte-identical OOF CSVs as v5: mean-fold group AUROC 0.9908 [0.9790, 0.9990], confusion 97/3/4/179. This is a correctness repair, with no performance gain or new clinical/transportability claim. Actual PAPILA labels, historical CEXT/Shortcut Map point estimates and manual geometry metrics were reconciled without rewriting their source artifacts.

Validation: 121 local tests pass. The actual 99-image parity check passes at max difference 2.77e-6. All 970 inspected RIM-ONE masks use 0/255; the production dataset path now supplies 0/1 to BCE. Twelve synthetic temperature fits match an independent oracle within 1e-7 NLL, including a former boundary failure. Separate NumPy formulas reproduce all 5000 v6 bootstrap draws and probability scores. Eight execution-source hashes match the pre-run lock. Add CPU Torch/OpenCV CI so those integration checks are executed alongside the core suite. No raw data, row predictions, weights, new target or mixed-source retraining are published.

The full Git tree at 91c43caf102e81dd7efe88dc21b0588b2df65091 exactly matches the locally tested candidate; all 37 publication SHA-256 checks pass.

author: jwloka
body:
`.gitattributes` named `board-server.mjs` alone while `build.mjs` grew eight more outputs, and none of them arrived here.

**Measured 2026-09-05**, rebasing `feature/a-story-lifecycle-refuses` onto main:

```
board-server.mjs      0 conflict markers   (marked -merge)
plot-ask.mjs          5 conflict markers   (NOT marked)
plot-registryd.mjs    3 conflict markers   (NOT marked)
```

A spliced marker makes a bundle invalid JavaScript that is still committable and pushable, in a file nobody is meant to read a diff of. Four branches hand-resolved the same three bundles while this plan sat in Draft.

## What changed

**All nine `build.mjs` outputs are marked `-merge`,** and the comment block says the list is the build's output rather than one file.

**`scripts/check-bundle-attributes.sh` derives the set from `build.mjs`** — the `shippedX = path.join(…)` declarations — and fails when one is unmarked. This defect was born the way a prose reminder fails, so the fix is a gate: CLAUDE.md's test asks whether you can answer *did I complete this?* without doing the work, and a note asking the next author to remember a list fails it. A list inside the gate would be a second place to forget.

It reads `git check-attr` rather than grepping for the path, so a later line that unsets a mark is not read as marked.

**`plot-monitor.mjs` is not marked, and the reason is in the comment.** It appears in no `outfile`, so nothing rebuilds it — and the deterministic rebuild is the entire licence for `-merge`, since *take either side, then rebuild* is safe only where the rebuild overwrites what was kept.

## Nine, not eight — the gate found one the plan had not

The brief counted eight, verified 2026-09-06. **`plot-landed.mjs` arrived with #706 the same day**, after the count was taken. The derivation demanded it; a hand-written list would have shipped the identical hole under a new filename, one day old. That is the argument for deriving the set, measured on itself.

## Proof

A merge conflicting in every bundle, run against this `.gitattributes`:

```
plot-ask.mjs         0 markers
plot-registryd.mjs   0 markers
plot-landed.mjs      0 markers
plot-monitor.mjs     3 markers   (deliberately unmarked)
```

The two files that took 5 and 3 markers now take zero. `plot-monitor.mjs` behaving as before is the exclusion working, not a gap.

`test/reconcile/bundle-attribute-gate.test.mjs` proves the refusal on a deliberately added tenth output — a gate nothing tests is a gate that passes because nobody looked. It also pins the derivation, the `plot-monitor.mjs` absence, the `check-attr` read, and a build whose declarations the gate cannot find, which is an error and never a pass.

## Tests

- `pnpm test` — pass
- `pnpm run typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm run test:reconcile` — 1260/1260
- `pnpm run test:board` — 2825/2825 across 152 files
- the four sibling declaration gates — clean

The bundles rebuilt byte-identical, which is the deterministic-rebuild property the licence rests on.

Slice 1 of two. `plot-resolve-artifact.sh`'s set is slice 2 and is untouched here.

author: bascht74
body:
Second batch of the collapse: **59 sites in `resolve` and `cut`**. 52 `group_text` become `number_text(n, 0)`, 4 `decimal_text` become `number_text(x, 1)`, 3 keep `decimal_text` on purpose. The entry keeps both old helpers -- other pieces still call them.

**Measured over all 59 sites, both languages, against a pristine copy of the commit this branches from: no site's text changes.** The proof loads two whole programs and puts the values the instrumented run actually recorded through the helper each site actually used.

## The float question, all 52

`group_text` truncates and `number_text(n, 0)` rounds, so the swap is exact only where the argument is an `int`.

- **38 measured.** A scratch copy logged `(call site, argument type)` on first sight per type; the whole suite ran through it. Every one an `int`.
- **15 read at the producer** -- `len()`, a `+= 1` counter, `GetTrackCount()`.

Two that look like floats and are not: one-argument `round()` returns an `int`, and `s // 60` has `s = int(round(...))` above it.

**One soft spot, read not measured:** seven sites take Resolve's own `GetTrackCount()`. Nothing here can force that call to answer with an `int` -- but the code around it puts the same value in `range()`, which would fail first.

## Three sites keep `decimal_text`, and not because of a ceiling

`"%g"` carries a **variable** number of places by design: 30 prints as `30`, 29.97 as `29,97`, 23.976 as `23,976`. No fixed `places` reproduces all three. A scratch copy with `number_text(rate, 0)` turns `project_amounts_grouped` **red** -- the line becomes "Gemessen wurden 30 Bilder/s … genommen wird 30", and the measured 29.97 the sentence exists to report is gone.

The third of them prints a number the user is told to **type into Resolve by hand**, and three lines below, the same `"%g"` string is what gets set. A thousands mark in a number somebody is about to type is a defect.

**A correction to what I was told:** there is no 240 cap on the measured frame rate. `fps_measured` is `round(fps, 4)` of whatever the container reports, and nothing clamps it. The case for keeping these sites rests on `"%g"`, not on a bound.

## Two findings, reported not repaired

**The `Hz` contradiction is five sites, not two.** `metadata:84` and `metadata:666` print the raw sample rate as `48000 Hz`; `resolve:1217`, `material:2209` and `preflight:619`/`627` group it as `48.000 Hz`. Same number, same language, three of five grouped. Not decided here -- it needs one rule for all five.

**A gap in `project_amounts_grouped_test.py` section 3.** The check is `"29,97" in rates and "29.97" not in rates`. A copy printing `29,970` stays **green**, because `29,97` is a substring of it. So the check catches a lost decimal place but not a gained one. Left alone: no judgement moved there, and touching it would owe a fresh counter-proof.

The counts in the order were low again: resolve has **32** `group_text` not 29, cut **20** not 17 -- `grep -c` counts lines, and three lines carry two calls.

**No check added and none reworded, so none is owed** and `tests/state/counterproof` is untouched. Suite: 251 green, 1 skipped, 0 red, no traceback.

body:
The deep catch-up E2E (`testFreshChildJoinerCatchesUpThroughCarrierOnlyHistoryAcrossChurn`, added in #86) mines ~120 real parent blocks to reach the retarget window — the only way to produce the carrier-only rounds it needs — which is ~16 min of unavoidable CPU mining, plus a full deep sync across a serving-node restart. On 3× CI runners sharing a 90-min E2E budget it times out, and has now blocked unrelated PRs (#89, #90, #92 twice) — a correctness-passing but resource-heavy test taking down the merge gate for everything.

Gated opt-in via `LATTICE_E2E_DEEP_CHURN=1` (the codebase's established heavy-test quarantine pattern), for on-demand and nightly runs. It stays fully runnable and is still the acceptance gate for the sync architecture; the fixed sync path is also exercised by the other, lighter E2Es on every PR.

body:
## Scope
Execute I007 as a candidate-zero measurement on exact I006-closed main `dd15a956e52e9bc04fe103c62163c6cfa870b57b`.

This does **not** reuse or merge the stale `research/bf-hard-mic-fault-discovery` or `feat/bf-wind-health-bypass` candidates. Those branches are regression/test-design history only.

## Fresh development matrix
3 fresh deterministic seeds × 8 scenarios × 2 frontend-equivalent partitions = 48 measured partitions:
- healthy control
- broadband soft wind on either mic
- mild phase mismatch on either mic
- asymmetric reverberation on either mic
- moving TDOA sweep `-2..+2` samples
- both `bf-only` and `hpf-bf`

Revision 1 is retained as measurement-attribution lineage only because moving-TDOA quality was scored with one fixed alignment and wind was too tonal. Revision 2 fixes both without changing seeds, scenarios, frontends, RMS, or frozen gates. Its pre-I006-closure exact-main replay (`34023281489`, artifact `9986228358`, digest `3a939ed3...`, independently verified `509/509`) removes all motion failures: motion and phase-mismatch pass on all partitions. Remaining failures are isolated to wind and asymmetric reverberation.

The current rerun is rebound to `dd15a956...` so final archival authority matches the latest reviewed main after I006 closure.

## Authority boundary
- candidate limit `0`
- confirmation limit `0`
- no shipping DSP/API/default change
- no coherence/ratio/roughness threshold tuning
- no candidate ranking
- no promotion/release authority
- Product Qualification remains `DEFERRED_BY_SCOPE`

A measured acoustic gap is retained as successful evidence and transitions only to review; infrastructure/contract/oracle failures remain fail-closed.

body:
This pull request addresses the issue where the photos UI table was displaying the collection ID instead of the collection name. The following changes were made to resolve this:

- **Database Changes**: Added Row Level Security (RLS) policies for the `collections` table to allow public read access.
- **Data Layer Updates**: Modified the `getPhotos()` function to include a join with the `collections` table, ensuring that the collection name is fetched alongside the photo data.
- **UI Adjustments**: Updated the dashboard to display the collection name instead of the ID in the photos table. Added a collection selection feature in the Edit Photo modal.
- **New Components**: Introduced several new components for managing collections, categories, and cameras in the dashboard.
- **Styling Improvements**: Enhanced the overall UI for better readability and user experience, including adjustments to the background color and text visibility.

These changes ensure that the photos UI table correctly displays the collection names, improving the usability of the dashboard.

body:
### Motivation

- Make controller construction explicit about artifact ownership and remove the speculative one-variant sink abstraction so no output path is invented implicitly.
- Add builder parity for `mode` and normalize public template vocabulary to `mode`/`output_path` while preserving correct reload/fallback semantics.
- Flatten the controller TOML shape to a truthful, minimal contract and update docs/validators to the new shape.

### Description

- Replaced the public `ControllerSinkTemplate` / `sink_template` + `selected_mode` with concrete `output_path: PathBuf` and `mode: CaptureMode` on `TailtriageControllerTemplate` and `ControllerActivationTemplate`.
- Made the builder record an optional `output_path: Option<PathBuf>` and added `TailtriageControllerBuilder::mode(CaptureMode)`; removed the public `new(...)` constructor so canonical construction is `TailtriageController::builder(...).`
- Added a private immutable `BaseControllerTemplate` to retain builder-origin base values so `reload_config()` resolves sparse TOML correctly back to builder bases; implemented the exact output/mode precedence matrices and a transactional missing-output validation.
- Flattened TOML parsing so `controller.activation` accepts `output_path: Option<PathBuf>` and `mode: Option<CaptureMode>` and `run_end_policy` is a flat string; removed the nested `[controller.activation.sink]` and tagged `run_end_policy` table support.
- Added `ControllerBuildError::MissingOutput` and a narrow `ControllerTemplateError::MissingOutput` (mapped during build/reload) and `ConfigLoadError::MissingOutput` for standalone loader behavior.
- Updated generation helpers to derive per-generation artifact file names from the resolved `output_path` and preserved explicit core boundary by passing the generated artifact path to `Tailtriage::builder(...).output(&artifact_path)`.
- Updated tests, examples, README, docs, CHANGELOG, and the docs-contract validator scripts to the new flat TOML contract and to forbid reintroduction of removed public surfaces.

### Testing

- Ran unit tests: `cargo test -p tailtriage-controller --all-targets --all-features --locked` and `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked`; all controller and workspace test suites passed (controller tests: 65 passed, 0 failed; workspace tests: all passed).
- Ran docs validators and policy tests: `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_validate_docs_contracts` and `python3 scripts/validate_docs_contracts.py`; the updated validator tests and contract validation passed.
- Ran invariant checks and public-example smoke tests: `python3 scripts/validate_invariant_proofs.py` and `python3 scripts/smoke_public_examples.py`; both passed and smoke examples produced and validated artifacts.
- Ran lint/build checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps --locked`; these completed successfully.

All focused resolution and reload tests (builder/TOML output/mode matrices, sparse-reload transactional missing-output behavior, and mode precedence cases) were added/updated and passed.

author: danimon10
body:
Hasta ahora, para hablar con alguien había que estar en la casilla de al lado **y** mirándole. En cuanto quedabas en diagonal o a un paso de más, el botón de acción no hacía nada y tocaba recolocarse. Y a quien atiende un bar, una tienda o un despacho no se le podía hablar desde el lado del cliente: había que rodear la barra hasta la única casilla libre que le quedaba al lado.

## Qué cambia

**Un radio pequeño alrededor de la persona.** Cuando no hay nada justo delante (ni objeto, ni puerta, ni cama, ni tablón), el botón de acción habla con quien ande a `RADIO_NPC` pasos — dos, una sola cifra que se puede subir o bajar. Al hablar de lejos los dos se giran, para que no conversen de espaldas.

**Son pasos andando, no distancia en línea recta.** `npcCerca()` va abriendo anillos por casillas libres, así que una pared no deja hablar al otro lado, ni se habla con quien está detrás de otra persona.

**Un mostrador sí deja hablar.** Al topar con un mueble de `ASOMABLES` —barras y mostradores, escritorios, mesas, vitrinas, sillas y taburetes— se mira quién hay justo detrás en línea recta: es apoyarse en el mostrador. Las estanterías, las máquinas, los armarios y las puertas siguen tapando. En el claustro las letras significan otra cosa (árboles, muros de contención), así que allí la lista es aparte y solo se salva el banco.

**Con dos personas a tiro, el radio se apaga.** Elegir por el jugador sería adivinar a cuál quería, así que manda el trato de siempre: ponerte delante de quien sea y mirarle. El aviso `!` acompaña la regla — salta sobre la persona a la que llega el radio, y desaparecer es justo la señal de que hay dos y toca acercarse.

Las puertas y los objetos siguen pidiendo estar justo enfrente, sin cambios.

## Lo que se desbloquea

Los 11 mostradores y los 13 escritorios del juego, desde el lado del cliente: kiosco, panadería y taquilla de la estación, tiendas del EKZ, cafetería del Audimax, la barra de Nora, la taberna Gmoa, recepción del Sportzentrum, las dos bibliotecarias y toda la administración (secretaría, gerencia, finanzas, los despachos de los profesores).

En total, el radio da conversación desde **1391 casillas** del juego y solo se apaga en **17**, repartidas en mensa2, vg_notas, vg_registro, niko_patio, ekz1 y wh_salon. La más vistosa: plantado entre las dos cajas de la mensa, las dos quedan a tiro por encima de su escritorio, así que el `!` desaparece y hay que ponerse delante de una.

## Comprobado en el navegador

- `node --check` sobre el `<script>`; validador de mapas sin banner rojo; sin errores de consola en ninguna prueba.
- **Barrido de todo el juego** (exterior + 84 salas): 1406 configuraciones con pared o armario en medio, **ninguna** deja hablar al otro lado; 1036 con mueble de asomarse, **todas** dejan.
- Los 44 casos reales de «persona detrás de un mueble», uno a uno; los 8 con estantería, fotocopiadora o pared siguen mudos.
- End‑to‑end con teclado: Max a dos casillas en la Innwiese, kiosco de la estación, taquilla, taberna, y las dos cajas de la mensa (antes y después de ponerse delante de una).
- **Ningún NPC queda incomunicado**: todos siguen siendo hablables de frente desde la zona a la que llega el jugador.
- Segunda implementación de la búsqueda, distinta, dentro del test: coincide con `npcCerca()` en cada casilla del juego.
- Regresión: puertas, recoger objetos, las 84 salas dibujando sin excepciones.
- Mando táctil con eventos reales (CDP), en vertical (390×844) y horizontal (844×390).

El mapa no se toca, así que `plano-campus-passau.png` no hace falta regenerarlo.

author: asyrawih
body:
Akar masalah "release masih pakai API": sejak #65 frontend produksi dimuat dari `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, yang bagi ACL Tauri adalah origin **remote**. Command aplikasi tidak punya izin untuk origin remote, jadi **setiap `invoke` ditolak** (`ping not allowed. Plugin not found`) — `isTauri` true, halaman normal, tapi tidak ada satu command pun yang jalan: kepustakaan, Roblox, model, dan SoundCloud (yang lalu tampak "memakai API" karena health-nya gagal).

## Bukti
Halaman probe di build debug yang melapor balik lewat server loopback:
- sebelum: `isTauri=true, isolated=true, ping=ERR: ping not allowed. Plugin not found`
- sesudah: `ping=pong, soundcloud_json(/health) → {status:200, body:{mode:"in-process"}}`

Sekaligus bukti pertama langsung dari WebView produksi bahwa `crossOriginIsolated=true` (engine `mt`) di jalur loopback.

## Isi
- `build.rs`: `tauri_build::AppManifest::commands(COMMANDS)` → izin `allow-/deny-<slug>` untuk 48 command. `permissions/autogenerated/` di-gitignore.
- `capabilities/default.json`: `allow-<slug>` untuk semua command (bersama `remote.urls: ["http://127.0.0.1:*"]` yang sudah ada).
- Tes kontrak baru: `COMMANDS` di build.rs == `generate_handler!`; capability memuat `allow-` tiap command + origin loopback. Lupa satu baris → merah di CI, bukan `.app` yang bisu.

## Verifikasi
`cargo test -p daw-desktop-host` 131 (+2), `daw-desktop` 10, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, `cargo tauri build --debug --no-bundle` + probe di atas.

author: maverivk
body:
Two issues on the admin side of the Bulletin Board (`/configuration/WebBulletinBoard`).

## 1. Upload Video modal invited repeat clicks

The modal stays open for the whole upload (which is slow for a video) with nothing disabled, so impatient clicks fired multiple uploads.

- `handleUpload` sets a `mediaUploading` flag for the duration of the request and returns early if it is already set.
- While it runs: submit handler no-ops, both modal buttons + the file input are disabled, the primary button reads **Uploading...**, and an "Uploading video, please wait..." line shows.
- Mirrors the existing `mediaDeleting` pattern on the delete-video modal.

## 2. Announcements: manual date/time, no category or pin

**Removed** the Date and Time inputs from the create and edit modals. They are now automatic, like the mobile app:

- `inputAnnouncement` stamps `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and `time` (`HH:MM`) from the server clock in the school timezone (`config/appTime` `TZ`) when the client omits them. An explicit value is still honoured, so the mobile app (which still sends them) is unaffected. The schema keeps `date: required` and it is always satisfied.

**Added** to both modals:

- **Category** dropdown — `Events / System Updates / Achievements / Reminders`, the same list the mobile form uses.
- **Pin this announcement** checkbox.
- The edit modal keeps a posts current category as an extra option when it is not one of the four (e.g. legacy `General`), so opening + saving an old announcement cant silently change its category.

**`updateAnnouncement`** is now an explicit partial update over `title/description/category/pinned` only, in a try/catch. It no longer spreads arbitrary `req.body` into the document, and a blank date/time can no longer overwrite the required field. The pin toggle from mobile (`PUT` with just `{pinned}`) still works.

**Existing Announcements table** gained a **Category** column and shows a pin glyph (lucide `Pin`) before the title of any pinned announcement.

## Safety / blast radius

- Public kiosk `BulletinBoard.jsx` is untouched. It reads `a.date` / `a.time`; both are now always populated (server-stamped), and its `a.date || formatDate()` / `a.time &&` guards already tolerated missing values anyway.
- Mobile create/edit/pin flows unchanged and still supported by the controller.
- `node -c` passes on the controller; timezone formatter verified to emit `2026-09-06` / `16:49`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Upload a large video, click Upload repeatedly -> exactly one upload; buttons disabled; modal closes on success.
- [ ] Create announcement with only a title -> succeeds; list + kiosk show todays date.
- [ ] Create with category + pin checked -> row shows pin glyph and the chosen category.
- [ ] Edit a legacy announcement (category `General`) -> `General` preselected and preserved on save; can switch to a listed category.
- [ ] Toggle pin from the mobile app -> still works.
- [ ] Rapid double-click Add/Save in the announcement modals -> single request.

author: johnnyt
body:
`core.invoke`'s `assign_to` was declared `type: :string` with no path annotation while `emit/2` wrote an `<assign expr="_event.data" location="...">` from it. A path the block really writes was therefore invisible to ADR-0011 decision 2's write signature and to ADR-0005 clause 11e's undeclared-path advisory, and the field offered no candidate list. It is `{:path, %{}}` now.

The same change carries ADR-0011 decision 13's argument to the two refusals its deferred list names, and folds `sb-3j9u`: the refusal's *shape* is now written once for all four `<assign>` location fields.

## What changed

| Site | Declaration | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `core.invoke`'s `assign_to` | `:string` -> `{:path, %{}}` | `identifier?/1` -> `datamodel_path?/1` |
| `StatifierBlocks.InvokeStep`'s `assign_to` | moduledoc example only (a host declares the field) | `identifier?/1` -> `datamodel_path?/1` |
| `core.subchart`'s `assign_to` | unchanged | unchanged (`sb-xk1h` already widened it) |
| `core.map`'s `collect` | unchanged | unchanged - still a bare lowercase identifier |

All four now go through `StatifierBlocks.Core.AssignLocation` (`@moduledoc false`), which owns the shape three copies had each spelled themselves: a blank value passes and emits nothing, a value the field's rule accepts passes, anything else is one finding anchored on the field's own key (ADR-0005 decision 11). The rule and the wording stay with the field, because they are not the same rule at all four sites.

## Why `core.map`'s `collect` was not widened

ADR-0009 decision 4 decides that field's grammar outright - "`assign_to` keeps the one grammar it already has: a bare lowercase identifier ... There is no per-item path grammar and no dotted form" - of the field that ships as `collect`. Widening it is an amendment to *that* record, on that record's own argument, and nobody ruled it. Doing it here on the strength of ADR-0011's argument would be exactly the sweep-by-implication decision 13 declined to make. The deferred question therefore closes for two of its three members and stays open for one, with the owner named in the record.

## Records

Two dated Notes, amend-by-addition, `git diff origin/main -- docs/adr/` at the branch head is **103 insertions, 0 deletions** (45 in ADR-0002, 58 in ADR-0011):

- **ADR-0011**: the deferred item "The other three bare-identifier refusals on an `<assign>` location" is answered for `core.invoke` and `InvokeStep`; the flip Note's reading 6 ("still in place, still deferred") is historical for two of the three; and the field is now an input to decision 2's write signature. No decision moves.
- **ADR-0002**: the 2026-08-28 amendment's section D table declares `assign_to` as `:string` and is to be read as `{:path, %{}}`; the 2026-09-06 writes table's `core.invoke` row ("none | none | its `<assign>` location is emitted rather than declared, so nothing here sees it") is replaced by a row given in the Note; and G15's "the same words `core.invoke` and `core.subchart` produce" sentence is to be read as naming the refusal's shape, since the three wordings diverged in two steps (`sb-xk1h`, then this).

## Verification

Machine-checked on this branch, no plan artifact having run (`backlog.rb` reports 0 documents), so each acceptance criterion was checked against the live artefact:

- **Declared as a path**: `Invoke.config_schema(%{})`'s `assign_to` is `{:path, %{}}`, `BlockType.datamodel_path?/1` true.
- **The environment sees the write**: `Environment.write_signatures/3` returns `[{"assign_to", "cards.authorization", :unknown}]`; the block after it reads `:unknown` at that path.
- **The 11e advisory covers it**: with a datamodel declaring only `cards.settlement`, `Datamodel.findings/3` returns an `:info` finding anchored `{:config, "blk_INV", "assign_to"}` reading "cards.authorization is not declared in the datamodel". It produced nothing before.
- **A dotted location survives to the bytes**: the compiled SCXML carries `<assign expr="_event.data" location="cards.authorization"/>`.
- **One helper, four sites**: eight call sites across `core/invoke.ex`, `invoke_step.ex`, `core/subchart.ex`, `core/map.ex` - each site's `validate_config/1` check and its `emit/2` re-check.
- **No new public surface**: `git diff origin/main -- lib/` adds no `def`/`defmacro` to any existing module; the one new module is `@moduledoc false` with `@doc false` on both functions, as `StatifierBlocks.Core.Config` is.
- **Records**: 0 removed lines under `docs/adr/`; neither new section carries a `Status` line, and each opens on its own record's precedent wording - ADR-0002's on "A dated Note rather than an amendment", ADR-0011's on "A dated note rather than an amendment." (that record uses the lowercase form).
- Full `mix quality` green on the rebased HEAD: 2,254 tests, 95.7% coverage, dialyzer clean.
- Ten sabotage mutations were each applied to a copy, run, confirmed red, and reverted from the copy - one per new or reworded `# sabotage:` note.

## Provenance

- Bead `sb-r313` (campaign 033, lane A), filed by the campaign 032 conductor (D30-3) from the `sb-u7zt` worker's finding on PR 289. Folds `sb-3j9u` (the shared refusal helper across the four sites); that bead closes as folded.
- **Rebase over a sibling**: rebasing onto `9a1d22c` conflicted in `docs/adr/0002-block-type-behaviour.md`, which `sb-ae12`'s merged PR #301 declares it appends a Note to. The conflict is additive - both sides append a new `## Note (2026-09-06)` section at the foot of the file and neither rewrites a line of the other - so it was resolved keep-both, PR #301's Note first, and the full gate was re-run on the rebased HEAD.
- `core/subchart.ex` and `core/map.ex` are not in the bead's file map for `subchart`'s part, but the bead names all four sites and the helper is only shared if all four call it; both edits are behaviour-preserving at those two sites (same predicate, same message).
- `StatifierBlocks.InvokeStep.check_assign_to/2`'s doc no longer points a host at `check_identifier/4` for a required `assign_to`: that helper applies the identifier rule, which `assign_to` is no longer. The sentence now says a step requiring the key adds its own refusal of the blank, and names `check_identifier/4` for fields whose rule really is a bare identifier.

## Cures

**Pass 1** returned QUALIFIED with two NON-BLOCKING RECORD-PROSE findings, both cured at `490811b`:

1. The ADR-0011 Note attributed two line citations (`core/invoke.ex:299`, `invoke_step.ex:430`) to the flip Note's reading 6, which carries no citations - they sit in reading 7's "still resolve exactly" list - and said they now land on the shared helper's call sites, which they do not: neither line holds a refusal or a call. The paragraph now names both readings, quotes each, and points a reader at `AssignLocation` by name.
2. The ADR-0002 Note cited section D by its 2026-08-29 acceptance date; this record cites amendments by heading date, so it now reads "section D of the 2026-08-28 amendment". The quoted row is unchanged.

**Pass 2** (fresh cold reviewer, scope-frozen) verified both cures and returned QUALIFIED with one NON-BLOCKING BODY-ONLY finding: this body's insertion count was stale after the cure. Corrected above; no record or code line is involved.

## Residue, for a follow-up bead rather than this PR

`ADR-0009` is the owner of `core.map`'s `collect` and this PR deliberately does not touch it. Two of its sentences are now half-stale in the same way ADR-0002's G15 sentence was - its 2026-09-05 Note ("keeps the same finding text so an author meets one complaint and not two") and its 2026-09-06 Note ("whether the two fields should agree is named there as a deferred question rather than answered") - and `collect` now carries the candidates-vs-validation mismatch ADR-0011 decision 13 called "a defect either way round" for `core.subchart`: it is declared `{:path, %{writes: {:list, :unknown}}}` while its rule stays a bare lowercase identifier. body: `dev` `401f077` → `main`. **PR 일곱 건이고 이슈는 #372 · #374 · #375 · #377 · #378 · #379 · #380 · #381 여덟이다.** ## 왜 지금 올리는가 **계약이 크게 움직였다.** 프론트 CI 는 **기본 브랜치**(`main`)의 `docs/openapi.yaml` 을 보므로, `backend` 에만 두면 같은 코드가 로컬과 CI 에서 정반대 이유로 실패한다. - **새 오퍼레이션 둘** — `readDraftImage` · `readReviewImage`. 승인 전 이미지를 서버가 중계한다 - **새 스키마 셋** — `ImageObjectKey` · `CoverImage` · `PortraitImage`. `ManuscriptCharacter.portraitImageKey` 도 늘었다 - **`coverImage` 의 뜻이 바뀌었다** — 승인된 UGC 작품은 이제 **서명된 URL** 이 온다. 그 전까지 그 자리에 있던 것은 객체 키였고 화면은 그것을 `` 에 넣어 **UGC 커버가 전부 깨지고 있었다** - **원고 `payload` 의 상한 설명** — `flags` 의 `maxItems` 는 진짜 상한이 아니고, 챕터·엔딩에 새 개수 상한이 생겼다. 넘기면 `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` 이며 화면이 그 응답을 그릴 자리가 필요하다 ## 무엇이 들어가는가 | 이슈 | PR | 무엇 | |---|---|---| | **#377** (P1) | #387 → `caea384` | 승인 전 이미지를 **서버가 중계**한다. 게이트(S-4)·열람 감사 안에 머문다 | | **#378** (P1) | #389 → `d8b96bd` | 승인된 커버·초상을 **서명해서** 낸다. 공식/UGC 는 `author_type` 으로 가른다 | | **#372** (P1 safety) | #386 → `c6b1743` | 사후 검수가 **인물과 상태 어휘까지** 읽는다. 활성 세션이 고정한 옛 버전도 | | **#379 · #380** | #385 → `304885e` | L1 이 **한 표기**를 쓰고, 원고가 검수 한 번의 크기를 정하지 못한다 | | **#375** | #388 → `58dddba` | **`OUTPUT SPEC` 이 연산자 표기의 정본**이 된다 | | **#381** | #384 → `0d0dc94` | 한 턴의 `state_schema` 를 하나로 만든다 | | **#374** | #390 → `87bc089` | **벤더와 말하는 HTTP 클라이언트를 클래스패스가 아니라 코드가 고른다** | **#374 는 flaky 수정이 아니라 실제 결함이었다.** `RestClient.builder()` 를 요청 팩토리 없이 쓰면 스프링이 클래스패스에서 집는데, httpclient5 가 #315 이미지 업로드의 AWS SDK 를 타고 들어와 있었다 — **AI 와 무관한 의존 하나가 모델과 말하는 방식과 재시도 정책을 리뷰 없이 바꿨다.** 곁들여 ollama 어댑터에 없던 소켓·연결 상한을 세웠다(멈춘 로컬 모델이 취소된 호출의 스레드를 영구히 가져가던 자리). ## 경계 새 `common/spi` 계약 **둘** — `PinnedStoryVersions`(play 구현) · `ImageReadUrlSigner`(authoring 구현). 둘 다 ADR-0002 · ADR-0003 이 이미 세운 형태이고 **`package-info` 는 한 줄도 바뀌지 않았다.** 새 ADR 을 쓰지 않은 근거가 그것이다. ## 검증 **합류 지점을 머지 전에 직접 돌렸다.** 일곱을 임시 브랜치에 합쳐 `test` **820** · `integrationTest` **653** · 실패 **0** 을 확인했고, 리베이스한 각 브랜치의 **트리 해시를 그 합류 지점의 해당 시점과 대조**한 뒤 머지했다. 다섯 건 모두 일치했다. **지금 `backend` 의 트리(`1bcd2a62`)는 그 검사한 트리와 같다.** 각 PR 의 CI 도 리베이스 후 새로 돌려 전부 초록이었다. 기준선은 `258e70a` 의 806 / 629 다. 충돌은 `docs/corrections.md` 세 번뿐이었고 전부 *"둘 다 유지, 순서대로"* 였다 — 절 번호(§13-78~82)를 착수 전에 배정해 재번호가 없었다. ## 마이그레이션 **하나** — `promptlog/V5__access_audit_draft_image.sql`. CHECK 제약 확장이며 **expand-only** 다. ## 태그는 붙이지 않는다 게시는 `v*` 태그가 하고 스테이징 호스트가 아직 없다. **승격과 릴리스는 다른 일이다.** ## 리뷰 **소유자 지시로 승인 없이 머지한다.** `docs/git-workflow.md` §8.1 은 "리뷰 1인 승인 후"를 조건으로 두며, 그 조건을 우회한 묶음이라는 사실을 여기 남긴다. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: gitit-sehyeon
body:
`#464` 의 **ⓒ(alpha 데모)** 결정이 서 있는 가정을 CI 로 옮깁니다. `@junseo2323` `@yoonjiseok`

## 왜

ⓒ 의 유일한 약점(*"alpha 는 개방 모드라 역할 차단이 안 보인다"*)을 nginx 미경유 우회가 메우기로 했는데, **그 우회가 무엇을 낼지 아무도 안 재고 있었습니다.** 두 분 다 호스트 접근이 없어 실행이 막혀 있고(`@junseo2323`: *"SSM 명령이 로컬 권한 게이트에 걸려 있어"*), 저도 없습니다.

**그래서 같은 것을 다른 방법으로 쟀습니다** — 같은 프로파일(`prod`)·같은 명부·같은 체인으로.

## 조각은 다 있었고 «조립» 이 안 잠겨 있었습니다

```
DemoAccountsTest             명부 seller-01 이 정책상 막힌다              ✅ 있었다
DashboardEndpointWiringTest  ROLE_SELLER 가 403 · enforce=true          ✅ 있었다
SecurityConfigTest           prod 프로파일이 인증을 요구한다               ✅ 있었다
DemoModeAccountMapTest       개방 모드가 compl-01 을 주입한다             ✅ 있었다
❗없던 것                     명부 계정으로 «HTTP 를 태워» 403 이 나는가
```

❗**가운데 둘이 어긋날 수 있습니다.** `DashboardEndpointWiringTest` 는 `.with(user("seller-01").roles("SELLER"))` 로 **모의 권한을 손으로 심습니다.** 실제 배포에서 그 권한을 만드는 것은 `SecurityConfig.prodUsers` 가 명부에서 읽는 `roles(a.role().name())` 이고, 둘이 갈리면 **기존 테스트는 전부 초록인 채로 시연이 깨집니다.**

그 갈림이 실제로 있었습니다 — 계정이 `roles("API")` 하나였을 때 *"인증은 서는데 인가가 아무것도 안 가르는"* 상태였고(`#41`), **그때도 정책 테스트는 통과하고 있었습니다.**

## 재는 것 넷

```
★ SELLER  → 403      시연 1번 (ADR-001 · 7-4)
  COMPL   → 200      ❗양성 대조
  무인증  → 401      401(누구인지 모른다) ≠ 403(알고 막는다)
★ MGR     → 200      시연 2번 — 역할만으로는 부족하다(«닿는다» 까지만)
```

**양성 대조가 특히 필요합니다.** nginx 가 접두어를 벗겨 넘기므로(`web/app.conf:42`) 시연 명령에 `/api` 를 붙이면 404 가 나는데, 그것을 *"막혔다"* 로 읽으면 결론이 뒤집힙니다. 제가 `#464` 에 그 버그를 적은 것과 같은 자리입니다.

## 변조 2/2

```
ⓐ SELLER 에게 aggregate:heatmap:read 를 준다   3건 죽는다   ← 역이용 경로가 열린 상태
ⓑ prod 의 sphinx.security.enforce 를 끈다       3건 죽는다   ← 배포 설정 사고
```

ⓑ 가 중요합니다 — **배포 설정 하나로 차단이 통째로 사라지는 것**이 이 시연의 실패 양식이고, 그건 코드 리뷰로 안 보입니다.

## ❗이 파일이 «대신하지 않는» 것

호스트에서 실제로 돌리는 것을 대신하지 않습니다. 남은 것은 그대로입니다.

```
docker compose exec 가 서버 컨테이너에 닿는가       ← 실행이 필요하다
basic auth 가 그 경로로 실제로 전달되는가            ← 실행이 필요하다
```

**돌리기 전에 답을 알 수 있게** 하고, 그 답이 나중에 조용히 바뀌지 않게 합니다. 403 이 안 나오면 원인이 **서버 설정이 아니라 그 두 줄**이라는 것도 이걸로 갈립니다 — 진단 범위가 줄어듭니다.

## 소유

`SecurityConfig` 는 강희진 소유라 **새 파일로 뒀습니다.** 이 단정이 재는 것은 `AccessPolicy`+명부(정세현)가 그 체인과 만나는 자리이고, `SecurityConfigTest` 의 prod+H2 패턴만 빌렸습니다(MySQL 을 띄우면 CI 가 도커에 의존합니다).

## 검증

```
./gradlew test    BUILD SUCCESSFUL (전체)
신규 4건 · 변조 2/2
```

author: yhjang0315-source
body:
## 무엇을

카카오 로그인이 `KOE205` 로 막히던 문제를 고쳤습니다. 요청 범위에서 이메일을 뺐습니다.

## 증상

배포본에서 **카카오로 계속하기** 를 누르면 로그인 화면에 닿기도 전에 이렇게 떴습니다.

> 잘못된 요청 (KOE205)
> fitage 서비스 설정에 오류가 있어, 이용할 수 없습니다.

콘솔 동의항목에 닉네임·이메일을 **켜 둔 상태였는데도** 똑같았습니다.

## 원인

카카오는 이메일(`account_email`)을 **두 단계로** 막습니다.

1. 콘솔에서 동의항목 켜기 ← 했음
2. **별도 검수 신청** ← 안 함

일반 앱이 `scope` 로 요청하려면 2번까지 통과해야 하고, 아니면 인증 요청 자체를 거부합니다.

## 고친 것

- 카카오 기본 scope 를 `profile_nickname` 하나로 줄였습니다
- **계정 키는 원래부터 카카오 회원번호(`id`)** 라 이메일 없이도 로그인과
  기기 간 이어보기가 그대로 동작합니다. `normalize_profile` 은 이미
  `email=None` 을 허용하고 있었습니다
- `scope_for()` 추가 — `{PROVIDER}_SCOPE` 환경변수로 덮어쓸 수 있습니다

나중에 검수를 통과하면 **코드 수정 없이** 환경변수만 넣으면 됩니다.

```
KAKAO_SCOPE=profile_nickname account_email
```

받는 정보가 하나 줄었을 뿐이라, 기획안의 개인정보 최소 수집 방침과도 더 맞습니다.

## 배포 전 확인 (실제 카카오 서버 응답)

```
우리 서버 /auth/kakao/start
   → kauth.kakao.com/oauth/authorize      앱 인식 OK
   → accounts.kakao.com/login             로그인 화면 도달
```

`KOE006`(미등록 Redirect URI)·`KOE101`(앱 없음) 이 안 났으므로 **키와 Redirect URI 는 정상**입니다.
남은 건 scope 하나였습니다.

## 검증

**pytest 89개 + 서브테스트 13개 — SQLite / Postgres 양쪽 통과** (4개 추가)

- `/auth/kakao/start` 가 실제로 `scope=profile_nickname` 만 보내는지
- `account_email` 이 URL 에 안 들어가는지
- 이메일 없는 카카오 프로필로도 계정이 만들어지는지
- `KAKAO_SCOPE` 로 다시 넣을 수 있는지

## 스스로 체크

- [x] 콘솔 설정 변경 없이 배포만으로 해결
- [x] 구글·네이버 영향 없음
- [ ] 이메일이 필요해지면 카카오 검수 신청 후 `KAKAO_SCOPE` 추가

author: morphqdd
body:
The login cookie was set with nothing but its value. `Rack::SSL` appends `secure` and
nothing else, so the cookie was readable by JavaScript and travelled with cross-site
requests, while it is the whole session.

Both places that set it now pass `httponly: true` and `same_site: :lax`, with an explicit
path.

Closes #468

author: truecristi
body:
## Summary

The fourth real destination behind the workspace nav (Today → Learn → Build → **Execute** → Review), stacked on #68. Execute covers "tasks, experiments, launches, outreach and implementation" (README primary navigation); this first slice does **tasks** — the headline of that list and the most self-contained Execute domain. Built entirely on the already-tested Phase 2/5 task domain layer — **no domain or API changes**.

- **`/workspaces/[workspaceId]/execute`** — the task list, grouped into **Open / In progress / Done** sections, each task showing a priority badge, its due date, and an **overdue** flag (status ≠ done and dueDate in the past — the same rule the scorecard computes, applied inline). Honest empty state when there are none.
- A **quick-create form** (title + priority + optional due date). The date-only input is anchored to UTC midnight to satisfy the API's ISO-datetime contract.
- **Inline per-task controls**: a status select (the dedicated PATCH route, which sets/clears `completedAt` server-side) and a priority select (the PUT route). Both refresh the page so the task re-renders under its new group/badge; a failed change surfaces an error rather than lying.
- `lib/browser-api.ts` gains a `putJson` helper alongside `postJson`/`patchJson`, for the task PUT route.

## Scope

Tasks only, deferring experiments, launches, projects, AI task-proposals and improvement loops (each a tested domain surface) to their own later slices — the same incremental shape as Build = offers. Note the existing task domain has **no title/description edit or delete route**, so this slice doesn't fake one: it creates, lists, and changes status/priority — exactly the surface that exists.

## Testing

- **`tests/e2e/execute.spec.ts`**: register → Execute empty state → create a task → see it under Open → move it to In progress → move it to Done, browser-driven, with its own `x-forwarded-for` rate-limit bucket (the per-spec pattern introduced in #68).
- **`today.spec.ts` updated**: Execute is no longer the shared "isn't built yet" placeholder, so the nav test now confirms Execute renders a real page (its "No tasks yet" empty state); only **Review** remains a placeholder.
- `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` all clean; all 248 domain tests green; production build shows the real Execute route; full Playwright suite (auth + today + learn + build + execute, **8 tests**) green against a fresh server in **both** serial and CI parallel/retry mode.

author: johnitvn
body:
## Description

Phase 6 of the execution roadmap: hooks as steps (issue #33, contract merged in #34).

The contract's amendment holds here as the implementation's shape: each hook declares **one** guard name (`HookStep.guard`), the kernel's single aggregate claim check (`held + holder === attemptId + verify(token)`) runs before the write-ahead start, the caller-injected effect (`effects` map) is the only code the engine executes and the only seam user code touches, replay is scheduler-driven and answered by the ledger projection (a completed hook replays even when the effects map carries no entry), and a failed postcondition is classified through the attempt's `blocked(validation:hook:<id>:<kind>)` state — the §2.7 resolution loop re-arms from the hook key, not a crash.

- `src/execution/types.ts` — §2.5b hook vocabulary: `HookStep`, `HookAnchorPosition`, `PostconditionKind`, `HookObservation`, `HookEffect`, `HookOutcome`, `HooksRun`; `ReleaseAttempt.hooks?`; `StepRequest.stepKey` widened to `StageKey`.
- `src/execution/attempt.ts` — `validateHooks` protocol (unique ids, canonical anchors, non-empty guards, known postcondition kinds, deep freeze) and `openAttempt(register, plan, hooks?)`; `successor()` now carries declared hooks across every edge while `blockedCause`/`terminalReason` stay bound to the states that record them (destructured out, re-added only for their state).
- `src/execution/hooks.ts` — `hookStepKey`, `isHookStepKey`, `effectiveSteps` (anchor-anchored, declaration order breaking ties), `scheduleHooks` (replay check before the effects lookup, refusal breaks the walk, postconditions checked before the completion record exists).
- `src/execution/resume.ts` — `firstUncompleted` walks `effectiveSteps`; failed hook records classify through the blocked state (continue) and escalate when the tail contradicts it; external satisfaction still judges only the canonical stages.
- `src/execution/ledger.ts`, `outcome.ts`, `step.ts` — `appendStart` records the declared guard verbatim; guard lists and stage math narrowed to `StageKey`.
- `test/execution/hooks.test.ts` — the five contract fixtures: attachment/ordering, kill-anywhere truncation with double-run equality (every effective boundary), refusal by construction, postcondition failure plus its re-arming resolution, and scheduler determinism.

Part of #33

## Could this fail silently?

- A completed hook could be re-executed if the replay check ran after the effects lookup — it runs first, and the fixture proves replay works with an **empty** effects map (`never re-executed, no effect needed`).
- A failed hook could crash the walk like a failed stage if resume treated hook keys as canonical — the classifier branches on `isHookStepKey` and the fixtures cover both the blocked path (resume from `hook:scan`) and the contradictory tail (escalate).
- The declared hooks could vanish on state edges if `successor()` rebuilt the attempt from fixed fields — they now ride every edge explicitly, and the §2.1 fixture pins `planFingerprint`/`attemptId` stability while `effectiveSteps` sees the hooks after `start()`.
- A hook could write its completion record with a guard name the ledger never verified — `appendStart` takes the declared guard verbatim and the fixture reads it back from the start record.

## How was this verified?

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run test/execution test/provider-isolation.test.ts` — 15 files, 121 tests passing (109 baseline + 12 new).
- `pnpm check` — all canonical gates green (exit 0).
- `pnpm check:policy` — four policy gates green (exit 0).
- Kill-anywhere fixture: every boundary of the 10-step effective list classifies identically under double-run (`classifyResume` twice, `toStrictEqual`).

author: yu5rin
body:
## 概要

異常系の点検で挙がった「中」3件・「低」4件の指摘をすべて修正しました。各項目の詳細（実測値・直し方・テスト）は下記のとおりです。

## 修正した項目

### 1【中】多重起動・自己再起動でログファイルが欠落・破損する
- ログファイル名にプロセスIDを含める（`logs/yyyyMMdd-<pid>.log`）方式に変更し、複数プロセスが物理的に別ファイルへ書き込むことで競合そのものを無くしました。
- 「最新のログを表示」（設定画面）は、同じ日付の複数プロセス分のファイルをすべて集め、各行のtimestampで時刻順にまとめて表示するよう対応しました（`LogTailReader.FindLatestDateLogFiles` / `ReadTailMerged`）。
- 90日を超えた古いログの自動削除も、新旧どちらの命名でも対象になるようにしました。
- **実測**: 修正前は2つのLoggerで各300行=計600行を同時書き込みすると366行しか残らず4行がJSON破損。修正後は同じ条件で600行すべてが残り、全行がJSONとして解析可能なことをテストで確認しました（`LoggerTests.多重起動を模した同時書き込みで全行が残る`）。

### 2【中】設定値に上限が無く、update.checkUrlは空でも通る
- `NormalizeMin` を上下限つきの `NormalizeIntRange` に変更し、`editor.tabSize`（1〜16）・`safety.maxFileSizeMB`（1〜1024）・`backup.maxRevisions`（0〜100000）・`backup.maxTotalMB`（0〜1TB相当）・`matching.rangeWarningLines`（1〜10万）・`diff.contextLines`（0〜999）・`safety.maxFilesPerRevision`（1〜10万）・`context.tokenWarnThreshold`（1〜1000万）に上限を追加しました。
- `context.tokenRatio` も `NormalizePositive` から `NormalizeRange`（0.1〜100）に変更しました。
- `update.checkUrl` に「空でない」「絶対URL」「スキームがhttps」の検証を追加し、不正な場合は具体的な理由（「空です」「絶対URLではありません」「httpsである必要があります」）を設定画面に表示するようにしました。
- **実測**: 修正前は `editor.tabSize=100000` 等が警告0件で採用されていたことを確認済み。修正後はいずれも既定値へフォールバックし、警告（E404）が返ることをテストで確認しました。

### 3【中】トークン概算がintオーバーフローで負数になる
- `TokenEstimator.EstimateLength` で、桁あふれする手前（double型のまま）で `int.MaxValue` かどうかを判定してからキャストするよう変更しました。
- **実測**: 修正前は `EstimateLength(long.MaxValue)` 等が `-2147483648` を返していました。修正後はいずれも `int.MaxValue`（2147483647）を返すことをテストで確認しました。
- 呼び出し元（`ContextResult.EstimatedTokens` 等）は既存どおり `int` 型のままのため、表示側の桁区切り等への影響はありません（プレーンな `{0}` フォーマットのみで桁区切り自体を使っていないことも確認済み）。

### 4【低】新規作成・名前の変更でパス区切りや不正文字が素通りする
- `FileTreeService.CreateFileAsync` / `CreateFolderAsync` / `RenameAsync` に、名前1つ分（1階層）に対する検証（`ValidateEntryName`）を追加しました。パス区切り・`Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars()`・制御文字・末尾の空白/ピリオド・255文字超過をそれぞれ具体的な日本語メッセージで拒否します（新エラーコード `E214`）。
- `RenameAsync` のdocコメント（「同じ親フォルダ内での名前変更のみ」）と実装の食い違いを、実装側をdocに合わせる形で解消しました。
- **既存コードとの重複解消**: `PathGuard` 側の `:` 文字専用の検証（`E212`、代替データストリーム対策）と重複・矛盾しないよう、こちらの不許可文字判定からは `:` を除外し、より詳しい理由を持つPathGuard側のメッセージへ委ねています。エラーコードは `#63`（E211・E212）・`#67`（E213、プロジェクトフォルダ未検出）と衝突しないよう、空き番号の `E214` を使いました。
- **実測**: `newName="dir/moved.txt"` で別フォルダへ移動できてしまう不具合、内部の一時ファイル名の露出、300文字の英語例外、末尾空白の誤ったメッセージ、改行/タブを含む名前がLinux上で作成できてしまう不具合を、いずれも回帰テストで再現→修正を確認しました。

### 5【低】更新ダウンロードに読み取りタイムアウトが無い
- `HttpUpdateDownloader` に「一定時間（既定30秒）バイトが1つも届かなければ自動中断する」停滞検出を追加しました。既存の「中断」ボタン（呼び出し元のCancellationToken）はそのまま独立して機能し、どちらが発火したかで `Cancelled` / `Failed` を区別します。
- ダウンロード全体の合計時間には引き続き固定タイムアウトを設けていません（低速回線での正常なダウンロードを妨げないため）。
- 名前解決不能・プロキシ到達不能時の英語の生の例外メッセージも `ExceptionMessages.Describe` 経由で日本語化しました。
- **`#67` との重複解消**: `#67` が `ExceptionMessages.Describe` に無条件の `HttpRequestException => "ネットワークに接続できませんでした..."` を追加していましたが、こちらの分岐（名前解決不能かどうかで細分化する`when`句付き）より前に置かれると、switch式の性質上こちらが常に先にマッチして後段の分岐が到達不能になっていました。無条件の分岐を削除し、名前解決の判定を含む1系統へ統合しています。
- **正直な報告**: サンドボックスのプロキシ制約により、実際のネットワーク越しの切断・無応答は試験できていません。停滞検出の単体テストは、遅いストリームを模したテスト用の `Stream`（フェイクの `HttpMessageHandler` 経由）で検証しています。

### 6【低】一時ファイル・退避ファイルの掃除が無い
- 起動時に、`AppPaths.BaseDirectory` 直下の `*.tmp.*` と、登録済みプロジェクト配下の `*.graft-bak-*` のうち24時間以上古いものを掃除する `TempFileCleanup` を追加し、`StartupCoordinator` から呼び出しています。
- UIスレッドを塞がないよう `Task.Run` によるバックグラウンド実行（fire-and-forget）にしています。
- プロジェクトルート配下の走査は、大きなプロジェクトでも起動が重くならないよう、深さ（既定6階層）と件数（既定2万件）に上限を設けています（根拠はコード内コメント参照）。`node_modules` 等の重いディレクトリには降りません。
- `#66` で `GitignoreFilter` に2秒のタイムアウトが追加されましたが、本掃除処理は `GitignoreFilter` を使わない軽量な決め打ちの除外リストのため影響ありません。

### 7【低】layout.jsonのペイン系の値に検証が無い
- `WindowLayoutStore.LoadAsync` に正規化処理を追加し、`CodeFontSize` を通常操作（Ctrl+マウスホイール）と同じ8〜32へ、`LeftPaneSplitRatio` を0〜1へクランプするようにしました。
- `OpenTabState.CaretLine` / `CaretColumn` の0以下の値は1へ、`GraftPanelPlacement` の未知の文字列は既定の `"bottom"` へ、それぞれ読み込み時に補正します。
- 既存の `ResolveWindowBounds`（ウィンドウ位置・サイズの補正）と同じ「静かに補正する」流儀（ログは残さない）に揃えています。

## 変更履歴
`docs/変更履歴.md` の `## 1.0.15` 節へ `### 修正（堅牢性）` 見出しを追加しました（既存の「セキュリティ」「データ整合性」「安定性」「性能」「表示・文言」「配色・見やすさ」の各節はそのまま残しています）。あわせて、`#67` が追加した通信断メッセージの記述を、本PRでさらに細分化したことが分かるよう一言添えました。

## 確認したこと
- `dotnet build Graft.sln`: 警告0件・エラー0件
- `dotnet test tests/Graft.Tests`: 1229件全件成功
- `dotnet test tests/Graft.UiTests`（`xvfb-run -a` 経由）: 809件全件成功（`PerformanceTests` 含む）
- Xvfb上でアプリを実際に起動し、25秒間クラッシュせず稼働することを確認（データ保存先は他セッションと衝突しないよう別ディレクトリを使用）。ログファイル名が新方式（`yyyyMMdd-<pid>.log`）になっていることも確認済み。

## その他
- `origin/main` の先行PR（`#63`〜`#68`）とマージ済みです。
- `ErrorCodes.cs` の番号衝突は2回発生しました。1回目は本PRのE211が`#63`のE211・E212と衝突したためE213へ振り直し、2回目はそのE213が`#67`の「プロジェクトフォルダ未検出」用E213と衝突したため最終的にE214へ振り直しています。
- `HttpUpdateDownloader.cs`・`ExceptionMessages.cs` は `#67` と同じ箇所（ネットワークエラーの日本語化）を触っていたため、重複を解消して1系統へ統合しています（項目5参照）。

author: f1xgun
body:
Round-2 api batch: the server side of the landing hybrid mode (#500) and of the Free/Pro billing UI (#503).

- **LND-12-API** — new public `POST /landing-events`: anonymous CTA capture with enum validation, bounded body/path, per-IP rate limiting, persistence in `landing_events` (migration in both paths) and a Prometheus counter `landing_cta_clicks_total{cta}`. Without it the landing's `data-cta` beacons had nowhere to land and the entry-mode switch thresholds were unmeasurable.
- **D1-WAITLIST** — the waitlist request accepts optional `source` and `plan`, so «Оставить заявку» from the billing screen and from the Free organisation limit is recorded as a Pro request. Duplicate e-mails update the supplied attribution while preserving values that were not sent; consent validation and legacy requests unchanged.

author: dudeinhoodie
body:
PD-19, closes #328. The three screens a paid deck needs, and the wiring that reaches them.

## What changed

**One rule decides access.** `DeckRecord.isOpen(given:)` in the domain: free, or an entitlement key the account holds. An access model this build does not know reads as closed. A feature flag decides whether *buying* is offered and never whether a deck is *open* — an owner keeps a deck with `commerce.apple_iap.enabled` off, and a non-owner is told purchases are unavailable rather than handed the deck.

**Catalogue.** Paid decks the account does not own go to a `Featured decks` shelf above `Free decks`; the same deck bought is an ordinary row again. The lock is on the row before anything opens. A price appears only once StoreKit answers — "Price loading" until then, "Purchase temporarily unavailable" when the product is missing, never a placeholder. The row and its `Explore deck` action both open the details; neither starts StoreKit. Free rows are untouched, and a catalogue with no paid deck gets no headings at all.

**Paywall.** Preview fan, name, "N cards · coats of arms", description, one status card when there is something to explain, one purchase explanation with the price and Restore, and one prominent action at the bottom. No middle panel — the four candidates were rejected in design review and stay in `DESIGN.md`'s appendix. A guest gets "Sign in to buy" and is sent to the account screen.

**Owned deck (§10.4).** Compact hero with a reduced fan, the progress readout and track, search, and the full lazy list — aspect-fit thumbnail, entity name, the emblem's own localized name where the release publishes one, chevron into the existing detail sheet — with `Start learning` / `Continue` pinned. No price, lock, restore or badge once the entitlement is verified. The paywall becomes this screen with no pop and no relaunch.

**Pending and refund (§11.4).** A pending purchase says so, the action is disabled, and a second tap starts no second purchase. After a revocation the deck closes on the next refresh, a neutral "access has ended" card explains it, the progress is untouched, and a session already open can still be finished.

**Progress leaves a locked deck out.** A guest's rows fall back to the published card count where the device has counted nothing — right for a free deck whose cards have not landed, wrong for a paid one, because "0 of 52" in a deck nobody bought states a size that is true and a promise that is not. Such a deck is omitted, the way a deck the backend has not spoken about already is.

**Backend sync failure never takes a purchase away (§11.3).** `CommerceCenter` holds the server's own snapshot beside the coordinator's answer; the difference between them is a purchase this device verified and the backend has not acknowledged. The deck opens on it, and the owned screen says quietly that it is still being saved.

## Contract change to PD-18's protocol — please read

I added one method to `PurchaseCoordinating`, which is PD-18's:

```swift
func entitlementChanges() async -> AsyncStream<Set<String>>
```

`PurchaseCoordinator` yields on it after every settle; `CommerceCenter` consumes it.

Without it there is no way for a screen to learn that what the account may open has moved. The interesting cases all arrive at the transaction listener rather than at a button: an Ask to Buy a parent approves an hour later, a purchase made on another device, a refund. The only alternative was to leave the paywall saying "awaiting confirmation" until the app was relaunched — and §11.3 says the lock disappears *without* a relaunch, so that was not available. It is additive, one stream per call, and the coordinator finishes them in `stop()`.

## The marketing version moves to 0.2.0

All three configurations. It is what the minimum-client-version gate in #372 keys on: an app built before this work has no access model, no paywall and no entitlement check, and the server can tell the two apart only by the version they send. Left at `0.1.0` the gate would have nothing to key on. `PAID_CONTENT_MINIMUM_CLIENT_VERSIONS` is then set to `ios=0.2.0` — a deployment setting, so not in this diff.

The other note #372 left for iOS is already satisfied: the app never calls `GET /v1/decks/{id}`, so a locked deck answering 404 during a rollback reaches nothing. Deck metadata comes from `GET /v1/decks` and is read back out of the local store.

## Content, because a paid deck arrives without its cards

`ContentBootstrapCoordinator` now skips the cards of a deck the account cannot open, and tolerates the guard's `403` on one deck without failing the run — otherwise one deck for sale costs a guest the whole catalogue. The handful of cards a deck publishes as a public preview arrive with the deck list and are stored **without a deck membership**: that is what draws the fan, and what keeps a locked deck out of progress and out of session composition. After a purchase only that deck's cards are fetched, not the whole release again.

## What a reviewer should tap through in the Mock build

The Mock backend now sells one deck. `SPECIAL_AREAS` is served with an `ENTITLEMENT` access block and three public preview cards, and its cards answer `403 ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` until the account holds the entitlement. `EUROPE` stays free — it is the deck the browse and screenshot suites walk through.

1. **Run `CountryFlags-Mock`.** The scheme carries `ios/Config/CountryFlags.storekit`, so the store answers.
2. **Catalog tab.** `Special areas` sits under `FEATURED DECKS` with a lock, `7 cards`, a price line and `Explore deck`; everything else is under `FREE DECKS` and looks exactly as it did.
3. **Open it.** The paywall: preview fan, description, the purchase card, `Sign in to buy` at the bottom (you are a guest). No card list.
4. **Open a free deck** (`Europe`) — unchanged, `Start` where it always was.
5. **The storefront flag is off by default**, so the price says "Purchase temporarily unavailable" and a status card explains it. To see a real price and a working Buy, launch with `-feature-flag commerce.apple_iap.enabled=true`.
6. **Sign in** through the avatar (`-fake-signin`), then buy. Or launch with `-owned-deck` to arrive already owning it: the row loses its badge, the deck screen is the owned list, and `Start learning` is at the bottom.

## Checks

- **CI is green**: `build-and-test` passed in 46m52s with `PaidDeckUITests` in the smoke set, plus `quality` and `security`. The checks below were also run locally.
- `CountryFlagsKit-Package` suite green, including the new `CommerceCenterTests` and the catalogue-grouping and progress cases.
- `CountryFlags-Mock` builds; `PaidDeckUITests` (3 cases) green locally and added to the CI smoke set — a lock that stops being drawn is content given away, and nothing else in that set would notice.
- Unsigned `CountryFlags-Prod` archive succeeds; `check-release-app.sh`, `check-advertising-policy.sh`, `check-signing-entitlements.sh` and `sync-mock-content.mjs --check` all pass. `project.pbxproj` is untouched: the only project change is the `StoreKitConfigurationFileReference` in the Mock `.xcscheme`.

## The `.storekit` configuration, and the tests that are not with it

`ios/Config/CountryFlags.storekit` lists the two production deck identifiers and the one the Mock build sells. The Mock scheme points at it, so running that scheme gives a store that answers: products resolve, prices are formatted, and a purchase can be completed by hand. It belongs to no target — that is what keeps it out of every shipped binary, verified against the archive, and why it sits in `ios/Config` rather than beside the app sources, which are a synchronized group and would adopt it.

I wrote `StoreKitTest` cases against it and then removed them, and that is worth a reviewer's minute. They passed here and failed on CI twice. The first failure looked like a race, so the suite was made to wait for the store rather than for a duration; the second ruled that out — on a clea
