author: 8seneca-global
body:
Closes [ALC-61](https://projects.8seneca.com/8seneca/browse/ALC-61/) (WF1, lane `control-plane`, depends on A6).

Workflows become saved objects: a stage carries its member, `reversibility`, `inherited_cost` and `required_checks`; a transition carries a trigger. Three tenant-scoped tables with row-level security forced, and CRUD over the whole graph on the Control API.

## Decisions worth reading before the diff

- **The wire addresses a stage by `key`, not by id.** Ids stay internal, so a save is idempotent, a reorder is a single request, and WF3's board-column bindings get something stable to point at. `key` is already the ledger's join column (`step_outcomes.stage_key`, `autonomy_policies.stage_key`).
- **`version` is optimistic concurrency, not a published snapshot.** The client sends the version it read; a mismatch returns `409 { error: 'version_conflict', version }`. The check runs under `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` inside the write transaction, so two concurrent saves cannot both win. Immutable published snapshots were considered and rejected for WF1 — roughly double the ticket, and nothing pins a version to a run until stages bind to dispatch (WF3).
- **Stage-authored required checks win over the project's, and an empty stage list still wins.** Only a *missing* stage falls back to `project_required_checks`, so a stage never silently inherits a rule it did not author. `project_required_checks` and its route are untouched, so D5's `required-checks-fetch.ts` keeps working. The resolver ships as a pure function; its consumer is WF3.

Ordinal contiguity is enforced on the wire rather than by a unique index — the index would fail mid-statement on a reorder. Cycles are legal (WF2 makes the return edge first-class), but at most one transition per `(from_stage, trigger.kind)`, so dispatch stays deterministic. Deleting a member unassigns its stages (`ON DELETE SET NULL`) instead of cascading a workflow away.

## Cross-owner touches (per OWNERSHIP.md)

| File | Owner | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `control-plane-contract/src/workflow.ts` + `index.ts` | Huy | **New module**, not a field change. Enums to mirror on the desktop: `STAGE_REVERSIBILITY = free \| contained \| irreversible`, `INHERITED_COSTS = low \| high`, `TRIGGER_KINDS = on_success \| on_failure \| manual`. Stage key shape: `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$/`. |
| `control-api/src/schema-postgres.test.ts` | Huy | **Required** edit — it asserts an exact ordered table list and goes red the moment the tables land. |
| `control-api/src/schema-sql.ts` | Huy | Append-only: three tables, three RLS policies. |
| `control-api/src/app.ts` | shared | Additive one-liner (import + register), per the shared-files rule. |
| `dev/scripts/seed-alicorn-local.mjs` | Huy | Additive `seedWorkflows()`. |

## Verification

- 39 control-api tests (10 new route tests), 10 contract, 5 postgres-package, 16 ledger-api, 6 seed — green against Postgres 16.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean across the cloud workspace.
- Live run of the compose stack: seed, list, get the full graph including the `review --on_failure--> build` return edge and the stage-authored `diff_coverage` check; stale version → 409 with the current version; missing bearer → 401; wrong `x-alicorn-org` → 403; seed rerun idempotent.

## Known gap, deliberately out of scope

The template's stages verify with `test`/`types`/`lint`/`e2e`/`smoke`, but `RequiredCheckSchema` only expresses `diff_coverage`. A second check kind is a separate ticket; nothing here pretends otherwise.

Plan: `docs/alicorn/plans/2026-09-06-wf1-workflows-stages.md`.

author: hashirahmed2982
body:
Admin-managed dynamic content (business categories, About Us, Privacy Policy, Terms & Conditions) was only ever entered in one language, so the website/app showed that one language to every visitor regardless of locale — the mobile app's category translations were a separate hardcoded map with no connection to the admin panel, so a category an admin added there could never be translated without a new app release.

## Categories

- Added `name_de`/`name_sq` columns (`schema.sql` for fresh installs, `migrate.js`'s `COLUMNS_TO_ENSURE` for existing databases). `name` stays the single canonical value `businesses.category` actually stores/matches against — `name_de`/`name_sq` are additional required translations, not a replacement.
- `createCategory`/`updateCategory` now reject a request missing any of `name`/`nameDe`/`nameSq` (on update, only when the request touches a name field at all — editing just `sortOrder`/`iconName` still works without resending all 3 names).
- `getPublicCategories`/`getAdminCategories` return `nameDe`/`nameSq` alongside `name` so clients can pick their own current locale's label without a per-language round trip.
- `seed.js`'s 7 seeded categories carry real `nameDe`/`nameSq` values, carried over from the app's previous hardcoded translation map (already-reviewed translations, not new ones invented here).

## Site content (About Us, Privacy Policy, Terms & Conditions)

- `content.service.js` now requires each of these three keys' `data` to be `{ en: {...}, de: {...}, sq: {...} }` — a save missing any locale is rejected, and each locale's sub-object still goes through the same shape validation as before. `social_links` is deliberately unchanged/not locale-keyed — a URL isn't translated.
- Added `migrate-content-i18n.sql` for an existing database: wraps an already-flat row into the new 3-locale shape, duplicating the existing (English) copy into the `de`/`sq` slots as a starting point so nothing goes blank the moment this ships. **That's a placeholder, not a real translation** — an admin still needs to replace the German/Albanian legal text with a proper translation via the Content page.
- `seed.js`'s default content updated to the new nested shape the same way (English duplicated into `de`/`sq` as a starting point).

## Migration steps for an existing deployment

1. `npm run db:migrate` (adds the new category columns).
2. `mysql -u <user> -p <database> < src/db/migrate-content-i18n.sql` (wraps existing site content into the 3-locale shape).
3. Existing categories keep their English `name`; an admin should fill in `nameDe`/`nameSq` for any category not already covered by the seeded 7 via the admin portal (once that side of this feature ships).

## Summary

W11 card: real Dodo Payments *sandbox* bank-side data source, built strict-TDD against a mocked/fake Dodo client.

- **`src/ledger_sense/data/dodo_source.py`** (new): paginated read-only pull from Dodo's sandbox "list transactions" endpoint via an injectable `DodoClient` protocol, normalized into the exact `BankTransaction` shape (Decimal/cents, never float — law L3), deduped by Dodo transaction id (idempotent ingestion).
- **`src/ledger_sense/data/dodo_pairing.py`** (new): synthesizes a paired `LedgerEntry` + `MatchLink` around each pulled bank row, reusing `data/defects.py`'s `DEFECT_RATES` proportions over a documented, reduced defect subset (`clean`, `wrong_reference`, `fx_rounding`, `negative_amount`, `zero_amount`, plus observed `missing_reference`). See the module docstring for why `duplicate`/`partial_payment`/`out_of_order`/`malformed`/`orphan_*` don't apply when the bank row is a fixed external observation rather than something this package synthesizes.
- **CLI**: `--source dodo` on the existing `python -m ledger_sense.data` entrypoint selects this path (default remains `synthetic`, `LEDGER_SENSE_DATA_SOURCE`-aware). Missing `DODO_API_KEY` + `--source dodo` exits cleanly — nonzero, one-line stderr message, never a stack trace (law L18). Synthetic default is unaffected (verified via a real subprocess run).

## Locked decision followed

Pull-then-synthesize (PRD "Locked decisions" #1): pull existing Dodo sandbox transactions first, then synthesize matching `ledger.csv` rows around them, mirroring the generator's defect-injection logic. Documented in `dodo_pairing.py`'s module docstring.

## Strict TDD

`tests/test_dodo_source.py` and `tests/test_dodo_pairing.py` were written first against a mocked/fake Dodo client (zero live network calls — law L20) and watched fail before any implementation existed. Covers all 5 acceptance criteria:

1. Unit tests against a mocked Dodo client — zero live network calls, zero sandbox spend
2. Dodo-sourced output rows pass the exact same schema validation as `generator.py`'s output
3. Idempotency: pulling the same mocked transaction list twice produces zero duplicate rows
4. Integration test: `matching.engine` runs unmodified against Dodo-sourced fixture files, producing a valid `match_outcomes.csv`
5. Missing-key test: `DODO_API_KEY` unset + `--source dodo` exits nonzero with a clear message; synthetic path unaffected

```
362 passed, 2 skipped
```

`matching/routing/guardrail/learning/metrics` are untouched — confirmed by `git diff --stat` (only `data/cli.py` modified) and the full suite passing unchanged.

author: milodule3-debug
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two independent pieces of work. They landed on one branch because a stop hook required the second to be committed while this branch was checked out — **say the word and I'll split the swarms plugin onto its own branch and PR.**

---

# Part 1 — Blender + game scaffolding

Two new tools that compose into one pipeline: author 3D art in Blender, scaffold a game that loads it, play it.

**`blender`** — drives a local install headless (`blender --background --python`):

| Action | Does |
|--------|------|
| `check` | Locate the binary (PATH, well-known paths, `AURA_BLENDER`) and report the version |
| `exec` / `script` | Run inline bpy Python or a `.py` file — model, light, bake, rig |
| `scene` | Report objects, poly counts, materials, cameras in a `.blend` |
| `render` | Still or animation range, with engine / resolution / sample control |
| `export` | `glb`, `gltf`, `fbx`, `obj`, `usd`, `stl` |

Generated Python is wrapped so a traceback exits non-zero instead of reporting success, output is stripped of Blender's startup noise, and every model-supplied path goes through the existing project-root path jail.

**`game_scaffold`** — writes a complete, playable project, not a demo. Each template boots with no package install and no build step:

- `three` — 3D platformer: AABB character controller, coin objective, HUD, orbit-follow camera, glTF drop-in, plus `blender/make_assets.py`
- `godot` — Godot 4: `CharacterBody3D` player, mouse look, pickups found by group, score/timer UI
- `phaser` — 2D platformer: arcade physics, patrolling enemies, lives, procedurally generated textures, win/lose

The Three.js template loads `assets/player.glb` / `assets/level.glb` when they exist and falls back to primitives when they don't, so a Blender export drops straight in without touching the code.

Also adds `gamedev` and `graphics3d` domain-expertise blocks.

---

# Part 2 — The `swarms` plugin

Six named multi-agent topologies as commands, under `plugins/swarms/`. Loaded by the existing plugin loader; **no changes to `src/`**.

| Command | Shape |
|---|---|
| `/technitai <roles> -- <goal>` | Fixed specialists, disjoint file scopes |
| `/epitropi <task>` | Coordinator appoints, reviews, aggregates |
| `/synergasia <goal>` | Many agents converging on **one** artifact |
| `/koinon <guild> <goal>` | Persistent guild with shared memory |
| `/strategos <objective>` | Phased campaign: general → officers → units |
| `/stratos <op> -- <items>` | Homogeneous worker pool, map-reduce |

Four axes keep them distinct: coordination (peer / dispatched / shared-context / layered), role stability, capability heterogeneity (`stratos` alone is homogeneous), and depth (1 everywhere except `strategos`).

The guardrails are the load-bearing part, since a command that sizes its own fan-out will otherwise spend quota without asking: **≤5 concurrent sub-agents** (`stratos` scales the batch, never the pool), **no sub-swarms** except `strategos` officers spawning ≤3 units, **announce before spawning**, and **failures reported individually** rather than hidden in an aggregate.

Two topology-specific rules: `synergasia` must pick section ownership or sequential passes and say which — concurrent edits to one file lose each other, and "merge in real time" is not a plan. `koinon` persists to `.aura/guilds/<name>.md`, reading it before working and writing back before finishing.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Test improvement

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run build` passes (no type errors)
- [x] `npm test` passes — all five checks green on the current head `589219f`, `test (24)` and `lint` included. (Locally, 11 `tests/browser.test.ts` cases fail; they also fail on `master` with the diff stashed, and CI passes them, so they're an artifact of this sandbox's dependency install.)
- [x] New code has tests (50 new: `tests/tools/blender.test.ts`, `tests/tools/game.test.ts`, `tests/swarm-commands.test.ts`)
- [x] Docs updated (`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/aura-code-overview.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.env.example`, `plugins/swarms/README.md`)
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated (repo has no CHANGELOG)

## Screenshots / Logs

**Three.js game** — headless Chromium against real three.js, driven by keyboard:

```
resting  { y: 0,    z: 0,     grounded: true  }
jumping  { y: 1.54, z: 0,     grounded: false }
landed   { y: 0,    z: 0,     grounded: true  }
coin     { score: 1, hud: "Coins 1 / 9" }
fall     respawned at origin after crossing the kill plane
restart  { score: 0, hud: "Coins 0 / 9" }
pageerrors: []
```

**Blender tool** — against bpy 4.2:

```
Scene: Scene | frames 1 - 250 | engine BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT
Objects (3):
  Camera    CAMERA  loc=(7.00, -7.00, 5.00)
  Hero      MESH    loc=(0.00, 0.00, 1.00) verts=8 polys=6
  Sun       LIGHT   loc=(4.00, -4.00, 8.00)

hero.glb 1.7 KB · hero.obj 0.9 KB · hero.fbx 23.0 KB · hero.stl 0.7 KB · shot.png 33.3 KB (Cycles)
```

`blender/make_assets.py` generated `player.glb` (31 KB) and `props.glb` (21 KB), and the game replaced its placeholder capsule with the generated character on reload.

Two bugs surfaced by that verification and fixed in the templates:

1. `THREE.Box3.intersectsBox` counts *touching* faces as an intersection, so a player standing on the floor read as inside it and the horizontal pass ejected them out the side of the ground box. Now requires an epsilon of real penetration.
2. The Godot level had a 16-unit gap and a 4-unit rise between platforms — further than a 9 m/s jump at 7 m/s can cross, so it was uncompletable; plus an inverted `look_at` and a wrong `load_steps` in `coin.tscn`.

## Known limits

- **Godot was not executed** — no Godot binary in this environment. That template was reviewed by hand and its jump arithmetic checked against the arc.
- **The swarm commands are prompt bodies.** Loading, resolution, argument handling and guardrail text are verified by tests. Their *behaviour* under a live model — whether an agent actually holds the write lock, actually gates a phase — is unproven and needs a real run against a provider.

author: fryanpan
body:
In the signed-out posture `#main` stopped 3px short of the bottom of `#shell` at 1180x820 and 55px short at 430px, and that strip hit-tested to `#shell` instead of the editor. It is the same dead band explicit row placement was added to prevent once before, back through a selector nothing covered.

## The measurements

Headless Chrome (`bun run ui:shot`, throwaway profile), short doc so the shell is measured against content that does not fill it. `visibilityState` was `visible` for every reading.

| | posture | `#shell` bottom | `#main` bottom | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before** | signed out, 1180x820 | 820 | 817 | **3px** |
| | signed out, 430x932 | 932 | 876.66 | **55.34px** |
| | signed in, 1180x820 | 820 | 820 | 0 |
| | signed in, 430x932 | 932 | 932 | 0 |
| **after** | signed out, 1180x820 | 820 | 820 | **0** |
| | signed out, 430x932 | 932 | 932 | **0** |
| | signed in, 1180x820 | 820 | 820 | 0 |
| | signed in, 430x932 | 932 | 932 | 0 |

A tap at the last pixel row, signed out — before: `#shell < body.signin-gated < html` at both widths. After: `#editor < #editor-pane < #main < #shell` at both widths.

The signed-in posture is byte-identical before and after: tracks `48px 0px 772px` / `48px 0px 884px`, `#main` in row 3, gap 0. That is the control, and it did not move.

## Why the band was back

`body.signin-gated #shell` declared a fourth track and no placement to go with it. `#topbar`, `#meeting-strip` and `#main` stay pinned to 1/2/3 by the block beside `#shell`'s own template, so `.signin-bar` was the only child left to auto-place. It took row 2, `#main` stayed in row 3, and the flexible fourth track held nothing:

```
1180x820   37px 48px 732px 3px          .signin-bar@row auto, topbar@row 1, main@row 3
430x932    45px 48px 783.66px 55.34px   (same)
```

## Where the bar belongs, and why that is not a design question

Three signals already agreed and one was silent, so this declares what shipped rather than choosing something new. `mountSignInBar`'s own comment says "the row goes directly under [the header]"; the board branch does exactly that (`insertAdjacentElement('afterend')` on `.board-topbar`); and the doc surface **already rendered** the bar under the topbar, via auto-placement. `grid-row: 2` preserves that appearance. Putting it above the topbar would have been the option that changed a shipped surface, and that one would have needed Bryan.

**One thing I did not change and want to flag.** `mountSignInBar` inserts the bar as `#shell`'s *first* child while the grid renders it *second*, under the topbar — so DOM order and visual order disagree by one, which is a reading-order / visual-order mismatch (WCAG 1.3.2). It is not what caused this bug, fixing it would change tab and screen-reader order on a shipped surface with no measurement behind it, and `write-gate.test.ts` asserts the current insertion point deliberately ("becomes a declared row of the doc shell, above the topbar"). Now that placement is explicit the CSS no longer depends on DOM order at all, so the insertion point can move whenever someone decides it should. Noted in the code beside both halves.

## The grid, and why each track is what it is

```css
body.signin-gated #shell { grid-template-rows: 48px auto auto minmax(0, 1fr); }
body.signin-gated .signin-bar    { grid-row: 2; }
body.signin-gated #meeting-strip { grid-row: 3; }
body.signin-gated #main          { grid-row: 4; }
```

- Track 1 is `48px`, not `auto`. The topbar is in row 1 in both postures and is the same topbar; the old `auto` shrank it to **37px at 1180x820 and 45px at 430px** against the 48px every other page gives it. A second thing that rule changed, which no test read.
- The bar's track is `auto`, not a second `48px`. At 430px its two spans wrap and it wants **49px** — the fixed track was already 1px short.
- The last track is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, matching the signed-in rule: bare `1fr` is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, whose floor is content-driven and works only because `#main` sets `overflow: hidden` 2500 lines away.

## The test, shown failing first

`shell-grid-placement.test.ts` compared `rulesFor('#shell')` selectors for exact equality, so `body.signin-gated #shell` matched nothing and every assertion ran against the signed-in stylesheet. Every read now takes a posture, resolving `body.signin-gated <sel>` over the bare selector the way the cascade does — as an *override*, so `#main` saying row 3 in one posture and row 4 in the other is not a disagreement the model has to reject.

Against the **unmodified** stylesheet it failed four ways (commit 1 lands before the CSS):

```
declares four tracks, the last shrinkable to zero
  → last track is `1fr`, expected minmax(0, …): expected undefined to be '0'
gives the topbar the same track it has signed in
  → expected 'auto' to be '48px'
pins the four in-flow children to rows 1, 2, 3, 4
  → [null, 1, 2, 3], expected [2, 1, 3, 4]
keeps #main in the last row whether or not the strip is displayed
  → strip visible: false: expected 3 to be 4
```

The seven signed-in tests stayed green throughout. The gated child list is not hard-coded: `showSignInBar()` runs against index.html's real markup and the list is read back, so where the bar lands is whatever the shipped code does. A hand-kept copy would have been a second place to state DOM order — which is how `write-gate.ts`'s "`#shell` is a two-row grid (`48px 1fr`)" survived two track-list changes.

`signin-css.test.ts` asserts the same placements through the real cascade, which is the half a text model cannot do: whether `body.signin-gated #main` actually outranks `#main`. It reads `gridRow`, not `gridRowStart` — happy-dom does not expand the shorthand, so the longhand reads `''` however the cascade resolved and a check written against it would have passed on anything. (Caught by probing; the first draft of that assertion was vacuous.)

## The nightly job renders the posture now

It ran only `CW_REQUIRE_SIGNIN_TO_WRITE=0`, and its own header called the other posture "a different layout that deserves its own checks" — a correct sentence standing in for a check nobody had written.

A posture is a *server* setting, so covering both means two servers, not two URLs: they boot in turn on consecutive ports with their own data dirs, each stops as soon as its shots are taken, and a posture that fails to boot fails its own shots while the other still reports. Sequential because the expensive part is Chrome. Six shots, 17 checks. The board is deliberately not duplicated — its bar is an ordinary flow child under `.board-topbar` with no grid to be placed in.

The gated shots wait on `.signin-bar`, not `#main`, and `posture-rendered-*` is the control that makes the pair worth anything: `CW_REQUIRE_SIGNIN_TO_WRITE=1` is a server setting, but `fetchWriteAccess` fails **open** on a timeout, a 404 or a junk body, so a gated shot can come back as an ordinary signed-in page and every geometry check would pass on it. It is asserted both ways — the gated shots must be gated, the signed-in shots must not be — because without the second half a build that mounted the bar for everybody would satisfy the first.

**Verified red, not just green.** Rebuilt with the pre-fix stylesheet and ran the whole job: 4 of 17 failed, with the measured numbers and the fix named, and all four signed-in shell checks stayed green — so it isolates the posture rather than reporting one page's bug against the other.

```
shell-main-reaches-bottom-gated-ipad: #main ends 3px above the bottom of #shell —
  a dead band that hit-tests to the shell. Tracks: 37px 48px 732px 3px;
  in-flow children: .signin-bar@row auto, topbar@row 1, main@row 3
shell-main-reaches-bottom-gated-phone: … 55.34px above …
posture-rendered-doc-{ipad,phone}-gated: the sign-in bar is AUTO-PLACED. […]
  It needs `body.signin-gated .signin-bar { grid-row: 2 }` in styles.css
```

Restored, the full job is 17/17 against two real servers and six real renders.

## Gates

`bunx vitest run` 5523 pass

author: deveshk0
body:
#433's backend job now fails before the e2e suite even starts, in the unit test #440 added:

```
---- endpoint_query::tests::wire_fields_are_camel_case stdout ----
assertion `left == right` failed
  left:  ["pod", "port", "path", "statusCode", "totalLines", "returnedLines", "metrics", "summary"]
  right: ["metrics", "path", "pod", "port", "returnedLines", "statusCode", "summary", "totalLines"]
```

## Why

The test asserted the output keys in sorted order — which is what serde_json produces when its `Map` is a `BTreeMap`, and what `cargo test -p srelens-kube` gives you locally. CI runs `--workspace`, and in that build `thirtyfour` (the desktop smoke-test driver, a dev-dependency) turns on serde_json's `preserve_order` feature. Cargo unifies features across the whole build, so every crate's `Map` becomes an `IndexMap` and keys come out in declaration order. Same class of trap as the rustls-provider one in #439: `-p <crate>` and `--workspace` are two different builds, and only the second is the one CI runs.

## Fix

Sort the keys before comparing. The contract is the set of names, never their order. One hunk in `crates/kube/src/endpoint_query.rs`, with the reason written beside it.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p srelens-kube --lib endpoint_query::tests::wire_fields` passes with default features **and** with `--features serde_json/preserve_order` forced on, which reproduces CI's unified build.
- `cargo tree --workspace -e features -i serde_json` confirms `thirtyfour` is the crate that enables `preserve_order`, and that `-p srelens-kube` alone does not.

## What happens next on #433

With this unit test green the backend job reaches the e2e suite, which is where the `k8s.queryPodEndpoint` case from #440 gets its first CI run against kind. The suite ran clean locally against kind through the real registry with the exact fixture, so I expect it to pass, but that run is the proof. As before, CI does not trigger for PRs into `add-tui`, so this PR will show no checks; #433's next run is the one to watch.

body:
## Resumen
Cierra el ticket 032 (HU-7) -- íconos junto al texto (nunca solo ícono) en los controles principales, y transiciones cortas en cambios de estado visual, respetando `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Cambios
- Íconos (glifos Unicode, sin librería nueva): ↶/↷ Deshacer/Rehacer, 🗑 Borrar, 📁 Archivo, 💾 Proyecto/Guardar, ← Volver al inicio (ganó texto visible, antes era ícono-solo).
- `.ts-fade-in` (nuevo, reusa `--transition-fast` del ticket 025): fundido al cambiar de mob (remonta `Editor`) y al activar "aislar parte" (canvas condicional). "Modo borrar" y abrir/cerrar menús ya venían cubiertos gratis desde el ticket 025.

## Bug real encontrado y corregido en vivo
`.ts-fade-in` escribía `animation: ts-fade-in var(--transition-fast) ease` -- pero `--transition-fast` ya incluye el easing, así que el shorthand resultante tenía DOS funciones de easing (inválido), y el navegador descartaba toda la declaración (`animation: none` confirmado con `getComputedStyle`, no solo sospechado). Corregido quitando el `ease` sobrante.

## Verificación
- 169/169 tests, `lint` y `build` en verde.
- En vivo (Claude in Chrome): íconos visibles en los 6 controles listados en el ticket; nombres accesibles limpios (`read_page`, sin glifo duplicado); animación real confirmada por `getComputedStyle` en el contenedor de `Editor` y el canvas de aislar-parte.

author: krsna1729
body:
## Status

**needs_more_work** — not merge-ready until quiet-host evidence is on this PR.

Rebased onto current `main` (includes #85 batched UDP + #84 host-contention). Next: claim a bench window, then run E0 → E1 → E3 on this PR's `HighResWaiter` (not scratch), under the #83 refuse/mark gate. Post methodology and tables here.


Implements the **A2 code path only** for #82: a reusable shared/sharded high-resolution transport scheduling waiter. This is not a throwaway scratch binary, and it is not Route B.

## Why

PR #81 repaired sub-period pacing phase. The residual Tokio service-visit deficit remains. Issue comments established:

- **A1** (per-connection Tokio tail-spin) works at N=1 and is **rejected on CPU economics at N=30**.
- **A2** (one waiter per worker, absolute `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` deadlines, `epoll_pwait2` / absolute-`timerfd`, service every due connection after a single wake, **no spin**) is the challenger that must be tried before ownership changes.
- Scratch A2 already showed N=1/30 at full rate (N=30 at *lower* CPU than Tokio). Nothing from that scratch was merged; N=200 was invalid harness work.

## API shape

`srt_transport::HighResWaiter<K>` is owned by one worker. Connections are sharded onto workers; no shared dataplane state is required.

- `DeadlineHeap<K>` — min-heap of absolute nanosecond deadlines (production replacement for the scratch’s linear scan)
- `plan_wait` — due-now → one non-blocking poll (`Immediate`), never a spin tail
- `wait` / `wait_with_idle` — park **once**, then return every due key plus ready fds
- Backend: `epoll_pwait2` (nanosecond `timespec`) with absolute-`timerfd` fallback

Mio and Tokio `Conn` expose `schedule_wait(now)` and `schedule_on(&mut waiter, key, now)` so a worker can arm sockets and deadlines without going through `tokio::time::sleep` + `TAIL_SPIN` (that is A1).

After `wait`, the caller services **every** due key. One packet per visit remains the contract.

## How this differs from A1

| | A1 | A2 |
|---|---|---|
| Wait owner | each connection / Tokio task | one waiter per worker |
| Precision | tail-spin after coarse `sleep` | `epoll_pwait2` / absolute `timerfd` |
| CPU at N=30 | collapsed (tasks starve each other) | scratch: full rate, lower CPU than Tokio |
| Spin | yes | no |

## Tests

Unit and integration tests cover deadline selection, wake-all-due after a single park, Immediate/no-spin behaviour (including that a consumed deadline is not re-armed), both wait backends, and socket-readiness wake. No live N=1/30/200 campaign.

Docs: [docs/perf/high-res-waiter.md](docs/perf/high-res-waiter.md), plus a #82 disposition note in `docs/perf/pacing-phase.md`.

## Deferred (intentionally)

- Quiet-host N=1/30/200 timing campaigns and matrix sweeps
- **Route B**: accumulated debt / multi-admit / `SrtConnection` ownership
- Forcing completion runtimes (Monoio/Compio/Glommio) onto this waiter
- #83 host-contention work and #73 batched UDP I/O

Measurements follow separately. This PR only lands the A2 primitive so the next campaign has a reviewable production path rather than scratch.

Refs #82.

author: ibeltoft
body:
Nyt, selvstændigt spil i mappen `klodsjagt/`. Boblejagt er urørt — der er ikke rørt en linje i rodens `index.html`, `sw.js` eller `manifest.webmanifest`. Efter merge ligger spillet på https://ibeltoft.github.io/boblejagt/klodsjagt/

## Spillet

Blokpuslespil i Block Blast-stil: tre brikker ad gangen lægges på et 8×8-bræt, fyldte rækker og kolonner forsvinder. Ingen tid, ingen faldende brikker — det slutter, når ingen af de tre brikker kan være der.

| Element | Beslutning |
|---|---|
| **Greb** | Én finger: tag, træk, slip. Brikken løftes 1,5 felt op over fingeren — et felt er kun 45 px på en iPhone 12, så uden løftet dækker fingeren præcis det felt, man sigter efter. |
| **Feedback før slip** | Skygge på brættet, og de striber der vil forsvinde lyser op, mens man holder. Brikker uden plads tegnes halvt gennemsigtige. |
| **Point** | 1 pr. celle lagt; `ryddede celler × 10 × antal striber × kombo` (kombo op til ×8). To striber på én gang giver 300 mod 80 — hele det taktiske indhold. |
| **PWA** | Egen service worker, eget manifest og eget ikon. Virker offline, installerbart på hjemmeskærmen, stilling og rekord gemmes efter hvert træk. |
| **Kode** | Én HTML-fil, canvas + WebAudio, ingen afhængigheder, danske kommentarer — samme konvention som Boblejagt. Balancetal samlet i `TUNE` øverst i filen. |

## Fairness-reglen

Bakken trækkes om, indtil alle tre brikker kan bruges i en eller anden rækkefølge (tilbagesporing på en brætkopi, hvor striber også ryddes undervejs). Store brikker trækkes desuden sjældnere, jo mere fyldt brættet er.

Målt effekt, auto-spiller med støjknap ε (sandsynligheden for et tilfældigt lovligt træk), 60 spil pr. linje:

| Spiller | ε | Median træk **med** regel | **Uden** regel | Median point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Perfekt | 0 | 659 | 479 | 34.514 |
| Rutineret | 0,15 | 140 | 89 | 6.887 |
| Almindelig | 0,35 | 56 | 47 | 2.257 |
| Distræt | 0,6 | 23 | 25 | 549 |

Reglen forlænger spillet mest for dem, der spiller bedst, og er inden for støjen for den distræte. Den fjerner altså lodtrækningens nederlag uden at gøre spillet lettere for den, der spiller dårligt. Pris i regnekraft: 0,0 ms i median og 1,7 ms i værste af 74 målinger — usynligt selv på en gammel telefon.

En almindelig spiller lander på 3–5 minutter pr. runde, en rutineret på 7–12. Medianen svinger ±20 % mellem kørsler (meget lang hale); metode og forbehold står i `klodsjagt/DESIGN.md`.

## Verificeret

Kørt i Chromium med touch-emulering (390×844, deviceScaleFactor 2):

- Finger-træk lægger brikken der, hvor skyggen stod, og løftet over fingeren virker
- Lydknap slår til/fra; forfra-boksen åbner, "Nej" lukker, "Ja" rydder bræt og point
- Stilling og point overlever genindlæsning
- Service worker registreres, og spillet starter med netværket slået fra
- Ingen konsolfejl under hverken interaktion eller lange auto-spil
- Layout tjekket i portræt (390×844), landskab (844×390) og lille skærm (320×568)

## Filer

| Fil | Rolle |
|---|---|
| `klodsjagt/index.html` | Hele spillet — regler, grafik, lyd, gem/hent |
| `klodsjagt/sw.js` | Service worker, offline efter første besøg |
| `klodsjagt/manifest.webmanifest` | Installerbar på hjemmeskærmen |
| `klodsjagt/icon-*.png` | Ikon, tegnet med samme klodser som spillet |
| `klodsjagt/DESIGN.md` | Spildesign, balancetal, målinger, næste skridt |
| `klodsjagt/README.md` | Kort spillervejledning |
| `README.md` | Tilføjet afsnit og link til det nye spil |

## Ikke med

Fortryd-træk, daglig udfordring, bombeklods og lokal top-5-liste er beskrevet som idéer i `klodsjagt/DESIGN.md`, men ikke bygget.

author: mavrovde
body:
## What
Three #274 review findings, fixed together because they live in one handler — and per the new rule 11, fixed in the work rather than filed away.

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **#279** | a double-click or retry minted a **second permanent card** (phase 1 ships no DELETE) — and the first fix for it was still racy: two sessions with a barrier produced two cards | a **DB-level UNIQUE** on the new `opportunities.promoted_from_interaction_id` (migration `promote0005`, self-adopting, backfilled). The loser of a race rolls back and returns the winner's card. Plus the frontend AC I had skipped: the button latches in flight, and — because the admin app is zoneless — explicitly repaints, so it visibly reads "Promoting…" |
| **#278** | every `cv_request`/`booking` was relabelled `recruiter_outreach`, corrupting the one dimension the pipeline exists to measure (#249) | `source` derives from the interaction through an explicit map, with a tested fallback so a future channel (#263, #264) can't 500 promote before its mapping lands |
| **#277** | post-commit re-select returns the same identity-mapped instance with a stale collection (lessons §22) — it only *appeared* to work because `notes` was never loaded | `db.refresh(attribute_names=["notes"])` |

**Documented consequence of idempotency, pinned by a test:** overrides passed to a *repeat* promote are ignored. Changing a card is an edit, not a re-promote.

## Also fixed here (it blocked this work three times)
The integration/E2E overlay published Postgres on **5433** — the same port the local pytest DB uses — so every verification stack silently evicted it and the next `pytest`/pre-push run died with `password authentication failed for user "postgres"`, a symptom that looks nothing like a port conflict. The overlay now publishes **5533** (`POSTGRES_HOST_PORT` overrides); nothing inside the stack uses the host port. Documented in `README_TESTING.md`.

## Layer validation (rule 12 — all three apply, all three done)
- **Backend unit**: 883 passed, 7 skipped, **100.00%** under CI's `-n auto --cov-fail-under=100`. Includes a parametrized origin case per interaction source, an unknown-source fallback case, a duplicate-row assertion **against the DB** (not just the response), and the idempotency-consequence pin.
- **WireMock integration tier**: idempotency and cv_request-origin asserted over **real HTTP through the proxy** — the contract proven past serialization and the session boundary, not merely in-process.
- **E2E**: new `recruiter-journey.spec.ts` walks the product's core flow in a browser — inbox → promote → pipeline, with the original message surviving as the first timeline note — plus double-click-yields-one-card and cv_request-keeps-its-origin. 3/3 green against the prod-topology stack.

Closes #279 #278
Refs #277 — **not** claimed as closed: its acceptance criterion asks for a mutation-pin, and the reviewer proved (and I reproduced) that the re-select and `db.refresh` forms are observably equivalent in this handler, so no test can distinguish them. What this PR does deliver for it is the audit: `move_stage` and `add_note` already used the refresh idiom, promote is now aligned. #277 stays open for a decision on retiring that AC.

author: honeybeesquad
body:
`china-chongqing-hydro` and `china-guizhou-hydro` reached the globe with `sourceStatus: "live"` on data nothing had fetched. Both loaders run the decorative-probe pattern - fetch `ember-energy.org`, then throw unconditionally - and return `buildTypicalHydroRegion` output scaled to a hardcoded annual anchor (0.22 TWh/yr Chongqing, 0.25 TWh/yr Guizhou).

They slipped past #812's guard on a technicality. `stampLive` downgraded a region only when it carried `confidenceTier: "T3-modelled"` (or a canonical `estimated` tier with no `confidenceTier` at all), but `buildTypicalHydroRegion` passes `regionTier: "anchored"`, so its output lands on `T2-annual-calibrated` and neither test fired. The 2026-08-20 China push hit the same thing and patched `china-hubei-hydro` and `china-hunan-hydro` by hand; Chongqing and Guizhou were missed.

## What changed

**`src/lib/resilient.ts`** - `stampLive` now also refuses to stamp any region the canonical REGIONS table declares `sourceProvenance: "modelled-fallback"`, whatever its confidence tier. It reads the table rather than the record, because `stampSourceProvenance` runs *after* `stampLive`. `scripts/ci/check-source-provenance-coherence.ts` already classes a live tier paired with `modelled-fallback` as an **impossible** pairing; this stops `withFallback` minting one.

**`src/data/china-chongqing.json.ts`, `src/data/china-guizhou.json.ts`** - the hydro sub-region gains the explicit `sourceStatus: "cached"` / `sourceProvenance: "modelled-fallback"` override that `china-hubei` and `china-hunan` already use, and `regionTier` moves `"live"` → `"estimated"`.

**`src/data/pakistan.json.ts`** - same latent mislabel: `regionTier: "live"` on a decorative probe. Its two sub-regions are T3, so the existing guard already caught them and nothing shipped wrong, but the option was still a false claim one hydro builder away from the same bug. `regionTier` moves to `"estimated"`, matching every other China sibling.

**`tests/resilient.test.ts`** - one case: a `T2-annual-calibrated` region whose canonical provenance is `modelled-fallback` must not be stamped live. It fails on the pre-fix code (`expected 'live' to be 'cached'`).

**Three snapshots regenerated** through the real loader path - `sourceStatus` and `lastSuccessAt` are the only fields that differ.

**`STATUS.md`** - new entry.

## Blast radius

Exactly the four China hydro regions. Of the 240 regions declared `modelled-fallback`, 234 are `tier: "estimated"` and were already caught by the existing clauses. The other six are those four hydro records plus `austria` and `russia-murmansk-wind` - and both of those are built by `statics.json.ts`, which never calls `withFallback`, so `stampLive` cannot reach them. For hubei and hunan the new clause is a no-op behind their hand-written overrides.

Swept the rest of the loaders for the same shape: 59 use the decorative-probe pattern, and after this change none of them pairs it with `regionTier: "live"`.

## No tier moved

No `tier:` field in `src/lib/regions.ts` changed - `china-chongqing-hydro` and `china-guizhou-hydro` were already `anchored` - and `ci:tally-golden` is untouched (459 regions; T1a=160 T1b=26 T1c=1 T2=23 T3=249). This is a freshness-label change only: profiles, `peakGW` and uncertainty bands are unchanged. As with hubei and hunan, the hydro records' `lastSuccessAt` now reads `2024-01-01` (the anchor's own date) rather than a build timestamp, because the explicit `cached` override is preserved ahead of the stamping.

## Gates

`npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm test` ✅ 1213 pass · `ci:tier-coherence` ✅ · `ci:tally-golden` ✅ · `ci:docs-drift` ✅ · full `ci:gates` ✅ (includes `ci:source-provenance-coherence`, relevant here).

## Follow-ups

26 records across 25 committed snapshots still carry pre-guard stale `live`. That is the inert caveat logged at #812 - the fallback read path runs `stampCached`, which overwrites `sourceStatus` unconditionally, so a stale label in the file never reaches the site. Clearing it wants a full data-refresh build, not a hand edit.

author: 709sakata
body:
The seeded opportunities were owned by whichever real OWNER or MANAGER the community happened to have — on `neo88` that resolves to a named person — so a real member showed as the host of five invented experiences, on the deployment Milestone 5 points reviewers at.

Making the shared demo account the host instead trades that for two other faults. Resident recording ⑪ is "look at another resident's profile", reached by opening an experience and tapping the host's name: if the host is the account the reviewer is signed in as, that opens their own profile. And every seeded evaluation would then be self-awarded.

So the host is a third party the script creates: a `MANAGER` of this community who is nobody real and is not the account the reviewer signs in as. It carries no `Identity` row, so it cannot sign in.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opportunity host | a real community member | `Demo Host` |
| Evaluator | the same real member | `Demo Host` |
| Recording ⑪ | works | works |
| No eligible member in the community | exits 1 | no longer possible |

`--remove` deletes the host last, after the opportunities and evaluations that name it; the membership goes with the user.

## A verification note that applies to the two merged PRs as well

`tsconfig.json` sets `include: ["src/**/*.ts"]`, so `scripts/` is outside it and `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` never looked at this file. The "`tsc --noEmit` passes" line in #1263 and #1264 was true of the command and empty of meaning for the file they changed.

Checked properly this time, with a config that includes the script: both the merged code and this change type-check clean. Nothing was actually broken — the check was.

The directory is presumably excluded because several other scripts do not compile (`backfill-user-did.ts` has a real `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` mismatch, and four scripts import with `.ts` extensions). Bringing `scripts/` under CI would mean fixing those first, which is a separate change.

author: copilot
body:
Intercut can now be driven by explicit hold intervals (e.g. `2, 1, 1, 2, 3, 2`) instead of only Hz ramp timing. When interval lists are not provided, existing Hz ramp/easing, beat-sync, sourceClock, consumeMode, forceFinalClip, and tail behavior remain unchanged.

- **Planner: interval-list automation path (`src/utils/intercut.ts`)**
  - Extended `FrequencyAutomationConfig` with optional `sliceIntervalsSec`.
  - Added interval utilities:
    - `sanitizeSliceIntervals(raw)`
    - `parseSliceIntervalList(text)`
    - `sliceIntervalListSum(intervals)`
    - `formatSliceIntervalList(intervals)`
  - Updated `buildIntercutSlices` to:
    - use sanitized interval durations in order (cycled) with `minSliceSec` floor
    - clamp the last target-duration slice to remaining budget
    - bypass Hz ramp and beat-sync slice timing when interval lists are active
    - preserve existing slot rotation, source clocking, landing, and tail mechanics

- **Planner tests: interval semantics and edge cases (`src/utils/intercut.test.ts`)**
  - Added parsing test for comma/space/semicolon input and junk filtering.
  - Added deterministic slice tests for:
    - explicit list sequencing and freezeHidden resume behavior
    - list cycling to fill target duration
    - final-slice clamping
    - beat-sync ignored under interval-list mode

- **Modal UX: cut timing mode switch + interval lane (`src/components/IntercutModal.tsx`, `src/styles/modal.css`)**
  - Renamed **Cut frequency** → **Cut timing**.
  - Added mode toggle: **Frequency ramp** vs **Interval list**.
  - Interval mode adds:
    - `aria-label="Interval list"` text input (default `2, 1, 1, 2, 3, 2`)
    - proportional interval preview lane labeled by slot/duration
    - “Repeat list to fill swap duration” toggle

author: nizovtsevnv
body:
## What this changes

Re-declaring a name **already bound in the same scope** is now a compile error, as Declarations §6.2
requires. `check` used to accept it, and the four backends then disagreed: the different-type
spelling passed `check`, was refused only by the x86 lowering fence, and trapped at run time on
aarch64/riscv64/wasm (133/133/134) — before that fence landed, x86_64 took no `match` arm and
answered a silent `77`. The same-type spelling was accepted on all four and answered `109`
everywhere. It is now one located `check` diagnostic naming the second declaration's line, so
`check`, `-o` and the three emit-to-stdout backends refuse it identically and emit nothing.
§6.1 cross-scope shadowing is untouched.

## Kind

- [ ] A **wrong value** fixed — a clean compile that produced the wrong answer now does not
- [ ] A valid program that used to fail now works
- [x] A failure made **loud and located** where it was silent or unplaced (the program was already
      refused, or should have been)
- [ ] New surface: a construct, a backend shape, a CLI verb or flag
- [ ] Gate or tooling only — no change to what the compiler emits
- [ ] Refactor with **no** behaviour change (the GAS delta is empty, see below)

- [x] Changelog line added, or this change is one of the last two kinds

## The specification answers this directly

`b4e7979:spec/40-declarations.md`, §6.2 (verbatim, via `git show`):

> #### 6.2 Same scope — forbidden
>
> Re-declaring a name **already bound in the same scope** is a **compile error**. This is the same
> rule as "no duplicate names, no implicit winner" for module scope (Modules, decisions MOD-8).
> (Same-scope shadowing, as in Rust, is **rejected** — for clarity: a name means one thing within its
> scope.)
>
> The **one exception** is **function overloading by signature** (Functions §1.4 / FN-7): a name MAY
> be bound to several **function values** in the same scope when they differ in their **parameter
> signature**, resolved per call by the argument types. […]

The exception is not reachable today: the lower has no local overload set (`local_ty`'s last push
simply wins), and no fixture in `test/` spells two same-named local `fn` values. If it is ever
implemented, `sema_redecl_candidate` is where the signature carve-out goes; the predicate says so.

## Why the refusal is in `sema`, and why that does not contradict #412

Two neighbouring fences, opposite in kind — this is the paragraph to read before assuming they
disagree.

**#406 / PR #412** put its guard in `src/lower.al` (`require_agg_type`). That was right: the program
it refuses is **valid** under §5/§6.1 — two declarations in *different* scopes — and three backends
already lower it correctly. What refuses it is an x86 slot-map limitation: the map reuses the FIRST
reservation together with the FIRST binding's recorded type. A backend limitation belongs in the
backend, and that guard is untouched here.

**#414 is the opposite case.** §6.2 makes the program **ill-formed**. The three non-x86 backends were
not "working correctly" on it — they were diverging: they trapped on one spelling and answered
alongside x86 on the other. A rule about an ill-formed program belongs in the front end, where one
refusal closes all four backends at once, exactly as the `enum_disc_dup` check was moved into `check`
for the same reason. This is also why the lowering guard could not substitute: it never sees the
same-type spelling at all, and it cannot reach `alatyr wat|aarch64|riscv64`.

## How it is implemented

"The same scope" is **one statement list**. `stmts_same_scope_redecl` is a structural prepass in
`src/sema.al`, beside `stmts_bad_loop_control`, called from `check_decl` before the ordinary
statement walk (guarded on `failed == false`, so an existing more specific structural diagnostic
stays authoritative). Each list is scanned against itself only; every nested list — `While`, `For`,
`Loop`, `Unchecked`, `AllocWith`, both `If` branches, every `Match` arm body, `CompIf`, `CompFor`,
`CompForRange`, `CompMatch` — is scanned separately. A candidate is a `Stmt::Assign` whose name is
followed by `:` in source (`ast::assign_is_decl`, so `x := v` and `x : T = v` but not `x = v` or
`x += v`), is not `_`, and is not the same source occurrence (`ns2 != ns`, since one source
declaration can reach the AST as more than one node).

Deliberately *not* folded into `check_stmts`: the checker's `locals` table is flat and
function-scoped — a `:=` local leaks out of its block here — so it cannot answer "already bound in
THIS scope" without new per-block bookkeeping on that hot path. The statement list is the scope and
it is already in hand.

Diagnostic: a new located `CheckErr` class, `SAME_SCOPE_REDECL_DIAG_MARKER = 6897000000000000000`,
placed between the nested-array-parameter and qualified-private-constant markers, so only the
former's upper bound moves and every other decoded range stays byte-identical. Both driver decoders
(`d_sema_reject` and `check_files`) learn it.

Worth a line for a reviewer: `stmts_bad_loop_control` next door does **not** recurse into
`CompForRange` (it falls to the `_` arm and its body is never walked); the new predicate does. Either
that is a gap in the older walker or it is deliberate — not resolved here, and worth its own issue
after landing rather than a drive-by change to a working checker.

## `src/lower.al` changes as a consequence, not as part of the fix

The compiler violated §6.2 in exactly **one** place. `src/lower.al` declared `fbi :=
field_base_index(base)` twice in one statement list — lines 17581 and 17799, both at indentation 6
with no block boundary between them. The second is renamed `dfbi` (4 occurrences: the declaration and
its three uses at 17931/17933/17934). Both bound the same value into the same slot, so behaviour is
unchanged; the sibling `s3fbi` at 17777 had already been forced to dodge the identical collision,
which is the best evidence this is a true positive rather than an over-fire.

An independent brace-depth scan over `src/` and `lib/` finds exactly that one duplicate — the same
verdict the compiler itself reached, which is what validates the scanner.

## Two existing fixtures encoded the now-forbidden shape

Both are corrected in this commit. Neither is weakened, and neither changes an observable: both pass
on the parent *and* on this branch, which is why they produce **no** corpus transition.

**`test/issue268_comptime_rebind.al`** — `seq()` spelled its rebinding as a second same-scope
`x := 7` right after `comptime x := 5`. That is precisely the §6.2 shape. #268 is still open and this
is its acceptance artifact, so the change is deliberate and narrow: `seq()` now asserts the comptime
binding's value (`if x != 5 { return 1 }`) and returns through `y := 7`. What #268 is *about* — the
comptime binding carrying its real value rather than 0 — is preserved and still measured. The
function still returns 7, so `run issue268_comptime_rebind 26` is unchanged, `fmt_test_has_all`'s
needles `"comptime x := 5"` and `"x := 7"` both still appear (the latter in `branch()`/`block()`),
and all three e2e rows stay green on both trees. The lost coverage did not vanish: the same-scope
`comptime` rebind is now `test/same_scope_redecl_comptime.al`, a reject fixture, and the fixture
header says so. Read as history this must not look like someone quietly weakened another issue's
test.

**`test/fmt_compound_assign_ops.al`** — line 146's `mut fresh343 : u64 = 4` is removed, so the long
whitespace-run declaration `fresh343 <520 spaces> := 5` is the only binding of that name. This
**strengthens** the row it belongs to: previously, if the long-whitespace `:=` were misread as a
reassignment, `fresh343` would still hold 5 and `fresh343 != 5` would not notice; now a misreading
leaves the name unbound and the program is rejected outright. Exit stays 42 and the `"fresh343 := 5"`
formatter needle is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **The fixture failed first.** Baseline: a detached wor

author: themeinerlp
body:
Replaces the patch-based approach this PR originally carried. MetalLB now comes from the official chart, the way every other controller in `base-controllers` already does.

## Why

MetalLB was the only controller still pulled as raw upstream kustomize. The upstream `config/` overlays expose no knobs, so resources and `priorityClassName` had to be hand-maintained as strategic-merge patches, and adding the frr-k8s workloads would have meant roughly seventy more lines of them.

It is also why IPv6 did not work. The native backend rejects any `IPAddressPool` with a v6 CIDR, and the speaker cannot parse a v6 peer address at all:

```
dial "fd83:4192:3b5e:15::1": invalid remote address:
address fd83:4192:3b5e:15::1:179: too many colons in address
```

Since #238 merged, that rejection also hits the **v4** `BGPAdvertisement local`, because the webhook validates the configuration as a whole against cluster state.

Current impact on `feather-core`:

- `base-configs` fails every reconcile and never converges, blocking `configs`, `rook`, `rook-fr01`, `base-apps`, `apps`, `monitoring` and `security`.
- All ten live fr01 speakers report `ConfigurationState: Invalid`. Announcements still work because each pod runs on its last loaded config, but **the next speaker restart drops that node out of BGP**.

## What changed

| File | |
|---|---|
| `base-sources/metallb.yaml` | new `HelmRepository` |
| `base/controllers/metallb/` | new base: namespace, HelmRelease, kustomization |
| `base-controllers/metallb/kustomization.yaml` | references the base, patches it with `release.yaml` |
| `base-controllers/metallb/release.yaml` | chart pin `=0.16.1` and values |
| `base-controllers/metallb/kustomization.yml` | removed, with all its patches |

`frrk8s.enabled: true` is the chart default in 0.16.1, set explicitly so a future default change cannot move it back. The deprecated in-speaker `frr` mode is pinned off.

Resources and `priorityClassName: feather-platform` are set through values for controller, speaker and all four frr-k8s containers. The `frr` container gets 256Mi against 64Mi for the sidecars: an OOM there drops every BGP session on the node, while the sidecars only copy files and reload config. The four initContainers stay unset, because the subchart offers no values for them and patching them would reintroduce exactly what this PR removes.

## Verification

`scripts/validate.sh` passes (exit 0, 0 invalid, 0 errors across all layers).

`helm template` against chart 0.16.1 with these values, checked object by object: every long-running container in all four workloads carries requests and limits, all four carry `priorityClassName`.

The `metallb-system` namespace is declared in the base with `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged`, which the `frr` container needs for `NET_ADMIN`, `SYS_ADMIN` and `NET_BIND_SERVICE`.

## Rollout: this is a replace, not an upgrade

Read before merging.

Helm prefixes workload names with the release name, so `speaker` becomes `metallb-speaker` and `controller` becomes `metallb-controller`. The speaker runs `hostNetwork: true` on ports 9120 and 7946, so the old and new DaemonSets cannot overlap on a node. Flux prunes the old objects and Helm installs new ones, which means **every VIP is withdrawn for the length of that gap**, including `10.200.90.1` (the Envoy gateway, so all external ingress).

The CRDs keep their names and are adopted rather than recreated (take-ownership is on by default in helm-controller v1.6.4), so `IPAddressPool`, `BGPPeer` and `BGPAdvertisement` survive untouched and the same addresses get re-announced afterwards.

Worth merging into a window where a few minutes without ingress is acceptable.

## Pre-existing problems this does not fix

- `fr01-str-01/02/03` have had **no** v4 BGP session since well before this change (`read OPEN from "192.168.15.1": EOF`), cutting effective redundancy from seven paths to four. Looks like missing neighbour entries for .7/.8/.9 on the peer.
- The `metallb` PodMonitor in the `configs` layer scrapes `port: monitoring`, but the speaker port is named `metricshttps`. MetalLB metrics are not being collected today. The chart can render PodMonitors itself (`prometheus.podMonitor.enabled`), which would retire that hand-written object; left for a separate PR.

v6 sessions come up only once the peer has the ten v6 neighbours configured under `address-family ipv6 unicast`.

author: akashtalole
body:
…lure

Two bugs compounding into an opaque "Analysis failed: /api/analysis/run -> 500" in the dashboard, with no way to tell what actually broke:

1. webapp/public/js/app.js's getJSON() threw on any non-OK response using only the status code, before ever reading the response body -- so the {error, detail} JSON the server actually sent (e.g. a Python traceback in `detail`) was silently discarded. Now reads the body and surfaces `error`/`detail` in the thrown error's message.

2. agents/kumbh_analysis/nodes.py never had a live end-to-end test against the real Anthropic API during development (no key was available in the dev sandbox) -- only the no-key rule-based fallback path was ever exercised. Any failure in the real LLM call (bad model string, auth error, network egress, unexpected response shape) was completely uncaught, crashing run_analysis.py and surfacing as a 500. Wrapped both LLM calls in try/except: on failure, the report now still generates successfully (200) using the rule-based fallback, with the actual exception message embedded inline so the real cause is visible in the report itself instead of requiring a CloudWatch Logs lookup.

Verified locally with a deliberately invalid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: the report now generates successfully and embeds the real error ("authentication_error: API key is invalid.") instead of crashing -- confirms this is likely the actual cause of the reported issue, and that the fix makes it self-diagnosing regardless of the underlying error.

author: worxnation-collab
body:
The virality changes, everything but the numbered series.

**Hook-first frames.** Every layout opens on the hook line, large, at 0.0s, with the voice starting 0.35s in under it. The brand and the reference moved to the end card. The story's hook is now its own most dramatic sentence and the challenge's is the question itself (`LEAD`, `HOOK_HOLD`, `drawHook`, `drawBrand` in `lib/tiktokRender.ts`).

**A rotating cast on nine roads.** `autoCast(date)` walks forward from a fixed epoch (2026-09-07) taking the first preferred reader not used in the last two days and the first preferred scene not used in the last six, memoised, so the dashboard and the runner compute the same cast for a date. Seven new 9:16 road paintings (`art/tiktok-scenes.json`, a `tiktok-road` kind, `public/tiktok/roads/`) generated with the Harvest Road and Lamplight as references. A missing painting falls back to the Harvest Road (`loadScene`) rather than failing a post. Verified over sixteen days: no reader within two days, no scene within six.

**The one-question challenge.** Kinds `challenge` and `challenge2`: one of yesterday's five questions, read aloud as a twelve-second clock starts, the reveal with the teach line, and an ask to comment. About twenty seconds. The quiz layout in `solo` mode, no fourth renderer. The second slot is a different question (two apart) by the next reader on the next road. The CPU's play is sliced from the same `quizPlan` the replay uses, so the two posts never disagree. New form `ChallengePost.tsx`; the runner schedules five posts a day (verse 07:00, challenge 10:00, quiz 12:30, challenge2 16:00, story 19:30).

**Per-network asks.** `callToAction()` / `withAsk()` in `social.ts`: TikTok and Snapchat captions are not tappable, so those ask for the follow rather than carrying a URL; Instagram the bio link; YouTube, Facebook and X live URLs; a challenge asks for the comment first. The copy prompt asks for the same per network, and `social.ts` appends the ask if the words come back without one.

**A minute-long story.** The `story` prompt asks for two paragraphs, 80 to 100 words, opening on the dramatic moment, with the hook as the most dramatic sentence. A cached three-paragraph story still renders.

**Your own clip.** Kind `own`: the operator uploads an MP4 they recorded, says in a line what it is, and the caption is written in their voice for every network and posted through the same `MadeCard`. No AI note on it.

**The week's numbers.** An `analytics` action reads Ayrshare's per-post numbers for one (date, kind), normalised to views, likes, comments, shares, seconds watched and new followers, cached six hours in the bucket. The hub's "The last seven days" card totals a week per network and per kind.

body:
The `Tests (Web)` job ran `npx playwright test --project=desktop`. The mobile project was defined in `playwright.config.ts` and never executed by CI.

That is a structural blind spot, not a stylistic one. The two navs are separate markup, a top bar on desktop and a bottom tab bar on mobile, with CSS showing exactly one. A desktop-only run cannot observe a mobile-only regression.

**It already caught something.** The nav walk added in #468 passed on desktop and failed on mobile, because the mobile bar composes each link from an icon span and a label span, so its accessible name is `"≡ Workouts"` against desktop's `"Workouts"`, and an exact name match found nothing. I only saw it because I ran the mobile project by hand. On this job as it stood, that defect would have merged green.

The job now runs `npx playwright test`, which covers both projects. Cost is about a second.

## Also documents what the smoke does not prove

`docs/CUTOVER.md` claimed the parity smoke as a gate check without saying what it actually covers. It now records the limit: the suite exercises routing, auth, rendering and nav reachability, not the production server shape.

`next.config.ts` sets `output: "standalone"` only off Vercel, and the suite serves that build with `next start`, so the server under test matches neither Vercel's runtime nor `.next/standalone/server.js`. That is a deliberate trade, since forcing standalone output on Vercel corrupts the Edge middleware bundle. I did not change the build config to chase the warning, because the regression risk there is real and the gain is cosmetic. Better to state plainly what a green smoke means: the app is coherent, not that production was rehearsed.

## Verification

- `CI=1 npx playwright test` 6/6, three desktop and three mobile, which is exactly what the job now runs
- vitest 213/213 across 40 files
- `tsc --noEmit` clean

author: kokorolx
body:
Adds `npm-publish.yml`, a reusable workflow scoped the same way `governed-tag-release.yml` is: it validates the immutable state a pushed release tag already points at, then publishes it to the npm registry with `--provenance`. It never calculates a version, creates or moves tags, commits source, or edits a changelog.

Validation before publish:
- tag is canonical v-prefixed SemVer and matches both `package.json` and the caller's version file (`version: X.Y.Z` metadata, or a `.json` file with a top-level `version` field — plugin repos keep their canonical version in `plugin.json`)
- refuses any `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`/`prepare` script in `package.json`
- re-running a tag whose version is already on the registry is a no-op, not a failure

The caller-owned `test-command` runs in a separate job with no access to the npm token. Prerelease tags publish under their prerelease identifier as dist-tag (`-beta.N` → `beta`), stable tags under `latest`.

First consumers: the five `@img2threejs/plugin-*` packages and the `img2` harness (caller PRs open in their repos and will re-pin to the merged SHA of this PR per the pinning policy).

author: alcinoafonso
rob-branchleft
body:
Closes branchLeft/workspace#511

## What

`provision-tenant.yml`'s first step — `Refuse to provision through a half-migrated flow` — is the only thing standing between a dispatch of that workflow and a created repository, a live identity, an undeployable stack and a PAT copy, with no automatic rollback. Nothing tested it.

This adds `infra/provisioning/scripts/test_provision_tenant_flow_gate.py` (21 tests). It is discovered with no workflow change by `infra-platform-ci.yml`'s `provisioning-typecheck` job, which already runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` from `infra/provisioning` — and that job is a **required** status check on `main`, so this is enforced, not merely present. Suite: **519 → 540**, all green.

**Test-only. `provision-tenant.yml` is byte-identical to `origin/main`** — `git diff --stat origin/main -- .github/workflows/provision-tenant.yml` is empty, and the whole-branch diff is one added file.

## The gate's behaviour, established by execution before anything was written

The step's shell was extracted by hand with `sed` — independently of the test file's own extraction, so the test could not be the thing certifying itself — and run against nine values:

| `FLOW_READY` | exit |
|---|---|
| `true` | 0 |
| `""`, unset, `TRUE`, `True`, `true `, `1`, `false`, `yes` | 1 |

The issue's premise holds exactly as filed: strict `!=` against the literal `true`, fails closed on unset, `exit 1` follows the annotation. **The gate does gate.** This PR is about keeping it that way, which is what the issue asks for.

## The finding: running the gate's script is necessary and nowhere near sufficient

Whether the gate *refuses a value* and whether the *job stops* are different questions. Nine things sit outside the extracted shell and each decides whether `exit 1` reaches anything. Every one was applied to `provision-tenant.yml` in the worktree, and every one **left the behavioural assertions green with the gate, in effect, open**:

1. **`env:` rebinding** — `FLOW_READY: 'true'`, or a bind to a different variable name. The script is byte-identical and refuses everything but `true`; it is simply never handed anything else. The repository variable an owner sets no longer reaches the gate.
2. **`continue-on-error: true` on the gate step** — `exit 1` no longer stops the job.
3. **`if:` on the gate step** — a skipped step is a passed step to everything after it.
4. **`if: always()` on a step *below* the gate.** The gate refuses, the job goes red, and `Generate the tenant repo from the template` runs anyway — it needs no checkout, and `GH_PAT_TENANT_PROVISIONING` and `$TENANT_REPO` are both job-level env. A red run that created a tenant repository is worse than either outcome alone, because nobody searches a failed run for state it created. This idiom is **already live in this workflow** on the `Summary` step, four hundred lines from where the same line would be a disaster.
5. **A second job.** `_steps_block` ran to end of file, so it spanned every job below `provision`. Moving the repo-generation step into a new job with no `needs:` satisfied the ordering assertion while removing the gate from in front of it.
6. **A trailing `# comment` on that second job's key.** The job-key pattern required end-of-line after the colon, so the hidden job was neither counted nor bounded — and the `provision` block ran on through the unrecognised key and swallowed the hidden job's steps, so an ungated parallel `gh repo create` still read as "after the gate".
7. **A step inserted *above* the gate.** "The gate precedes the first mutating step" is satisfied by a new step at the top of the job, because that step precedes the named one too.
8. **A step with no `name:`** — invisible to a file that addresses every step by name.
9. **`defaults: run: shell:`** at workflow or job level, which substitutes the interpreter handed every `run:` block, the gate's included.

## What closes them

- `_job_names` / `_job_block`, with `_steps_block` bounded by the `provision` job rather than by EOF; job keys tolerate a trailing comment.
- **Both parsers refuse a shape they cannot read rather than skipping it.** Any line at job-key indent that is not a readable job key, and any step that does not open with `name:`, raises with a message naming the assumption. A quoted job key or a flow mapping is now a red test, not a silent gap — (6) and (8) both got through precisely by being skipped quietly.
- `STEPS_ALLOWED_BEFORE_THE_GATE`, empty today. There is no such thing as a step this file can *prove* creates nothing, only a step somebody has read and decided creates nothing; adding a name is that decision, recorded once and in the open.
- `STEPS_ALLOWED_TO_SURVIVE_A_FAILED_PREDECESSOR = ("Summary",)` — every step's `if:` and `continue-on-error:` checked against it, not just the gate's.
- `ALLOWED_GATE_STEP_KEYS = {env, run}` — an allowlist, so an unfamiliar key on this one step stops the test rather than slipping past.
- The `env:` binding asserted to be exactly `FLOW_READY: ${{ vars.TENANT_PROVISIONING_FLOW_HETZNERISED }}` and nothing else.
- No `defaults:` at workflow or job level.
- The extracted script is run as `bash -e <file>` — what a `run:` with no `shell:` gets on a Linux runner — rather than `bash -c <string>`, which differs on exactly the point this gate is about.

## Sabotage: twelve cases, each red for the right reason

Every round purged `__pycache__` and ran `python3 -B`, so a cached `.pyc` could not re-test the original file. Each was applied by an anchored substitution whose diff was confirmed non-empty, then reverted, then re-run green before the next.

| # | Sabotage | Red on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `env:` → `FLOW_READY: 'true'` | `test_flow_ready_is_bound_to_the_repository_variable` |
| 2 | `env:` → a different variable name | `test_flow_ready_is_bound_to_the_repository_variable` |
| 3 | `continue-on-error: true` on the gate | `…_is_not_soft_failed`, `…_carries_nothing_else`, `…_no_later_step_survives…` |
| 4 | `if: ${{ false }}` on the gate | `…_is_not_skippable_by_a_condition`, `…_carries_nothing_else`, `…_no_later_step_survives…` |
| 5 | `if: ${{ always() }}` on `Generate the tenant repo from the template` | `test_no_later_step_survives_the_gates_refusal` |
| 6 | `continue-on-error: true` on `Clone and generate` | `test_no_later_step_survives_the_gates_refusal` |
| 7 | mutating step moved to a second, un-`needs:`-ed job | `…_share_one_job`, `…_precedes_the_first_step_that_creates_anything` |
| 8 | same, with `# split out for readability` on the job key | same two |
| 9 | named `gh repo create` step inserted above the gate | `test_nothing_unvetted_runs_before_the_gate` |
| 10 | **unnamed** `gh repo create` step inserted above the gate | 4 failures incl. `test_nothing_unvetted_runs_before_the_gate` |
| 11 | job-level `defaults: run: shell: bash -c "true" {0}` | `test_no_defaults_block_can_replace_the_shell_that_runs_the_gate` |
| 12 | quoted job key `"provision":` | 21/21 — the parser refuses a shape it cannot read |

Plus the four original behavioural ones, all still red: gate moved below the repo-generation step (2 failures), comparison loosened to `=~ ^([Tt][Rr][Uu][Ee]\|1)$` (3), `exit 1` deleted (8), gate step deleted (16 + 2 errors).

**Cases 1–11 were all green before this branch.**

## Control cases — the tests can also stay green when they should

An all-red table proves nothing if the tests fail on any edit at all.

- Rewording the refusal message — **green**.
- `timeout-minutes:` on an unrelated step — **green**.
- Moving `Checkout` above the gate — **red**, deliberately, and green again once `Checkout` is added to `STEPS_ALLOWED_BEFORE_THE_GATE`. The workflow's own comment calls that move survivable and it stays available; it is now a two-line change rather than a silent one.

## Review round

One adversarial pass (spawned reviewer, worked from the issue rather than the diff). It raised six findings; five are implemented above (its findings 1, 2,

author: abdulrehmann231
body:
# Fix two bugs that let paid turns go unbilled

## The background, in one paragraph

When you send a message, the agent runs inside a sandbox. A tool called
**tokscale** counts the tokens it used. tokscale only ever tells us a **running
total** for the whole chat session — never "this one message cost X". So to
bill a single turn we do:

```
this turn = tokscale's running total  −  what we already saved
```

Then we save that number and take the credits. Both bugs below are about that
saving step going wrong.

---

## Bug 1 — a crashed turn was never billed

**What happened:** if the agent crashed, hit a rate limit, or ran past the 25
minute cap, we marked the chat as failed and **immediately threw away the
session ID** — the thing we need to look the usage up with. For scheduled jobs
we also **deleted the sandbox**, which is where tokscale lives.

So we destroyed the receipt before reading it. The model had already done the
work and we had already paid for it upstream, but the user was charged nothing.
And because both the session ID and the sandbox were gone, we could never go
back and recover it later.

Oddly, this only happened when your browser was **closed**. If you were sitting
watching the chat, a different piece of code handled the failure, and that one
*did* bill correctly. So the bug was invisible unless you looked at background
chats.



**The fix:** count the tokens *first*, then tear the session down. There's a new
helper, `meterDyingTurn`, and it's called inside the two teardown functions
themselves rather than at each call site — so all six places that end a failed
turn get it automatically and nobody can forget it.

---

## Bug 2 — a new chat's first real reply was free

**What happened:** we started counting tokens on 15 June. Chats that existed
*before* that date have history nobody ever paid for. If someone reopens one, we
don't want to suddenly bill them for months of old messages — so we have a rule:
"if this is an old chat, record its history but don't charge for it."

The problem was **how we decided a chat was old**. The test was:

> no usage saved yet **and** the chat has more than one reply in it

That sounds sensible, but a **brand new** chat looks exactly like that whenever
its first reply fails. The failed reply saves no usage (bug 1 above!), and it
still leaves a reply row sitting in the chat. So by the time you send your
second message, both conditions are true — and we marked that turn as "old
history" and gave it away for free.

Anything that leaves a reply without usage triggered it: a crash, an error
notice, or even a "pushed to git" message.



**The fix:** just check the chat's **age**. If the chat was created after 15
June, it has been counted since its very first message, so it cannot have
unpaid history — full stop, regardless of what its replies look like. The old
reply-counting check is still there as a backup for genuinely old chats, but now
it only counts real replies and ignores errors, git messages, and empty crashed
ones.

---

## How I know it works

New tests in `meter-dying-turn.test.ts` assert the **order**, not just the
result. That matters: a test that only checked "the tokens were counted" would
still pass against the broken code whenever the teardown happened to lose the
race.

```
expect(calls).toEqual(["meter", "clear-session", "error-message"])
```

Move the counting back below the teardown — i.e. put the bug back — and that
one test fails and nothing else does. I checked.

They also cover the two ways this has to fail safely: a chat must still get
unstuck even if counting throws, and counting must quietly do nothing when
there's no sandbox to ask. Leaving a chat stuck on "running" would be worse
than missing a bill.

Bug 2's age check is unit-tested directly — including that a genuinely old chat
still answers "yes, this one predates metering", which is what keeps it free.
The end-to-end "and therefore it is not charged" step is not covered by a unit
test; I verified that against a real database (below) rather than in CI.

While writing these I also ran a one-off script against a real local database,
driving the actual code paths end to end. Before the fixes: 3 pass, 6 fail.
After: 9 pass, 0 fail. It also caught a mistake in my own first attempt — I
wrote a database filter meaning "not a git message", but in SQL, comparing
something to an empty value gives *"don't know"* rather than *"yes"*, and
normal messages have an empty type, so the filter quietly threw away almost
every message. That script isn't in this PR; it was a one-off, and the unit
tests above are what actually guard the fix from now on.

Full suite: 321 passing (8 new). No database changes.

author: ceesaxp
body:
## What

`TestAFailedOpenIsReported` never tested anything: its command closure really built and started the platform opener, and on macOS `open <any well-formed https URL>` succeeds regardless of whether the host resolves — handing the URL to the default browser *is* success. So the status was always `"opened"`, the assertion `opened || error` could never fail, and every test run popped a browser tab. The bogus-host URL was a red herring: `Start()` fails when the opener binary is missing (the case the test's own comment says it wants), never because of the URL.

## Fix

- A `startOpener` seam next to `defaultOpenCmd`: the same `Start()` + `go Wait()` two lines, behind an indirection. `Wait` lives *inside* the seam, so a test fake never touches a real process and cannot leak a reaper goroutine. Production behavior is byte-identical.
- `openArmedLink`, `playVoice`, `playVideo`, and `downloadAndOpen` all route through it — they shared the identical start/wait shape.
- The test is rewritten as two subtests overriding the seam: a failed start reports `"error"` naming the URI and the reason; a recorded successful start reports `"opened"` and the armed `safeURI` is actually among the built command's args.

Mutation-checked: inverting the success/error branches in `openArmedLink` makes both subtests fail with clear diffs.

## Audit

Grepped the repo for other tests that really exec: this was the only one launching a platform opener. (`clipboard_darwin_test.go` execs `osascript` by design; `telegram-mcp` uses the standard recurse-into-self pattern — both legitimate, untouched.)

Note: the `feat/tme-links` PR builds on this seam for its own opener-path tests — this PR merges first.
