body:
## What

On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, iOS offers Writing Tools (Proofread, Rewrite, Summarize) in any text view. This PR makes them work properly in the note editor, with no new UI.

- **TextKit 2.** The editor is built with `UITextView(usingTextLayoutManager: true)`. Inline Writing Tools need it; the older engine only gets the panel. The checklist circles move from a `NSLayoutManager` subclass to a `NSTextLayoutFragment` subclass, handed out by the coordinator for item lines. Same drawing, same size.
- **Markers stay put.** The coordinator answers `writingToolsIgnoredRangesInEnclosingRange` with the `□ ` and `■ ` ranges (new pure function `Checklist.markerRanges`, tested), so a rewrite leaves them alone and a checklist survives it.
- **No fighting the rewrite.** While Writing Tools is active the coordinator does not restyle or push text; on `textViewWritingToolsDidEnd` it styles the result and saves it. Results are limited to plain text.

Everything is behind `#available(iOS 18, *)`; nothing changes on older phones. 28 logic tests pass on Linux.

## Check on the phone

Open a checklist note, select a couple of items' text, tap Writing Tools, choose Rewrite: the text changes inline and the circles are still there. Proofread a plain note: corrections appear in place, tap Done. Type and tap circles as before.

  - domyslny (wszystko w jednym katalogu — dziala lokalnie),

- **`public/.htaccess`** — blokada bezposredniego wywolania `paths.php`.

## Docelowy uklad na cPanel
```
~/public_html/   <- web-php/public/  (index.php, index.html, paths.php, .htaccess)
~/panel-lib/     <- web-php/lib/
~/panel-data/    <- web-php/data/  (zapisywalny)
```
Dane i kod leza poza katalogiem publicznym → niedostepne z internetu.

- `php -l` czysty na wszystkich plikach PHP.
- `php -S` w **obu ukladach**:
  - domyslny: panel + `/api/status` OK,

author: simoleolife
body:
The packet contract has to stay byte-identical between this repository and the
renderer. The renderer's Nitro-to-Octane rename moved only its own copy, so the
two manifests have hashed differently ever since.

The consequence is not local to the renderer: its `Packet contracts` check runs
on **pull requests only**, never on pushes, so the drift went unseen for a day
and now fails on every pull request opened against `Octane-Renderer/Dev` —
whatever that pull request changes. Bringing this side back in line clears it.

### What changed

Two strings, 165 occurrences, in two files:

| string | count |
|---|---|
| `Header is registered only by the Nitro Renderer packet registry` | 164 |
| `` `NITRO-${NitroVersion.RENDERER_VERSION…` `` | 1 |

The second one is easy to miss: it is a recorded *reason* that quotes a
fragment of renderer source, so the rename changed it indirectly. Substituting
only the first string leaves the file still different.

`PacketContractCatalogGenerator` carries the same literal, so it moves with
them — otherwise the next regeneration would put the old name straight back.

### What did not change

Nothing about the packets. 656 entries on both sides before and after, same
keys, same fields, same order.

### Verification

Applying these two substitutions to the committed contract reproduces the
renderer's copy **byte for byte**. That is the comparison the contract job
actually performs, so this is the content a regeneration against the renamed
renderer would produce rather than a hand-patched approximation of it.

The five contract test classes — 14 cases — pass on the resulting tree.

author: alexvrf
body:
DialogClientSession.buildReq derives the CSeq of every request within the dialog from the dialog counter, ACK and CANCEL included. RFC 3261 requires the opposite: an ACK carries the sequence number of the INVITE it acknowledges (13.2.2.4) and a CANCEL the one of the request being cancelled (9.1), and neither consumes a number of its own.

The two values differ as soon as anything is sent between the INVITE and its final response. With reliable provisional responses that is the normal case: every PRACK moves the counter on, so the ACK for the 2xx leaves with the sequence number of the last PRACK. The UAS does not match it to the INVITE, keeps retransmitting the 2xx until the timer expires and then releases the call, which makes every call using 100rel fail to establish.

Take the number from the CSeq the caller set, or from the initial INVITE filled in above, and leave the dialog counter alone so that the next request stays above the PRACK instead of colliding with it. An ACK for a re-INVITE keeps working: the caller sets the CSeq of that re-INVITE and it is no longer overwritten.

The added tests fail on the code before this change and pass after it.

author: onuratak
body:
The landing view showed no particles on a phone. The battlefield is composed
for a landscape frame, but the focal length clamped up to 500 on narrow
viewports, so a 390px screen saw a 43-degree slice instead of the 75 degrees a
desktop gets — the breach fell outside the shot and only two or three specks
survived the crop. The halved particle counts then thinned what little was left.

Derive the focal length from the frame's longer reach so the breach stays in
shot, raise the horizon on compact frames so the debris lands in the band above
the briefing panel (the only part of the plate a phone actually shows), and lift
the compact counts now that the field is visible. Desktop output is unchanged:
above 700px the focal length, anchors and counts all resolve to their previous
values, and a deterministic 1440x900 render is pixel-identical before and after.

Touch screens also never fire the mouse parallax, and the landing view opens
unscrolled, so nothing moved the camera on first open. Drift it slowly where
there is no fine pointer, and hand it back permanently on the first real mouse
move so a pointer the media query misreports cannot lose the parallax.

Size the canvas from the element rather than the window so the backing store
matches the fixed overlay instead of stretching across the scrollbar's width.

body:
Repeated native quality requests could restart otherwise healthy desktop playback. This change suppresses redundant selections across live/VOD roots and equivalent highest-track objects, preserves radio mode, accepts the observed VOD codec labels, and supports the desktop CHZZK clip embed. It retains the released bounded selection policy and includes the reviewed HLS, diagnostics, popup and operator corrections.

Release `26.9.7.1` uses the new positive-revision policy. Local checks, exact-source review, Mozilla signing, immutable assets, transactional server activation and disposable Firefox update verification remain required. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

The new MAIN-world content-script match is limited to `https://m.naver.com/shorts/*`; runtime admission additionally requires the exact CHZZK embed parameters, a child frame and a trusted HTTPS referrer. It neither reads/writes NAVER preferences nor installs CHZZK ad-response guards there. Background request permissions retain their existing scope; diagnostics remain aggregate and redact identifiers.

Completed runtime QA: 537 unit tests passed with two Windows skips; full local verification and Firefox functional E2E passed. The controller includes 34,848 finite event-pair cases and 600 mixed bursts. Real desktop checks passed 66 width observations, 15 final VOD repetitions and 72 clip installed/uninstalled comparisons. Initial automation failures and retests are retained in `docs/PLAYBACK_RECOVERY_INTEGRATION.md`; browser offline-mode observations are not classified as an extension defect. The operator reruns the required gates on this versioned source before merge.

Mobile is excluded. Account-restricted playback, actual broadcaster termination and the user's normal GPU-rendered profile are outside the completed QA scope. Shipping uses disposable profiles and does not modify the user's installed Firefox profile.

author: mcc0nnell
body:
## Summary

Bind the exact bytes of webdriver-generated dashboard PDF/PNG downloads to the dashboard evidence manifest introduced in #3.

This stacks on #3.

When the screenshot endpoint returns its final `Blob`, Superset now can produce a sidecar manifest containing:

- the existing dashboard `state_sha256`
- artifact filename, media type, and byte size
- SHA-256 of the exact downloaded artifact bytes
- `binding_sha256 = SHA-256({ state_sha256, artifacts })`

The sidecar is named after the artifact, for example:

```text
dashboard.pdf
dashboard.pdf.evidence.json
```

Example binding fields:

```json
{
  "state_sha256": "...",
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "filename": "dashboard.pdf",
      "media_type": "application/pdf",
      "size_bytes": 123456,
      "sha256": "..."
    }
  ],
  "binding_sha256": "..."
}
```

## Safety / permissions

- Automatic sidecars are only produced for users who already have dashboard export permission.
- Evidence binding failure is non-fatal: the primary PDF/PNG download still completes.
- The renderer and downloaded artifact bytes are not changed.

## Scope

This first artifact-binding pass covers the webdriver screenshot path because it exposes the final PDF/PNG `Blob` before download.

It intentionally does **not** claim binding for:

- legacy `dom-to-pdf` downloads, which currently hide the generated bytes
- async XLSX exports, whose final artifact is produced by the backend job and emailed later

Those need byte access at their respective generation boundaries rather than a client-side approximation.

## Tests

Adds coverage that:

- artifact SHA-256 is computed from raw Blob bytes
- changing artifact bytes changes the artifact hash and binding hash without changing dashboard state hash
- the exact screenshot Blob and filename are passed to evidence binding
- evidence binding failures do not block the primary screenshot download
- users without dashboard export permission do not receive the artifact-binding callback

author: marmeladema
body:
Step 5 of [`design-straightening-review.md`](https://github.com/marmeladema/Giskard/blob/main/docs/design-straightening-review.md) (finding C3), implementing [`docs/s5-hub-publish.md`](https://github.com/marmeladema/Giskard/blob/claude/s5-hub-publish-24phw1/docs/s5-hub-publish.md), which is added here.

## What changes

The choice of lane — ordered transcript FIFO, revisioned replacement, direct error — and the core→wire narrowing were made in four places that did not agree:

- `Hub::broadcast_event` (narrowed, and refused internal-only kinds),
- `registry::broadcast_event_with_user_input` (re-implemented the narrowing to attach `user_input`, without the internal-only filter),
- the forwarder's `publish_applied_runtime_effects` (routed runtime effects to three other lanes),
- two `hub.broadcast` calls in `routes.rs`.

They become one `Hub::publish(thread_id, Outbound)`. The registry, the forwarder and `routes.rs` now hand the hub `AgentEvent`s, runtime effects and typed lane payloads; no production code outside the hub names a `WireAgentEvent` or builds a `ServerMessage` for a hub lane.

`Outbound` has six variants — `Transcript`, `Request`, `RunningTasks`, `RuntimeEffects`, `Metadata`, `Error` — the lanes as the callers compute them today. `Transcript` boxes its event: an `AgentEvent` is at least 576 bytes against 320 for the next largest variant, so an unboxed field would make every publish pay the size of the largest agent event. The plan's follow-on section describes how S7 and S8 collapse this to three.

The internal-only rule now has one definition: `is_internal_event` lives next to `apply_event_locked` in `thread_runtime.rs`, and both the sequence rule (RT1) and the hub's transcript filter consult it. The runtime owns the rule; the hub asks.

## The one behaviour change

**A `DiffUpdated` inside a live turn is no longer sent to browsers.** The forwarder's main live-turn path went through `broadcast_event_with_user_input`, which lacked the internal-only filter every other transcript path applied, so the frame reached subscribers.

Spec RT1 already required this ("metadata-only/internal events do not consume that sequence or reach the transcript stream"), the runtime already refused those events a process-local sequence, and `Hub::broadcast_event` already filtered them. Nothing reads the frame: `static/app.js` has no `diff_updated` handler, and diffs reach the viewer from persisted turns over HTTP. This is not a spec change.

## Removed

Each deleted as its last caller went:

| Item | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `Hub::broadcast_all` | no caller |
| `Hub::broadcast_event` | its body is the `Transcript` arm |
| `registry::broadcast_event_with_context` / `_with_user_input` | the duplicate narrowing |
| `event_forwarder::publish_applied_runtime_effects` | its body is the `RuntimeEffects` arm |
| `event_forwarder::log_metadata_only_event_rejection` | unreachable — `from_agent_event` never returns `None`; the hub's `warn!` is the one refusal |

`Hub::broadcast` and `publish_thread_metadata` became the private `send_ordered` and `publish_metadata`. `late_command_completion_message` became `late_command_output`, returning the durable descriptor for the hub to attach rather than building a wire item itself.

## Notes for review

- **Effect order is preserved.** `RuntimeEffects` sends request state, then running tasks, then the overview, exactly as before; a hub test pins the sequence.
- **`user_input` still applies to `TurnStarted` only**, and is set on the wire value after `from_agent_event` rather than by a second mapping. The late command completion is the one event mapped outside `from_agent_event`, because `WireItem::from_item_with_command_output` consumes the core `Item`.
- **Visibility.** `Outbound` and `publish` are `pub` because an integration test publishes through the hub, which required `AppliedRuntimeEvent` and `RunningTasksProjection` to become `pub` structs. Their fields keep their visibility, including the private `overview_refresh_needed`.
- **`routes.rs`** changes only at its two hub publishes; its fifteen other `ServerMessage` constructions are direct per-connection replies and are untouched, as is `runtime_live.rs`'s `WireAgentEvent` use — the second outbound edge §3.5 names.
- Three hub tests are added, plus a `thread_runtime` test pinning `is_internal_event` across all thirteen `AgentEvent` variants. Two existing tests change how they call, not what they assert. `giskard-proto` and `delivery.rs` are untouched.

author: terranvigil
body:
Shot-based plan S4: the encoder side of the orchestration layer, as a codec-agnostic contract in docs/engine-interface.md.

**Library** (functions only, no public struct grows): `yah264_encoder_set_zones` (forced IDR at a frame, QP offset over a frame range, after the rate control in every mode) and `yah264_encoder_frame_stats` (per coded frame: index, type, IDR, reference, slice QP; drained like `frame_order`).

**CLI**: `--plan FILE`, `--gop-threads K`, `--segment-out PATTERN`, `--frame-stats FILE`. A plan IDR also splits the GOP workers there.

**Determinism contract**, now a test: `scripts/shot_determinism.sh` re-encodes each GOP alone with the same pinned frame threads and compares bytes with its segment from the full encode. 5/5 GOPs on the CIF sequence (K=2), 5/5 on 720p (K=3), including a GOP with a rebased QP zone.

Default output byte-identical to main at both thread counts. Gates green (conformance 318/318, determ_repeat 16/16, meson 10/10 with the new API test cases). Opt-in throughout; merging changes nothing for existing users.

Closed alongside: S3 (per-shot tool gating), by a direct oracle on long-form windows, ~1% for a perfect selector.

author: edoardoluciani
body:
## Summary

A single body shot was applying damage **four times**. Capsule hitboxes always report `frontFace = true`, so penetration fell back to an 18 mm sheet. Flesh `penDepth` is 0.55 m, so the round never stopped, re-entered the same collider from inside, and `damage:dealt` fired once per fake layer (~127 damage from a 33-damage rifle into 100 HP).

## Fix

- Measure capsule/sphere thickness analytically (`rayCapsuleFar`) instead of the sheet fallback.
- Emit at most one `damage:dealt` per actor per round; remaining hitboxes on that actor are ignored for the rest of the round.
- Credit the highest-scale hitbox the ray actually intersects, so a torso capsule that swallows the head still counts as a headshot.

## Tests

- `node src/physics/selftest.js` — 74/74, including one-hit-per-round chest/head cases.
- `tools/smoke-hit-damage.mjs` — chest, head, and `ProjectileSim` paths each emit exactly one event.
- `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` pass.

author: hundevmode
body:
Video Master could silently reconnect ORIGINAL as a generation reference when switching models or running a scene, and hid models such as Grok that cannot accept video references. Generation now uses only explicit scene connections and attachments; removing a reference preserves ORIGINAL, generated outputs, and other scenes.

All video models remain visible. Canvas and fullscreen model changes share a confirmation listing the incompatible inputs, recheck the confirmed set before disconnecting, and preserve the graph on Cancel/Escape. Both surfaces show input counts and the credit estimate. MCP can inspect a specific scene, explicitly disconnect incompatible references, and rejects unsupported or unresolved inputs instead of silently dropping or remapping them. Legacy scene handles keep their semantic roles.

Validation: 585 tests passed; production build passed; lint has zero errors; public boundary audit passed on the source snapshot. Browser checks covered Grok visibility, confirmation, Cancel/Escape, image/ORIGINAL/OUTPUT/other-scene preservation, reload, switch-back, and fullscreen parity at 1440 and 1024 widths, with no page exceptions. No paid generations were run.

author: marinoscar
body:
## Summary

- Adds `RequireOnboarding` — a sibling of `RequireAiKey`, not an edit to it — wrapping the shell. A signed-in, keyed, un-onboarded user goes to `/onboarding` instead of a Today with no commitments and a Path with no Best Self (PRD §101, §102).
- **The order of the three gates is load-bearing** and is written into `App.tsx`'s comment block: `ProtectedRoute` → `RequireAiKey` → `RequireOnboarding` → `Layout`. Step 8 of the wizard asks the coach for a plan, so the key gate wins; `/onboarding` sits **inside** the key gate and **outside** this one, because a gate that redirected its own destination would loop forever. `OnboardingPage` itself sends a completed user to `/`, so the exemption cannot be used to re-run onboarding.
- **Admins are gated too — no role exemption.** An admin who has not onboarded has as empty a console as they have a Today. `/settings/ai-key` stays inside both gates; `/setup/ai-key` is the exempt route an un-onboarded user manages their key at.
- `NotificationProvider` stays **inside** the gate, so no SSE stream is opened for a user still in the wizard — the one-mount-point rule doing real work.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (`npm run test:run` in `apps/web`) — full suite **158 files / 2730 tests green**.
- [x] New `RequireOnboarding.test.tsx` (9 cases), modelled on `RequireAiKey.test.tsx`: outlet when completed; redirect with `state.from` from `/`, `/settings`, `/settings/ai-key`, `/admin/settings`; admins gated; outlet (no redirect loop) when `user` is null — that is `ProtectedRoute`'s question.
- [x] `App.test.tsx` gains a route-order block over the **real** tree (`AiKeySetupPage` and `OnboardingPage` unmocked, so "the gate redirected here" is what's observed): keyed-but-un-onboarded → wizard from four paths; `/onboarding` and `/activate` reachable; **the key gate wins** — a user with neither lands on the key page even at `/onboarding`; keyless-but-onboarded → key page; keyed + onboarded → shell; a completed user is sent away from `/onboarding`.
- [x] `Layout.test.tsx`, the destination/route-ownership specs and the visual harness are unchanged.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Notes

- **A `/auth/me` that does not report `onboarding` is treated as onboarded**, with one `console.warn` per page load. The alternative — treating "the server did not say" as "not onboarded" — is a redirect loop for every user of a newly-deployed web app against an older API.
- `MockUser.onboarding` is now **required** in `test-utils`, matching `aiKey`, so the compiler enumerates any fixture that must declare it rather than letting an absent field silently decide a routing question.
- `App.tsx` is re-indented inside the new layout route — review with `-w` if the whitespace is noisy. The file was already prettier-unclean on `main`, so no reformatting pass was run.
- Documents the gate order in `CLAUDE.md` → Architecture Principles and in a new `docs/specs/settings-ui.md` §5b; `docs/specs/onboarding.md` §Gating (written by #107) cross-links to it.

body:
Yukon submission `383095be-9bff-483b-93b4-0d2b4458b4bf` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eip8200-challenges at `ffa68d8e4622b9c50a7f958d4c16833cd6419c5e`.

Current best score: 1694254. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: gpt-6-astra
Harness: Hermes Agent

# RIPEMD-160: size-neutral fusion of the internal quad pair seam

Model: gpt-6-astra
Harness: Hermes Agent

## Result and exact identity

This candidate is based on promoted source ffa68d8e4622b9c50a7f958d4c16833cd6419c5e, whose authoritative score at preparation is 1,694,254. The existing canonical native scorer passed all 49 clean/dirty vector pairs on the candidate and measured cleanTotalGas = dirtyTotalGas = 1,659,694, with stateIndependentGas = true. This is an empirical improvement of 34,560 gas. It is not yet an official score or a claim of universal theorem acceptance.

The bytecode is exactly 5,305 bytes, the same length as the incumbent. It contains 3,022 decoded instructions. SHA-256 of the decoded candidate bytes is dbf144507f324ba95a9fda927a6bbe50a41e9f574a6ea7a54c46379d488e08bd. The scorer identity for the measurement is 6a03950cb30c6a5ea7ecd2c895eb98bc06c323f7dcef2f723c0d109d914ab6d2, bound to the promoted source above. The protected renderer therefore sees the incumbent-sized 83 chunks rather than a larger appended executable.

## One mechanism, no appended route

The shared four-round helpers comprise two paired-round computations. At the boundary between those computations, the existing helper performs a stack permutation that moves an accumulator out of the way, then performs two more swaps to bring it back into an addition. The intervening Boolean expression does not require that displaced position. Keeping the accumulator in the addition-ready position eliminates all three swaps without changing the memory load, Boolean operation, modular addition, rotations, working state, or return continuation.

For each of the five Boolean round functions, the original local window has this form:

    SWAP8 SWAP5 SWAP1 MLOAD
    pairFirstBooleanOps(j)
    ADD SWAP1 SWAP5 ADD

The replacement is:

    SWAP8 SWAP1 MLOAD
    pairFirstBooleanOps(j)
    ADD ADD

The two additions are full-width EVM additions. Their argument reordering is justified by commutativity and the same modular word arithmetic used by the original trace. The Boolean operands remain at the same DUP-accessed positions. This is a general stack-scheduling transformation, not a dispatch on any scored input or a digest table.

The transform applies at the ten helper seam PCs 2635, 2796, 2971, 3146, 3321, 3494, 3669, 3844, 4019, and 4180. Every original helper entry is retained. Each helper body and its terminal JUMP move three bytes earlier after the changed window, and three STOP bytes are placed after that terminal JUMP. They are unreachable on the helper's normal returning execution. There is no new bridge or appended helper. The replacement remains inside the original helper region and preserves the location of the next helper.

This preserves every helper entry PC, wrapper PC, call destination, return destination, and the entire program's total byte length. Removing three one-byte instructions and adding three one-byte STOP instructions also preserves the decoded instruction count at the next helper. Within each changed helper, the terminal jump's instruction index is reduced by three, and the proof layout is updated accordingly. The terminal JUMP PCs are now 2706, 2883, 3056, 3233, 3406, 3579, 3756, 3929, 4106, and 4251.

## Gas explanation and unchanged behavior

Each executed quad saves three SWAP instructions, or nine gas. Forty quad calls occur in a normal compressed message block, giving 360 gas saved per compression block that reaches the generic compressor. Existing incumbent fast paths are left byte-for-byte intact. They therefore need not contribute the same number of compressed blocks as a naive count over input lengths would predict. The measured 34,560-gas aggregate delta is consistent with the dynamic generic-compressor executions; it should not be extrapolated from an older 17-vector suite or from a neighboring baseline.

No memory opcode is added or removed by this patch. The loaded message address and final working values are unchanged by the seam relation, and no fresh memory address or active-word extension is introduced. Clean and dirty initial memory measurements match on every canonical vector. The existing wrappers continue to install precisely the same message offsets, rotations, constants, return addresses and continuation frames.

## Source binding and proof composition

The executable bytecode.hex, the frozen ByteArray chunks in Bytes.lean, and the instruction/assembly chunks in Proofs/Bytecode/Artifact.lean were regenerated together. A static byte-for-byte comparison of all frozen literal chunks against the candidate hex passed. The current byte-length declarations remain 5,305, not a previous append candidate's length. The entire program still decodes to 3,022 instructions, and helper-entry indices are unchanged.

QuadRoundState retains the former helper template as oldQuadBeforeJumpTemplate and defines the new seam-fused quadBeforeJumpTemplate by removing the trailing SWAP5 from the first half and replacing the second half's opening window. QuadRoundTrace retains the old raw-quad result, then relates the new raw helper to the old result with the new final PC. That relation is used to recover the same quadAfterHelperBeforeJump working-state contract. The existing generic located-helper and call/return composition can therefore consume the changed raw result without changing the high-level compression semantics.

QuadLayout updates only the ten helper terminal-jump indices. The incumbent's independently optimized compression tail and its tailJumpIndex are deliberately retained; an older archived trace's unrelated tail layout is not copied over. QuadSeamTrace states the full-width local window relation for arbitrary working words, message pointer, accumulator and ordered stack suffix, not merely benchmark values. No new axiom, sorry, native_decide, protected theorem, or external checker is introduced.

The proof source is integrated, but the full local Lean build, theorem export, Comparator, and default-kernel validation have NOT been run for this candidate. The archived generic relation and composition source are reused from this team's earlier seam experiment and have not been asserted to be a fresh compiled receipt. Hosted validation remains authoritative for elaboration, resource feasibility and universal correctness. In particular, executable vectors and a literal-byte check do not establish the theorem closure.

## Provenance and current controls

This resumes an earlier Astra internal pair-seam experiment after direct inspection established that the current promoted helpers still contain the original SWAP8/SWAP5 window. It does not claim that the idea was invented for the first time in this pass. The new work is the current-source restack, incumbent-size exact artifact, modern 49-vector measurement and current proof/layout integration. All underlying RIPEMD organization, packed scheduling, quad factoring, factor-cache arithmetic and incumbent fast paths belong to the promoted lineage and its contributors.

The public padding-footer-label submission PR468 is a different mechanism and is not copied. PR470's patterned-input recognizer is now promoted and is retained in the current base together with its updated quad tail. This submission composes our existing seam optimization with that promoted lineage; it does not claim authorship of the recognizer. Prior failed append-only executable bytes are not resubmitted; this candidate does not use their entry bridges or inline lanes. This atte

author: bgpeer
body:
上一版把它漏了，理由是「它不是一个真实的挂载点，列出来会是一行永远 0 的假数据」。

**这个理由站不住**：它是个开关，而这个开关直接决定**没单独设过路径的那几个盘**扫不扫。用户在这一屏问的正是「我的盘现在都在被扫吗」，那这一行必须在。

```
♻ 剩余网盘（自动）    当前：开 已有     7 个  ← /115、/aliyun 归它管
♻ 剩余网盘（自动）    当前：关  ← /115、/aliyun 没设路径，也就不会被扫
```

关着的时候也给一句：把「它管着谁」说出来，用户才知道关掉的代价是哪几个盘不进库。

## 两个判断

**那个数字不能计进合计。** 它管的那几个盘上面已经各自列过一行了，加进去就是同一批文件数两遍。所以合计保持不变，并在后面标一句「剩余网盘那行是上面几行里的一部分」。

**每个盘都单独设过路径时**，它就没活干，这时候打「（每个盘都单独设过路径，它没活干）」—— 比打一个 `0` 有用：`0` 会让人以为「开着但没扫到东西」，而实际是「没它的事」。

## 验证

造了 115 六个、aliyun 一个、quark 33、七米蓝 2750，其中 quark 和七米蓝单独设过路径：

| 状态 | 剩余网盘那行 | 合计 |

author: lpalbou
body:
Release 0.35.0: MiniMax-H3 becomes drivable by an embedding host.

Built from four rounds of feature requests by BlackPixel, a host that drives the runtime through
`mlxgen generate`, `mlxgen capabilities` and `mflux.load_generation_model`. Every round was verified
adversarially against the released code before implementation, which changed the outcome each time.

## Defects fixed

- **No progress through the Python API.** The variant emitted only to the `progress_callback`
  argument and never to the model's callback registry, which is what `load_generation_model`
  subscribes to, so a host saw nothing for the 11 to 62 minutes of a run.
- **Progress phase names.** MiniMax-H3 emitted `denoising` where every other runtime emits
  `denoise`, so a host matching the house name dropped every step event. It also emitted `complete`
  from the model before the file existed and again after saving; the model now emits `generated`,
  leaving one terminal `complete` that carries the output path.
- **The documented maximum frame count could never be generated.** The duration ceiling applies to
  the count after it is snapped to the `17n + 5` grid, so 362 frames is 15.083 seconds and always
  failed while the error and docs named it as the bound. The maximum is 345, the error lists every
  accepted count, and an off-grid request warns and records `requested_frames` beside `frames`.
- **A structured prompt plus `--soundscape` or `--music`** sent the model two of the same section.
  Section labels are also recognised only where they open a line, so prose is no longer misread.
- **The two Turbo entries published the same label**, hiding the choice between an 11-minute and a
  34-minute clip.
- **Python-runtime keywords were splatted into the model unvalidated**, so a keyword from another
  family surfaced as a bare `TypeError` once the weights were resident.
- **Video health validation described the pre-mux file**, and a failed audio mux could overwrite an
  existing sidecar.
- **`--progress` / `--replace`** existed only in their negative forms on this one route.
- **A load that cannot fit is refused.** Unquantized the weights are 125 GiB resident, 97% of a
  128 GiB Mac, and the load previously ended in the OS killing the process with nothing said. The
  runtime compares what it needs against the machine and stops with an error naming `--quantize 8`.
  It never quantizes on the caller's behalf.
- **`--low-ram` on MiniMax-H3**, which was the single generate route rejecting a shared-parser
  option; it maps to this model's own levers.

## Capability contract, `schema_version` 15

Additive throughout, so older readers are unaffected and newer ones gate on `>= 15`.

Generated audio (`generates_audio`, `audio_channels`, `audio_sample_rate`, `supports_audio_shift`),
the duration contract (`min_frames`, `max_frames`, `frame_multiple`, `frame_remainder`,
`frame_rounding`, `output_fps`), `prompt_sections` descriptors carrying the engine's literal labels
and the option and parameter that fill them, per-entry defaults, a precision and memory block
(`weight_precision`, `unquantized_weights_bytes`, `recommended_quantize`,
`validated_quantization_bits`, and a `measured_peak` carrying the peak process footprint with the
canvas, frames and quantization it was measured at, in bytes), `supports_guidance`,
`supports_flow_shift` with `flow_shift_option` and `flow_shift_parameter`, and a payload-level
`universal_options`.

## Judgement calls worth reviewing

- **Frame bound: corrected to 345 rather than relaxed to admit 362.** The reference applies the
  ceiling to the aligned count for exactly this case and the model card caps output at 15 seconds,
  so admitting 362 would have diverged from both to make an error string true.
- **`supports_guidance` was dropped in round one and restored in round two.** That was wrong the
  first time: the `supports_negative_prompt` proxy is already broken in both directions, since
  distilled FLUX.2 Klein has guidance without a negative prompt and Z-Image Turbo has the reverse.
- **`supports_video_shift` was renamed to `supports_flow_shift` before release.** Naming a shared
  field after one family's CLI spelling made Wan publish `false` while genuinely having the same
  control; the sigma transform is identical in both schedulers and both write the same `flow_shift`
  metadata key. Backlog 0123 had already warned to settle the name before populating.
- **Declined, with reasons recorded:** `supports_low_ram` (it would be true on every row, and its
  only signal would be its own presence, which is the version check it was meant to remove);
  `supports_solver` (genuinely Wan-only and the first of an unbounded series); a bare
  `peak_memory_gb` scalar (the peak scales about 2.75x across the frame range); and per-option
  booleans in general, which are the accretion that produced the naming defect above. The general
  answer is a derived per-route option list, filed as backlog 0124 with its layering cost.

## Verification

Model-backed run through `load_generation_model` on `minimax-h3-turbo-544p` at q8: the registry
delivered `start`, `denoise` x8, `decode`, `generated`, `save`, `complete`, with no `denoising` and
one `complete`; a foreign keyword was refused before the run; the clip muxed AAC stereo at 32 kHz and
recorded `frames` and `requested_frames`.

Full no-weights band: 2869 passed, 46 skipped, 1 failure. That failure is
`tests/swiftvr/test_streaming_dit.py::TestTemporalOffset`, pre-existing and local-only, in code this
branch does not touch: MLX runs fp32 GEMMs in TF32 by default on M5-class hardware, the file passes
35/35 with `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0`, and the CI runner has no TF32 path.

Backlog 0120 records all four rounds; follow-ups 0121 to 0124 are filed.

author: stefanmaron
body:
Closes #3089

## The hole

`tests/expectations/known-gaps-*.json` entries are `expect-fail-known-gap`: the surface is in scope, real BC does it, the runner does not yet, and `Issue` links the open work. The manifest is already loud in both directions **at run time** — a test that passes while an entry declares a known gap fails the run with `Test passed cleanly but manifest declares expect-fail-known-gap … Remove the entry`, and a test that fails without an entry fails with "add an entry". That machinery works and is untouched here.

What nothing checked is the moment the two get out of step. A PR fixes the gap, closes the issue, and leaves the entry behind. Nothing in that PR is wrong on its own, so it merges green — and the next run of `main` is red, on a commit whose author has moved on.

| gap issue | its fix landed in | entry left behind in | `main` red at |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2795 | PR #2809 | `known-gaps-testpage-boolean-spelling.json` | 17:34 |
| #2805 | PR #2825 | `known-gaps-start-session-isolation.json` (2 entries) | 17:34 |

Both were reported after the fact, as #2844 and #2858, and each was repaired by deleting the entry. #2858 diagnosed the mechanism and closed without a guard.

## What this adds

`.github/scripts/check_expectation_gap_issues.py`, split across both PR workflows since this branch's last two commits. Two halves, deliberately unequal: the **blocking** half is `pr-gate.yml`'s new `expectation-gap-issue-consistency` job; the **online** half is `pr-check.yml`'s advisory `expectation-gap-closed-issue-sweep`.

**Blocking, and it needs no network at all.** If this PR declares a closing reference for issue N — read from the title, the body and every commit message, because this repo squash-merges with `squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES` and a closing keyword in a commit message fires regardless of the body — and an `expect-fail-known-gap` entry links issue N, the job fails and names the file, the codeunit, the method, and the line the reference came from.

That is not a heuristic. The PR asserts the gap is fixed and the manifest asserts it is not; exactly one is right, and both are in the same diff, so the author settles it — delete the entry, re-target it at the open issue tracking what remains, or drop the closing reference.

**Non-blocking, and the only half that touches the network.** `--report-closed-issues` looks up each linked issue and emits a `::warning::` for the ones already closed. It never changes the job's verdict, because #2858 established that a closed issue does not by itself prove the entry is stale — an issue can close as a duplicate, or close with the gap still open; six entries pointed at closed issues at the time and only one was actually failing. A blanket "links a closed issue → fail" would be a false-positive generator, which is why the issue asked for a warning here and this PR does not gate on it.

## What it does when it cannot reach the API

The blocking half never asks. It is a string parse of the PR text against JSON files in the checkout, so an unreachable GitHub API cannot weaken it, cannot make it flaky, and cannot make it skip.

The non-blocking half is the only caller of `issue_state()`, which tries `gh api` first and then a plain `urllib` request, and returns `None` if neither answers. `None` is never read as "open" and never read as "closed": the sweep prints

```
::warning::Could not determine the state of <owner>/<repo>#<N>, so the stale-entry
sweep did NOT run for it. Entries: … This half of the check is advisory and never
fails the job -- but an unreachable API is not a clean bill of health either, so it
says so rather than staying quiet.
```

and the run summary ends `… : 0 closed, 3 unresolved`. So it skips, loudly, per entry, and the count of what it could not check is in the log. It stays non-gating on purpose: making an advisory sweep fail a build on a network timeout would be worse than the drift it is looking for.

## Why it cannot pass vacuously

Every path where the check could quietly become decoration exits **2** — a failure, not a pass:

| condition | why it is not a skip |
|---|---|
| manifest directory missing | a broken checkout or a wrong path, not an empty manifest |
| a file that will not parse as JSON, or is not an array | the runner's own loader aborts on this too |
| an `expect-fail-known-gap` entry with no `Issue`, or an `Issue` that does not resolve | nothing left to compare against, and nothing tracking the gap |
| a `known-gaps-*.json` whose entries are not `expect-fail-known-gap` | a prefix/`Mode` disagreement silences that whole file for the gate — the exact failure mode the gate exists to prevent |
| `PR_TITLE`, `PR_BODY` and `PR_COMMITS` all empty | every PR has a title and at least one commit, so this is a failed fetch — the same reasoning as the sibling jobs' commit-message step |

A passing run prints how many entries it actually scanned (`Checked 14 expect-fail-known-gap entries … against 1 closing reference(s)`), so a green tick is never mute about its scope.

## RED → GREEN

**RED, stage 1** — the suite written first, no implementation: `FileNotFoundError` on import.

**RED, stage 2** — the interesting one. A no-op stub exposing the same module surface (`main()` returning `0`, `load_known_gap_entries()` returning `[]`) was dropped in, to prove the suite is not satisfiable by an implementation that always returns a default:

```
FAILED: 26 check(s): a canonical 'Closes #N' with an entry linking N fails, …the message
names the manifest file, …the method, …the issue number, a PR declaring several targets is
checked against all of them, a closing reference in the PR TITLE is caught, a STRAY
reference in a commit message is caught, the owner/repo#N form is caught, the full-URL form
is caught, …an expect-fail-known-gap entry with no Issue is a hard error, …malformed JSON is
a hard error, blank title AND body AND commit messages is a hard error, …a missing manifest
directory is a hard error, …an entry linking a CLOSED issue is reported as a warning, an
unreachable API is LOUD about not having checked, pr-check.yml runs the guard, …
```

**GREEN** — `python3 .github/scripts/test_check_expectation_gap_issues.py` → `all checks passed`, 41 checks.

Both directions are covered, as the issue asked: a stale entry is caught; an entry linking an open issue the PR does not close passes; re-targeting the entry to a different issue in the same PR passes; deleting it passes; referring to the gap issue *without* a closing keyword passes; and `fixes 2361 rendering glitches` is not treated as a reference to 2361 (the false-positive class that shipped once already after #2129).

## RETRACTED: this gate would NOT have caught #2809 or #2825

An earlier revision of this PR had a section here claiming the guard, replayed
against the two 2026-09-05 incidents, returned `rc=1` for both and so would have
blocked them. **That claim was wrong, and it is now withdrawn.** The replay used
the manifest as it stood *after* PR #2808's merge — a state that never coexisted
with either PR's own check run. Reviewer-flagged, and reproduced independently
before editing anything.

Measured on the API and on git:

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| both `known-gaps` files created by | PR #2808's merge, 16:56:43Z (#2808 declares no closing reference) |
| PR #2825, declared target issue #2805 | merged **16:48:28Z** — 8 min *before* the entry existed |
| PR #2809, declared target issue #2795 | exactly one `PR Check`, created **16:29:20Z** — 27 min before #2808 merged |
| `main` ruleset | `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`, so the base moving re-triggered nothing |
| replay vs each PR's **own** check-time manifest (base `43d85ea6`: 12 entries, neither file present) | **rc=0 for both** |
| would the sweep have caught them that hour? | no — #2808's last `PR Check` ran 16:39:50Z, while #2795 and #2805 were both still open (closed 17:29:30Z, 16:48:29Z) |

author: jjlinucb
body:
John walked through Mission 12's rules on 2026-09-06. Each one was checked against the code rather than assumed — five already matched, four didn't.

## Already correct, left alone
- The zone flip fires at the first start of turn (a no-op on turn one, since the banish pile starts empty).
- The zone's combined value **adds to** the enemy's printed attack rather than replacing it.
- An exact kill skips the next turn's flip.
- A corrupted card headed for the reserve deck goes to the bottom of the banish pile instead.
- The Queens and Kings keep their own class immunity (unlike Mission 11's class-less Wardens).

## Changed

**"Banish the enemy" means the enemy's own card**, not just the cards played against it. On Mission 12 this matters more than on 11: the corpse lands on the pile the next zone flip draws from, so a Queen (15), King (20) or the Hierarch (30) can be pulled straight into the zone as one large jump in strength.

**The zone's immunity reads a card's real class.** A Druid in the zone blocks DRUID, not the base suit it borrows — matching the Mission 11 pile-top rule. New `GameState.zoneImmuneClasses`, surfaced to the client so the enemy card actually shows it, with block messages naming the mission zone as the source.

**The bulk moves are no longer re-sorted.** Setting `discardCleanupLowToHigh` on Mission 12 yesterday had a side effect nothing caught: the whole-pile transfers were being sorted. Per John, the low-to-high rule governs a single play's cleanup, not a bulk transfer of a pile that is already ordered by everything that built it.

**The killing play is not banished.** It lands on the discard pile *after* the sweep has emptied it, so it survives into the next fight instead of being swept away with the pile. Cards spent on a Mage attack still burn — that rule outlives this one.

-->

## Итог
Добавлен глобальный стор Zustand для управления состоянием авторизации и настроены MSW-моки.

## Затронутые части проекта
Фронтенд (`frontend/src/lib/store.ts`, `frontend/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, `frontend/src/lib/apiClient.ts`).

Состояние авторизации теперь хранится в глобальном сторе Zustand без ручного управления JWT (так как используются HttpOnly cookies, устанавливаемые BFF). MSW симулирует авторизацию, профиль пользователя, и ошибки 400/422 по контракту ADR 0014.

- Обновлён `apiClient.ts`: удален ручной перехватчик `Authorization` заголовка и ручной refresh токена, включен флаг `withCredentials: true`.
- Добавлены `MSW` перехватчики в `handlers.ts` для моков успешного логина/логаута/профиля, а также валидационных ошибок 400/422 (ADR 0014).

Локальный запуск юнит тестов фронтенда (`npm run test`) и typecheck (`tsc`).

## Не проверено и риски
Нет.

## Интеграция
Не требует миграций БД или переменных окружения.

body:
Five independent test and doc debts, one commit each, plus a review fix round and a merge of master:

1. `test/doctor.test.ts` "hints: is empty when no required tool is missing": the flake is a concurrent `probe -i worktree` (or any live scratch worktree registered in the repo) making doctor emit one hint under the real cwd through its `git worktree list` registry; the test now uses the isolated cwd/lockDir fixture its siblings use (reproduced 40/40 before, 0/40 after by an independent reviewer).
2. `src/probe/session.ts` stale-worktree marker removal after a successful recovery is pinned by a probe-worktree test plus a negative control (beginWorktree mocked to fail before its own marker write so the recovery's removal is the only remover); the inverted-condition mutant is killed.
3. README `--plan` example uses neutral placeholders throughout with a non-runnable caveat.
4. `test/import-boundaries.test.ts`: an AST-based layering guard for src/probe (session -> step/setup/index, step -> setup/index, setup -> step/index forbidden; side-effect, dynamic and extensionless imports covered; the type-only index<->plan cycle tolerated only while both directions stay type-only).
5. `test/drift.test.ts` "++ " content case uses a real rename so a compound mutant disabling the whole `+++ ` header branch is caught.

Verification on the merged tree (after #201): 816 tests; build, typecheck, typecheck:test, format:check, flag-order lint clean; mutation probes through agent-primitives probe for every item (seven in round 2 incl. the AST forms); two review rounds (accept_with_notes, accept).

author: claude[bot]
body:
Les trois cadres de « Mes réalisations » portaient tous le même pictogramme d'appareil photo. Sur une page livrée au client c'est juste — ils disent « vos photos iront là ». Sur `exemple.html`, **seul aperçu concret du produit pour un prospect**, trois fois le même appareil photo se lit « il n'a rien à montrer » — et c'est le bloc qu'un artisan regarde en premier.

Six métiers, trois motifs chacun, qui suivent les légendes déjà en place : la vue d'ensemble, le détail, l'ouvrage fini.

## Ce que ces dessins n'ont pas le droit d'être

`generer.mjs` portait déjà la règle, et elle a conduit tout le lot :

> « Rien n'est fabriqué qui puisse passer pour un vrai chantier : le dépôt interdit le faux témoignage, et **une image de synthèse présentée comme une réalisation en serait un**. »

Une belle scène de toiture dans un bloc intitulé « Mes réalisations » serait exactement ce faux témoignage. Donc **trait schématique, jamais une image** : pas d'aplat qui imite une matière, pas de perspective, pas d'ombre portée. Le cadre pointillé reste — c'est lui qui dit « il manquera quelque chose ici » — et la légende continue d'annoncer un *emplacement* de photo.

## Ce que le regard a corrigé, et qu'aucune mesure n'aurait dit

Ces cadres sont des SVG encodés en base64 : le contrôleur de lisibilité lit le HTML et ne les voit pas. Les trois défauts sont sortis de la capture d'écran, pas des tests.

| défaut | correction |
| --- | --- |
| les motifs passaient **sous** « Votre photo 1 » | la bande libre est y ∈ [30, 200] ; ils y entrent à 88 %, recentrés sur 115 |
| les ardoises étaient en joints décalés — soit **l'appareillage du maçon** | redessinées en écailles ; deux métiers qui partagent un dessin annulent l'argument même de la galerie |
| la gouttière se lisait « table », puis le collier ajouté pour la sauver **croisait la descente** et redonnait une croix | le coude au pied la nomme à lui seul |

## Le métier passe par la ligne de commande, pas par `commande.json`

`node scripts/generer.mjs <dossier> --demonstration --motif=couvreur`

Le fichier de commande est écrit par la route d'API et relu par un type éprouvé dans `src/lib/site.ts` : lui ajouter un champ pour un détail de dessin ferait porter au contrat de commande une décision qui n'est pas la sienne. Un métier absent ou inconnu **retombe sur l'appareil photo**, comme un domaine absent laisse la page complète plutôt que d'inventer une adresse.

## Vérifications

`bash .claude/skills/verifier/scripts/verifier.sh` — vert sur les deux projets touchés :

- **Artisan Express** : lint, typecheck, tests, build, regard 393 × 873
- **TITAN Builder** : lint, typecheck, tests, build, regard 393 × 873

Et sur les pages rendues : **aucune image cassée, aucun débordement horizontal**, à 393 px sur le terrain de référence.

## Ce qui n'est pas dedans

La page en ligne ne changera pas avec cette fusion : le projet Vercel `artisan-express` n'est pas lié à Git, et son dernier déploiement date du 03/09. Le rebranchement est une action de tableau de bord, hors de portée d'ici — `vercel.com` et `api.vercel.com` sont refusés par le mandataire de la session, et `create_git_project` rend `409 conflict` sur un projet existant non lié.

## Customer Investigation & Resolution Evidence

Implements a first-class investigation trail for customer-facing AI interactions, starting with Enterprise Chat.

### Included
- Tenant-scoped `customer_investigations` records with channel, customer/conversation/interaction correlation, intent, status, resolution and confidence.
- Ordered `investigation_steps` for intent, evidence, findings, actions, verification and customer response.
- Exact `tool_invocations` with provider/server/tool name, arguments, result, authorization context, latency and status.
- `customer_resolutions` storing the customer-facing response and evidence summary.
- RLS policies for authenticated tenant members plus service-role writes.
- Enterprise Chat automatically creates an investigation and records the authorized evidence tools and AI model invocation.
- Chat UI exposes the investigation ID, exact tools/servers/arguments and investigation steps beneath the customer response.

### Important scope
This is the first vertical implementation. The evidence contract is provider/channel neutral so Voice, WhatsApp, Email, Messaging and bot-runtime integrations can attach to the same investigation model next.

No mock customer data or seeded production evidence is introduced.

author: tkhduracell
body:
Three related improvements to the Sonos UI on the dashboard.

## 1. The whole zone card opens the speaker view

The speaker view (`SonosZoneManager`, at `#speakers`) already existed and the room name was already a link — but it was styled identically to the surrounding plain text, and the album art and track line weren't part of it. Small target, invisible affordance.

The link now wraps the album art, room name and track info as one target, with a hover background, a `›` chevron, and a member-count badge for multi-speaker zones. The transport buttons stay **siblings** of the link rather than children, so play/pause/next/volume/mute still work without navigating (verified in the DOM: 0 buttons nested inside the link).

## 2. Per-speaker Say → a single Announce dialog

The `Say` button was repeated on every unassigned speaker chip and could only target those speakers — announcing to a grouped room was impossible.

Now one green **Announce** button sits below the unassigned speakers and opens a centered dialog with a speaker dropdown, a message field and a Send button. The dropdown lists every speaker in the house, grouped ones included, sorted with Swedish collation.

Behaviour details:
- Escape closes the dialog *before* the panel, so it no longer dismisses everything at once
- Send is disabled while the message is empty; Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline
- A failed request now surfaces an error instead of silently clearing the field

## 3. Drag-and-drop hint

A one-line hint under the panel header — "Drag and drop speakers to move them between groups." — since the drag affordance was otherwise undiscoverable. In English, matching the panel's own labels (Unassigned Speakers, Announce, Speaker, Message, Send).

## 4. Announcement volume

A volume slider above the message field. `node-sonos-http-api` takes the volume inline — `/{room}/say/{text}/{volume}`, where an all-digit second path segment is parsed as the announcement volume (verified against `lib/actions/say.js` on the running container). It's an *announcement* volume, so the player's previous level is restored afterwards; no separate `/volume` call is made. Defaults to 40, matching the API's own `settings.announceVolume`.

## Test plan

**Local (done)** — against the live Sonos setup:
- [x] Clicking the album art (previously dead) opens the speaker view: Kök 21, Uterum 22, Kontor 26, Tvättstuga 31, plus unassigned Pool and Vardagsrum
- [x] Announce dialog lists all 6 speakers, correctly sorted (`Kök` before `Pool`)
- [x] Send disabled on empty message, enabled once text is entered
- [x] Escape closes the dialog but leaves the speaker panel open; a second Escape closes the panel
- [x] Transport buttons still act on the zone without navigating
- [x] Volume slider builds the right request: with the slider at 65, the call is `/sonos/Kontor/say/Middagen%20%C3%A4r%20klar/65` (verified with `fetch` stubbed, so no audio was played)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean for both changed files, `npm test` 36/36

Note: `npm run typecheck` reports 4 pre-existing errors in `app/hooks/useFluxQuery.ts` — that's the dead hook #446 deletes, unrelated to this PR.

**Post-merge:** confirm on the wall-mounted iPad that the larger tap target and the dialog work with a finger, and send a real announcement to a grouped room.

author: blindpirate
body:
Unblocks the `milestone-30` publish Mikhail Lopatkin is waiting on.

Failing build: https://builds.gradle.org/buildConfiguration/GradleNative_NativePlatform_Publishing_PublishJavaApiAlpha/117007595

```
groovy.lang.MissingPropertyException: Could not get unknown property 'archivesBaseName' for object of type org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.dsl.dependencies.DefaultDependencyHandler.
```

## Root cause

`Project.archivesBaseName` was removed in Gradle 9, and this build is on 9.4.1.

The Gradle 9 migration (dfe69529, "Migrate to gradle 9") converted the *setter* usages in `test-app/build.gradle`:

```diff
-applicationName = 'native-platform-test'
-archivesBaseName = 'native-platform-test'
+application { applicationName = 'native-platform-test' }
+base { archivesName = 'native-platform-test' }
```

…but missed the remaining *reader* at `test-app/build.gradle:25`. The error surfaces against `DefaultDependencyHandler` because that's the innermost delegate in the enclosing `dependencies {}` closure.

## Blast radius

Worth being precise about this, because the failing line lives in `test-app` but that is *not* where the build actually breaks.

`PublishJavaApiAlpha` itself only reported `Snapshot dependencies failed: 5`. The real failures were in all eight per-platform Alpha jobs, in the `:native-platform:uploadJni` / `:native-platform:uploadNcursesJni` steps — e.g. [117007587](https://builds.gradle.org/build/117007587), whose build problem is the identical `archivesBaseName` exception.

That's expected: `test-app/build.gradle` is evaluated during the configuration phase regardless of which project's task you invoke, so a broken line in it fails *every* task in the build. The one-line fix therefore unblocks the entire publish matrix, not just `:test-app:uploadMain`.

## Why only publishing jobs hit it

The block is guarded by `versions.useRepo`, and `gradlebuild.VersionDetails.isUseRepo()` is true only for the Snapshot/Alpha/Milestone/Release build types. Ordinary dev and CI test builds never configure it, which is why this went unnoticed since December.

## The fix

Read the value from the `base` extension, which is already configured at line 12 of the same file:

```groovy
download "$group:${base.archivesName.get()}:${version}"
```

`PublishPlugin.getArchivesBaseName(Project)` in buildSrc does the same thing via `BasePluginExtension.getArchivesName()`; using the extension directly from the Groovy DSL is equivalent and avoids pulling a buildSrc import into the script.

## Verification

Reproduced locally before the fix (a dummy `publishToken` is needed to get past `ReleasePlugin`'s configuration-time credential check and reach `:test-app`):

```
$ ./gradlew :test-app:help -Psnapshot -PpublishToken=dummy
* Where: Build file 'test-app/build.gradle' line: 25
* What went wrong: Could not get unknown property 'archivesBaseName' ...
```

After the fix, both the snapshot and the alpha/milestone path configure cleanly, and the dependency resolves to the intended coordinates:

```
$ ./gradlew :test-app:help -Psnapshot -PpublishToken=dummy
BUILD SUCCESSFUL

$ ./gradlew :test-app:dependencies --configuration download -Palpha=milestone-30 -PpublishToken=dummy
download
\--- net.rubygrapefruit:native-platform-test:0.22-milestone-30 FAILED
BUILD SUCCESSFUL
```

(The `FAILED` marker is just the artifact not being published yet — the point is that the coordinates are now built correctly. Configuration-time success is what was broken.)

A plain `./gradlew :test-app:help` dev build is unaffected, as the changed line sits inside the `useRepo` guard.

CI verification on this branch:

[`PublishJavaApiSnapshot` #189](https://builds.gradle.org/buildConfiguration/GradleNative_NativePlatform_Publishing_PublishJavaApiSnapshot/117050395) — **SUCCESS**, all 17 builds in the dependency graph green on `bdc12fc9`, published `0.22-snapshot-20260906135345+0000`.

I used the Snapshot job rather than Alpha/Milestone deliberately: it exercises the identical `versions.useRepo` code path (`isUseRepo()` is true for both) and runs the same `:native-platform:uploadJni` and `:test-app:uploadMain` steps, but publishes a disposable timestamped snapshot to `libs-snapshots-local` instead of writing to `libs-releases-local`. In particular it avoids consuming the `milestone-30` coordinate from an unmerged branch.

The eight per-platform `uploadJni` publishes — the exact jobs that failed on master — all passed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| `PublishMacOsAarch64Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishMacOsAmd64Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishLinuxAmd64Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishLinuxAarch64Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishLinuxAmd64Ncurses6Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishLinuxAarch64Ncurses5Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishWindowsAmd64Snapshot` | ✅ |
| `PublishFreeBsdAmd64Snapshot` | ✅ |

## Scope

I grepped the repo for other Gradle-9-removed APIs that would only be exercised on the `versions.useRepo` / publishing path — `archivesBaseName`, `libsDir`, `distsDir`, `mainClassName`, `uploadArchives`, `getConvention()`, `archiveName`/`destinationDir`/`classesDir`, `project.buildDir`, and the removed `compile`/`runtime`/`testCompile` configurations. This line was the only hit; `versions.useRepo` itself appears nowhere else. No other changes needed.

One caveat on that sweep: this bug's signature is *dynamic* Groovy property resolution, which static grepping cannot fully rule out — it only fails at configuration time, on a code path that no dev or CI build exercises. The durable guard would be a cheap CI job running a configuration-only task with `-Psnapshot`, which would have caught this in December. Out of scope here, but worth considering separately.

body:
## What this lands

The EEF corpus markdown projection in `@oaknational/graph-corpus-sdk`, the delivery node `eef-corpus-markdown-projection` (ratified 2026-09-06, "build it next"): a pure rendering of the fixed EEF Teaching and Learning Toolkit corpus into formatter-normal markdown, one file per strand plus one corpus-reference file, with a thin writer script. Nothing rendered is committed in this repository; a consumer commits the files it needs with a provenance pin naming the corpus data version.

- **Renderers** (`src/eef-strands/`): `renderStrandMarkdown(id)` — provenance block, headline metrics with the corpus's own labels and ratings and its `headline_summary` verbatim, definition, key findings, then every section the strand carries (effectiveness, behind the average with per-phase, per-subject and moderating-factor detail, closing the disadvantage gap, implementation with common pitfalls and the digital-technology note, related guidance reports, related strands linked by name, update history) and tags — and `renderCorpusReferenceMarkdown()` — source and attribution, methodology with every cost band, evidence factor and conversion row, every caveat, the strand index. Every rendered line is corpus text read from a named source path or a fixed structural label. A null `impact_months` renders as "no figure in the corpus".
- **Not rendered, stated**: `school_context_relevance`, the block the evidence tools select on; on some strands it also carries per-phase and per-application impact figures and a study count. The module and the corpus reference both say so; rendering those figures is a named follow-up in the node's Out of scope.
- **Compile-time key pins** (`eef-markdown-rendered-keys.ts`): the keys each renderer reads are subtracted from the keys the corpus carries and the remainder is constrained to `never`, so a corpus refresh that adds a field fails the build naming it. The leaf-completeness test walk is the prose catch-all behind the pins.
- **Pure file set**: `renderEefMarkdownFiles()` returns the reference plus one entry per strand with relative paths (`strands/<id>.md` beside `eef-corpus-reference.md`); layout and every relative link come from one paths module.
- **Writer**: `scripts/render-eef-markdown.ts` (`pnpm render:eef-markdown --out <dir>`), the only place that touches the filesystem. It imports the file-set module directly, never the package barrel. Each target directory is asserted inside the output root before a write; every written file is checked against the repository's formatter configuration resolved from the script's own location (a missing configuration fails, never passes vacuously); an empty `--out` is refused; a filesystem failure is one stderr line and exit code 1. It only writes: stale files from an earlier render are the caller's to remove.
- **Tests** (`src/eef-strands/*.unit.test.ts`): set equality with no orphan and no gap; the path-shape pin (relative, no parent segment, under the root) and relative-link resolution against the rendered set; every rendered text equals its prettier-normalised form; per-strand provenance, headline lines, key findings and EEF page; the leaf-completeness walk; named cases for the heterogeneous `by_phase` key set, per-phase months and notes, and the study-count strands; the corpus reference's source, authors, licence, attribution note, caveats, cost bands, factors, conversion rows and index verbatim; an absence pin on the school-context lines. No test touches the filesystem: the writer is proven by its own verification on every run plus the named script run below.
- **ADR-179 amendment**: repository-local tooling excluded from the published surface (this script) is not a transport surface; status line marked amended 2026-09-06.
- **Configuration**: `@oaknational/type-helpers` (dependency; the estate bans `Object.keys/values/entries`), `@oaknational/safe-path`, `prettier` and `tsx` (devDependencies), the package script, `scripts/**/*.ts` in both tsconfig includes and the package's ESLint boundary block, and the package's existing knip block extended. The lockfile carries one registry-metadata line for an unrelated `xmldom` deprecation; the survivability rebuild from declarations was byte-identical, holds intact, audit unchanged, frozen install clean.
- **Governed-source review ledger**: `src/eef-strands` is a governed agent-facing source scope, so every changed file there is recorded in the current-source delta-review ledger (`agent-tools/src/mcp-content-current-source/current-source-delta-reviews-sdk-corpus-projection.ts`): the six renderer modules as a projection for a file export registered on no served surface and reached by no MCP consumer, the key pins and the two type-helper edits as type-only, the barrel as implementation-only, the test helper as test-only. The generated delta inventory is refreshed from that ledger; anchors, the current-source truth set and the audit report are unchanged (`validate-mcp-content-current-source`: OK, 728 items accounted).
- **Node re-true** (second commit): the Tests bullet, the third acceptance criterion reworded to "Writable to any directory" with the path-shape test as proof (owner: wording fix, the ratification stamp stands), the writer's verification and no-delete behaviour, and the `school_context_relevance` follow-up in Out of scope.

## Review contract

A finding is cured when it names a failing scenario; design-intent findings are dispositioned by reply. Intake budget per PDR-140: two settlement pushes, then dispositions only. Reproduction, from `packages/sdks/graph-corpus-sdk`: `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint` (zero errors; the eight `no-throw-statement` warnings are pre-existing in files this PR does not touch), `pnpm test` (405 passing across 14 files), and `pnpm render:eef-markdown --out <scratch>` (31 files, "all in the repository formatter's normal form") followed by `pnpm exec markdownlint-cli2 --no-globs --config .markdownlint.json "<scratch>/**/*.md"` and `pnpm exec prettier --check "<scratch>/**/*.md"` from the repository root. Reviewed before execution by code-expert and after by code-expert, test-expert, type-expert, config-expert and docs-adr-expert; every cure applied, the one owner question (a writer test through the test-helpers IO sandbox) refuted at the seat under the estate's no-IO-in-tests rule.

author: findmybasket
body:
Built, dispatched, measured. **`refresh-fragrance-shop-import.yml` at `0 1 * * *`; second import completed 13:46, `ok`.**

## ★ Second time this month a live retailer ran a week without a refresh

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Beauty Flash** | 4 Aug – 4 Sep | feed frozen 31 days, then 404 (item 588) |
| **The Fragrance Shop** | 31 Aug – 6 Sep | **no schedule at all** (items 578, 597) |

**Different mechanisms, same visible state, neither detectable from the retailer's own status.** `last_import_status` answers *"did the last run succeed"* and never *"was there supposed to be another one"* — the gap state 7 exists to close, and why it is a state rather than a check.

## The slot

`0 1 * * *`. Today's window ran **02:22 → 10:04**, monitor at 09:00. **01:00 is the only clear hour before it**, so a failure lands in that morning's email rather than the next one.

Rakuten shape after `refresh-superdrug.yml.disabled`. Directory **`/43488`, established by the census** — Superdrug's was `/50336`, not its SID, and a guessed path fails as an empty fetch that reads as a finding about the feed.

## ★★ The price rule survived, because the workflow calls the script

```
inspected 3173, wrote 3173, skipped 0 with no URL
rows with BOTH sale and retail: 544
  sale taken (below retail):    544
  sale IGNORED (>= retail):     0   <- why the comparison is there
```

**544 of 544 took the sale.** The 31 August figure was 557 of 557 — the feed has moved, and **the rule was re-measured rather than assumed.** That third line is the point: a was/now inversion shows up there on the run it happens, not in a price complaint.

Superdrug's converter reads `price/retail` and never reads `<sale>` — a **certainty** of the wrong price on every row carrying both, median 33% overstated. The workflow **invokes the script rather than reimplementing it**, so the rule can't drift into two copies.

## What six days cost

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | 3,199 → **3,291** |
| **Prices changed** | **27** — 10 up, 17 down, mean **£13.91** / **29.4%**, largest **£70** |
| New products | **92** · gone **0** · stock flips **0** |

> **0.8% of rows in six days, against Beauty Flash's 2.2% in thirty-one.** Fragrance is a stable catalogue and **this gap cost little** — the 92 absent products are the larger loss.
>
> **And "it cost little" is a fact about this feed, not a reason the schedule was optional.** The same six days on Beauty Flash moved 191 prices, and nothing about the arrangement knew which retailer it had.

## State 7, satisfied

Scheduled, and **completed twice**. The *twice* clause is why this reads as satisfied rather than pending — a has-run test would have passed six days ago while nothing recurred. Marked in `docs/onboarding-completeness.md`.

**Retailer 35 is the first onboarding to satisfy all seven.**

author: janlampert08-dev
body:
## Summary

Abgemeldete Besucher kamen bisher nur bis zur Streckenliste. Feed und Bestenlisten waren zwar längst öffentlich lesbar (`public_fahrten` und die Leaderboard-Views sind an `anon` freigegeben), standen aber in keiner Navigation — erreichbar nur über einen geteilten Link. Und „Fahrt starten" leitete ohne Session direkt auf `/anmelden` um. Ein Besucher ohne Konto sah damit nichts von dem, was das Produkt ausmacht, bevor er sich registrieren sollte.

Das Anmelde-Gate wandert deshalb an das Ende des Kernloops — an die Stelle, an der zum ersten Mal etwas dem Nutzer gehören muss:

**Ohne Konto nutzbar**

| Schritt im Kernloop | Wo |
|---|---|
| Strecken entdecken, Streckendetail | `/`, `/strecken/[id]` |
| Feed (global) lesen, Profile suchen | `/feed` |
| Bestenlisten, Streckenbestzeiten | `/leaderboards` |
| Fremde Fahrten und Profile ansehen | `/fahrten/[id]`, `/fahrer/[id]` |
| Freie Fahrt vollständig aufzeichnen bis zum Fazit | `/fahrten/neu` |

**Konto erforderlich** — jeweils dort, wo etwas entsteht, das einer Person zugeordnet wird:

| Aktion | Gate |
|---|---|
| **Fahrt speichern / teilen** | neu: im Fazit-Screen (`FreeRideForm`) |
| Kudos, Bewerten, Favorit, Melden | unverändert |
| Strecke vorschlagen, eigenes Profil, Premium, Moderation | unverändert |
| „Folge ich"-Filter im Feed | unverändert |
| Streckenfahrt („Strecke starten") | unverändert — bleibt vorerst hinter der Anmeldung, siehe „Bewusst nicht enthalten" |

### Im Einzelnen

- **`lib/nav.ts`** — Feed und Bestenlisten stehen jetzt auch in der abgemeldeten Navigation (Header und BottomNav, fünf Einträge wie im angemeldeten Zustand). „Vorschlagen" und „Profil" bleiben weg: beide wären ohne Konto nur eine Umleitung auf `/anmelden`.
- **`app/fahrten/neu/page.tsx`** — kein Redirect mehr ohne Session. Der Recorder läuft für Gäste; Fahrzeuge werden nur für angemeldete Nutzer geladen (ein Gast sieht die Auswahl ohnehin nicht).
- **`components/FreeRideForm.tsx`** — ein Gast bekommt im Fazit statt des Speichern-Formulars das Anmelde-Gate („Konto erstellen" / „Ich habe ein Konto" / „Fahrt verwerfen"). In der Aufzeichnungsleiste steht vorab ein Hinweis, dass das Speichern am Ende ein Konto verlangt — keine Überraschung nach der Fahrt.
- **`lib/trackingStorage.ts`** — die als Gast aufgezeichnete Fahrt liegt unter einem eigenen Gast-Schlüssel (`GUEST_TRACKING_USER_ID`) und wird über `adoptGuestTrackingSnapshot` an das Konto übergeben, das sich dafür anmeldet. Abgesichert über einen Einmal-Marker, siehe Sicherheitsbetrachtung.
- **`components/useRideRecorder.ts`** — neue Option `guestContinuationToken`, die diese Übergabe beim Mount genau einmal auslöst, vor dem Laden des eigenen Snapshots.
- **`lib/actions/auth.ts` / Registrierung** — `signUp` akzeptiert wie `signIn` ein optionales `next`, damit ein Konto, das nur zum Speichern dieser Fahrt angelegt wurde, auch wieder dort ankommt (auch über den Bestätigungslink).

## Definition of Done

- [x] The implementation matches the task's actual scope (no scope creep).
- [x] Relevant tests exist and pass (`npm run test`).
- [x] Lint passes (`npm run lint`).
- [x] The production build succeeds (`npm run build`).
- [x] A security review has been considered for any Protected Area touched (see `AGENTS.md` → Protected Areas).
- [x] No secrets, keys, or credentials are present in the diff.
- [x] This description explains what changed, why, and lists the validation commands actually run and their results.

## Sicherheitsbetrachtung (Protected Area: `lib/actions/auth.ts`)

**An der serverseitigen Autorisierung ändert sich nichts.** `logFreeRide` weist eine Fahrt ohne Session unverändert ab (`if (!user) return { error: … }`), RLS bleibt unangetastet, es gibt keine neue Migration und keinen zusätzlichen Aufruf des Admin-Clients. Gelockert wird ausschliesslich die *Sichtbarkeit* von Seiten, die ohnehin für `anon` lesbar sind — plus der Recorder, der rein clientseitig läuft und nichts persistiert.

Drei Punkte, die beim Review Aufmerksamkeit verdienen:

**1. Nutzertrennung der Tracking-Snapshots.** `lib/trackingStorage.ts` hält den GPS-Verlauf bewusst unter einem Schlüssel mit Nutzer-ID, damit auf einem geteilten Gerät eine abgebrochene Aufzeichnung nicht dem nächsten angemeldeten Konto angeboten wird. Diese Grenze bleibt bestehen.

Die erste Fassung hatte hier eine Lücke, die im Review gefunden und in `336addc` geschlossen wurde: der Rücksprungpfad war `?fortsetzen=1`, ein fester, öffentlich bekannter Wert. Damit hätte auf einem geteilten Browser jedes angemeldete Konto die liegengebliebene Gastfahrt eines anderen übernehmen können, indem es diese URL einfach aufruft — realistischerweise nicht einmal absichtlich, sondern weil die URL nach dem Gate-Klick in der Chronik steht und beim Tippen vorgeschlagen wird.

Jetzt gilt: Das Anmelde-Gate stellt **im Moment des Klicks** einen zufälligen Marker aus (`crypto.randomUUID()`), der zwei Stunden gültig und **genau einmal einlösbar** ist; er wandert als `?fortsetzen=<token>` durch die Anmeldung und wird bei der Rückkehr gegen den gespeicherten Wert geprüft und dabei gelöscht. Ein erfundener Wert, derselbe Link ein zweites Mal (Chronik, Zurück-Taste) oder ein abgelaufener Marker übernehmen nichts. Zwei Stunden, weil der Rückweg bei einer Neuregistrierung durch eine Bestätigungsmail führt. Ausserdem: ein bereits vorhandener eigener Snapshot gewinnt, ein abgelaufener Gast-Snapshot (>24 h) wird nicht wiederbelebt, und auch nach der Übergabe wird nichts von selbst gespeichert — der Nutzer sieht Distanz/Zeit/Ø-Tempo und drückt „Fahrt speichern".

Was das ausdrücklich *nicht* abdeckt: wer auf demselben Gerät die Devtools öffnet, liest Snapshot und Marker direkt aus dem `localStorage`. Gegen Angreifer mit Gerätezugriff schützt clientseitige Speicherung grundsätzlich nicht; abgedeckt ist der Fall, dass die blosse URL genügt.

**2. Open-Redirect über das neue `next` bei der Registrierung.** Der Wert kommt aus client-kontrollierter `FormData` und läuft deshalb durch `safeInternalPath` — dieselbe Sperre wie bei `signIn` und dem Fahrzeug-Formular (Tests in `lib/utils/url.test.ts`, u.a. gegen protokollrelative `//evil.example`). Er landet ausserdem in `emailRedirectTo`, also in einem Link in einer echten Bestätigungsmail; `app/auth/callback/route.ts` prüft ihn dort unabhängig ein zweites Mal, bevor daraus ein Redirect wird. Der mitgeführte Marker ist ohne den passenden `localStorage`-Eintrag wertlos, in einer E-Mail also unkritisch.

**3. Keine neue Datenexposition.** `/feed` und `/leaderboards` waren bereits ohne Session erreichbar und geben nur her, was ohnehin öffentlich freigegeben ist; die Änderung verlinkt sie lediglich.

## Bewusst nicht enthalten

- **„Strecke starten" auf der Streckenseite** bleibt hinter der Anmeldung (`app/strecken/[id]/page.tsx` zeigt weiterhin den Hinweistext). Für eine Streckenfahrt wäre dieselbe Mechanik nötig, das ist ein eigener Schritt.
- **Nebenbefund, nicht angefasst:** Der Hinweis „Melde dich an, um diese Strecke als gefahren einzutragen und zu bewerten." auf der Streckenseite ist reiner Text ohne Link auf `/anmelden`.
- **Bekannte Grenze der Übergabe:** Wer die Bestätigungsmail in einem *anderen* Browser öffnet, findet die Gastfahrt dort nicht — Snapshot und Marker liegen im `localStorage` des Browsers, in dem aufgezeichnet wurde. Das ist der Preis dafür, die Snapshot-Trennung nicht aufzuweichen.
- **Docstring-Coverage-Warnung** aus den Pre-merge-Checks (58 % statt 80 %) bewusst nicht bedient: die Codebasis dokumentiert Funktionen durchgehend mit vorangestellten Kommentarblöcken, JSDoc kommt nur an einer Handvoll Prop-Definitionen in `components/ui/` vor. Hier JSDoc nachzurüsten wäre gegen den umgebenden Stil.

## Validation

```
$ npm run test
 Test Files  22 passed (22)
      Tests  203 passed (203)

$ npm run lint
(keine Ausgabe, keine Befunde)

$ npm run build
✓ Compiled successfully
  Finished TypeScript
✓ Alle Routen generiert (u.a. ƒ /fahrten/neu, ƒ /feed, ƒ /leaderboards, ƒ /regist

author: wesm
body:
Embedding hosts can mount Kata's HTTP service below a path, but the browser
application assumed the origin root. Its navigation, API calls, sessions,
event stream, and production assets could therefore escape the selected mount.

This adds `Service.HandlerAt`, makes release asset references relative, and
derives the browser route and API base from the loaded entrypoint. Root
deployments keep the existing `/kata` route; mounted applications stay below
the host-selected path. The browser's `/api` namespace remains reserved.
Authentication remains the host's responsibility and is unchanged.
