author: franklinbaldo
davidmetcalfe
body:
## Summary

The Desktop model-selector search finds models regardless of hyphen-vs-space in the query, but the blue per-character match highlighting only works for queries that appear literally in the space-separated display label. `qwen3.8` highlights; `qwen3.8-flash` reveals the row while highlighting nothing. The standalone picker dialog has the same class of failure with the opposite polarity (space queries find rows without highlighting). The search input also runs dictionary spellcheck over model ids.

Closes #104509

## Root cause

The filter and the highlighter read two different text corpora. The filter haystack in `model-catalog-menu.tsx` (`groupModels`) contains both the raw id (`qwen3.8-flash`) and the display name ("Qwen3.8 Flash"); the highlighter (`HighlightMatches`) sees only the display label and is a literal case-insensitive `indexOf` matcher. A hyphen query matches the id segment but never occurs in the label — rows appear unexplained. This violates `highlight-matches.tsx`'s own documented contract: *"The query must mirror the surface's OWN filter semantics, or the emphasis lies about why a row matched."*

Sibling surfaces share the bug class:
- `model-visibility-dialog.tsx` (Edit Models): identical id+display filter vs display-only highlight.
- `model-picker.tsx`: inverse polarity — filter on raw id + aliases, highlight on raw id.
- `dropdown-menu.tsx` `DropdownMenuSearch`: no `spellCheck={false}` while composer/settings inputs already disable it.

## Fix

One length-preserving search-equivalence fold in `lib/text.ts`, applied on **both** sides of every model-search filter and inside `HighlightMatches`' range finder:

- `searchFold(v)` = `asText(v).toLowerCase().replace(/[-_.]/g, ' ')`; `foldIncludes(text, query)` for the filters.
- One char in → one char out: highlight ranges computed on folded text index the original text unchanged, so `<mark>` rendering is untouched and marks slice the original characters.
- Superset guarantee: a per-character substitution applied to both sides, so any query that matched before still matches — only highlight coverage grows.

`model-picker.tsx`'s inverse polarity is fixed by the same fold rather than a parallel mechanism (one resolver owns the policy, per the repo's one-resolver rule). `DropdownMenuSearch` sets `spellCheck={false}`.

## Testing

TDD — tests written first and confirmed failing (10 red / 2 pass), then implementation to green:

- `lib/text.test.ts` (new): fold equivalence (`qwen3.8-flash` ≡ `Qwen3.8 Flash`), 1:1 length preservation, idempotence, `foldIncludes` superset over plain `includes`, rejection of genuinely different text.
- `components/ui/highlight-matches.test.tsx`: original contract suite restored verbatim (multi-term `string[]` queries, overlapping-range merging, empty/whitespace queries, multi-occurrence marking) plus separator-fold cases including index fidelity (marks slice original characters, e.g. `gpt 5` → marks `GPT-5`).
- `app/shell/model-catalog-menu.search-fold.test.tsx` (new): end-to-end menu behavior — hyphen query both filters AND marks the spaced label (the reported defect, red pre-fix); space query finds the hyphenated id (superset) and highlights without over-matching.
- `model-catalog-menu.test.tsx`'s hidden-model search test updated: its id-style query (`gemini-3.1`) now legitimately highlights, so the assertion reads the marked label instead of a single text node.

Results:
- Targeted suites: 52/52 across the 7 affected test files; 19/19 on the three touched in review round 1 after fixes.
- Full desktop vitest suite: 9,433 passed / 1 failed — the failure (`electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts`, subprocess exit 127) reproduces identically on unmodified `main` (environmental).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; ESLint clean on all changed files.
- Verified live against the running app by building the renderer from this branch and swapping it into the local install; `qwen3.8-flash` now filters and highlights, and the spellcheck squiggle is gone.

## Notes

**Scope:** Desktop surfaces only. The TUI (`ui-tui/src/lib/model-search-text.ts`) and web dashboard (`web/src/lib/model-search-text.ts`) model-search paths were left untouched to keep this PR focused; the same helper extends to them in a follow-up if wanted.

Pre-submission review: the design and the implementation were each vetted in cross-model review passes (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-OSS 120B) before submission. Round 1 flagged two test-quality issues (a false-green assertion and dropped contract tests), which were fixed and re-reviewed to a clean second pass.

author: ekalinin
body:
base<<retries in the infra-error retry schedule is a plain int64 shift on
time.Duration, so a wide enough --max-retries made it wrap into a negative
delay (retry_at in the past) or zero, breaking the min(base<<retries, cap)
formula from SPEC §13. Unreachable at the default --max-retries 8, but
latent for any operator who raises the budget.

Extract the pre-jitter computation into backoffDelay, a pure function
testable without a queue, and make the shift saturate at the cap: the
overflow check itself uses a right shift (base > cap>>retries), which
cannot overflow, so the answer is correct for any retries value without
ever performing the shift that would wrap.

Closes #129

author: dkayiwa
body:
Refs #379. **Not `Fixes`** — the measurement the issue names as a precondition was not run, and the rendering therefore ships off. See *What this does not do*.

## What the issue asked

An injected `safety_finding` tells the model which of the patient's own orders each substance it names came from — by **display string**, never by record number. The model is then left to join `Solu-Medrol 125mg/5ml` to one of several hundred numbered chart records on its own. Measured on the issue's own reproduction (RefApp 3.7.1, bundled DDInter KB, `chartMode=fullChart`, 341 chart records, three identical runs): the model cited the right chart record for **2 of the 5** interaction sentences. The attribution clause was emitted for two of those five, and both of those two were mis-cited.

The issue's own reading: the module computes the correspondence correctly every time and then asks the model to re-derive its last step. That is the shape `eval/drift-metric/README.md` records under *"The two-hop join is impossible, not unlearned"*, one level down.

## What this does

A rendered item carries the number of the chart record its order IS — `<Substance> from <order display> [14]` — **behind `chartsearchai.drugSafety.citeOrderRecords`, which ships `false`.** On a stock install the clause is Decision 64's, character for character. The flag is the answer to the issue's own precondition: the beat-or-match measurement it asks for needs a live inference engine and was not run here, so the rendering is not switched on by a merge, and running the probe later is a one-flip A/B on one binary rather than a revert of the decision, the fidelity fix and the tests.

`SafetyWarning.ChartOrderBridge` is untouched, so #347's two wire keys are unchanged and the number reaches no client.

- **The resolution is the injector's, and could not be the validator's.** `DrugSafetyValidator` still decides which attributions may be printed — #349's scoping and #347/#353's silence tests are untouched — but it runs from `preAnswerFindings`, before any record has a number. Only `injectRecords` holds the mappings.
- **Resolved after the reconciliation**, so an order the chart carried no `drug_order` record for cites the `active_drug_order` record injected for it. Moving the call earlier reddens `anOrderTheChartHadNoRecordForIsCitedByTheOneInjectedForIt`.
- **One rule, not a second walk.** The order→record walk moved into `DrugReferenceInjector.DrugOrderRecords`; `unrepresentedActiveOrders` now reads it as `.isEmpty()`, so *substantiated* is defined AS that walk answering. Each caller indexes the mapping list it asks about.
- **The citation reading is stricter than the boolean.** #118's name leg is fail-OPEN by design — it decides whether to WARN and inject, where over-matching costs nothing. Citing is an affirmative claim about WHICH prescription, so the same over-match is false. A name-leg answer is refused where the record is another active order's own by uuid, where the order reaches more than one record, and where more than one ORDER names the record — the last asked of candidacy rather than of what orders resolved to. Beside those, one ITEM is refused a number where the orders spelling its display do not resolve alike, which has two halves and a case each: they resolve to different records (`twoOrdersOfTheSameDisplayAreNamedOnce`), or one resolves and a sibling resolves to nothing (`aDisplayWhoseOtherOrderCanCiteNothingStatesNoNumberWhicheverComesFirst`) — and each half strikes the DISPLAY rather than the map entry, which needs a third order of that display to show (`aDisplayStruckByOneSiblingIsNotRestoredByAThird`). An attribution none of them resolves renders as it did before, per item, so an unambiguous neighbour keeps its number.
- **No `isCompleteFor` gate on the numbering.** That gate answers *is an ABSENCE meaningful*, which is the reconciliation's question; a query-scoped chart can carry the record an order is. Copying the gate across reddens `aQueryScopedSliceStillNumbersTheRecordsItDoesCarry`.

### The regression it would otherwise have caused

`ReferenceProseFidelityCheck` stripped `INLINE_CITATION` from the **answer** and compared against the record text unstripped — sound while no record carried a marker. Its tokeniser splits runs of letters and digits, so a record's `[14]` becomes the record word `14` that the stripped answer can never reproduce. An answer copying an attribution **verbatim** — exactly what the number is for — broke its reproduction there, and the gap `" ["` carries no sentence terminator, so nothing explained it: a divergence reported at WARN and published on #337's `unfaithfullyRenderedCitations`, manufactured by the faithful behaviour. Both operands now go through one stripping step. This is **not** behind the flag, and neither is `unrepresentedActiveOrders`: neither is the unmeasured question, and an order's own display can carry brackets with no help from this change.

## How it was verified

Deterministically, through the real `DrugReferenceInjector.injectRecords` wired to the real `DrugSafetyValidator` over fixtures parsed by the real parser — the number printed is the number of the chart record that order is, across the substantiated, injected, drifted-uuid, contested, ambiguous and query-scoped arrangements, and `aStockInstallStatesNoRecordNumberAtAll` asserts the shipped default over the very arrangement its neighbours assert with numbers. Every refusal was mutated and reddens a named case; the fidelity fix reverted reddens exactly its own. The full build is green from the repository root.

That sentence about the mutations was not true until round 3, and each review round found the previous one's mutation too weak: round 2 that one half of the display refusal reddened nothing when DELETED, round 3 that both halves stayed green when SUBSTITUTED with the obvious simplification, and that the arrangement pinning one of them depended on the order `OrderService` happened to return the patient's prescriptions in. Each is how the gap was found rather than argued.

Verified rather than assumed, because the whole change rests on it: a mapping's `getIndex()` really is the `[N]` prefix the model reads, driven through the real serializer with date-run compression on, where chart lines do differ from mapping text.

On a real standalone (3.7.1, port 8083) after deploying the merging head and clearing the module lib-cache: the module starts (liquibase through `chartsearchai-009`, no `startupErrorMessage`), `chartsearchai.drugSafety.citeOrderRecords` is `false`, all 53 `chartsearchai.*` rows are byte-identical before and after the redeploy, `GET /chartsearchai/drugreferencestatus` returns 200 with `entryCount: 2283`, and the loaded `DrugReferenceInjector` and `ChartSearchAiConstants` classes hash equal to the ones in the built omod.

**One operational caveat that verification turned up, and it is core behaviour rather than this change's.** The reworded property description lands byte-identically on a fresh install, but it will not appear on a standalone that already carries this module at `1.0.0-SNAPSHOT`: OpenMRS gates module setup on `module.<id>.version` changing, and when setup does run it only CREATES a missing global property and never rewrites an existing row's description. Established by forcing setup and then by deleting the row, which recreated it with the current text. The value the merge argument rests on — `false` — is unaffected either way.

## What this does not do

- **It does not carry the beat-or-match measurement the issue asks for**, which is why the rendering ships off. Nothing in the tests can tell *the number is correct* from *the number helps*, and they are green either way. The plan's first justification — "it adds data, not an instruction, so the three reverted prompt variants do not bind" — was **withdrawn at the refutation gate**: `eval/drift-metric/README.md` records a data-adding change in this same render layer that *"worked, and it did not h

author: bugrabilim
body:
Bir ajan denetimi katkı verici rolünde (#279/#280/#281) on bulgu çıkardı; ikisi özelliği **pratikte kullanılamaz** kılıyordu. Hepsi yeniden üretilerek doğrulandı ve düzeltildi.

## Kritik: hayalet değişiklikler ve bayat çığı

`normalizeValue` yalnız `undefined`/`null`ı boş sayıyordu; form ise doldurulmamış alanlar için her zaman `[]` / `false` / `"uye"` gönderiyor. Kayıtta o alanlar hiç **yokken** "değişmiş" sayılıyorlardı:

```
Tek alan değiştiren öneri → 11 alanlık çıkıyor
birthDate 1943→1945 + photos ""→[] + videos ""→[] + … (10 hayalet alan)
```

Asıl yıkım bir adım sonra: bir kişi için **bir** öneri onaylandığı anda, aynı kişiye ait bekleyen bütün öneriler — katkı vericinin hiç dokunmadığı on alan gerekçe gösterilerek — **kalıcı olarak** "bayat" olup bir daha onaylanamıyordu. Özelliğin çekirdek akışı buydu.

**Çözüm iki katmanlı.** `bosMu()` beş boşluk biçimini (`undefined`, `null`, `""`, `[]`, `false`) tek kavrama indiriyor — sayılar hariç, çünkü `siblingOrder: 0` gerçek bir sıra. İstemci de artık gövdenin tamamını değil yalnız **gerçekten değişen** alanları gönderiyor.

**Kendi testim hatayı doğru diye kilitliyormuş:** `"false boş DEĞİL"` iddiası yeşildi çünkü yanlış olanı kanıtlıyordu. Bilerek değiştirildi.

## Diğer düzeltmeler

| Bulgu | Ne oluyordu |
|---|---|
| **İdempotentlik** | Onay iki adımlı (önce ağaç, sonra damga); ikinci adım düşerse öneri bir daha **asla** onaylanamıyordu. Artık alan zaten `to`ya eşitse bayat sayılmıyor, ve damga yazılamadığında 404 değil ne olduğunu söyleyen 500 dönüyor. |
| **Boş değer `""` yazıyordu** | Kayıt defteri (`mergeValue`) alanı siler. Ayrışma sessiz yanlış çıktı üretiyordu: doğum tarihi öneriyle temizlenen kardeş, `?? "9999"` sıralamasında en sona değil en **başa** düşüyordu. Aynı kalıp defin yeri haritasında da var. |
| **Anahtar sırası** | `JSON.stringify` sıraya duyarlı; GEDCOM olayları `{id,type,title,…}`, form `{id,date,type,…}` sırasıyla kuruyor — içerikçe aynı olay "değişmiş" görünüyordu. Artık sıralanıyor. |
| **`kind: "uye"`** | Varsayılan; kişi rotaları `undefined`e çeviriyor, öneri yolu bu çeviriyi atlıyordu. |
| **Sessiz kırpma** | 4500 karakterlik biyografi 4000'e kırpılıyor, düzenleyici tam metni gördüğünü sanarak onaylıyor, 500 karakter kayboluyordu. Artık reddediliyor. |
| **Maskelenmiş kayıt** | Çekmece sahiplik kararını `view(person)` üzerinden veriyordu; `maskPerson` beyaz liste ve `addedBy` taşımıyor. Katkı verici kendi eklediği kaydı gizli işaretlediğinde çekmece "öner", form "güncelle" diyordu. |
| **Depoda kilit yok** | İki katkı verici aynı anda öneri açtığında ikinci yazma birincinin önerisini siliyordu. Kitabın `updatedAt` damgasıyla oku-doğrula-yaz eklendi. |
| **Arka arkaya onay 409** | İstemcinin taban sürümü kendi az önceki onayıyla eskiyordu — kuyruğun asıl kullanımı toplu onay olduğu için özellik pratikte kullanılamıyordu. Onay yanıtı artık ağacın yeni sürümünü döndürüyor. |

## İki güvenlik bulgusu

**Kişi ekleme ucu** gövdedeki `spouseIds`/`formerSpouseIds` ile **var olan kayıtlara** yazıyordu: katkı verici tek istekle ağaçtaki her kaydın eş listesine kendi kişisini sokabiliyor, silme yetkisi olmadığı için geri de alamıyordu. O diziler artık yalnız tam yetkide; katkı vericinin yolu `relation`.

**`ai/suggest` hiçbir rol kapısı taşımıyordu** — oturumu olan herkes (görüntüleyen dâhil) ağaç sahibinin YZ kotasını harcayabiliyordu. Kapı testi de göremiyordu: yalnız `canContribute` **geçen** rotalara bakıyordu, hiç kapısı olmayan bir rota ona görünmezdi. İddia "listeye girmeyen hiçbir uç açık olmasın" diyordu ama kanıtladığı "canContribute yazan her uç listede"ydi — **vaat ettiğinden azını kanıtlayan bir iddia**. Artık kapısız rotalar da gerekçeli bir muafiyet listesine karşı denetleniyor.

## Testler

`tests/proposals.test.mts` 49 → 69 iddia. Gerçek istemci gövdesiyle uçtan uca senaryo ve bayat çığı artık regresyon testi.

**Mutasyon denemesi:** dokuz mutasyon. İlk turda **üçü yakalanmadı** — idempotentlik, boş değerin alanı silmesi ve `kind` denkliği düzeltmelerini testsiz bırakmışım. İddialar eklendi, üçü de yakalandı.

`npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build` — hepsi temiz.

Forager sweeps must fail when planning returns `dynamic_selection_not_supported`. Previously those plans became failed points and the overall command could report success or persist an empty experiment/sweep.

This change raises `plan_unsupported` before tape downloads, WASM execution, or persistence, retaining the Engine reason code and message. Ordinary invalid sweep candidates can still be reported individually. Single-run behavior is unchanged.

A separate integration check connected this CLI commit to actual Engine WASM `aa7a6cbc`: run, standard sweep and fast sweep each exited 1 with `plan_unsupported` / `dynamic_selection_not_supported`. Network was blocked and zero requests were attempted; persistence was disabled. Engine counterpart: https://github.com/alphafoxai/alphafox-engine/pull/550.

Part of the approved Forager integration PR4: https://github.com/alphafoxai/alphafox-engine/issues/538. No package release or deployment.

author: zaxovaiko
body:
## Summary

`minAmount`/`maxAmount` on a chat command become a single `{currency, amount}` pair instead of a per-currency map, and migration `0002` rewrites every row written under either older shape.

## Why

Two reasons.

The per-currency map shipped without a data migration, so a row seeded before it still held a flat amount string. That row fails the descriptor schema, and because the list route validates the array as a whole, one bad row returned a 500 for the entire backoffice command list. A freshly seeded database never hit it, so CI stayed green.

The map itself was also the wrong shape for the requirement: a currency with no entry had no limit enforced at all, so a BTC minimum could be walked around by sending ETH. A command limit is now stated the way a responsible-gambling limit already is - one amount, one currency - and an overlay converts a transfer into that currency when it checks it, failing the transfer closed when no rate is available. The funds are never converted; the recipient is still credited in the sender's currency.

## Alternatives considered

Keeping the map and adding a fallback currency: still leaves an operator able to configure a limit that silently does not apply to a currency they forgot, and needs the same migration anyway.

Migrating only the flat-string rows named by the incident: stands are in different states, and a freshly seeded database holds maps. Both shapes had to be handled or the next environment would break the same way.

## Risks

A flat amount string carries no currency of its own; USD is what the seed used when that shape was written and is the only record of it. A map keeps its USD entry when it has one, otherwise its alphabetically first key, so every stand converges on the same row - no multi-entry maps exist on real stands today. Rows already carrying a `currency` key are skipped, so the migration is re-runnable.

Breaking for consumers: an overlay reading `config.minAmount` as a map must move to the pair and take on the conversion and the fail-closed path. Needs a release of `@openora/core` before the downstream overlay can follow.

author: zmz-commits
body:
Adds a section covering the big-data platform, and settles two open questions.

## One feed, two speeds

Kafka in the middle; three consumers at three speeds. The bot trades in milliseconds, the aggregator seals minutes into TimescaleDB for the website, Spark writes every raw tick into Delta on MinIO for research. **The slow lane failing must never stop a trade** — which is why they are separated by a queue rather than a function call.

TimescaleDB stays and its job gets *smaller*: it stops being the archive and becomes the application database plus recent bars. Since TimescaleDB is Postgres, it already fills the "Postgres for orders and positions" slot — there is no second database.

## Repository ownership — now decidable

Two rules you can grep for:

> `data-pipeline` never imports Spark.
> `lakehouse` never holds an API key.

The Kafka→bronze writer goes in `lakehouse` despite being ingestion by purpose: it shares almost nothing with the websocket reader and a lot with the batch jobs — schema, Spark session, MinIO endpoint, checkpoint convention. Put code where its neighbours are. The backfill stays out of Spark by writing dumb resumable Parquet into a landing prefix.

The live bot runner goes in `engine`, beside the sandbox worker, so "a strategy behaves identically in backtest and live" is structural rather than aspirational.

## Build order — Kubernetes is step 4, not step 1

Terraform and k3s first is the documented way this kind of project dies: four platform layers and not one tick consumed. Moving a *working* pipeline into a cluster is contained; debugging ingestion inside an unfamiliar cluster is two unknowns at once. Step 1 is ~200 lines of Python and is the only step that proves the rest is worth building.

## Honest

The section states plainly that at eight symbols none of this earns its keep, and where the line actually is: thousands of symbols, years of history, and questions that compare symbols to each other rather than processing them one at a time.

author: onaim500
body:
…after boot fix)

Follow-up to the boot-determinism fix (PR #81). CI run b27efa61 confirmed the device now boots the USB image deterministically and reaches login (WRAPPER_PIN_OK
+ WRAPPER_SSH_CONFIG_OK both ran), but the run then failed at the growpart step with paramiko "Authentication failed". Traced to two issues:

1. _pin_usb_boot_first() used a marker (WRAPPER_PIN_OK) that appears verbatim in the command it sends, so p.expect_exact() matched the command's ECHO and returned before the pin finished. The next sendline (the SSH-config command) then interleaved with the still-running pin command and corrupted the sshd setup (visible in output.txt as "...else echecho 'PermitRootLogin yes'..."). Fix: build the marker from a shell var (PMARK=WRAPPER_PIN; echo ${PMARK}_OK) so the literal string only appears in the command OUTPUT, making expect_exact wait for actual completion.

2. The wrapper enabled PermitRootLogin but not password auth. Reaching serial login proves the root password is valid, but if the image ships PasswordAuthentication no, paramiko root-password SSH still fails. Add 'PasswordAuthentication yes' to the sshd drop-in alongside PermitRootLogin.

Validated live end-to-end on agx-orin-11: ran the real wrapper.py with SKIP_PREPULL=1 and a trivial test command. WRAPPER_PIN_OK printed as output (no interleave), WRAPPER_SSH_CONFIG_OK applied cleanly, the wrapper got past growpart SSH (paramiko auth succeeded), and the test command ran with sys.exit(0). A fresh-power-cycle read-only recon afterward confirmed the pin took effect: BootCurrent pinned first in BootOrder, RHEL boot entries reduced from 81 to 1.

body: Closes #381. ## Summary Align MRL-0805 real-preflight evidence semantics with the canonical no-training Experiment-0 authority boundary without creating or admitting any real authority. This change preserves the existing training-authorization kind and its dual-trust admission path, and adds one mutually exclusive no-training evaluation authority kind: ```text mesc.mrl.real_preflight.no_training_evaluation_authority.v1 ``` The no-training payload requires: ```text authorization_disposition = AUTHORIZED authorization_scope = NO_TRAINING_EVALUATION evaluation_execution_authorized = true real_training_authorized = false training_prohibited = true ``` The production MRL real-evidence trust registry remains empty. Parsing a valid envelope does not grant authority or close MRL-0805. Admission still requires exact outer MRL real-evidence trust; the training-authorization trust validator is invoked only for the existing training kind. ## Bounded scope Net diff from canonical base `e2daaec64e78c206a2858e639f3ba7fc4b761e7b` is exactly: - `src/medscale/mesc/_mrl_real_preflight_evidence_v1.py` - `tests/test_mesc_mrl_0805_applicable_authority.py` - `specs/mesc-research-loop-v1/real-preflight-evidence-v1.md` No task ledger, real-evidence slot, production trust-registry value, model/data/runtime configuration, or training surface is modified. ## Supporting pre-PR verification - exact proposed Python blobs compile syntactically; - implementation blob: `fafc3013ca9af0b8524570aefe48a439002f81ae`; - focused regression-test blob: `21e4dda99467fe03b9623d29b457a682d6a6e9d5`; - specification blob: `a346f3ce715304ef81a56f58ae4fbb307a2d23be`; - compare against base is ahead-only and the surviving net diff is exactly the three paths above. These are supporting transport checks only. They are not exact-head CI, runtime qualification, independent review, real evidence, or authority. ## Required qualification Before merge this exact final head requires: - Ruff lint and format; - strict mypy; - docs hygiene; - full pytest on Python 3.11 and 3.12; - MRL machine-state drift/manual-edit gate; - `medscale check`; - CodeQL `analyze (python)`; - fresh substantive independent exact-head correctness/security/governance review; - reconciliation of every material finding; - zero unresolved material review threads; - active ruleset re-verification; - expected-head guarded merge using method `merge` only; - post-merge canonical-main qualification. ## Authority boundary This PR does not create or supply a Founder/operator authority artifact, model/weights custody, corpus rights, contamination evidence, runtime/GPU evidence, evaluator evidence, sandbox evidence, real Experiment-0 execution authority, or training authority. It must leave: ```text MRL_0805 = OPEN / ABSENT MRL_REAL_EXPERIMENT_READY = FALSE TRAINING_READY = FALSE TRAINING_EXECUTED = FALSE ``` No model, dataset, provider, GPU, inference, fine-tuning, SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, Unsloth, RL, preference optimization, distillation, or teacher-data generation is authorized by this PR. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a new no-training evaluation authority kind for MRL-0805 so real-preflight evidence can represent bounded evaluation programs without implying any training authority. **Key details** - The new kind `mesc.mrl.real_preflight.no_training_evaluation_authority.v1` requires `authorization_disposition = AUTHORIZED`, `authorization_scope = NO_TRAINING_EVALUATION`, `evaluation_execution_authorized = true`, `real_training_authorized = false`, and `training_prohibited = true`. - It does not invoke the training-authorization trust validator and cannot be admitted by schema parsing alone; outer MRL real-evidence trust is still mandatory. - The existing training-authorization kind is unchanged, and the production trust registry remains empty. Written for commit cb7c57258279e7deeb44e5b65b70a5dcf4600f5f. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added support for a no-training evaluation authority for MRL-0805 evidence. - Added validation for required no-training declarations, including evaluation authorization and prohibition of real training. - No-training evidence can now be accepted without training authorization, while remaining separate from training-based evidence. - **Bug Fixes** - Prevented no-training evidence from closing MRL-0805, populating the training trust registry, or authorizing Experiment-0 on its own. - Added safeguards against altered authorization fields, unexpected trust entries, and use with unrelated roles or tasks.

author: agentbridge-fixer[bot]
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1008

When viewing a tool call in the message history, the "Input" panel sometimes showed empty/missing arguments even though the correct tool clearly ran (e.g. `read_file` opening the right file). The `arguments` column in the `tool_call_events` SQL table was `null` for these entries.

## Root Cause

ACP allows a `tool_call` notification to be sent without arguments, with the real arguments arriving later in a `tool_call_update` (`status=running`). The `arguments` value was already being plumbed all the way from `SessionUpdate.ToolCallUpdate` through `ChatPanelApi.ToolCallUpdate`, but `ConversationEntryStore.updateToolCall` had no way to apply it because `EntryData.ToolCall.arguments` was declared `val` (immutable) — so late-arriving arguments were silently dropped and never persisted.

(Root cause originally diagnosed by @surgicalcoder in the issue thread — thank you!)

## Fix

- `EntryData.kt` — changed `ToolCall.arguments` from `val` to `var`
- `ConversationEntryStore.kt` — `updateToolCall` now applies `update.arguments` when present
- `ConversationExporter.kt` — captured `e.arguments` in a local `val` before passing to `escapeHtml(String)`, since Kotlin can no longer smart-cast a public mutable `var` property to non-null
- Added a regression test (`updateToolCall_capturesLateArrivingArguments`) covering the late-arrival case

## Testing

- `run_tests` — `ConversationEntryStoreTest` (all 37 tests pass, including new regression test)
- `build_project` — clean build, 0 errors/warnings

author: drdalessandro
body:
Dominio puro del PB100D: lo que la IA puede elegir, hasta dónde llega la escalera, y cómo se lee una serie de presión. El cableado con el generador va en el PR del dashboard.

## Biblioteca de acciones — Nivel 1

Las 40 acciones del Anexo C en cuatro pilares, cada una con su práctica cuantificada, su racional clínico y las señales del baseline que la habilitan.

El cambio de fondo es el reparto de responsabilidades:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Qué se le puede indicar a este perfil | `accionesDisponibles()` — determinístico, auditable. No elige: acota |
| Qué se le indica en concreto | La IA propone, el médico publica |
| Dosis / inicio / suspensión de GLP-1 | Nunca la IA |

`validarSeleccion()` es el guardarraíl que corre **antes** de tocar FHIR: rechaza códigos inventados, contraindicados, duplicados o contradictorios, y devuelve el motivo de cada rechazo para que el médico vea qué se filtró en vez de recibir un plan misteriosamente más corto.

**Seguridad modelada, no comentada.** `A03` (caminata de impacto) queda vetada por caídas recientes o densitometría alterada; `A04` (sin impacto) existe justamente para reemplazarla, y las dos nunca pueden salir juntas. Las acciones atadas al fármaco no se ofrecen sin GLP-1 activo, y la derivación a kinesiología pelviperineal sale con el flag clínico, no con la molestia auto-reportada.

## Escalera de niveles

`nivel` es el escalón clínico y vive en los recursos; `versión` queda para la PlanDefinition. En marketing la escalera puede seguir siendo V1, V2…

Los cuatro escalones están nombrados, pero **los niveles 3 y 4 tienen `puertasDeSeguridad: null` y no se habilitan**. Mandan a una mujer en menopausia a correr 21 K o a un triatlón; qué apto, qué ergometría, qué regla de piso pélvico antes de correr y cómo se tamiza RED-S son decisiones clínicas pendientes. El código bloquea en vez de suponer.

Los objetivos del nivel son *tipos*, no cifras: los kilos los fija el médico en cada `Goal`, por paciente. Hay un test que impide que se cuelen como promesa.

## MDPA

Protocolo diario: sólo a la mañana, 3 monitoreos, **se descarta el primero** y se promedian los dos siguientes. Ese promedio es el control del día.

No es un detalle del método. La primera lectura es sistemáticamente la más alta y contarla infla la serie entera: hay un test con 150/95 como primera toma todos los días que da `ok` justamente porque no la arrastra.

- El promedio de la serie es el promedio de los **controles diarios**, no de las tomas sueltas: cada día pesa igual aunque se haya medido de más.
- El descarte es **por orden**, no por posición en el array, así el resultado no depende de cómo lleguen las tomas del servidor.
- El umbral urgente (180/110) es la única regla que mira todas las tomas, incluida la descartada. Una lectura de 190/115 importa aunque haya salido primera.
- `mensajeParaPaciente()` le muestra su número contra su meta, en positivo. El escalón de alarma es para el equipo: esa noticia no se da sin un profesional al lado.

Además los 8 pasos para medir bien, en voz de paciente. Una serie mal tomada es peor que no tener serie: parece un dato y no lo es.

## Arreglo de paso

`apps/demo` seguía pidiendo `@epa/plan-bienestar-react@^0.4.0` después del bump a 0.5.0, así que `npm install` fallaba en un clone limpio de `main`.

## Verificación

84 tests (18 de biblioteca, 21 de MDPA), `tsc --noEmit` limpio y `npm run build` OK.

## A validar

- Los umbrales de aviso de MDPA son propuesta, no están confirmados.
- La regla de repetición pasó de "dos tomas ≥ 140/90" a "dos **días**": con el protocolo nuevo la medición del día es el control, no la toma individual.
- Que lo urgente cuente aunque salga en la toma descartada es criterio propio.
- La redacción de los 8 pasos sale de la preparación estándar de la AHA.

author: rockbubba
body:
## Summary

PR #2 was closed unmerged, so this reopens the same branch against `main` and adds one commit on top. The branch as a whole is the vault: a verification-first scaffold under `vault/` where Lean 4 with Mathlib is the only judge, the ledger records claims, the audit checks every claim against compiled code, and the crew runner drives models at open entries through that gate. See PR #2 for the first three commits.

## What is new in this push

Lean catches every cheat the crew can commit inside a file: a changed statement, a smuggled `axiom`, a proof leaning on `sorry`. It cannot catch the cheapest one, which happens a level up. Invent a lemma that is the target wearing a hat, mark it `open`, and the ledger shows structure while all of the difficulty sits untouched in one entry. It compiles like anything else, and nothing in the audit noticed.

- **Ledger `circularity` field.** Every entry with `toward` carries a verdict: `independent` (strictly weaker than the target it serves, with the argument written down and an `assessed_by`), `equivalent` (the target in disguise), or `unassessed` (nobody has looked). `scripts/audit.py` rejects a missing verdict, an unknown one, an `independent` or `equivalent` verdict with no argument or no signature, and a `circularity` block on an entry that serves no target. It also now rejects an entry that names itself in `toward`, and prints a one-line verdict tally.
- **The crew runner refuses non-independent entries** before round one, so no rounds are spent on a lemma nobody has checked. `--allow-circular` overrides, and the override is written into every attempt record and into the entry's `attacked_by` rather than passing silently.
- **The critic gets the same job inside the file:** a fourth check asking whether the difficulty was merely relocated into a helper lemma, a definition, or a hypothesis, since that is the failure Lean cannot flag. Both proposer and critic are now told which target the entry serves and how it was assessed, so the question is answerable. The proposer prompt also asks for helper lemmas genuinely smaller than the target.
- **The two stage-two Riemann lemmas are assessed `independent`.** Both are classical zero-free-region results (Titchmarsh ch. 2; Hadamard and de la Vallée Poussin 1896) proved without RH and used in the prime number theorem, and RH is strictly stronger than either: they deliver the open strip, RH pins `re s = 1/2` inside it.

## Verification

Run in this session:

- `scripts/audit.py --schema` passes on the ledger: 11 entries, 2 independent.
- Four negative paths checked by hand and each rejected with the right message and exit code: `toward` with no `circularity` (schema, exit 2), an `equivalent` verdict with no argument or `assessed_by` (schema, exit 2), `circularity` on an entry with no `toward` (schema, exit 2), and an `unassessed` entry stopping the runner before any build (exit 2).
- The `--allow-circular` path exercised end to end against a stubbed Lean: the gate warns instead of refusing, the brief carries the target statement and the assessment, and the verdict lands in both the attempt record and `attacked_by`.
- Two of these are now regression tests in `crew/test_crew.sh`, placed before the Lean-dependent cases because neither needs a build.

Not run here: `scripts/check.sh` and the Lean-dependent half of `crew/test_crew.sh`. This container has `elan` but no fetched Mathlib, and the prebuilt cache is roughly 5 GB. The changed code paths are all pre-Lean, and CI runs the full door.

body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

This corrects a stale claim in `docs/prerelease-quirks.md` that `ovos.session.sync` uses `SpecMessage.SESSION_SYNC` — SESSION-2 §2.7 defines no push topic for session sync, so `ovos-spec-tools` never had a spec-backed constant for that topic to lend, and the client has owned a local `LEGACY_SESSION_SYNC` string constant since #336 — and adds a `2.11.13a1 - 2.11.13a2` entry documenting the pre-spec shims the client now owns outright plus an alpha-pairing hazard, verified against the published sdists on PyPI rather than against source memory.

`ovos-spec-tools` session.py/messages.py, by release:

| spec-tools | `_store` classmethod | `SpecMessage.SESSION_SYNC` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.10.0a1 | present | present |
| 1.10.1a1 | absent | present |
| 1.10.2a1 - 1.10.8a1 | absent | present |
| 1.11.0a1 | absent | present |
| 1.11.0a2 | absent | absent |
| 1.11.1a1 | absent | absent |

`ovos-bus-client` session.py/client.py, by release:

| bus-client | calls `cls._store(...)` | references `SpecMessage.SESSION_SYNC` |
|---|---|---|
| 2.7.0a1 - 2.10.0a2 | yes | yes |
| 2.10.1a1 | yes | yes |
| 2.11.0a1 | yes | yes |
| 2.11.1a1 - 2.11.9a1 | no (fixed by #313) | yes |
| 2.11.10a1 - 2.11.13a2 | no | no (replaced by `LEGACY_SESSION_SYNC`, #336) |

Every one of the 19 releases from `2.7.0a1` through `2.11.0a1` calls `cls._store(...)` directly (not only `2.10.1a1` and `2.11.0a1`, which is what I expected going in — the wider range is what the extracted sdists actually show, confirmed by grepping `ovos_bus_client/session.py` in each one and cross-checking that no release in that span defines its own `_store`, so the call resolves onto `ovos-spec-tools`'s private method). None of those releases cap `ovos-spec-tools`'s upper bound in `pyproject.toml`, so an install that upgrades only `ovos-spec-tools` past `1.10.0a1` while keeping a `ovos-bus-client` below `2.11.1a1` raises `AttributeError: _store` on an inbound session-sync frame, before local dispatch. The supported pairing is the latest alpha of each: `ovos-bus-client>=2.11.10a1` with `ovos-spec-tools>=1.11.0a2`.

author: wshallwshall
body:
ASVS packet E: frontend, API and files. Fourteen research rows, `#1116` through `#1130` less `#1122`. Thirteen carried work; nine commits.

**Every row here stays OPEN.** All of them carry `Closing-act: scorecard-rescore`, which is an act on `docs/security/asvs-scorecard.toml` in the separate vault repository. A Builder cannot make it and did not try. Landed code plus an open row is the intended outcome.

## Three rows did not reproduce, and building two of them would have made things worse

| Row | Finding |
|---|---|
| `#1130` | Already shipped. The row's own banner reads **"SHIPPED IN #488 AT cf38e16a, AND STILL OPEN ON PURPOSE. DO NOT REBUILD IT."** `_is_contained_name` is wired at the listing-loop head, before the glob filter and before the join. Driven across nine hostile names with a three-name positive control. Nothing changed. |
| `#1129` | The permissive default is gone under `#1237`. `max_output_bytes` is keyword-only with **no default**, so `zip_decompress(b'PK')` raises `TypeError`. Restoring a default would reinstate exactly the defect that fix removed. Both limbs of the verb already hold: bytes charged as written, member cap read from the central directory before extraction. Nothing changed. |
| `#1116` | Its decisive finding is stale. The guard split shipped under PR 497. The recorded baseline of 19 passed / 3 skipped is now 22 / 3, and the three skips are only the runbook-comparison legs. A mutation control confirmed the shipped guard was already falsifiable before any edit. Four narrower holes remained and are closed. |

## What changed

**`#1126` — the tray probed the wrong protocol on the shipped default.** It keyed the engine URL's scheme on `[api].tls_cert_file`, a key a minting engine deliberately never writes. Since ADR 0172, no operator chain and no declared proxy means the engine mints and serves https, so the tray composed `http://127.0.0.1:8765` against an https listener and would render a running engine as WEDGED. ADR 0172 wrote that defect down in advance. The predicate now mirrors `ensure_api_tls_material`'s three return paths and is renamed `engine_serves_https`, because the retired name says the settings file decides and the shipped default is the case where it says nothing.

This makes the tray reach the right socket. It does **not** make the probe succeed — the minted pair is self-signed and `build_verify` never disables verification, by design. `docs/TRAY.md` now says so and names the generated file.

**`#1117`/`#1118` — a browser premise three cells stand on, measured false.** `security_headers_context`, `_security.py`, ADR 0143 and the console suite all assert that a browser rejects a `Secure` / `__Host-` cookie over http, and that sentence is the stated reason the loopback cookie stays bare. Measured against Chrome 148.0.7778.280 with a server presenting the chain `make_self_signed` mints: on `http://127.0.0.1` and again on `http://localhost`, all four probe cookies were **stored and returned**. Two vacuity controls rode in every run and both reported missing; `curl` confirmed the server emitted all four first.

Behaviour is unchanged, on two stated grounds: Firefox and Safari are unmeasured, and since ADR 0172 no `serve` posture reaches that branch, so widening it would trade a measured-inert behaviour for an unmeasured one.

`#1118`'s one open measurement is **half answered**. Four navigations to the minted https chain returned `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` with no bypass offered, and the server log recorded zero requests against two curl requests as control. No connection, so no cookie — the question fails at the antecedent. That measures one build's policy, not stock Chrome's proceed flow, so it stays open.

**`#1123` — the obvious postMessage guard would have failed closed.** Read out of the shipped VS Code bridge (1.135.0): it injects `window.parent = window` into the extension document, so `ev.source === window.parent` is **false** for a genuine host message. A source check keyed that way would silently kill every panel. The guard is a 144-bit per-render channel token, separate from the CSP nonce, which is a script-execution capability. All 33 sends stamped, all 8 receivers discarding. Falsified: two planted mutations give 5 failing / 650 passing; restored, 655 passing.

**`#1116`/`#1124` — the browser-support contract now reaches a deploying site.** `docs/BROWSER-SUPPORT.md` is derived from code, not copied from the docstring, which the item names as the disqualified move. The floor rests on **CSP nonce-source support, not `'strict-dynamic'`** — a CSP Level 2 browser ignores the keyword it does not know and matches the nonce, so scripts still run. The two cases are indistinguishable in a smoke test, which is why it is written down. Per-engine versions are published as **unresolved**: the repository pins no compatibility dataset, and an underived number is worse than a stated gap.

The false CI-guard sentence in `_security.py` is replaced with a bounded one. One hole was a self-evidence bug: `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy` satisfied the check about itself, from the sentence saying it is deliberately not set. Six planted mutations all red.

**`#1128` — archive members are admitted or refused by their own name and type.** The ingress sniff keys on the inbound's *declared* `content_type` and an archive member has no connection declaring anything; what it carries is its own name. Every discriminator is aliased onto the shipped tables so the two checks cannot drift apart. A refused member fails the whole archive rather than being skipped — dropping one member of a feed is the accept-and-drop CLAUDE.md section 12 forbids.

**`#1127` — the two pieces that need no ruling.** ADR 0123 documented all three decompressors as `max_output_bytes=None`, the opposite of shipped policy in the direction that understates the control. Corrected. The embedded-document detach ceilings are now stated in `docs/CONNECTIONS.md`.

**`#1119` — the engine was already emitting an un-notable HSTS policy on the shipped default.** This row predicted the danger for "when `#1276` lands". ADR 0172 landed it. Measured **before** any change: `create_app` driven at `scheme=https, host=127.0.0.1` returned `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` on a `/health` 200, with `ApiSettings()` reporting `tls_enabled=False`. That policy is un-notable on two independent RFC 6797 grounds, and `includeSubDomains` on one a browser *did* note would force https onto every other http service on the host.

`hsts_notable` adds an IP-literal-host test (section 8.1.1) and a minted-self-signed-chain test (section 8.4). Applied at **both** emitters — `_security_headers` is innermost and wins the `setdefault` race, so guarding only the floor would have been inert while reading as done. `host` is keyword-only and required, so no emitter can silently fall back to permissive.

Driven with both polarities in one run: four arms suppressed **while `hsts_applies` still returns `True` for every one of them**, so the old predicate would have emitted on all four; two positive controls still emit.

**`#1121` — `frame-ancestors` takes no fallback from `default-src`.** So the attachment sandbox, the strictest policy the engine writes, carried no framing decision at all. The directive is named in `_ATTACHMENT_CSP` itself, keeping that response one policy field and correct if the floor is ever removed. The floor **appends** a second CSP field where no policy already names the directive — measured, `setdefault` on a `MutableHeaders` that already carries one is a no-op, which is exactly what a prior disposition would have shipped. Tests assert the effective value per family through a helper that re-derives the parse, so the instrument can disagree with the implementation.

**`#1120` — only the clean piece.** `build_response` in the ADR 0023 listener now emits the baseline set, so a partner-derived `text/html` sync reply

## What & why

Documents the **uv/lockfile contribution convention** so contributors stop hand-editing
`uv`-exported `requirements.txt` files — the root cause of the #1757 break that produced a

author: davermaltby
body:
## The gap

`WavePlanBuilder` defaulted to `maxParallelism: 1` so validation would not need a git workspace. Reasonable in isolation; its consequence was not. The harness has exactly **two** validation rules that exist only for worktree mode, and both open with `if (plan.Config.MaxParallelism <= 1) return;`:

| code | name | why it is worktree-only |
|---|---|---|
| **GR2015** | `WorkspaceNotGitRoot` | parallel tasks need per-segment worktrees, which need a git repository |
| **GR2028** | `PlanGuardrailsMissingIntegrationReRun` | a parallel-topology wave's exit gate is a union soundness boundary; a serial run merges no parallel branches, so it has no union to certify |

**A fixture that cannot enter the mode cannot emit either.** That is how #501 shipped: GR2028 vetoed a truncated JIT prefix that the `breakdown-intent.json` manifest existed to preserve, the authored work was reverted wholesale, and fifteen `SchedulerBreakdownDurabilityTests` passed before *and* after the fix.

## The fixture

`new WavePlanBuilder(maxParallelism, gitBacked: true)` puts the plan at `<temp>/gr-wave-<id>/plan/` inside a real `git init`ed repository with a baseline commit, so the default workspace (`".."`, the plan folder's parent) resolves to a git root and **GR2015 is satisfied rather than dodged**.

A hand-made `.git` directory would also satisfy `IsInsideGitRepo` — and would be a fixture faking the very condition these rules exist for, which is #502 one level down. Hooks are redirected to an empty directory and an identity is set, so it works on a box with a global `core.hooksPath` and no git identity configured.

## The audit #502 asked for

`MaxParallelism` is read in **exactly two places** in `PlanValidator`, and they are the two rules above. GR2028 is the one that bit; it was not alone only in the sense that GR2015 shares the same blindness.

Both are now pinned in **both directions** — a fixture that silently failed to `git init` would otherwise read as "the rule does not fire in this shape" and quietly restore the blindness this change removes.

## The behavioural #501 reproduction that could not be written before

A JIT breakdown declares three folders, is cut off after two, and — because a breakdown authors task folders first and the wave's exit gate **last** — leaves a parallel-topology wave with no `guardrails/` at all. In worktree mode that is a GR2028 ERROR. It must be **excused** (it restates *the wave is unfinished*, which the manifest already told the harness) and the two authored folders must **survive**.

The control holds the other line: a session that satisfied its **own** manifest is not unfinished, so GR2028 is a real finding about a finished wave, it blocks, and the gate rejects. Without it, "excused" could quietly become "GR2028 no longer applies to waves" — the over-correction that turns the post-breakdown gate into a rubber stamp.

Both assert on `gate-decision.txt` as well as on the folders, because a fix that made the error *disappear* would satisfy the folder assertions and hide a real finding from the only person who can act on it.

## Measured

Removing GR2028 from `Scheduler.UnsatisfiableWhileIncomplete` — the pre-#501 behaviour:

| suite | result under the mutation |
|---|---|
| `WorktreeModeWavedValidationTests` (new) | **FAIL** — `01-compile was reverted` |
| `SchedulerBreakdownDurabilityTests` (15) | all **green** |
| `BreakdownSalvageAllowListTests` (policy half, #501) | FAIL — as designed; it asserts the allow-list directly |

That is #502's claim reproduced exactly: the policy half was pinned, the behavioural half was not.

`BreakdownSalvageAllowListTests`' header said this reproduction *"still needs a git-backed waved fixture that does not exist yet"*. It exists; the header now says where it lives and what the mutation measured.

Core suite: **2614 passed, 0 failed**.

Closes #502

body:
Third change for #25: the `init` interaction and the generated documents.

## What changes

- **One proposal, one answer.** `init` no longer asks to confirm the archetype and the trigger before drafting. It drafts from the evidence with `CONFIRM:` and `TODO` markers, then shows everything at once (archetype and trigger with evidence and alternatives, every marker with what resolves it, the files, the pointer line, gitignore entries, the readiness table) and writes on that single answer. Check mode presents the readiness table and all proposed edits in one message instead of one field at a time. Non-interactive behaviour is unchanged: no answer, no write (point 2 of #25).

The test-matrix template becomes the seed of the coverage table with the same columns as the release reference. The `.maintainer` README says where each kind of fact lives. The companion-file table in the schema reference (and the generated `docs/profile-reference.md`) follows (point 4).

author: jselvareef
body:
## Why I'm doing:

A 4.1.1 shared-nothing BE crashed with this stack (#78718, same signature as #68968):

```text
PC: starrocks::BinaryColumnBase<unsigned int>::append_selective
    starrocks::MemTable::insert
    starrocks::DeltaWriter::write
    starrocks::AsyncDeltaWriter::_execute
```

About 1.4 s before the signal, the same thread logged a `large memory alloc` of `4308971234` bytes from `bytes.resize()` inside that same `append_selective`, with zero query and fragment ids. The destination is a MemTable that `DeltaWriter::write` flushes as soon as one insert pushes it past `write_buffer_size` (100 MB by default), so the 4.3 GB was not accumulated across inserts: it is the sum of `src_offsets[idx + 1] - src_offsets[idx]` over the rows selected from **one** incoming load chunk, and the faulting instruction is the read of that chunk's bytes. The source column's offsets did not describe its byte buffer. A `BinaryColumn` with `uint32` offsets cannot legitimately hold 4.2 GB, and a single decreasing offset pair wraps to a row length of almost exactly that.

How the malformed column came to be is not established (no core), so this PR does not claim to fix the root cause of that incident. What it fixes is the one place on the load path where a binary column's offsets enter the process without being checked:

`LoadChannel::_deserialize_chunk` → `ProtobufChunkDeserializer::deserialize` → `ColumnArraySerde::deserialize` → `BinaryColumnSerde::deserialize` reads the byte payload and the offset array and installs the offsets as they are. It does not check that the offset payload is a whole number of offsets, that the array is non-empty, that it starts at 0, that it never decreases, or that its last element equals the byte payload size. `ProtobufChunkDeserializer` only checks the row count. Every consumer downstream (`append_selective`, `append`, `get_slice`, ...) indexes the byte buffer straight from those offsets, and the capacity guards from #77163 measure the byte size, not whether the offsets describe it. The same deserializer serves the exchange receiver, spill, the partial-update `.upt` and del files, the dictionary cache and primary key recovery, so the check covers those too. It is identical on branch-4.1, branch-4.0 and branch-3.5 (under `be/src/serde/`).

## What I'm doing:

Reject a malformed offset array in `BinaryColumnSerde::deserialize` with `Status::Corruption`, for both `BinaryColumn` and `LargeBinaryColumn` and on both the raw and the integer-encoded offset paths:

- the offset payload size must be a multiple of the offset width (checked before the buffer is read);
- there must be at least the leading offset;
- the first offset must be 0;
- the last offset must equal the byte payload size;
- the offsets must be non-decreasing (one branch-free linear pass, the only O(rows) part).

A rejected column is reset instead of being left with its bytes already resized to the payload, so the caller never sees a half-built column. The check honours `enable_dcheck_on_serde_failure` like the existing size checks in this file.

Cost: one pass over `rows + 1` offsets per deserialized string column, next to the copy of the byte payload itself. The O(1) checks alone are not enough: an inner decreasing pair with a correct last offset is exactly the case that wraps a row length to ~4 GiB.

Tests (`runtime_test`, `ColumnArraySerdeTest`):

- `binary_column_deserialize_rejects_malformed_offsets`: builds columns whose offsets decrease, overshoot or undershoot the payload, start at 1, or contain an inner offset past the payload that wraps the row length; serializes them (the serializer writes offsets verbatim) at every encode level from -1 to 7, and asserts that deserialization returns `Corruption` naming the violated property and leaves the target column empty. Covers `BinaryColumn` and `LargeBinaryColumn`, and a 101-offset case that takes the streamvbyte path. Also checks a well-formed 300-row column still round-trips at every level. On the unpatched code every one of these deserializes successfully.
- `binary_column_deserialize_rejects_empty_or_misaligned_offsets`: patches a valid serialized buffer to claim zero offset bytes, then 15 offset bytes, and asserts `Corruption`; the untouched buffer still round-trips.

Verification (x86_64, official dev image, `BUILD_TYPE=ASAN`):

```text
BUILD_TYPE=ASAN ./run-be-ut.sh --build-target runtime_test --module runtime_test --without-java-ext -j6 --gtest_filter='ColumnArraySerdeTest.*'
python3 build-support/check_be_module_boundaries.py --mode full   # OK
python3 build-support/render_be_agents.py --check                  # OK
clang-format-10 (the CI binary) on both files; git diff --check clean
```

Results are in the first comment. The incident was on aarch64; the change is plain C++ with no architecture-specific code, but it has only been exercised on x86_64.

Observability: deserialization failures on this path already surface through the `Status` returned to `LoadChannel::_deserialize_chunk` (reported to the sink as the load error, with the load id logged there) and to the exchange receiver, and the load profile's `DeserializeChunkCount`/`DeserializeChunkTime` cover the deserialization itself. The new rejection reuses that same `Status` path and the message style of the existing size checks, so no new signal is needed; the message names the violated property and the sizes involved.

Issue: #78718 (this PR is the hardening described there; the root cause of the malformed source column is still open, so the issue is not closed by this PR). Related: #68968.

## What type of PR is this:

- [x] BugFix
- [ ] Feature

Does this PR entail a change in behavior?

If yes, please specify the type of change:

A serialized string column whose offset array does not describe its byte payload is now rejected with `Corruption` at deserialization (load and exchange receivers, spill, `.upt`/del files, dictionary cache, PK recovery) instead of being accepted and consumed. Well-formed data, which is everything a correct writer produces, is unaffected; the wire and file formats are unchanged.

author: ekalinin
body:
SPEC §14 puts the OIDC callback on the per-IP failure budget because a
failing callback is the only unauthenticated route that makes the server
open an outbound connection to a third party. oidcStart makes the same
kind of connection - AuthCodeURL triggers discovery whenever the cache is
stale or empty - but never touched the limiter, so an issuer outage let
any anonymous peer draw an unbounded number of 10-second discovery
requests from the server through /oidc/start alone.

oidcStart now reserves against the same oidcLimitKey the callback uses,
failing the reservation when discovery (or building the flow) errors and
clearing it on a successful redirect to the provider - the same
Reserve/Fail/Success shape the callback already follows. A throttled
start gets the callback's neutral 429, not a detailed error.

Sharing the key means a budget spent on failed callbacks now also
refuses a fresh start, which is the point: there is no route back in by
beginning a new flow. TestOIDCCallbackChargesTheFailureBudget's last
assertion is updated to check that directly instead of driving a full
sign-in through the now-throttled start.

Closes #130

author: ajit-zer07
body:
Advances #130 and #115. Record-correction plus a new guard — no family changes bucket.

## 1. The ratchet now actually ratchets, in every CI job
New `CORE_INEXCUSABLE_FAMILIES` mirror plus two assertions:
- an **unconditional** `#[test]` (runs in the required `tests` job, no spec on disk): every mirror family is in `COVERED ∪ DEFERRED` and none is in `EXCUSED`;
- an **extension to the spec-gated guard** `no_excused_family_is_required_by_our_profile`, which `assert_eq!`s the mirror against the spec-derived required ∪ conditional set, so the mirror cannot silently rot.

**Why two halves rather than one.** Under `ACDP_REQUIRE_CONFORMANCE`, `spec_root()` panics; without it, it *skips*. So the spec-gated half alone would degrade to a **skipped test on a green PR** if the `conformance (spec fixtures)` context were ever dropped from branch protection — and that context is not fully under this repo's control (a sibling repo PUTs branch protection from a hand-maintained list). The unconditional half survives that.

**Moving a family `DEFERRED → COVERED` requires zero edits here** — the mirror is keyed to spec membership, not to which bucket currently holds a family. Verified non-hypothetically: `can`, `idem`, `pub`, `ret`, `vis` are already `COVERED` and already in the mirror, and both new tests pass against them unchanged.

## 2. A correction to the plan, caught in implementation
The plan specified the mirror as **"the sorted 13"**. The real spec-derived set is **18**. I verified this directly against the pinned spec's `registries/profiles.json`:
- required families (15): `body, can, caps, data-ref, did-ssrf, err, lin, meta, pub, rate, ret, schema, sig, status, vis`
- conditional (4): `dk, idem, rev, sig`
- **union: 18**; the plan's 13 is a strict subset, missing exactly `can, idem, pub, ret, vis`.

Those five are spec-required but **already COVERED**, so the plan's debt tally — which counted only *uncovered* debt — silently excluded them. A literal 13-family `assert_eq!` would have failed on every run of the required conformance job. Implemented as the correct 18 and measured passing.

The "13 mechanically-inexcusable families" framing stays valid for describing the **debt** (11 required + `rev`/`dk` conditional, all still `DEFERRED`) — it is just a different, narrower thing than the ratchet's 18-family spec-derived set.

## 3. Seven DEFERRED reasons corrected
Four were **factually false**, three merely overstated. The most wrong was `rate`, which claimed a missing clock/limiter seam — it is not missing: `limits.publish_rate_per_minute` (`config.rs:560-561`) is enforced by `AgentRateLimiter` (`rate_limit.rs`, wired `state.rs:87-88`) emitting 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` (`error.rs:42,61,75`), and `http_integration.rs:843-873` already demonstrates the pattern. `data-ref`, `status` and `rev` were similarly falsifiable from this repo's own source. `log`, `rcpt` and `lhr` overstated "needs a new seam" when the accurate reason is that the harness advertises only `acdp-registry-core`.

## 4. One further falsifiable reason found — flagged, NOT fixed
`did-ssrf`'s reason is likely also false: `main.rs:705-706` builds `WebResolver::new()`, and the upstream `acdp-did` `WebResolver` applies `SsrfPolicy::default()` internally. Deliberately not corrected here — unlike the other seven, the falsifying evidence lives in the SDK dependency rather than this repo's own crates, which makes it a judgement call rather than a clean correction. Raised for a separate decision.

## Verification — measured, not derived
`cargo` now runs in this environment (the long-standing EACCES constraint no longer reproduces), so these are real results, with the commands named:

```
ACDP_SPEC_DIR=<spec@d1f06d0> ACDP_REQUIRE_CONFORMANCE=1 cargo test -p acdp-registry-server \
  --features storage-sqlite,playground --test conformance --test conformance_gate -- --nocapture
  → 44 passed; 0 failed  /  1 passed; 0 failed
  → conformance: replayed 30 exchange(s); failures=0   (pub 3 / ret 1 / vis 26)

# the unconditional half, with no spec on disk:
cargo test -p acdp-registry-server --features storage-sqlite,playground --test conformance
  → 44 passed; 0 failed

cargo fmt --check → clean
```

`MIN_REPLAYED_EXCHANGES` is 30 and we replay exactly 30 — **zero headroom** — so the unchanged count is the load-bearing check here, not the pass count.

Issue-body corrections for #115/#130 are handled separately by the coordinator; re-derived citations: `EXCUSED` at `conformance.rs:7037-7070`, `no_excused_family_is_required_by_our_profile` at `:7816` (both stale in the plan by ~4,700-5,000 lines).

body:
Creating a BranchBase configuration no longer approves its commands. Initialization distinguishes detected commands from fallback suggestions, and the new revoke-trust command refuses to revoke approval while running operations or retained runs still need their Stop commands.

Tests cover initialization without approval and retained-run protection. Validation covers lint, type checking, tests, and the production build.

Part 1 of 8 in the replacement for #55. Review against the preceding branch; merge bottom to top.

1. [Require explicit approval for repository commands](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/56)
2. [Persist project names and pins with safe removal](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/57)
3. [Discover repositories and worktrees from development folders](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/58)
4. [Observe external services and process resource usage](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/59)
5. [Declare application and infrastructure app-group categories](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/60)
6. [Expose app-group operation and captured-run context](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/61)
7. [Persist command and runtime activity with observation baselines](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/62)
8. [Redesign the dashboard and unify loading and error feedback](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/63)


Validation: focused tests for this layer and combined-stack lint, type checks, tests, production build, routing integration, and packed-artifact smoke checks. Final results will be recorded on #63.

## Summary by Sourcery

Require explicit repository command approval and safely support revoking approval when no dependent operations remain.

New Features:
- Add a command to revoke repository command approvals.
- Expose initialization previews without treating fallback commands as detected commands.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent repository initialization from implicitly approving commands.
- Prevent trust revocation while setup, app-group operations, or retained runs still require repository resources.
- Refuse to overwrite malformed trust stores during approval changes.

Enhancements:
- Make trust-store updates safe for concurrent processes and atomic on disk.

Tests:
- Add coverage for explicit approval during initialization, protected trust revocation, malformed trust stores, and concurrent trust updates.

author: vsbuffalo
body:
The AS starvation instrument (#856) reports how many ancestor weights are finite. It cannot report how many the categorical can actually reach, and on a real fit those come apart by more than an order of magnitude.

## Observed, on a real run

A 400-particle, 2-chain, 60-sweep SIR PGAS fit through the release binary:

| sweep | `as_finite_frac` | `as_admissible_frac` | `as_ess_pre` | `as_ess_post` | `as_starved` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.999915 (≈400) | 0.881 (≈352) | 14.85 | **16.22** | 0 |
| 2 | 0.868 (≈347) | 0.128 (≈51) | 95.60 | 28.09 | 48 |
| 59 | 0.953 (≈381) | 0.674 (≈269) | 156.73 | 146.74 | 17 |

Sweep 0 is the case the feature exists for. On the counts alone it reads "88% admissible, healthy" — 352 candidates. The categorical was effectively drawing from **16**. And the guard *raised* the effective count while removing ~48 candidates, because what it removed was concentrating the draw. No combination of the two existing fractions can see either fact.

Sweep 2 is the opposite shape: the guard cut the effective count from 96 to 28. That distinction — the density concentrating versus the guard concentrating — points at different fixes, which is why both sides are reported rather than only the post-mask value.

## Why this discriminates

A low acceptance rate is compatible with two remedies of very different cost. If the weights are spread and acceptance is still low, the suffix ratio is what rejects and the fix is to restructure the update. If the weights pile onto one ancestor, the move is inert regardless of the ratio and the proposal itself needs improving.  gains the 2×2 with the remedy per cell.

## Numerics

`ess_from_log_weights` (`types.rs:417`) folds `max_lw` first and exponentiates `lw - max_lw`, so the statistic is offset-invariant and cannot underflow on the weight ranges a large filter visits — verified, not assumed. With at least one finite weight the max term is exactly 1, so the result is bounded in `[1, n]`, and that bound is asserted rather than trusted.

Its degenerate contract returns `0.0` when nothing is selectable, which is why `AncestorEssMean::record` **skips** such a step rather than folding a zero into the mean. `NaN` and `0.0` stay distinct end to end — a sweep with no AS step reports `NaN`, prints `NA`, serializes `null` — following the rule `as_accept_rate()` already documents.

## Units, stated in the field docs

These are effective **particle counts**; their two neighbours are fractions of `n_particles`. "ESS 3.1" is meaningless without its denominator: against `as_admissible_frac = 0.24` on 4,800 particles, 3.1 of ~1,150 is catastrophic concentration and 3.1 of 4 is unremarkable.

## Verification

`make test` exit 0, 3193 passed / 0 failed. Counters only, no RNG consumed — asserted rather than assumed: `csmc_exact_invariance` (4 passed) and `gate_pgas_thread_invariance` both green, so trajectories are bit-identical.

Five mutation checks, each reverted after. The load-bearing one is `the_guard_can_lower_the_count_and_raise_the_ess`, which asserts the *comparison* — count falls while ESS rises — not merely the two values. Recording `as_ess_pre` after the mask reddens it with pre == post. Folding unmeasured steps in, using a mean instead of a median, and pushing `NaN` sweeps as zero each redden their own test.

No golden, no `ir/VERSION`, no stored-artifact identity.

## One operational note for anyone resuming a run

`TraceWriter::new` skips the header when appending, so a run *started* on an older binary and *resumed* on this one appends rows two fields wider than its header. Start fresh rather than resuming across the upgrade. Pre-existing for every column addition, not new here.

author: jamescrowley321
body:
The Acceptance Auditor emitted **false MUST FIX findings on four production PRs**, blocking each one. The other five lenses passed every time.

| PR | Claim | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| healthcloud-console-web#52 | 4 ACs failed — "no workflow files in the PR" | Prompt-instruction PR; the CI work was a separate tracked issue |
| #56 | "the actual CI workflow files are not part of the pull request" | Same category error |
| #58 | "requires Chromium, Firefox and WebKit" | The config declares exactly one project, `chromium` |
| #58 | "the code changes are entirely absent" | Present in two files in the diff |

On re-review it wrote *"as noted in previous reviews"* — citing its own earlier false claim as evidence.

## Root cause

`shared-instructions.md` already forbids exactly this:

> **Not blockable — NITPICK or omit.** A concern resting on code you cannot see: … **a file not in the diff** …

`acceptance.md` structurally overrode it. It forced every AC into PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL and mapped `FAIL → MUST FIX` unconditionally. With no verdict meaning *"I could not see it"*, a lens that fails to locate an implementation **must** classify FAIL, and FAIL **must** block. The persona was obeying its instructions.

## The fix

- **`UNVERIFIED` verdict → `NITPICK`** — the missing escape hatch
- **`FAIL` requires positive evidence** — name the file it belongs in, and that file must be in the diff you fetched
- **Defers explicitly to the shared Grounding block**, which outranks the mapping
- **Judge the PR in front of you, not the work its body describes** — covers the #52/#56 category error
- Strictness preserved: "unforgiving **about what you can see**"

## Measured, not asserted

Same fixtures, old lens vs new:

| Fixture | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| absent claim, clean 20-line diff | **1/3** correct | **3/3** |
| absent claim, buried in 2,400 lines of lockfile noise | **1/5** correct | **5/5** |
| invented requirement | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| non-implementation PR | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **deleted auth guard (positive control)** | **3/3 blocks** | **3/3 blocks** |

**Diff volume is the trigger.** On a clean diff the old lens misfires occasionally; bury the same change under lockfile churn — exactly PR #58's shape, 5,855 insertions of which ~5,620 were `package-lock.json` — and it misfires **4 times in 5**. That is why this only ever surfaced on large PRs.

The control matters as much as the fixes: it proves the fix works by grounding the lens, not by defanging it.

## `evals/`

- **Layer 1** — offline, deterministic, no key, runs in `lint.yml` on every PR. Validates the JSON envelope. Its cases are recorded production failures: Sentinel emitting `lens: "Security Auditor"`, Edge Case Hunter returning prose.
- **Layer 2** — samples a persona against fixture PRs, asserts only on *whether it blocks*, never on prose. Skips cleanly without `pi`.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` now asks that a lens prompt change arrive with a fixture, written first and seen to fail.

*Caveat worth stating: my first eval run reported 4/4 failures on both lens versions. That was my validator rejecting markdown fences before it ever looked at the verdict — not a real result. Layer 2 now strips a wrapping fence, since envelope hygiene is Layer 1's job against recorded output.*

---

Requested and accountable: @jamescrowley321. Human review required before merge.

Headerless requests from tagged Tailscale devices previously inherited localhost owner privileges. Validation: real HTTP identity matrix across all platforms and Linux modes, capability privacy/rotation tests, dashboard (39), push (19), notification (27), and portable contracts; syntax checks. Hosted CI runs the full suite, appliance smoke and browser matrix. Local full-suite baseline limitations include the host's old Git and system Python.

author: rem3000
body:
---

## Basic Info

| Info | Please fill out this column |
| ------ | ----------- |
| Ticket(s) this addresses   | #5581. This is the issue discussing the hardware limitations of mecanum wheels, and the maintainer mentioned that contributions of a new critic are welcome. |
| Primary OS tested on | I am developing on Ubuntu 22.04, with builds and tests in a ROS rolling container (Ubuntu 24.04). |
| Robotic platform tested on | A mecanum robot, simulated in both Gazebo Classic and Isaac Sim within a 40 cm corridor maze. |
| Does this PR contain AI generated software? | Yes, the files are marked accordingly. |
| Was this PR description generated by AI software? | No. |

---

## Description of contribution in a few bullet points

I was testing Nav2 on last year's competition environment with the mecanum robot and noticed that diagonal motion in reality causes noticeable wheel slip and poor path tracking. I asked the AI to add a new critic named AxisAlignCritic for holonomic platforms. Its function is to penalize vx and vy commanded at the same time, essentially discouraging diagonal motion. This has no effect on non-holonomic motion models.

Reasoning: When a mecanum robot performs 45° diagonal motion, only two wheels drive, which in real-world navigation leads to wheel slip. In contrast, pure forward motion or pure lateral motion engages all four wheels, reducing slips.

The cost is based on the ratio of the minor to the major body-axis velocity, ranging from 0 to 1, and is independent of speed, so it does not slow the robot down. Like other critics, it is disabled within `threshold_to_consider` of the goal.

## Description of documentation updates required from your changes

- A companion PR to docs.nav2.org adds the parameter section and a migration guide entry: ros-navigation/docs.nav2.org#966
- The README parameter table has also been updated.

## Description of how this change was tested

- Unit tests were drafted with AI assistance, reviewed and executed by me, located in critics_tests.cpp, and built in the rolling container. All 26 critics_tests passed, and lint checks are clean.
- Gazebo experiments: 4 parallel runs per setting. With a weight of 4.0, the share of commanded diagonal motion decreased from 45% to 30–32%, and the lap time improved from 14.3 seconds to 13.4–13.6 seconds (each set validated over 3–4 runs). Clearance remained the same or slightly better: 3.0 cm without the critic, 3.6–4.1 cm with the critic enabled.
- Note: Recovery behaviors appeared starting at weight 6.0 (3 recoveries in one run). In-place rotation increased to 23% only at 8.0 or above. The README recommends a weight of 2–4.

---

## Future work that may be required in bullet points

- Haven't yet measured improvements in wheel slip on the physical robot. I plan to perform real-world tests within two weeks and update the results. Current tests are only with one simulated robot in a single maze.

This is my first contribution—feedback is welcome!

#### For Maintainers: <!-- DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE -->
- [ ] Check that any new parameters added are updated in docs.nav2.org
- [ ] Check that any significant change is added to the migration guide
- [ ] Check that any new features **OR** changes to existing behaviors are reflected in the tuning guide
- [ ] Check that any new functions have Doxygen added
- [ ] Check that any new features have test coverage
- [ ] Check that any new plugins is added to the plugins page
- [ ] If BT Node, Additionally: add to BT's XML index of nodes for groot, BT package's readme table, and BT library lists
- [ ] Should this be backported to current distributions? If so, tag with `backport-*`.
