- (divergence) The vendor's documented mutation contract carries the verification the guard goes looking for elsewhere. Linear's SDK documentation states that 'Mutations will often return a success boolean and the mutated entity'; the engine's UPDATE_ISSUE_MUTATION (real-linear-api.ts:427-431) selects ONLY `success`, and updateIssue discards everything else. Because the mutated entity is never requested, the store can verify a state flip only through a SEPARATE getIssue — which is precisely the read exposed to the read-replica lag this row's 4x500ms window exists to absorb. Selecting `issue { state { name } }` on the mutation payload would let the write's own response confirm the write. The departure is uncommented at the point of departure (no note at the mutation document or at updateIssue explaining why the entity is not selected). Fair counterweight, which is why this is reported and not flagged: the founding KW-F2 incident was a mutation that reported success:true while the state never moved, so a payload-carried entity from that same write path might lie in the same way a success flag did — the separate read is arguably the stronger check. ## Changes
Editing a wall length previously moved only that wall, separating joined corners and losing detected rooms. Numeric resizing now keeps either endpoint fixed, moves joined wall endpoints together, and rejects changes that would collapse a neighbor. Openings keep their relative positions and room metadata is preserved.

Wall and opening dimension fields preserve fractional values, ignore invalid drafts, and avoid changing geometry when rounded imperial values merely receive focus. Desktop properties now occupy sidebar space so the layer list stays clickable.

Closes #45.

- 281 unit tests pass, including 25 connected resizing and dimension validation cases.
- Svelte check: zero errors; production build passes.
- All 10 browser workflows pass on the final commit, including new 1440px and 390px coverage of connected rooms, undo/redo, invalid input, imperial length/height/thickness precision, export/reload, and 3D rendering.

- Interactive production-build browser checks passed on desktop and phone layouts, including pointer layer selection, both fixed endpoints, invalid drafts, exact metric heights after visiting imperial fields, and mobile 3D. No browser errors.

See docs/reviews/2026-09-06-connected-wall-dimensions.md for scope and remaining limitations.

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
`beta` held 1 commit(s) `development` did not — release version bumps committed onto the branch the release ran from, and anything else that arrived out of band. Left unreconciled, both branches change the version file independently and the next `development` → `beta` promotion conflicts on it.

**0 file(s) change.** A 0-file result is the normal and correct outcome once the content has already reached `development` by other means — recording the ancestry *is* the payload. Without it the merge base never moves and the next promotion conflicts exactly as before.

Version files were resolved to `development`'s side, whose line is ahead of the released one, so this never moves a version backwards. Any conflict outside them aborts the merge for a human instead.

Opened by fleet-back-merge.yml, using the algorithm `release.yml` already applies to its own `sync/*-to-development` pull requests.

body: YAMLを書けない人 (UXライター・運用担当) が、チームの禁止ワードを足せるようにします。`docs/custom-rules-and-autofix.md` のフェーズ3です。 ``` dead-cliche ui [--port 7777] [--file .deadcliche/custom-rules.yml] # dead-cliche ui: http://127.0.0.1:7777/?token=... ``` ## 何を通し、何を通さないか 辞書への書き込みはコード実行に近い権限なので、Issueが挙げた3条件 (loopbackバインド・CSRFトークン・surface限定) に加えて、実際に破られる経路を塞いであります。 | 守り | 実装 | | --- | --- | | 外から届かない | `127.0.0.1` にだけ束ねる | | 別名からの到達を拒む | Hostヘッダを検査 (DNSリバインディング対策) | | 他のページからの操作を拒む | 起動時に作る合言葉をGET・POSTの両方で要求 (バイト長を揃えて定数時間比較)、Originが別サイトなら拒否 | | 実行に近い入力を受けない | 受け取るのは `surface` (リテラル) だけ。`pattern` も `id` も入力から取らない | | 書き込み先を限る | カスタム辞書ファイルのみ。`rules/` (共有辞書) を指すと起動時に止める | | 構造破壊を起こさない | 保存は `js-yaml` の `dump`。フォーム入力を文字列連結でYAML化しない | | 情報を外に出さない | CSP `default-src 'none'`、`frame-ancestors 'none'`、`referrer-policy: no-referrer` | 追加した規則がその場の例をどう判定するかを検査し、悪い例が検出されない・良い例や検出しない例を誤検出する場合は警告として画面に返します (辞書に入れるのは止めません。判断は書き手のもの)。 削除は確認ページを挟みます。ページ内でJSを動かさない (CSPで禁じている) ため、`confirm()` ではなく画面で確かめる形です。 ## セルフレビューで直したもの `/code-review high` を通し、出た9件をすべて再現→修正しました。要求の処理に例外の受けが無く、3つの入力経路がプロセスの停止になっていた点が主でした。 - 同じ文字数の多バイト文字を合言葉に渡すと `timingSafeEqual` が例外を投げ、サーバーが落ちた (外部ページの `` から誘発可能) - `Origin: null` や壊れたOriginで `new URL` が投げていた - 辞書ファイルのYAMLが壊れていると、ページを開いた時点で落ちた - ポート使用中に生のスタックトレースが出ていた。`--port` の値も未検証だった - 削除の `confirm()` が自分のCSPで動かず、確認なしで消えていた - 64KB超の投稿で、接続を切ってから返そうとしていたため413が返らなかった - 入力不備の再表示で `severity` の選択だけが `error` に戻っていた - 配列でないYAMLを空として扱い、次の保存で中身を消していた - 保存のたびに先頭コメントを書き換えていた (手書きのコメントが消えた) ## 確認したこと - `npm test` 581件パス。新規12件は、合言葉なし・別名Host・別サイトOrigin・pattern混入・確認なしの削除・壊れた辞書・多バイト合言葉・壊れたOrigin をそれぞれ固定しています - 実サーバーでの手動確認: 追加 → `.deadclicherc.json` 経由で `dead-cliche check` が検出 → 削除 → 検出0件の往復、ポート検証、使用中ポート、上限超えの投稿、手書きコメントの保存 - 自己検査0件、`npm run check:plugin` 通過、`npm pack` に `src/ui.mjs` が入ることを確認 Closes #5 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGyEBeYggLNgWrRtjKJnfN --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGyEBeYggLNgWrRtjKJnfN)_ ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **新機能** - `ui` コマンドを追加し、ブラウザ上のフォームからプロジェクト固有の禁止ワード辞書を編集できるようになりました。 - ローカル接続、トークン認証、入力検証に対応し、禁止ワードはリテラルとして登録されます。 - 追加・削除や保存先を指定できるオプションを提供します。 - **ドキュメント** - 利用方法、保存先、セキュリティ上の制約、運用方法を追加・更新しました。 - **テスト** - author: ziad-amr1
body:
## Sidebar footer — state-specific layout + real user identity + DD Mon YYYY dates

### 1. Sidebar footer

**Before:** Both states shared one identical flex-row structure; the expanded status text block was hidden (not removed) during collapse, causing a visible jump in footer height.

**After (state-specific):**

| State | Width | Footer height | Layout | Contents |
|-------|-------|---------------|--------|----------|
| Expanded | 288px | 60px | row · justify-between | Status tile + label/subtext ("API Connected" / "E-commerce API") — collapse button at end |
| Collapsed | 80px | 60px | column · justify-center | Status icon above expand icon (both `icon-xs` / 24 px, vertically stacked in the 60 px rail) |

* Constant `h-[60px]` on both states — **no layout jump** during transition.
* `useApiAvailability` hook and PR #39 logic untouched; `apiLabel` key restored.
* Both buttons carry tooltips/aria-labels; collapsed status icon is clickable (`check()`).

---

### 2. Header user identity

**Before:** Account pill showed hardcoded "Admin" text regardless of authenticated user.

**After:** Header resolves the real user identity at render:

```js
getUserIdentity(user)
// priority: fullName → firstName + lastName → name → username → email
```

* If `user.avatar` is a valid URL → **image** fills the 24 px avatar circle.
* Otherwise → **first letter** of the resolved identity.
* Identity text truncates (`max-w-36`) with a `title` tooltip for long values (e.g. emails).
* No `firstName`/`lastName`/`fullName` fields were observed in the current API contract (`/auth/me`); the resolver is ready for them but will likely use `username` or `email` as the primary field in practice.

---

### 3. Dashboard date format

**Before:** `new Date(createdAt).toLocaleDateString(i18n.language)` → locale-specific numeric date (e.g. `9/3/2026`).

**After:** New `formatDisplayDate` utility renders `DD Mon YYYY` (e.g. `03 Aug 2026`) using three-letter English month abbreviations.

* Returns `null` for `null`/invalid/`undefined` → caller renders `—` (em dash).
* Wraps the output in Unicode **LRI/PDI** bidi isolates so the Latin date is readable when the surrounding document is RTL.
* Local-time semantics unchanged from the previous `toLocaleDateString` behavior.
* API contracts and `<input type="date">` controls not touched.

---

### Limitations noted

* **Name resolution:** The auth API contract observed in this codebase provides `username` and `email`; no `firstName`/`lastName`/`fullName` were found. `getUserIdentity` will prefer name fields if present (future-proof) but will currently show `username` or `email`. If a richer identity field is added to the API, the header updates automatically.
* **API status state in probe:** The probe environment resolved to "API Unavailable" because the remote Vercel API was unreachable; "Online" and "Checking" states were verified structurally (aria-label wired from the same config object).

---

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `npm run lint` | ✅ clean |
| `npm run build` | ✅ clean |
| `git diff --check` | ✅ clean |
| Expanded footer (288 px / light + dark) | Row, justify-between, status tile + "API Online"/"E-commerce API", collapse button, h=60 px |
| Collapsed footer (80 px / light + dark) | Column, justify-center, status icon above expand icon, h=60 px, no jump |
| Header: email user, no avatar | `D` initial + `dev@store.io`, no "Admin" label |
| Header: username user + avatar | `img` avatar + `ziad.ahmed`, no "Admin" label |
| Dates (light / dark / collapsed / rtl) | `03 Aug 2026` with LRI/PDI present; missing `→` em dash; zero `→` `$0.00` |

**Do not merge automatically.**

body:
Add a durable project catalog independent of runtime ownership and command approval. Projects retain names and pinned app references across restarts; the projects API preserves per-project errors, and removal keeps files on disk while rejecting retained runs, pending lifecycle work, and managed processes.

Validation: lint, type checking, build, and 9 focused tests passed, including persistence, invalid metadata, and removal guards.

Part 2 of 8 in the replacement for #55. Review against the preceding branch; merge bottom to top.

1. [Require explicit approval for repository commands](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/56)
2. [Persist project names and pins with safe removal](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/57)
3. [Discover repositories and worktrees from development folders](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/58)
4. [Observe external services and process resource usage](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/59)
5. [Declare application and infrastructure app-group categories](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/60)
6. [Expose app-group operation and captured-run context](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/61)
7. [Persist command and runtime activity with observation baselines](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/62)
8. [Redesign the dashboard and unify loading and error feedback](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/63)


Validation: focused tests for this layer and combined-stack lint, type checks, tests, production build, routing integration, and packed-artifact smoke checks. Final results will be recorded on #63.

## Summary by Sourcery

Persist project metadata independently from runtime state and enforce safe project removal while preserving API error context.

New Features:
- Persist project names and pinned app references in a durable catalog across restarts.
- Expose saved project overviews through the projects API, including per-project workspace errors.
- Add commands for saving and removing projects without deleting project files.

Bug Fixes:
- Preserve invalid project catalog files and return a stable API error for catalog failures.
- Prevent project removal when retained runs, pending lifecycle work, or managed processes still belong to the project.
- Support removing saved projects through repository and worktree path aliases.

Enhancements:
- Separate project metadata from runtime ownership and command authorization.
- Validate project metadata, pins, and catalog records with explicit schemas.

Tests:
- Add coverage for catalog persistence, metadata validation, unavailable configurations, alias removal, removal guards, and projects API error handling.

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- Several docs examples fail as written on 1.4.2 and canary. The ESM bytecode example passes a top-level `outfile` to `Bun.build`, which is not a `BuildConfig` key. It is ignored, the `index` to folder-name fallback runs, and the build fails with `failed to rename ... ENOTEMPTY`.
- `docs/test/runtime-behavior.mdx` documents `bun test --hot` and `bun test --frozen-lockfile`. The test runner only re-runs under `--watch` (`test_command.rs:2653`), and `--frozen-lockfile` is an install-family flag. Both run once and exit 0 with no signal.
- `docs/runtime/sql.mdx` lists `PGUSERNAME` with fallbacks `USER`, `USERNAME`. The adapter reads `PG_USER || PGUSER || USER` (`src/js/internal/sql/shared.ts:1956`). Two guides call `blob.stream(1024)` to set a chunk size, which neither type-checks (`TS2554`) nor changes the chunk size. Three guides read `.name` off `JSON5.parse` / `YAML.parse` / `XML.parse`, which return `unknown` / `XML.Document` (`TS2339`).

### Fix
- Move `outfile` under `compile: { outfile }`, the form `docs/bundler/executables.mdx` already uses. Swap the loader map example to `text` / `file` (see Notes on `dataurl`).
- Drop the `--hot` and `--frozen-lockfile` lines. List the auto-install flags the runtime reads (`--prefer-offline`, `--install=fallback`, `--no-install`).
- Fix the Postgres table to `PGUSER` and add the `PG_*` aliases. Replace `blob.stream(1024)` with manual chunking. Cast the `parse()` results to the expected shape.
- Verified: each changed TS block type-checks with tsc 6.0.2 and `packages/bun-types`, and runs with the stated output. `prettier --check` passes on the touched files.

### Background
- `Bun.build` reads `outfile` only inside the `compile` object (`src/runtime/api/JSBundler.rs:405`). `bun-types` declares it only on `CompileBuildOptions`.
- `bun test` shares the runtime argument table, so `--hot` parses. The test command installs a `HotReloader` but only enters the watch loop for `HotReload::Watch`.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- `dataurl` / `base64` loaders: accepted by the CLI, `Bun.build`, and bunfig, but `ParseTask.rs` returns an empty-string lazy export for them (`var a_default = "";`). #36327 implements them and adds `"dataurl"` to the `Loader` union. Until that lands the docs example should not use them, so this PR swaps the example rather than touching types.
- `Loader` union gaps (`json5`, `md`, and others) are covered by #38267 and #38247.
- `Blob.prototype.stream(n)`: `Blob.rs` still parses the argument and `ByteBlobLoader` records it, but `materializeNativeSource` takes `max(chunkSize, 256 KiB)`, so any value below 256 KiB has no effect. `bun-types` removed the parameter in #7670. The guides now match the types.
- `JSON5.parse` / `YAML.parse` returning `unknown` is deliberate (#22129, #26439). The guides cast instead of loosening the types.
- Unknown CLI flags are not rejected by design (they pass through to scripts), so the `--frozen-lockfile` line gave no error.

</details>

author: 50thycal
body:
# Implementation Handoff

## Goal

> After this change, `theta4-fat-tail` and `mmsell-scheduled-settle-live` can be retired — by closing the two live deployment rows that currently make `STAND_DOWN` refuse them.

## Implemented

A new repair package, `dark-live-canary-repair`, registered in the transport's package registry. Running it (via `REPAIR_LINEAGE`) sets `ended_at` on `theta4-live-1` and `lmmsell-live-1`. Nothing else.

**Merging this changes nothing in production.** A package is inert until an operator names it in an envelope. This PR only makes the repair *available* to be run.

## Architecture / Flow

The problem is a circular dependency in the lifecycle rules:

```text
retire the experiment
  → _stand_down refuses: "holds N open LIVE deployment(s)"   (experiment_commands.py)
      → so close the live deployment first
          → close_epoch does that, but _stand_down only reaches it
            AFTER the open-live check passes                  (service.py:983)
          → no other verb in the vocabulary ends a live deployment
              (REGISTER_PACKAGE, REPAIR_LINEAGE, CLOSE_OUT_RETROSPECTIVE,
               ARM_CANARY, RETIRE_ON_GATE_FAIL, STAND_DOWN)
      → and RETIRE_ON_GATE_FAIL cannot substitute: it requires a recorded
        FAIL, and both keep gates read BLOCKED_DATA
```

`REPAIR_LINEAGE` is the correct verb by the registry's own definition — a repair "authors no contract, moves no lifecycle state and touches no gate." This does exactly that and no more. Retiring stays a separate `STAND_DOWN` an operator attests to.

## Major Areas Changed

- `kalshi_bot/experiment_os/repair_dark_live_canaries.py` — new. Targets named as module literals (`TARGETS`), so an envelope cannot point the repair at a different book; the transport names the package, the package names the rows.
- `kalshi_bot/experiment_os/experiment_commands.py` — registry entry + import.
- `tests/test_experiment_os_dark_live_canary_repair.py` — new. Ten tests, weighted toward the refusals.

## Design Decisions

- **Preconditions are checked, not assumed.** The entire justification is that these books are genuinely stopped, so that claim is verified two independent ways: the runtime allowlist must not arm either tag (matched by *prefix*, mirroring `config.py`), and no `live_orders` row may exist after the reviewed cutoff. Config is current but says nothing about what already traded; history is measured but says nothing about what is armed right now. Either check failing means a book resumed and its open record is *correct*, so the repair refuses.
- **The allowlist is read through `get_settings()`**, the cached accessor the worker uses — not a fresh `Settings()`. See Tests for why that distinction turned out to matter.
- **`experiment_key` names only the first target**, with a comment saying so. It is read solely by the close-out path, which this package does not have; the repair covers both experiments via `TARGETS`.
- **Only the LIVE deployments are ended.** The twins are left alone deliberately — the subsequent `STAND_DOWN` → RETIRED calls `close_epoch`, which ends every remaining deployment in the epoch at one instant.
- **Idempotent**, so a second run reports `already_repaired` rather than moving an `ended_at` a first run set.

## Spec Deviations

None.

## Tests / Validation

- `pytest tests/test_experiment_os_dark_live_canary_repair.py -q` — **10 passed**. New. Both halves of the stopped-book claim (runtime allowlist, order history), the shape checks (not LIVE_CANARY, closed epoch, unregistered experiment, wrong deployment kind), idempotency, and the happy path.
- `pytest tests/test_experiment_os_experiment_commands.py -q` — **28 passed** (registry invariants — the suite that would catch a malformed registration).
- `pytest tests/ -k "experiment_os or session_system or config" -q` — **860 passed, 1 skipped**.
- `ruff check kalshi_bot/experiment_os/ tests/test_experiment_os_dark_live_canary_repair.py` — clean.

**Writing the tests found a real defect, which is the argument for having written them.** The repair originally built a fresh `Settings()` to read the allowlist. That re-validates every required field, so on any environment without API keys and a database URL it refused with *"could not read the runtime allowlist"* — for a reason having nothing to do with the allowlist. It fails safe, but for the wrong reason, and it would have done so anywhere the full config isn't present. Fixed to use `get_settings()`.

- Not covered: the repair has still never run against production rows. That is what `REPAIR_LINEAGE` is for, and its refusals are now exercised.

## Known Risks / Limitations

- **No real-money exposure.** This authorises nothing and can arm nothing. It also cannot *stop* anything — the books were already stopped through `LIVE_STRATEGIES`, the audited runtime path. It only makes the record agree with the runtime.
- **No evidence is lost.** `close_epoch`'s own docstring is explicit that metric scopes resolve tags across every deployment in an epoch, ended or not; only the enforcement resolver reads `ended_at`. The 628 live orders behind these books stay exactly as readable.
- **The cutoff constant is a snapshot.** `LAST_LIVE_ORDER` was measured 2026-09-06. If these books resume before the repair runs, the check catches it and refuses — the intended failure mode, but it means the package goes stale rather than silently misapplying.
- No shared semantics touched; no Platform Revision required.

## Recommended Review Focus

- **Whether ending a live deployment row belongs in `REPAIR_LINEAGE` at all.** I read the registry's definition as permitting it ("fixes deployment rows an engine defect left inconsistent") and the `tmmsell-epoch-repair` precedent does end a deployment. But the inconsistency here was caused by an operator emptying `LIVE_STRATEGIES`, not strictly by an engine defect, and that distinction is worth a second opinion. This is now the main open question on the PR.
- The prefix-matching logic in `_assert_runtime_is_stopped` — it must match `config.py`'s semantics, since getting it wrong in the permissive direction would let the repair close a genuinely live book. There is a test pinning it; check the test asserts the right thing.
- The fixture sets `state = "LIVE_CANARY"` directly rather than transitioning. That mirrors how the real targets got there (grandfathered legacy imports) and avoids `PAPER → LIVE_CANARY`, which demands an operator approval *and* the PASS gate result that justified it. Reasonable, but it does mean the tests don't exercise a natively-promoted experiment.

## Follow-up Work

- Running it, then the two `STAND_DOWN` → RETIRED commands, is a **separate act needing `LIVE_OPS` or `TASK_SPECIFIC`** — `REPAIR_LINEAGE` excludes `RESEARCH_LAB` by design.
- XOS-000025 / XOS-000026 (the paper/live gate-addressing defect) become moot if both experiments retire, since a retired experiment's gates are never evaluated again. Fixing the addressing properly would need a successor Version, which under NEW_ONLY means arming fresh live canaries — not worth it for books that are done.
- XOS-000012 should record what this actually costs: not "config drift mislabelled", but "a book stopped via the runtime allowlist cannot afterwards be retired in the record."

## Owner Summary

Two live books stopped trading on 19 August when their runtime allowlist was cleared, but Experiment OS still lists them as armed, and that mismatch makes them impossible to retire — the safety check that refuses to retire an armed live book can't tell the difference between "armed" and "recorded as armed". This adds a small, reviewed repair that closes those two records so they can then be retired normally. It doesn't run on merge, doesn't touch real money, and doesn't retire anything by itself; it refuses outright if either book turns out to have resumed trading, and those refusals are now covered by tests — writing which turned up a real bug in how it read the config

author: holgerimbery
body:
## Bug

App registrations created via `az ad app create` don't get the default delegated **"User.Read" (Sign in and read user profile)** Microsoft Graph permission that the Azure Portal's app registration wizard normally adds automatically. This didn't matter for the backend service's app-only Graph calls (Mail.Read/Mail.Send), but breaks any **interactive** sign-in against the app - specifically, creating/testing a connection for the custom connector in the Power Platform maker portal, which performs a delegated AAD OAuth login using this same app registration as its OAuth client (`apiProperties.template.json`).

Without `User.Read`, Azure AD rejects the sign-in with:

```
AADSTS90008: The user or administrator has not consented to use the application
with ID '...'. This happened because application is misconfigured: it must
require access to Microsoft Graph by specifying at least 'Sign in and read
user profile' permission.
```

## Fix

- Add a new `-GraphDelegatedPermissions` parameter (default: `User.Read`), resolved dynamically from the Graph service principal's `oauth2PermissionScopes` (mirroring the existing `appRoles` resolution used for application permissions).
- Request it alongside the application permissions via the same `az ad app permission add` call (as a `=Scope` entry instead of `=Role`), and verify it landed via the same `requiredResourceAccess` check used for application permissions.

## Docs update

Live-testing the connector sign-in also surfaced a second, related requirement that wasn't documented anywhere: the connector's Azure AD "Security" tab requires a **redirect URI** registered on the app registration. Since `apiProperties.template.json` uses `redirectMode: GlobalPerConnector`, this reply URL is unique per connector and only exists once the connector itself has been created, so it can't be set up front. Missing it fails sign-in with `AADSTS500113: No reply address is registered for the application`.

Added a "Required" callout with exact steps/commands for both this and the `User.Read` permission, right after the connector's Security/Authentication configuration section, in both `custom-connector/README.md` and `docs/wiki/phase-1-mailbox-setup.md`.

## Testing

- Syntax-validated `create-app-registration.ps1` with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile`.
- Manually applied the same fix (`az ad app permission add ... =Scope` for `User.Read`) to a live tenant and confirmed sign-in succeeded once combined with the redirect URI fix.

author: alexsudakov
ekalinin
body:
`ANYGRADE_OIDC_LOGIN_CLAIM=email` was a documented switch that refused
everyone. internal/oidc extracts the claim and demands `email_verified`
correctly, but oidcAccount then gated the raw value on ident.ValidLogin,
whose rule (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`) no address can satisfy: the whole
`email` branch ended in the neutral "no account" page and a server-log
warning, with nothing an operator could do about it.

The claim now names an account by the local part of the address. The
domain is not compared, and that is what bounds where the option is safe:
with an issuer that serves a single domain the course owns, the address
is one the issuer verified and hands out itself, so the local part is as
trustworthy as `preferred_username` from the same issuer. Against a
public multi-tenant provider it is not - anyone who can register
`<login>@<the provider's domain>` would be matched to that login - so
§8, §11 and the README now say the option is for a single-domain issuer
and never for a public one. Deriving the login in web rather than in
internal/oidc keeps the protocol package free of anygrade's login rules;
it only reports which claim it filled Identity.Login from.

The derived value still goes through ValidLogin unchanged, so an address
whose local part cannot be a login is refused exactly as before and
nothing unbounded reaches the store or the audit log. The split is at the
last "@", so a value carrying more than one keeps it and is refused
rather than silently cut short. The address as it arrived stays in the
operator log, which is the one place it is safe. Any other claim keeps
the old rule: the value itself must be a valid login, so an email-shaped
`preferred_username` still matches nothing.

Closes #131

author: sahlanridwanofficial-oss
body:
## ⚠️ Apply `0006` before merging and deploying

Run `supabase/migrations/0006_product_inventory.sql` in the Supabase SQL Editor first — the app reads new columns and RPCs from it, and morning cart allocation now goes through `save_morning_allocation`. Safe to re-run.

## What this adds

A real inventory feature: **sealed ready-to-sell cups tracked per product at the base**. The existing "Stok Gerobak" menu is daily *cart allocation and reconciliation*, not central stock — there was no notion of how many cups exist to allocate, so a cart could be loaded with stock that was never produced. Now central stock is the source, and loading a cart draws it down.

## Server (migration 0006)

- `products` gains `stock_quantity` and `low_stock_threshold` (both ≥ 0).
- `stock_movements` records **every** change — restock, opname, allocation, allocation_return, adjustment — with the signed delta, resulting balance, actor and an optional reference to the allocation. Admin-read RLS; writes only through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
- `adjust_product_stock` (relative, for restock/correction) and `set_product_stock` (absolute, for stock-take) — admin-only, row-locked, refuse to go negative.
- **`save_morning_allocation`** replaces the client-side upsert loop: header, items and the central-stock movement in **one transaction**, computing the delta against the existing allocation so:
  - re-saving the same numbers moves no stock (idempotent),
  - raising the load consumes only the difference,
  - lowering it returns cups to stock.
  It refuses when central stock is short (naming the product) or the day is already reconciled.
- `admin_stock_overview` (per product: stock, today's allocated, ok/low/out) and `admin_low_stock_count` for the dashboard badge.

## UI

- **New "Inventori Stok" admin page**: per-product cards with stock, low/out badges, search and status filter, a **restock** and a **stock-opname** action (opname previews the difference), and a per-product **movement history**.
- **Morning cart allocation** now calls `save_morning_allocation`, so loading a cart draws down central stock and a shortfall is reported clearly ("Stok pusat tidak cukup untuk …"). Each allocation card shows the product's central stock.
- **Dashboard** shows a low/out-of-stock banner linking to the stock page.

## Scope note

Unsold cups returned at night reconciliation are **not** auto-added back to central stock in this version — return them via "Tambah Stok" if they're resealed. Called out in the migration header so it's a deliberate boundary, not an oversight.

## Verification

Ten behavioural tests (`supabase/tests/07_inventory.sql`):

| # | Asserted | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | restock | stock up, movement logged |
| 2 | load cart | central stock down 100→70/50→30 |
| 3 | re-save same numbers | stock unchanged (idempotent) |
| 4 | raise load 30→40 | stock −10 only |
| 5 | lower load 40→25 | stock +15, `allocation_return` logged |
| 6 | load beyond stock | `INSUFFICIENT_STOCK:Jus Alpukat` |
| 7 | opname to absolute | set + diff recorded |
| 8 | overview status | out / low classified correctly |
| 9 | dashboard count | out & low counted |
| 10 | driver attempts | denied restock, load, overview, history |

All seven suites pass from a clean database with the six migrations applied; 0006 is safe to re-run. `tsc`, `next lint` and `next build` clean (19/19 pages — the new page).

## Note on CI

The `Typecheck, lint, build` check is expected to stay red until the repository's GitHub Actions condition is resolved. Unrelated to this diff; detail in #2.

body:
Prepara o rename do repositório (`rouanet` → `incentivabr`).

O `backend/Dockerfile` fazia um clone sparse de `github.com/incentivaBR/rouanet.git` só para buscar `frontend/assets`, que estava excluída do upload pelo `.railwayignore` por ter 173 MB. Depois da centralização a pasta tem 856 kB. Este PR:

- remove o bloco `apk add git && git clone …` do `backend/Dockerfile`; o `COPY frontend/ /frontend/` já traz as imagens;

author: franciscomoretti
body:
Users can register development folders and discover Git projects without creating .branchbase.json. Scanning canonicalizes linked worktrees, respects manual exclusions, preserves renamed projects, and reports unavailable folders. Worktree and Codex inspection no longer require an initialized BranchBase configuration.

Scanning is bounded by depth, directory/repository counts, and refresh frequency; dependency directories and symlinks are skipped. This layer provides repository/worktree observation; process inspection is introduced in the next PR.

Validation: lint, type checking, build, and 13 focused tests passed, covering scan limits, linked worktree deduplication, exclusions, persistence, and configuration without command approval.

Part 3 of 8 in the replacement for #55. Review against the preceding branch; merge bottom to top.

1. [Require explicit approval for repository commands](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/56)
2. [Persist project names and pins with safe removal](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/57)
3. [Discover repositories and worktrees from development folders](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/58)
4. [Observe external services and process resource usage](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/59)
5. [Declare application and infrastructure app-group categories](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/60)
6. [Expose app-group operation and captured-run context](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/61)
7. [Persist command and runtime activity with observation baselines](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/62)
8. [Redesign the dashboard and unify loading and error feedback](https://github.com/FranciscoMoretti/BranchBase/pull/63)


Known follow-up: #65 moves cold discovery and Git inspection off dashboard request paths. This PR retains bounded synchronous scanning.


Validation: focused tests for this layer and combined-stack lint, type checks, tests, production build, routing integration, and packed-artifact smoke checks. Final results will be recorded on #63.

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable bounded discovery of repositories and worktrees from registered development folders while preserving user-managed project state.

New Features:
- Add development-folder registration and bounded repository discovery without requiring BranchBase configuration files.
- Expose repository observations, linked worktrees, development-folder status, and discovery-related command and HTTP APIs.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent discovered repositories from being duplicated through linked worktrees or symlinked folder aliases.
- Preserve manually removed projects and existing project metadata during subsequent scans.
- Report unavailable or unreadable folders and scan-limit conditions with actionable warnings.

Enhancements:
- Allow worktree and Codex inspection for observed repositories independently of initialized BranchBase configuration.
- Persist watched folders and excluded repository paths with backward-compatible defaults.

Tests:
- Add focused coverage for bounded scanning, exclusions, symlinks, linked worktree deduplication, persistence, unavailable folders, and configuration-independent observation.

author: apmantza
body:
## Summary

`resources_discover` (#205) resolves `<packageRoot>/skills` and registers
whatever it finds. When that walk lands somewhere with no `skills/` beside
it — the installed package is missing `skills/`, or the entry file was
copied out of the package tree by a managed extension cache so the nearest
`package.json` is the cache's own — the result is `SKILLS (0)`,
`EXTENSION ERRORS: []`, empty stderr. Completely silent (investigated on
#2587, whose latest comment pins the exact failure condition).

`clients/skills-resolver.ts` now backs the handler. **Updated in fix round
2** (see that section below for the full account): `resolveSkillPaths`
returns `[skillsDir]` **unconditionally** — exactly like the pre-fix
handler, since pi's own loader already treats a nonexistent path as zero
skills gracefully — and, purely as an observational side effect, records ONE
bounded `skills-dir-missing` degradation (`incrementDegradationCount`) and a
notify when `skillsDir` is absent, unreadable, or holds no skill pi's real
loader (`loadSkillsFromDirInternal`, verified against the extracted
`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1` tarball) would find. The
directory-read side is fail-closed and distinguishes `ENOENT` from `EACCES`;
neither is ever thrown out of the handler.

**Scope, per the issue's three acceptance boxes:**
- [x] Layout F (entry relocated) yields a visible degradation record with the
  resolved path — red-first against the pre-fix handler.
- [x] Standard layouts (skills/ beside package.json) produce no record.
- [ ] The release-qa `skills-registered` row asserting source + path — this
  is **#2619's** box, not this PR's. Refs #2619, not closed here.

This PR is `refs #2626`, not `closes`, because the third box is owned by an
already-in-flight PR (#2619).

Filed a follow-up from the class sweep below: #2636.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature (net-new capability)
- [ ] Enhancement (improvement to existing capability)
- [ ] Documentation

## Area

- [x] area:observability
- [ ] area:lsp
- [ ] area:dispatch
- [ ] area:installer
- [ ] area:diagnostics
- [ ] area:read-guard
- [ ] area:project-intelligence
- [ ] area:perf
- [ ] area:session
- [ ] area:config
- [ ] area:security
- [ ] area:tests

## Checklist

- [x] I have read CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md
- [x] The change has tests (happy path, edge cases, regression test for bugs)
- [x] Targeted test files for the touched seams pass locally after `npm run build`; the full suite is CI's job.
- [x] Every NEW regression test is proven RED on pre-fix code; the red output is quoted in this PR
- [x] Every new guard/branch/filter is mutation-proof: deleting or neutering it reds at least one test
- [x] PR title carries the conventional prefix and the issue ref
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run build:dist` succeeds (changed `index.ts` and `clients/`)
- [x] `package-lock.json` is in sync with `package.json` (no dependency changes made; reverted the unrelated `npm install` `libc` metadata churn)
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` is updated — not needed: no new convention/invariant, this follows the existing `incrementDegradationCount`/`recordDegradationOnce` + `notifyUserDegradation` seam other modules (e.g. `clients/tree-sitter-shared.ts`, `clients/config-warn.ts`) already use
- [x] `.changelog/fix-2626-skills-dir-missing-degradation.md` — Fixed section, validated with `node scripts/check-changelog-fragments.mjs`
- [x] Commit subject includes the issue number: `(refs #2626)`

## Tests

- **NEW `tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts`** (4 cases) — drives
  `resolveSkillPaths` directly, the exact function `index.ts`'s handler now
  calls (`skillPaths: resolveSkillPaths(import.meta.url)` verbatim), with
  synthetic `file://` URLs over real temp directories (real
  `fs.existsSync`/`readdirSync`, no mocked filesystem):
  - *layout F* (entry under `<cache>/npm/ext/pi-lens.js`, nearest
    `package.json` at `<cache>/npm`, no `skills/` there) — records the
    degradation and the notify. Regression proof for the issue's bug.
  - *standard layout* (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` beside `package.json`) —
    resolves, records nothing. The negative control.
  - *`skills/` exists but holds no `SKILL.md`* — records the degradation.
    Regression proof for the issue's third acceptance-adjacent case.
  - *only-once* — three calls with the same layout produce ONE ledger entry
    and ONE notify, proving `recordDegradationOnce`'s dedup and the
    `alreadyRecorded` notify-gate both work.
- **EDITED `tests/index-wiring.test.ts`** — the pre-existing "resolves
  skillPaths to an existing skills/ directory" test (which drives the REAL
  `resources_discover` handler via `pi.emit`, this repo's own on-disk
  layout) now also asserts NO `skills-dir-missing` degradation is recorded —
  the full-integration negative control, added `resetDegradationLedger()`
  for isolation.

Which of AGENTS.md's ten test-authoring screens: *invisible skip* (the bug
this PR fixes IS an invisible skip — zero skills, zero signal) and *ambient-
inspection double* screened against directly — see the shape-38 note below.

### Shape 38 (cheapest evasion) — does the fixture reach the handler?

`getPackageRoot` (`clients/package-root.ts`) memoizes its walk in a
module-level `Map` keyed by the exact `importMetaUrl` string. Reusing the
same synthetic URL across scenarios with different on-disk layouts would
silently read back an earlier scenario's cached root instead of re-walking —
the fixture would never reach the code under test a second time. Every
scenario in `skills-resolver.test.ts` uses `fs.mkdtempSync` for its OWN
unique temp dir (documented in the test file's header comment), guaranteeing
a real cache miss every time.

### Red-first proof (pre-fix behavior)

Reverted `clients/skills-resolver.ts`'s body to the OLD handler's exact
logic (unconditional `[path.join(packageRoot, "skills")]`, no check, no
record) via a saved patch, rebuilt, ran the new suite:

```
 FAIL  tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts > resolveSkillPaths (#2626) > layout F: entry copied out of the package (nearest package.json has no skills/) records the degradation
AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []
- []
+ [ "/tmp/pilens-skills-test-Y3OCS8/skills" ]
 ❯ tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts:83:18

 FAIL  tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts > resolveSkillPaths (#2626) > skills/ exists but holds no SKILL.md records the degradation
AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []
 ❯ tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts:123:18

 FAIL  tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts > resolveSkillPaths (#2626) > records the degradation only once per subject (recordDegradationOnce)
AssertionError: expected undefined to be 1 // Object.is equality
 ❯ tests/clients/skills-resolver.test.ts:140:43

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  3 failed | 1 passed (4)
```

Restored the fix afterward (`git diff` against the committed fix was empty,
confirmed byte-identical restore); the standard-layout test (the negative
control) passed on BOTH pre-fix and post-fix code, as expected.

### Mutation proofs (every new guard neutered, each reds)

1. Main check bypass (`if (hasSkillFile(skillsDir))` → `if (true)`):
   3 of 4 tests red — same failures as the red-first proof above.
2. `hasSkillFile`'s one-level-down directory check
   (`entry.isDirectory() && …` → `false && …`): the *standard layout* test
   reds —
   ```
   FAIL  … standard layout: skills/ beside package.json resolves and records nothing
   AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
   ```
   (also proves that test is a real guard, not vacuous).
3. Notify-once gate (`if (!alreadyRecorded)` → `if (true)`): the *only-once*
   test reds —
   ```
   FAIL  … records the degradation only once per subject (recordDegradationOnce)
   AssertionError: expected [ {…}, {…}, {…} ] to have a length of 1 but got 3
   ```
4. Fail-closed `readdirSync` catch removed (let it throw instead of
   returning `false`): 2 tests e

author: pedropaulovc
body:
Split out of #9368 at @H4vC's request; independent of the async-progress stack.

`filterChildShellEnv(env, cwd)` always consulted omp's own pre-dotenv launch snapshot, even when the caller passed an explicit env. For a caller-built env that is the wrong provenance: the dotenv mode came from omp's launch `NODE_ENV` instead of the supplied env's, and names present in omp's launch env were treated as launcher-owned. Inside a bun-test worker (`NODE_ENV=test`) filtering an isolated env against a cwd with `.env.development.local` looked for `.env.test.local` and leaked the mode-local value into the child.

Now launch provenance applies only when `env` is the live `process.env`/`Bun.env` (the object Bun's dotenv loading actually mutated). Any other env resolves its mode from its own `NODE_ENV` and uses the weak-provenance path, exactly as on platforms without `/proc/self/environ`. Filtering the real process env is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

`packages/utils/test/env.test.ts` "uses the supplied mode for an isolated environment and cwd" spawns a `NODE_ENV=test` bun subprocess and asserts the `.env.development.local` marker is dropped for an explicit env; it fails against the previous implementation.

`bun test packages/utils/test/env.test.ts` → 19 pass; `bun run check` in `packages/utils` clean.
</details>

## Summary by Sourcery

Observe externally started services and process resource usage across projects and worktrees while keeping discovery read-only and bounded.

- Detect independently started macOS listeners and associate them with repository worktrees without taking ownership of their lifecycle.

body:
## Summary

Prep job `eIruxfiBhYTFHgfXKWK5` (LinkedIn, run `pubsub-21701378631273457`) resolved a TechCrunch screenshot for the post, staged it to a signed URL, and wrote `Media: <url>` into the DRAFTS.md — and the asset at review showed no picture (`imageUrl: null`). The X/LinkedIn materializers never read the deliverable's `media` block that agent-engine RFC-12 added.

**Fix** (`materialize.ts`): `materializeXPost` / `materializeLinkedInPost` re-host `deliverable.media.url` the same way a carousel slide is re-hosted (the signed URL expires in 7 days and points at a bucket we do not control), into:
- the asset's `imageUrl` (the card's cover), and

author: withoutboat
body:
### Motivation

When traffic is routed in bypass of `awg0` to the physical network interface (`wlo1`), the packets had 100% loss due to two issues:
1. **Reverse Path Filtering**: NixOS firewall enforces strict reverse-path filtering (`rpfilter`). Inbound replies arriving on `wlo1` were dropped because the main routing table default route points to `awg0` for unmarked packets. Stopping `firewall` confirmed immediate 0% packet loss and 42ms ping directly via Wi-Fi.
2. **Source IP Masquerade**: Locally generated packets bound to sockets before `output` hook marking, so packets sent via `wlo1` needed source NAT (masquerade) to carry the physical interface IP.

### Changes

- Sets `networking.firewall.checkReversePath = lib.mkDefault "loose";` when `services.amneziawg.enable` is true.
- Adds `chain postrouting { type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept; }` with `meta mark 51820 masquerade` to `table inet awg_bypass`.

author: ekalinin
body:
Every `user` subcommand took `--data-dir` relative to the cwd
(`fs.String("data-dir", ".anygrade", ...)`), while `serve`, `check` and
`export` all resolved it against the git toplevel of the cwd first. Since
store.Open creates the directory and runs migrations on first use, running
`user add` or `user list` from anywhere but the exact repo root silently
grew a fresh, empty database next to the cwd instead of reaching the
course's real one - `user add` printed a token the running server would
never accept, and `user list` reported an empty roster with exit 0.

Factored the resolution export.go, serve.go and check.go each had a copy
of into one shared helper, courseDirs, and gave every user subcommand a
--repo flag and the same default. Unlike the other three, which have
always tolerated running outside a git repository by falling back to the
cwd itself, courseDirs takes a requireRepo flag: user passes true, so
resolving neither --repo nor a git toplevel (and no --data-dir either) is
a clear error instead of a silent guess. An explicit --data-dir keeps
working from anywhere, exactly as before.

Closes #132

body:
Closes #13

Work-Item: #13

## What each finding class got

**`githubactions:S8544`, dependencies installed without locked resolved versions.** The three `uv run` steps no longer install anything at all: one step installs, and it carries `--locked`, which refuses a stale lockfile instead of resolving fresh versions. Measured in the worktree: under `--no-sync`, `uv run --locked` does not check the lockfile at all (a `uv run --locked --no-sync` against a deliberately stale `pyproject.toml` ran without complaint), so putting `--locked` on those steps would have been a flag with no effect. **`githubactions:S8541`, a source build can run setup scripts.** The install step carries `--no-build`, so no dependency may arrive as a source distribution whose build script runs third-party code on the runner. `--no-build` alone is not enough here, as #13 predicted and as re-measured in this worktree: `uv sync --locked --no-build` fails with `Distribution hopin==0.1.0 @ editable+. can't be installed because it is marked as --no-build but has no binary distribution`. author: mnaza
body:
## What

`transport/h1.rs::get()` took the first status line on the wire as **the** response. Interim (1xx) responses precede the final one on the same connection — `100 Continue`, and `103 Early Hints`, which Cloudflare and Fastly send for any page with preload hints — so on the h1 fallback path against such an origin the caller got:

- `status: 103` with the hint headers instead of the real ones, and
- since a 103 block carries no `Content-Length`/`Transfer-Encoding`, the *read-to-close* fallback swallowed the real 200 response as an unframed body — on a keep-alive connection that's a hang until the 30 s `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` first, then the wrong answer.

RFC 9110 §15.2: "a client MUST be able to parse one or more 1xx responses received prior to a final response".

## Fix

The header-block read becomes a loop: parse a block, and if the status is 1xx, discard it and keep going (the block is advisory and has no body). Two guardrails:

- **`MAX_INTERIM = 8`**: a server streaming 1xx blocks forever hits a counter, not the response timeout (same spirit as the MAX_LINE caps from #144).
- **101 is refused outright** — this client never sends `Upgrade`, and the bytes following a legitimate 101 are not HTTP/1.1, so skipping it would misparse the stream.

Also hoists the test module's read-only stream adapter (`RO`) out of the one test that previously owned it so the new tests reuse it — no behavior change there.

## Testing

- `interim_responses_are_skipped`: a 103 + 100 + 200 sequence on one stream — fails on master with `left: 103, right: 200`, passes with the fix; also asserts the *final* response's headers are the ones returned.
- `endless_interim_responses_are_refused`: 50 back-to-back 103 blocks — errors with "more than 8 interim responses" instead of consuming them all.
- Full `cargo test --lib` (913 tests), `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` all clean.

author: fx-dove
body:
## Summary
Fixes correctness bugs in character/environment locking and job resume that could skip locking or leave the UI/stream in a bad state.

### High
- **Resume skipped locking on partial/empty stubs**: `startJobPipeline` used `.some()` on `characterLocks` / `environmentLocks`, so one real path (or a legacy string prompt) skipped locking for everyone else. Now `locksCompleteForPlan` requires **every** director-plan character and environment to have a **real on-disk** `referenceImagePath` (`existsSync`). Empty stubs (`referenceImagePath: null`) no longer count (regression guard for the prior empty-stub bug).
- **Locking advanced with missing images**: `processLockStep` could save null-path stubs and still `triggerNextStep` into segments. It now **fails the job** when any plan entity lacks an on-disk image (valid files are reused on resume).

### Medium
- **Env lock failures dropped silently**: character failures got text stubs; env failures got nothing. Env failures now persist text-only stubs (`referenceImagePath: null`) so resume can retry.
- **Thumbnail wiped after upload**: thumbnail was written under `temp/.../assembly/` then `deleteTempFiles` removed it while `thumbnailPath` still pointed there; `/stream` thumbnail 404'd. Thumbnail now lands in `outputs/<jobId>/thumbnail.jpg` next to `final.mp4`.
- **Render with zero localized scenes**: download failures could call `assembleVideo` with an empty list. Rendering now fails closed.
- **JobDetail mis-reported lock state**: UI treated any truthy `referenceImagePath` as locked even when `hasReferenceImage` was false. Also always showed “Detailed Prompt Lock Active” with no lock. Fixed to trust `hasReferenceImage` and show pending / text-only states.
- **getJobDetail disk discover key mismatch**: auto-discovered `john_doe_reference.jpg` keys did not merge onto plan names (`John Doe`). Merge by sanitized name before setting `hasReferenceImage`.

### Low
- Regenerate lock endpoints now prefer `job.animationStyle` (same as the worker) over `job.input?.style`.

### Reference images required?
Not required at job create (T2I + World DNA still allowed). Once locking runs, **on-disk lock sheets are required** to advance — uploaded photos are preferred when present.

### Smoke
`node backend/scripts/smokeLocksComplete.mjs` covers empty stubs / partial / stale path / complete cases.

## Test plan
- [ ] Upload character reference photo in Film Studio → create short job → confirm locking uses I2I and JobDetail shows green image lock + Preview works
- [ ] Job with cast but **no** uploaded refs → locking T2I succeeds → UI shows text-to-image lock, not “pending”
- [ ] Force a partial lock (kill worker mid-locking or stub one char with null path) → Resume → must re-enter **locking**, not jump to segments; completed locks reused
- [ ] Resume after empty stubs only → locking, not segment_generation
- [ ] Complete short job → `/api/jobs/:id/stream` and thumbnail stream both work after upload (temp cleaned)
- [ ] Run `node backend/scripts/smokeLocksComplete.mjs`

author: bdchatham
body:
One line: `version.json`, `v0.13.0` → `v0.14.0`.

## Why minor

A no-verdict run changes what it publishes. It published nothing; it now writes a check run to `--check-out` concluding `failure` under the title `no verdict`, carrying the reason and no `counts` key.

A consumer that gates on the check sees a new outcome where it saw an absent one. A repository requiring the check moves from "Expected — waiting for status to be reported" to a held merge — the same held merge, reported rather than implied. `ai-review.yml` forces `failure` on unreadable output for the same reason.

`failure` cannot say "could not read the change" versus "the change is bad". The `no verdict` title and the summary carry that, and the title is also the discriminator a caller should switch on: a decided review carrying blockers concludes `failure` too.

The summary names why there is no verdict. A run that produced no reply at all — a deadline, a transport fault, a failed turn, a bad config, a defect in the driver, a cancellation — says which one, rather than blaming a reply that never arrived.

## Contents

- #405 — write the no-verdict check run the caller publishes.

gofmt -s -l .            clean
go vet ./...             clean
go test -count=1 ./...   all four packages ok

author: lesnik512
body:
`context7.json` excludes a `planning/` directory that no longer exists. This repo migrated off the `planning/` convention over five PRs, and the exclusion has been a dead entry since — it was left behind because it sat outside that migration's recipe, so removing it is an independent call rather than migration fallout. Part of the cleanup around modern-python/.github#67.

## Why drop the key rather than leave an empty list

Checked against Context7's published schema (https://context7.com/schema/context7.json) rather than assumed:

- the schema declares no root `required` array, so every property is optional;
- `excludeFolders` carries `"default": []` and no `minItems`.

An absent key and `[]` are therefore equivalent to Context7. Absent is what the repos that never carried the line already look like (`eof-fixer`, `faststream-concurrent-aiokafka`), so dropping it converges the org on one shape.

## Non-goals

No other exclusion is touched — this repo excluded only `planning`, so there is no partial-list edit. Indexing behaviour is unchanged, since the excluded path does not exist.

`docs/context7.json`, the second Context7 config in this repo, is deliberately untouched: it carries only `url` and `public_key` and never had an `excludeFolders` key.

## Verification

- `git ls-tree -d origin/main planning` returns nothing: the directory is genuinely absent at `main`, not merely absent from the working tree.
- `just lint-ci` clean.

author: gomesalexandre
body:
`ChiselSession::load`/`latest` returned whatever the deserialized JSON's `id` field said, instead of the id actually used to locate the file. A hand-edited or corrupted cache file with a missing/null/mismatched `id` deserializes fine, and `ChiselDispatcher::load_session` then panics on `self.session.id.as_ref().unwrap()` once the load completes (`crates/chisel/src/dispatcher.rs:356`).

Same fix shape as the two prior session-id bugs in this module (autosave id reuse after a deletion/rename, and path-traversal via an unvalidated id) - trust the file's real identity (the requested id for `!load <id>`, the resolved file name for `!load latest`), not the blob's own self-description.

Also hardened the print site itself (`self.session.id.as_deref().unwrap_or("<unknown>")`) as defense in depth, in case a future caller resolves an id-less session some other way.

## Changes

- `ChiselSession::load`/`load_from`: normalize `session.id` to the requested id after deserializing, ignoring the file's embedded value.
- `ChiselSession::latest`/`latest_from`: derive `session.id` from the resolved cache file name (`chisel-<id>.json`) via a new `session_id_from_cache_file_name` helper.
- `ChiselDispatcher::load_session`: no longer panics if a loaded session somehow still has no id.
- Tests reproduce the panic against the old code (verified locally: both new tests fail on unpatched code, pass on the fix) using the same `_in(cache_dir)` tempdir-testable pattern already used for `next_cached_session_in`.

## Testing

```
cargo test -p chisel --lib
```
29 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p chisel --lib --tests` and `cargo fmt -p chisel -- --check` clean (no new warnings on touched files).

AI assistance: Codex performed a follow-up review and shortened comments.

author: muscles4817
body:
The last thing doc 18 §2.5 says that the engine disagreed with. The crowd model already concentrated attention on whoever the room came for; the **consequence** model still paid a challenger for pinning a star in a three-way exactly as if they had beaten them one on one.

§2.5 makes what look like two claims — a multi-man title match *"lets a champion lose the match without losing cleanly"* and *"lets a challenger win without beating the champion"*, and it is *"a poor place to elevate somebody"*. They are one fact seen from both ends: **with three in the ring, pinning somebody does not establish that you can beat them.** They were fighting two people, and one of them was probably lying on the floor at the time.

## The discount

`HeatEconomy.Conclusiveness(sideCount)` discounts the status swing by 0.65 per side beyond the second — a three-way says about two-thirds of what a singles match says, a four-way under half. A 55 beating a 92 in a four-star match:

```
                     singles   three-way
challenger gains      +2.95      +1.92
star loses            −0.28      −0.18
```

**Both ends discounted by exactly the same 65%**, and that is the design rather than a convenience. Protection is the point *and* the cost: a booker who could take the protection without paying for it in elevation would have a free lunch, and §2.5's whole argument is that there is not one. A test asserts the two ratios are equal, so the halves cannot drift apart.

**Kept separate from `FinishWeight`.** That describes *how* the match ended — a roll-up, a run-in — and this describes *how many ways it could have*. Independent facts that multiply independently: a clean pin in a three-way pays 1.92 against a singles roll-up's 1.47, so it still says more. Collapsing them into one enum would have made those indistinguishable.

Trios are unaffected, being two sides — §2.5 is explicit that they are not a multi-man match.

## The hookup was the untested half, again

Four mutations, and the one that survived the first pass was `ShowSimulator` always passing `sideCount: 2`. Every test in the new class called `HeatEconomy.ForMatch` directly, so the rule was covered and **nothing checked that anything called it**. Same gap A3's first review round found four of, and the third distinct flavour of one underlying error the design record now carries: testing the rule but not its wiring, testing a mechanism through the thing it feeds, and measuring the wrong quantity entirely.

The fix runs a real three-way through a real show. That needed a correction of its own — recomputing the candidates *after* the show had moved the wrestlers' overness put the answer between the two and looked like a half-applied discount, because both the upset gap and the ceiling damping read current overness. From pristine copies it is exact: **1.192 received against 1.192 predicted for a three-way, 1.834 for a singles.**

**569 tests passing.**

author: mlieberman85
body:
Closes #804.

## ⚠️ Read this first: intentionally incomplete

**Eight of 39 tasks are not done, and cannot be, without a live signing identity.** They are labelled `🔑` in `specs/778-keyless-cdx-sidecar/tasks.md` and deliberately **not stubbed** — a stubbed keyless test passes while proving nothing.

Unverified here: **FR-004** (it verifies with `cosign`), **FR-005** (tampering is detected), **FR-007/SC-008** (two formats in one run), **FR-014** (the three keyless tests retargeted). Everything else is done and green.

This split is why m777 deferred the work rather than guessing. Merging this lands the routing, the reference, and the docs; the remainder is a bounded follow-up for whoever can authenticate — not a blocker.

## Why not an in-document signature

A Sigstore bundle has three parts. Two map onto JSON Signature Format cleanly; one has nowhere to go.

| Bundle part | JSF slot | Fits? |
|---|---|---|
| signature bytes | `value` | yes |
| ephemeral cert chain | `certificatePath` | yes — exactly its purpose |
| Rekor inclusion proof | — | **nothing** |

JSF's `signer` definition admits exactly six properties and no extension point.

That gap isn't cosmetic. Fulcio certificates live ~10 minutes, and the tlog entry's timestamp is what establishes the signature was made while its certificate was valid. Embedding would produce a schema-valid signature with a ten-minute useful life, or one requiring the verifier to skip that check. Relocating the bundle to the root slot would be worse still — the schema *does* validate there.

So the signature travels beside the document, exactly as SPDX already does, and `cosign verify-blob` works against it with tooling operators already have.

## What changed

**Routing is most of it.** The sidecar signer was already byte-generic and the path helper already target-generic — only the signer's SPDX-specific *name* said otherwise, so it's renamed. A stale name is precisely what produced m777's false *"waybill never emits signed BOMs"* comment.

Keyless CycloneDX now joins the branch that writes a document then signs **the bytes it wrote**. Deliberately *not* canonicalized: that's the in-document signer's contract, living in the same file, and reaching for it by analogy would force every verifier to reproduce the transformation first.

**The document records where its signature lives** — a document-level `attestation` external reference naming the sidecar by bare filename, no directory component, so it resolves wherever the pair is stored. No checksum: circular, since the sidecar signs the document that would contain its hash.

## A guard the spec didn't ask for

Implementation surfaced a sequencing problem the plan missed. The reference must name the sidecar *before* signing, but the sidecar path was derived from the *post*-signing payload — circular.

`SigningMode::sidecar_suffix()` makes the name knowable from the mode, plus a cross-check that errors if the predicted suffix ever diverges from the produced one. Without it, a future change to that mapping ships an already-signed document pointing at a file that doesn't exist — undetectable downstream.

## Verification

```
cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets   → 0 errors
cargo +stable test --workspace --no-fail-fast    → exit 0
  296 suites, 296 ok, 0 FAILED
  5564 passed; 0 failed; 14 ignored
  0 golden files changed
```

Routing is provable without an identity, via the diagnostic itself:

```
before:  Error: --sign (Sigstore keyless) cannot currently produce a conformant…
after:   Error: signing failed for cyclonedx-json sidecar: … OIDC token acquisition failed
```

It now fails at *signing* rather than argument validation, and says **sidecar** — so it took the detached branch. Fail-close held; no file left behind.

More was pulled into the identity-free half than the plan assumed: the injection helper is a pure function, so the bare-filename rule and the no-checksum invariant became unit tests, and the schema question — a document-level `attestation` reference is new here — was answered by injecting it into a real emitted document and validating.

Unchanged and covered: static-key CycloneDX (signature stays in-document, no sidecar, no reference), SPDX signing both modes, unsigned byte-identity. The in-document signer keeps refusing keyless; this routes *around* that guard rather than removing it.

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**T028 reversed.** The task said remove the SUPERSEDED banner on the three keyless tests. Its premise doesn't survive contact: those tests assert *embedding*, which still doesn't happen — only the reason changed, from "refused" to "emitted elsewhere". Updated instead.

**No parity-catalog row**, on stronger grounds than "not gate-forced": the parity harness scans unsigned, so its fixtures structurally cannot contain the reference — and `CdxOnly` is inert in the gate (`let _ = (&spdx23_set, &spdx3_set);`). A row would document a mapping the gate can't check for a field its inputs never contain.

## Finding that escapes this milestone

`Directionality::CdxOnly`'s doc comment in `parity/extractors/common.rs` states the check *"asserts only that the CDX side is non-empty."* **It asserts nothing.** That predates m778 and means existing `CdxOnly` rows — C42 among them — are weaker than documented. Recorded in the plan; probably deserves its own issue rather than riding along here.

Spec Kit artifacts: `specs/778-keyless-cdx-sidecar/` — 18 FRs, 10 SCs, 39 tasks.

author: masra91
body:
Closes #4292 (follow-up to #4460, which threaded the resolver into model discovery but kept the precedence inverted).

## What was still wrong

#4292's first acceptance criterion asks that the harness sign-in preflight obtain the token **through the credential resolver — "the same path stage execution uses"** — with the ambient-env read kept only as an explicit, documented fallback. Both config-time probes shipped the opposite order: ambient first, resolver only if no ambient var was set.

That is not a stylistic preference. **Stage execution never reads the ambient environment for this at all**: `procenv`'s allowlist is default-deny and carries neither `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` nor `GH_TOKEN` nor `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`internal/procenv/procenv.go`), so a run authenticates with the resolver's credential and nothing else. Ambient-first therefore had two consequences:

1. **Preflight validated an account the run would never use.** Green against account A, every stage running as account B — the #3341 wrong-account failure, entered from the other side.
2. **The double delivery could not be undone.** While the duplicate pod env var was present it won, so the resolver's credential never took effect; the operator got no signal that removing it was safe. Hence the three places the production instance documents *"DELIVERED TWICE, DELIBERATELY — do not 'clean up' the duplication."*

## Change

Both probes now share one helper, `copilotModelToken`:

- **configured `agent:model` credential** when the instance declares a grant — `ModelCredential != nil` means exactly that, since `cmd/goobers.agentModelCredentialResolver` returns `nil` when no grant is configured;
- **ambient environment** otherwise. A laptop instance with no grant and `GH_TOKEN` in a shell profile is unchanged.

A resolution error still fails the caller outright rather than degrading into whatever login the CLI has cached.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **Sign-in preflight obtains the token through the credential resolver, ambient kept as documented fallback.** Both the preflight probe and admission-time discovery, via one helper whose doc comment states the reasoning.
- [x] **`instance.schema.json` declares any remaining env requirement / `goobers validate` warns.** *Conditional — not triggered.* No env requirement remains for this harness: a file-ref-only `credentials:` entry now satisfies discovery, preflight, and stage execution alike. `grep -rn "os.Getenv" internal/harness/*.go` (non-test) returns exactly one hit: the documented fallback.
- [x] **A test proves a file-ref-only `credentials:` entry satisfies the Copilot preflight.** `TestCopilotPreflightSatisfiedByFileRefOnlyCredential` (cmd/goobers) joins a real `instance.Config` file ref through `agentModelCredentialResolver` into a real `CopilotAdapter.Preflight` with all three ambient vars unset — the composition the issue reports as broken, which neither package could prove alone.
- [x] **`make ci` green** — pending CI here.

## Behavior change worth flagging in review

The two precedence tests are **inverted**, not deleted: `...ModelCredentialWinsOverAmbientEnv` (preflight and discovery) replace `...AmbientEnvWinsOverModelCredential`, with the reasoning recorded in each doc comment. The only configurations affected are those that set **both** an `agent:model` grant and an ambient token — i.e. exactly the double-delivery deployments, which now take the resolver's credential and can drop the duplicate.

`docs/guides/github-token-scopes.md` drops the `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN="$GOOBERS_COPILOT_TOKEN"` instruction and the "a `token.file` reference alone is insufficient for daemon startup" paragraph, and says plainly that the duplication should now be removed.

## Adjacent gap found, deliberately not fixed here

`ClaudeAdapter.Preflight` builds its probe env from `baseEnv` alone and consults no resolver, so a file-ref-only `agent:model` on `claude-code` is invisible to its sign-in probe too — it can only reflect the CLI's own stored login. That is the same class of hole but a different harness and outside #4292's evidence and scope; happy to file it separately.

`docs/PLAN.md` stated the endpoint gap **twice**, and the two did not agree:

| where | claimed |

## Also: a silent duplication, not a conflict

Two ordering lines were duplicated. They arrived in `01e703e8` through an auto-merge of PLAN.md — git kept **both** versions of an edited block and reported no conflict.

author: hkienlen
engine9r
body:
Continues #107 after final production ranged-read acceptance showed that Luna could legally walk a large tracked file sequentially in 120-line windows. The bounded `lines` capability worked, but without an explicit chain budget it could still consume unnecessary tokens by scanning most of a file.

## Fix
- adds a shared ranged-read policy parser
- permits at most 6 consecutive `repo.read ...:lines:...` windows for the same tracked file within 15 minutes
- the 7th window is rejected before external file access as `repo_ranged_read_budget_exhausted`
- bounded evidence contains only the blocked file identity, max window count and time window
- a distinct action or expiry of the 15-minute window resets the consecutive-read streak
- if Luna ignores `read_budget_exhausted=true` and requests another ranged window for the same blocked file, core blocks the job as `repeated_ranged_read_budget` before action planning
- Luna instructions explicitly forbid sequential whole-file scanning and require wait/complete/escalation or a distinct artifact after budget exhaustion

## Production finding
On production release f373a209, `repo.search` and bounded ranged reads worked correctly on `/opt/btc-radar/app/db/stats.py`, but Luna continued through multiple non-overlapping 120-line windows and production Luna spend rose to $0.0715162 before the supervisor was quiesced. Public ingress remains online while the full supervisor is inactive.

## Gates
- ranged-read budget focused/core/OpenAI tests: PASS
- legacy Node suite: 214/214 PASS
- Browserless suite: 137/137 PASS
- Python/JSON/git-diff/secret/host-path checks PASS
- production full supervisor inactive; public ingress healthy

No write permission changes. BTC Radar and NexoLab remain write-disabled. No merge/auto-merge/deploy, Chromium, trading, or hardware/Modbus capability is added.

body:
## Problema

O campo de competência (mês de referência da fatura/lançamento) só existia de fato para compras em cartão de crédito. Lançamentos regulares (débito, dinheiro, transferência etc.) tinham a competência sempre zerada por `corrigirCompetenciaTransacoes()` a cada carregamento do arquivo, e não havia como visualizar ou editar esse valor diretamente no modal de edição do lançamento.

## O que mudou

- **Novo campo "Fatura/Competência" no modal de edição** — passa a aparecer na edição de **qualquer** lançamento (não só cartão de crédito), usando o mesmo formato/rótulo já usado na coluna "Fatura/Competência" da tabela de Registros (`competenciaLabel`). O texto de apoio abaixo do campo se adapta conforme é lançamento de cartão ("fatura escolhida") ou não ("competência escolhida"), deixando claro que a edição não altera data, valor ou demais dados.
- **Novo helper `competenciaBaseLancamento(dataISO, conta, pgto)`**: generaliza a regra existente — cartão de crédito continua usando `competenciaFatura` (respeita fechamento/vencimento do cartão); qualquer outro lançamento usa `competenciaDeData` (mês da própria Data), já que fora do cartão não existe uma "fatura" com regra própria.
- **Preenchimento automático na importação**: todo lançamento criado por importação agora recebe `Fatura/Competência = competência selecionada/importada pelo usuário` (o período escolhido na tela de importação) — nunca fica em branco, independente de ser cartão, contracheque ou conta comum. Isso vale mesmo quando a Data do lançamento importado cai em um mês diferente do período importado (ex.: importando competência 08/2026, um lançamento com data em setembro ainda recebe Fatura/Competência = 2026-08).
- **Preservação de valores existentes**: `corrigirCompetenciaTransacoes()` deixou de zerar a competência de lançamentos regulares a cada carregamento — agora preserva qualquer valor já existente (manual ou importado). Isso corrige o problema de raiz que impedia o campo de "colar".
- **Precedência ao salvar (`saveTx`)**: se o campo foi alterado manualmente em relação ao valor original, o valor manual prevalece; caso contrário, se Data e Conta não mudaram, preserva o valor já existente; só recalcula pela fórmula quando não há valor manual nem original a preservar (lançamento novo, ou Data/Conta alteradas).
- **Parcelamento e duplicação** (`sincronizarParcelasFuturas`, `propagarParaParcelasAnteriores`, "Duplicar em Vários Meses"): lançamentos regulares gerados/duplicados passam a herdar/recalcular a competência pela mesma regra geral, preservando a identidade do lançamento em vez de sempre zerar para não-cartão.
- **Edição em Lote**: campo "Fatura/Competência" liberado para qualquer lançamento selecionado (antes só permitia quando a seleção era 100% de cartão de crédito); removida a restrição e o aviso correspondente.

## Regras atendidas

- A competência usada é a **selecionada/importada**, não necessariamente a data do lançamento.
- Registros importados anteriormente que já possuam Fatura/Competência mantêm o valor existente.
- A Fatura/Competência de um lançamento editado manualmente não é mais recalculada automaticamente.
- O valor é preservado em edição, duplicação, parcelamento e demais operações que mantenham a identidade do lançamento.

## Verificação

Testado via Playwright (servidor local + libs Chart.js/PapaParse vendorizadas, sem depender de CDN):
1. Campo "Fatura/Competência" aparece e é editável em um lançamento regular (não-cartão), com lista de opções e valor pré-selecionado corretos.
2. Escolher manualmente uma nova competência e salvar persiste o valor.
3. Reabrir e salvar novamente sem tocar no campo preserva o valor manual (não é recalculado pela Data).
4. `corrigirCompetenciaTransacoes()` (rodaria a cada carregamento do arquivo) não altera/zera o valor existente.
5. Importar um lançamento bancário comum cuja Data cai em mês diferente do período importado resulta corretamente na competência do período **importado**, não na do mês da Data.

Todos os cenários passaram, sem erros de console/página relacionados à funcionalidade.
