author: zeeman-effect
body: Takes `hardware/kicad/recorder/recorder.kicad_pcb` from "placement and pours only, signals open" to a board that can be uploaded to a quick-turn fab. ## Result - `kicad-cli pcb drc` on `recorder.kicad_pcb`: **0 violations at every severity, 0 unconnected items**. - `python scripts/check_gates.py`: **ok**. - `hardware/kicad/fab/` rewritten from this board: Gerbers, both Excellon drills, `recorder-pos.csv` and `recorder-jlc.zip`. - 695 tracks, 185 vias, 8 zones. [Routed board, F.Cu and B.Cu](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5d7e2a14-d845-4df3-9c66-6b00a54a929a/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Frouted_board_front_and_back.png) ## Routing Signals came from freerouting over Specctra DSN/SES. The USB-C escape, the D+/D− pair and the fine-pitch fanouts are hand-routed and locked so rip-up cannot cut them. USB D+/D− are a 0.2 mm pair on a 0.4 mm pitch over the solid In1 GND plane, deliberately **not** impedance controlled: the ESP32-S3 USB peripheral is full speed only, and 90 Ω on this 0.1 mm top prepreg would need roughly 0.06 mm traces, well under anything a quick-turn fab will run. ## Checking against the fab instead of house numbers The DRC floors were a mix of round numbers and values that had been relaxed until the board passed. Some were looser than JLCPCB: nothing enforced their 0.45 mm pad hole-to-hole spacing or their 0.5 mm minimum non-plated hole, and silk text was allowed down to 0.8 mm, which is only legal on their high-precision legend line. Every rule now carries the JLC figure it came from and says where it is deliberately tighter. The two checks that depend on item type cannot be a global minimum, so they live in a new `recorder.kicad_dru`. | | Board | JLC standard | | --- | --- | --- | | Track width | 0.15 mm | 0.1016 mm | | Via | 0.6 mm on a 0.3 mm drill | 0.25 mm on 0.15 mm | | Pad hole-to-hole | 0.62 mm | 0.45 mm | | Via hole-to-hole | 0.30 mm | 0.20 mm | | Hole to copper | 0.30 mm | 0.20 mm | | Copper to routed edge | 0.30 mm | 0.20 mm | | Silk text | 1.0 mm / 0.15 mm stroke | 1.0 mm / 0.15 mm | Hole-to-copper is held at 0.3 mm rather than JLC's 0.2 mm because non-plated holes carry a ±0.2 mm diameter tolerance, so a 1.7 mm mounting hole can come back 0.1 mm larger in radius and eat the difference. ## MK1 sound port That same margin is what forced the microphone land open. The stock Infineon ring pad leaves 0.18 mm of copper to the 0.8 mm acoustic port and its custom-pad anchor circle leaves 0.25 mm, so the drill could cut into the seal ring — and an open solder ring leaks, which costs the low-frequency response the part exists for. The ring and its stencil aperture move out to r=0.95 mm and the anchor shrinks to 0.32 mm so it sits wholly inside the annulus. The port itself is unchanged: the datasheet asks for 0.8 mm and says the board maker's rules should drive footprint adaptations. [MK1 sound-port land, before and after](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5d7e2a14-d845-4df3-9c66-6b00a54a929a/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmic_port_clearance_before_after.png) ## Silkscreen Raised to JLC's standard font. Every designator still found a clear seat at the larger size, so the only thing 0.8 mm bought was illegible reference designators. [Front silkscreen at 0.8 mm and 1.0 mm](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5d7e2a14-d845-4df3-9c66-6b00a54a929a/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fsilkscreen_text_height_before_after.png) ## Things the gate could not see - Every footprint carried a bare name like `C_0805_2012Metric` while the schematic asked for `Capacitor_SMD:C_0805_2012Metric`, because `FootprintLoad` takes a directory and stamps what it returns with the bare name. Nothing on the board was traceable to a library. Qualifying the names also needs `fp-lib-table` to list them, which only had `PSV` in it. - BT1 inherited "exclude from BOM" from the generic solder-wire land, which would have quietly dropped the battery from the parts list. - `check_gates.py` ran DRC with `--severity-error`, so every warning-level rule was invisible to it. It now runs at every severity and with `--schematic-parity`. - It also runs DRC a second time with `--refill-zones` and refuses to plot if the two disagree. `kicad-cli` plots the fill stored in the board, so a stale pour would ship while DRC quietly refilled and called it clean. - `route_pcb.py` grew a matching cleanup for vias parked beside a same-net through-hole pad they only duplicate. One sat exactly 0.45 mm from J1 pad 1, on JLC's limit with no room for drill tolerance. `--schematic-parity` still reports 27 notes and all are expected: 22 module pads with no schematic pin (spare ESP32-S3 GPIO castellations, NC pins, the USB-C SBU pair), the 4 mounting holes, which are mechanical and have no symbol, and SP1's Description field. ## Left for a human - **Speaker part number.** SP1 is still an invented 15 × 11 mm land. It is DRC clean and routed, but the pad size and spacing are made up. - **SW1 actuation.** Top-actuated PTS645 on a left-edge button. Needs a case lever or a side-actuated part. Case job; the footprint and its routing are done. - **MK1 acoustic seal.** The land is adapted, and Infineon assumes solder-mask-defined pads while this one is copper-defined (inherited from the KiCad library). Worth checking on the first assembled board. - **Caliper numbers.** Pixel body and Pixelsnap ring dimensions in `params.json` are still published defaults. No part moved, so `hardware/cad/params.json` and `case.scad` are untouched. [fab_readiness_checks.log](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5d7e2a14-d845-4df3-9c66-6b00a54a929a/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Ffab_readiness_checks.log) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: aldoruizluna
body:
**Draft, and blocked by design.** This is not mergeable until yantra4d's
`feat(graph): expressions in socket inputs` (lane D1 of Wave D) ships and the
platform pin moves. Graph format `1.1` and the `{"expr": …}` param value do not
exist before it, so the transpiler on today's pin rejects this document. The
coordinator owns that sequencing.

## What changes

`boltring.angle` becomes `{"expr": "360 / bolt_count"}`, and the
`bolt_spacing_deg` slider is removed. The graph's own `meta.notes` had been
admitting the workaround since it was authored:

> bolt_count and bolt_spacing_deg are independent params by design — the graph
> format has no expressions, so the author sets both (spacing = 360 / count).

## Why it is a bug fix, not a tidy-up

Leaving the spacing at its 60° default while raising `bolt_count` to 8 renders
**the six-bolt part, byte for byte**: 8 × 60° = 480°, so the two extra holes
land exactly on top of existing ones. The slider moved and the geometry did
not, with no error and no warning. The `bolt_spacing_deg * bolt_count <= 360`
constraint did not catch it either — 480 > 360 makes it a `warning`, not an
`error`, and warnings do not block a render.

## Proof

STL sha256 through `cq_runner`, transpiling each revision's own graph and
manifest:

| case | sha256 | bytes | |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|
| defaults, `flange` | `8cd4648a…` | 379284 | before == after |
| defaults, `blank` | `6d1a0575…` | 75684 | before == after |
| `bolt_count: 8` | `ff267b6a…` | 480484 | after == before-with-spacing-45 |
| `bolt_count: 8` | `8cd4648a…` | 379284 | before, spacing untouched — the bug |

Byte-identical at the defaults; at a changed count it now produces what the old
graph produced only when the author *also* remembered to set the spacing to 45
by hand.

## Follow-on edits

Removing a declared parameter leaves two references that had to go with it:

- the `bolt_circle` CDG interface no longer lists `bolt_spacing_deg`;
- the `bolt_spacing_deg * bolt_count <= 360` warning constraint is removed —
  it existed only to police the hand-set spacing, its message ("The graph
  evaluates no expressions") is now false, and it cannot fire because the
  spacing *is* `360 / bolt_count`.

`docs/README.md` keeps the history rather than quietly dropping it, since the
eighth control was documented as a deliberate design decision.

Document version bumped `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`. `spacer-block` stays at `1.0.0` and
still validates — the addition is backwards compatible.

author: d4rken
body:
## What changed

Folder rows in the Explorer stopped showing their item count in January, and on storage where it applies they also lost their ownership and permission details. Both show again. A pull-to-refresh no longer blanks those details for the length of the reload.

## Technical Context

- Root cause: the listing pipeline dedupes re-emissions through `hasSameItemsAs`, which compared lookup rows by id and runtime class only. `DirectoryLocationLoader` publishes a directory twice (basic lookups, then the extended pass with `childCount`, ownership, permissions, writability), and the second publish was judged identical and dropped. The `Modified` incremental hint was swallowed the same way. Introduced in e243d84b0; 4fd64c375 fixed the same symptom for storage rows only.
- Fix: rows now compare in full. Every `ExplorerItem` variant and all four `APathLookup` implementations are data classes, so an exact re-emission still dedupes and any changed field passes. A directory load makes at most three passes through the gate; metadata is attached in batch, so nothing re-emits per item.
- Making the basic pass visible again exposed a refresh flicker, so `retainContentFrom` now keeps the previous row for every lookup whose `APathLookup` is unchanged until the extended pass republishes. `withExtendedData` stores the extended fields on the item and leaves the basic lookup in place, which is what makes that equality match. `retainExtendedDataFrom` and its two tests in `BrowsingEngineTest` are the part worth a close read.
- Left as is: rows carrying a `CaString` (Shortcut, Storage, Trash) never compare equal, so a Home or Device reload always re-sorts a handful of rows. Storage rows have done that since August; the cost is negligible.
- Pre-existing and not addressed here: keyboard focus is a numeric index, so any re-sort under an unchanged count moves focus to whichever row now sits at that index. That already happens on every fresh load's peek-to-lookup re-sort; this change adds one more trigger (a `Modified` hint while sorting by date).

author: jvicen1345-coder
body:
"Flexion" appears **85 times** in `lib/atlas-content.ts`, "specificity" 67, "insertion" 99 — in copy a patient or a first-week student reads alongside a clinician. To that reader the word is a blank, and a glossary page they have to leave the Atlas to visit is a page they don't visit.

Jargon in Atlas prose is now a dotted-underlined button. Tapping it gives what the word means and, more usefully, **an example**: "curling your hand up toward your shoulder is elbow flexion" lands where "bending a joint" does not.

**51 terms**, chosen by counting what actually appears in the Atlas content rather than by guessing — down the tail from flexion and specificity to laxity, paresthesia and varus.

## Decisions

- **Tap, not hover.** A hover tooltip is invisible on a phone, and the readers this exists for are the most likely to be on one. It is a real `<button>`, so keyboard and screen-reader users get the explanation too — a `title` attribute or CSS-only popover would not give them that.
- **Only the first occurrence per string** is marked. Underlining all 85 instances of "flexion" would turn the panel into a field of dotted lines and teach the reader to ignore them, which is the opposite of the point.
- **Longest match first**, so "plantarflexion" is never read as the "flexion" inside it. Word boundaries nearly handle that on their own; the ordering makes the intent explicit rather than relying on it.
- **The labels are jargon too.** "Origin" and "Insertion" are as opaque as anything in the sentences beneath them, so they are tappable as well.
- **A hint line** at the top of each region — the underline is deliberately quiet so it doesn't compete with the prose, which also makes it easy to miss entirely.

## The clipping bug

`.atlas-content-panel` is `overflow-y: auto`, and an absolutely-positioned popover inside a scroll container is clipped by it — **25 of 36 terms were cut off** on desktop in the first implementation. Measured, not eyeballed.

Popovers are now portalled to `<body>` and positioned in viewport coordinates, repositioning on scroll (capture phase, since a scroll inside the panel does not bubble to `window`) and flipping above the word when there is no room below.

## Testing

Every marked term on a region was opened and measured, at both widths:

| | Desktop 1280px | Mobile 390px |
|---|---|---|
| Terms marked | 36 | 36 |
| Clipped by an ancestor | 0 | 0 |
| Off-screen | 0 | 0 |

Also confirmed: no match glued to a neighbouring word (nothing matched inside a longer term), Escape closes, outside-click closes, Enter opens, `aria-expanded` tracks state. Mobile reaches the Atlas through a `<select>` region picker rather than the sidebar list, and behaves identically once driven that way.

`typecheck`, `lint` and all 29 Playwright tests pass; `globals.css` brace depth still 0, new classes appended at the end.

## Worth a second opinion

The definitions are written for a layperson by someone who is not a PT. Two in particular are simplifications that deserve a clinician's eye before they reach patients: **supination/pronation** covers forearm and foot in one line, and **origin/insertion** is reduced to "the end that moves less" versus "the end that moves".

Applied to the Atlas only, since that is where the problem was reported. `PlainText` takes any string, so Clinical Reference, Special Tests and the patient-facing brief are straightforward follow-ons.

author: sahil5494
body:
## Summary

Completely rebuilt the homepage from a component-based architecture to a server-rendered "ledger" design. The new page is fully static HTML on first paint—every headline, section, and data point renders in the initial frame—with optional client-side motion layered on top via intersection observers.

## Key Changes

- **Server-rendered content**: Migrated from dynamic component imports (`HeroParticles`, `OrbCanvas`, `CardSlider`, etc.) to inline, static content. All page data (failures, steps, engagements, practices, objections, procurement terms, markets) is now defined as constants and rendered directly in the page component.

- **New homepage structure**: Replaced the old multi-section layout with a new "ledger" design featuring:
  - Fixed header with navigation and mobile burger menu
  - Hero section with shortlist artefact (3D card on pointer devices)
  - Engagement models (7 service types with facets)
  - Practices (10 industry verticals with role examples)
  - Objections & answers (6 common questions)
  - Working with us section (procurement, markets, clients)
  - Brief submission form

- **Motion contract inverted**: CSS holds the final state; JavaScript adds `armed` class to pull elements back, then `seen` to release them on intersection. If JS is disabled or motion is reduced, nothing is hidden—content is always visible.

- **Scoped styling**: New `home.css` stylesheet scoped under `.rvg` class to isolate homepage styles from the rest of the site. Includes custom properties for dark/light theme switching via `.bone` modifier.

- **Custom fonts**: Added `Archivo` (with variable width axis) and `IBM Plex Mono` fonts, scoped to this route only to avoid loading them on other pages.

- **Metadata & SEO**: Added proper `Metadata` export with Open Graph, Twitter card, and canonical URL. Includes four JSON-LD structures: Organization, Services, Breadcrumb, and FAQ.

- **Client components**: 
  - `HomeClient.tsx`: Handles header scroll state, reveal animations, and 3D pointer tracking for the hero artefact
  - `BriefForm.tsx`: Form submission via Web3Forms API with validation and success state

- **Site utilities**: New `lib/site.ts` exports `SITE_URL` resolved from environment variables (production domain, Vercel preview, or localhost).

- **Layout integration**: Updated `layout.tsx` to conditionally render site chrome (nav/footer) only on non-homepage routes via new `SiteNav` and `SiteFooter` exports from `SiteChrome.tsx`.

## Notable Implementation Details

- The shortlist artefact in the hero uses CSS `perspective` and 3D transforms; pointer movement is tracked via `pointermove` events and applied via `requestAnimationFrame` for smooth 60fps motion.
- Form validation is client-side with email regex check; submission is async to Web3Forms with error handling and success state.
- Mobile navigation uses a burger button that toggles the `.open` class on the nav links list.
- All content is intentionally descriptive rather than metrics-driven (no placement counts, retention rates, or delivery times per launch checklist).
- The page uses CSS custom properties for theming; `.bone` sections invert the color scheme for light backgrounds.

author: savisaluwadana
body:
## Performance
- Lazy-load Firebase Auth only when Google sign-in/sign-out needs it, reducing initial storefront JavaScript.
- Collapse bag quantity changes from DELETE + POST into one optimistic PATCH request and one server recomputation.
- Parallelize bag ownership/product lookups where possible.
- Route bag and wishlist operations through the shared API client and keep non-essential account data deferred on public pages.
- Remove the global Unsplash preconnect.
- Re-enable responsive Next image optimization for shared page-header hero images.
- Replace remote product placeholder images with a local fallback.
- Remove unused remote image hosts from Next config.
- Remove three below-fold remote images from the subscription page and keep the local hero optimized.

## Runtime configuration
- Add `lib/config/site.ts` for site URL, support/partnership email, WhatsApp, social links, and service areas.
- Add a tracked `.env.example` documenting public/API URLs, auth, Firebase, SendGrid, Azure storage, analytics, contact, social, and WhatsApp configuration.
- Checkout WhatsApp ordering now uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_WHATSAPP_NUMBER` and is hidden when it is not configured.
- Footer/contact/legal/LLM metadata now use shared configuration instead of duplicated runtime values.
- Placeholder `#` social links are removed; social icons only render when real URLs are configured.

## Remove fake/stale customer-facing data
- Delete the hardcoded `defaultSubscriptionPlans` fallback catalogue.
- Subscription storefront now shows only active API/database-backed plans with a real empty state.
- Remove hardcoded fallback prices, contents, quantities, `Free delivery`, `certified organic`, `carbon-neutral`, `top 1%`, `100% directly to farmers`, and `zero-plastic` claims.
- Checkout loads the current subscription plan from the API instead of constructing a fake preview.
- Normalize subscription plan IDs in API serialization for existing clients.
- Remove hardcoded Product JSON-LD claims for a 4.9 rating / 850 reviews, shipping cost, delivery timing, return policy, and arbitrary price-valid-until dates. Aggregate ratings are emitted only when real values are provided.

## API boundary + checkout
- Subscription listing SSR uses the server API boundary instead of importing Prisma directly.
- Checkout, contact, newsletters, bags, wishlist, and partnership forms use the shared API client.
- Checkout keeps bag, quick-order, recurring-order, saved/custom address, COD, and optional WhatsApp flows while removing placeholder business values.
- Checkout no longer claims delivery is free when that value is not sourced from the order.

## Site-shell cleanup
- Footer links now point to real destinations rather than generic collection placeholders.
- Contact, privacy, and terms pages use the configured support address.
- Privacy and terms pages are static server components instead of shipping unnecessary client JavaScript.

This PR is intentionally separate from merged PR #69 so the supplier-partnership redesign and the larger performance/config cleanup remain reviewable independently.

author: f-trycua
body:
Fleet users can now reuse an existing pool without reconciling its configuration, retain a claim across connections, and recover interrupted cleanup without provisioning a replacement. The guides distinguish disconnecting, releasing a claim, and deleting the pool namespace. They also explain why a 403 requires inspecting the operation and response body before choosing between authentication, payment, name, or template-policy remediation.

Refs #3592 and the separate legacy lifecycle API limitation #3315. No RFC is required: this documents released behavior without changing SDK or platform contracts.

The scope is five documentation files: the existing Python and TypeScript pool guides, expiry guide, a focused troubleshooting guide, and its navigation entry. The Python example requires an explicit pool name and pins cua-sandbox 0.4.3; TypeScript pins @trycua/fleet 0.1.1. TTL guidance distinguishes creation age from idle time and explicit release. Cleanup guidance covers existing-resource ownership, template-reconciliation rollback, shared pools, absent-resource retries, and asynchronous deletion verification.

Validation passed:

- Installed PyPI cua-sandbox 0.4.3 resolves cua-fleet 0.1.14. The checkout's manifest names 0.1.16, so release-contract checks used the installed 0.1.14 binding. Synthetic native HTTP checks verified pool-plus-namespace deletion and missing-resource acceptance in both Python 0.1.14 and TypeScript 0.1.1.
- 62 focused tests from `libs/python/cua-sandbox/tests/test_pool.py` passed against the installed release, with two unrelated signed-service tests deselected. Tests ran outside the source package directory to avoid importing checkout code.
- All nine Python blocks compile. Extracted create, get-only reuse, disconnect, and reference-reconnect examples execute against the installed Sandbox implementation with Fleet and guest boundaries mocked. Assertions cover claim release, pool preservation, no reconciliation on lookup, and no creation during reconnect.
- All nine TypeScript blocks pass strict TypeScript 5.9.3 checking against @trycua/fleet 0.1.1, including the browser example. The exact Node example executes through the published WASM binding with a synthetic HTTP transport for success, screenshot failure, and failed binding; each releases the claim and preserves the pool. Extracted recovery blocks release/retry a claim and delete a pool/namespace without provisioning or guest-service requests.
- From `docs`, `npx --yes pnpm@9.0.4 docs:check-hygiene`, `docs:check-links`, scoped Prettier checking, and `build` passed. The production build generated 141 routes. `git diff --check` passed; public-content audit found no credentials, private paths, or internal-only references in the change.

Known gaps: mock tests do not prove live guest startup, server-side expiry timing, or live cleanup convergence. The browser SDK example has static validation but no live GUI execution. The documentation pages were rendered in the combined local site, including narrow-layout troubleshooting. Ready for human review of these released-contract documentation changes; live Fleet runtime certification remains separate. No resources were provisioned and no live docs were published.

Related contributions were reviewed before implementation. #3116 remains a separate concept proposal with local/legacy lifecycle semantics. #3092 is authentication-only and outside this change. #2928 and #3051 propose earlier standalone pool guides; this work updates the existing guides against released Pool and claim-handle APIs. No prose or code from those proposals is adapted. Documentation-only Conventional Commit title; no component release is requested.

Final combined verification: the curated content passed hygiene, internal links, the production docs build, and both generator drift checks. The website integration is reviewed separately; no production content pin was changed.

author: joshualeestone
body:
## #2259: check-block-delivery.js is runner-aware (reads AGENTS.md too)

`tools/check-block-delivery.js` is a dev diagnostic that answers "which managed
instruction blocks actually REACHED the agents?" by reading the agents' brief files. It
filtered agents by `CLAUDE.md` presence and read only `CLAUDE.md`. After #2245 a codex
agent boots from `AGENTS.md` (not CLAUDE.md), so the diagnostic silently OMITTED every
codex agent - the exact population #2245 fixes - reporting a false clean, which is the
specific failure the tool's own header warns against.

### Fix
- New `briefPath(dir)` helper resolves each agent's real brief: `CLAUDE.md` if present,
  else `AGENTS.md`, else null. CLAUDE.md-first mirrors `engine/discover.js` `connect()`
  ("CLAUDE.md wins when both exist") and `engine/create.js` `briefFilename(runner)`; a
  codex-only dir resolves to AGENTS.md.
- The helper drives all three CLAUDE.md-only sites: the agent filter, the population
  floor, and the per-agent text read.
- Rejected unioning both files' text: a stale marker in an old CLAUDE.md would mask a
  missing one in the current AGENTS.md - the exact false-clean this tool catches.

### Tests (tools/test-block-delivery.sh, wired via package.json test:shell)
- a codex agent (AGENTS.md, no CLAUDE.md) is SEEN, not omitted;
- a block missing from a codex agent's AGENTS.md is caught (UNDELIVERED to 1) - the old
  CLAUDE.md-only code would read "delivered to all entitled", a false clean;
- a block present in AGENTS.md reads as delivered.
Per-row greps (the convention the file already fixed for the projects arm). Full suite
green (JS 4926/0 + shell). Dev-only diagnostic, low severity.

Addresses #2259.

**[e2e-coder]** — Closes #5873.

## What

`reyn.log` grew unbounded while the process sat idle (owner-hit, 2026-09-06: "放置してるだけで reyn.log 肥大化してシステム止まらないようにしてね"). `_setup_interactive_logging` now installs a `logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler` instead of a bare `logging.basicConfig(filename=...)`, sized from a new `logs:` config block (`max_bytes`, `backup_count`; default 16 MiB × 4 backups, total ≤ 80 MiB — architect's own provisional-but-reasoned numbers, config-tunable). The redirect still installs immediately with `LogsConfig()`'s own dataclass defaults (so config-load-time warnings are still captured), then `_apply_logs_config` refines the already-installed handler's `.maxBytes`/`.backupCount` in place once the real config is known.

`logs:` is a real `ReynConfig` dataclass field (`LogsConfig`), so it gets `config_schema`'s automatic unknown-key detection for free — no manual #5849③-style registry needed, unlike `permissions:`/`sandbox:`.

**Rides along** (architect-requested, alongside the concurrently-landed #5877): `stall_trace.find_file_handler_path()` no longer scans root-logger handlers for a path-shape match — `_setup_interactive_logging` now registers its handler's path directly via a new `stall_trace.register_file_handler_path()`, the one authoritative writer declaring its own path instead of a reader re-deriving it. Existing `isinstance(handler, logging.FileHandler)`-based readers (`litellm_bootstrap`) are unaffected — `RotatingFileHandler` is a `FileHandler` subclass, and its `.baseFilename` stays fixed across rotations by design.

The issue's own "same PR" ask re: #5870 stage 1's per-episode dump cadence needed no code change — `LoopTripwire.observe`'s dump is already once-per-episode (verified in `loop_probe.py`), as the issue itself noted.

**Round 2 (architect co-vet response)** — see the 3 checklist items below and the follow-up comment: fixed the tripwire-fd-vs-rotation inode hazard, collapsed the two literal-default sites into one (`LogsConfig()`'s own dataclass defaults), and switched all 6 test sites off the private `stall_trace._registered_file_handler_path` onto the public `find_file_handler_path()`. Also fixed a CI-only failure lead-coder caught: `test_example_documents_every_config_field` wants every `ReynConfig` field documented in `reyn.local.yaml.example` — added the `logs:` block there too (same class of gap as #5858).

- [x] Small `max_bytes` (e.g. 4 KiB) config + sustained WARNING writes produces `reyn.log.1`, and live `reyn.log` stays under `max_bytes` (strip-verified: reverting `RotatingFileHandler` → `FileHandler` lets it grow unbounded — confirmed during this fix).
- [x] Old rotated files beyond `backup_count` are deleted (total ≤ `max_bytes × (backup_count+1)`).
- [x] Both `chat.py` call sites use the same one handler-installing function; `git grep 'basicConfig(' -- src/` has no `filename=` call left.
- [x] A `logs: {max_byte: ...}` typo is caught as an unknown-config-key warning.
- [x] Existing "read reyn.log" paths (`stall_trace.find_file_handler_path`, `litellm_bootstrap.py`'s `FileHandler` search) still find the `RotatingFileHandler` — both structurally (`isinstance`) and via the new registration.
- [x] `reyn-dir-layout.md`'s `logs/` row documents `rotated, bounded by logs.max_bytes × (backup_count+1)`.
- [x] `reyn-yaml.md` gained a `logs:` config block.
- [x] `reyn.local.yaml.example` gained a matching `logs:` block (CI-caught, round 2).

(ADR-0046 Falsification entry is the architect's own to add, per the issue.)

## Gates (round 2, head `18b7902d5`)

- `ruff check .` — clean.
- `python scripts/test_tier_audit.py --strict tests/interfaces/test_3671_stall_trace_startup_wiring.py tests/interfaces/test_inline_interactive_logging.py` — 14/14 OK, 0 Tier-4 violations.

Substituted a manual `mypy --follow-imports=silent` scoped to all 6 touched src files: 39 pre-existing errors reported across 3 files, **all outside every touched diff hunk** — cross-checked against `git diff origin/main -- <file> | grep '^@@'` for each (`app.py`'s touched hunks are the ~2402-2559 range around `_watch_loop_responsiveness`; the 39 findings sit well outside it, scattered across this 7000+-line file's many other pre-existing untyped spots).

author: informativus
body:
Telegravim now uses bundled Hunspell with pinned Russian and English dictionaries on every platform. Both languages work offline from first use; existing extra languages and the user's disabled spellcheck setting are preserved. Personal dictionary words remain separate from the bundled files.

In view mode, physical Ctrl+E (Ctrl+У with the Russian layout) opens corrections for the word under the compose cursor. Arrow keys or j/k select a suggestion, Enter replaces the word, Esc closes the menu, and undo restores the original. Pending suggestions are cancelled when the draft, cursor, or focus changes. Existing exclusions for links and code remain in place.

The dictionary source revision, licenses and checksums are included. The Russian dictionary is stored as two readable text parts under the repository's 2 MB inspection limit and reconstructed byte-for-byte during installation. Two English source files have trailing whitespace normalized, with upstream and packaged hashes recorded separately.

Validation: macOS arm64 Release application build; 986/986 native checks covering offline installation, dictionary recovery, Russian/English and mixed text, user words, keyboard selection, replacement/undo, Escape and stale callbacks; 96/96 source wiring checks; application startup and clean exit with an isolated empty profile; strict bundle signature verification. Windows/Linux builds and a signed-in live-chat walkthrough were not run. Dictionary spelling does not provide sentence grammar correction, and suggestion ordering still has limitations.

author: hungchistudio-glitch
body:
Three reported faults on the word cards. Two are root-caused and fixed; the
third is not, and this PR does not claim it.

## Fixed: the learning status could not be changed

Tapping New / Learning / Mastered in the word sheet did nothing visible. The
write was working — it reached the database and the list behind the sheet.
The sheet was rendering a **copy** of the word taken when it opened, and
changing the status never wrote the new version back into that copy.

Two other actions already worked around this. Correcting a language ends with
`if (detailItem?.id === item.id) setDetailItem(next)`, and saving an edit has
the same line. The status path was simply never given its copy.

| Detail sheet action | Mutates the word? | Sheet updated? |
|---|---|---|
| **Learning status** | **yes** | **✗ never synced** |
| Edit | yes | ✓ synced |
| Change language | yes | ✓ synced |
| Delete | yes | ✓ closes |
| Send / Share / Collections | no | n/a |

There is no copy now: the sheet holds the id and the word is looked up from
the library each render. Every change reflects by construction, both manual
syncs are gone, and a deleted word closes its own sheet because it stops
being findable. Derived from `uniqueItems` rather than the filtered list, so
narrowing a search while the sheet is open leaves it alone.

## Fixed: a phrase could not be selected inside a card

Selecting text in an example sentence to save it or send it **could not work
at all**. The card wraps its content in `VocabularySelection` and waits for a
selection to be made inside it — and that selection was impossible, because
the swipe row the card sits in set `select-none` unconditionally,
`user-select` inherits, and nothing anywhere in the tree turned it back on.

Now scoped to an actual drag, which is what it was for: a horizontal swipe
across a sentence would otherwise select the sentence. `isDragging` is true
from pointer-down, before the finger has travelled far enough to move the
row, so the guard covers any gesture that turns out to be a swipe while a
still finger leaves the text alone.

This is also why it was a word-card problem and not a friends or messages
one: only the vocabulary card has a selection layer, though all three share
the row.

## Fixed: switching view mode left the list mislaid out

The virtualiser remembers the height measured for each row, keyed by the
word's id — and the id does not change with the view mode. So every
previously measured row kept its **compact** height while rendering as a
card: the spacer was sized for the wrong list, rows overlapped or left gaps,
and the scroll position pointed elsewhere. Only rows currently on screen
corrected themselves.

Cards is the mode with the pictures, so this is also why images looked wrong
after a switch — they arrived in rows sized for a mode that has none.

`measure()` in a layout effect drops the cache so every row is re-derived
from the estimate for the mode it is actually in.

## Not fixed: the double tap

Ruled out with evidence: a stale bundle (the service worker is network-first),
sticky `:hover` on iOS (Tailwind v4 wraps every `hover:` in
`@media (hover: hover)`, confirmed in the built CSS), the 300ms tap delay
(`width=device-width, initial-scale=1`), anything resetting the expansion,
and layout shift from phonetics loading (reported to happen long after the
page settles). A real browser click on this same list expands on the **first**
click, every time.

It is specific to iOS touch. I could not reproduce it: an iOS Simulator
attempt produced no evidence at all, because the simulator's input channel
timed out and none of the taps were delivered.

Worth noting for testing: the `select-none` change does alter touch behaviour
on the card, and it is the only change here that is both word-card-specific
and touch-related. That is a lead, not a claim.

## Also added: `/vocabulary-card-review`

The list lives behind the login and these faults only appear under a finger,
so there was no way to put it on a phone without an account. A review route
beside the other seven, same `reviewRouteOnly()` guard — development and
previews only, 404 on production. Real list, real swipe rows, real cards,
fixture words. It counts the toggles that actually arrive, so "it took two
taps" stops being a matter of memory.

## Fixed: the relevance sort read 62KB thousands of times per sort

This turned out to be far larger than a per-tap cost, and is the likeliest
explanation for the jank across scrolling, expanding, page entry and search
all at once.

`readInteractionMap()` was being called **inside the sort comparator**. A
comparator runs O(n log n) times, so 400 words is ~2,800 comparisons, each
pulling 62KB out of localStorage and parsing it to answer a question whose
answer had not changed.

Measured in a browser at 400 words:

| | 400 words |
|---|---|
| Read inside the comparator (before) | **686.7 ms** |
| Read once before the sort (after) | **1.5 ms** |
| | **458× less work** |

687ms of blocked main thread per sort on a desktop; four to eight times that
on a phone. It is the fallback branch, so it runs while the AI ranking loads,
when it errors, and offline — which is arrival at the screen, exactly when
the reader is touching it. A thread blocked that long does not stutter, it
drops taps.

The status weights came out of the comparator too — a fresh object per
comparison to hold three constants.

The cost is invisible to a correctness test (the list was always sorted
correctly, just slowly), so the new test counts reads instead: it fails at
**1,593 reads** against the old code and passes at one.

Separately, `readInteractionMap()` now caches, keyed on the raw text so it
cannot go stale — another tab, a sign-out or a cleared store all change the
text and force a re-parse. String comparison is 0.05ms against 0.34ms to
parse. The existing tests clear localStorage between cases, which is exactly
the hazard, and they pass unchanged. A tap now parses nothing at all.

Per-tap breakdown at 62KB, measured:

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `getItem` | ~0 ms | ~0 ms |
| `JSON.parse` | 0.337 ms | **0** (string compare, 0.048 ms) |
| `JSON.stringify` | 0.231 ms | 0.231 ms |
| `setItem` | 0.205 ms | 0.205 ms |

## Verification

103 test files / 900 tests, all passing.

`vocabularyListVirtualised` intermittently times out under parallel load; it
is pre-existing and renders 300 unvirtualised rows, taking **14.78s without
these changes and 15.09s with them** — a 2% difference against a 5s per-test
timeout.

`tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` and `next build` all clean.

author: millyinvr
body:
The prep tier stops being eight repetitions of *"is this part of what you like?"* and becomes two moves over one picture, followed by questions written for this client from everything read so far.

Pairs with **tovis-ios#418**, already merged — `FOLLOW_UP` is a new member of the message union, so the iOS fixtures had to be bumped ahead of this branch's schema.

## The two moves

Hair-colour inspiration pack **v3**: the three coarse cards byte-identical, and the eight `attr_*` prep cards replaced by `love_regions` and `change_regions` — the whole reference with every readable attribute drawn on it, multi-select.

**v2 is archived, not deleted.** A consult that answered `attr_tone: ['yes']` is served, read and briefed against v2's eleven questions forever; `resolveConsultSessionInspirationPack` pins on the first stored payload.

What the moves produce is byte-identical to what the eight cards produced: `attribute:VALUE` pairs derived from the reading. Nothing downstream — the analysis prompt, the brief, Stage 4's tier 2 — can tell which pack version answered. **No migration** for the cards: option values are attribute names, which the v2 payload guard already accepts.

One thing v2 could say that v3 cannot: *"not sure"* about one specific attribute. That is the trade the two-tap design makes; an untapped attribute already means "she did not point at this".

## The adaptive follow-ups

A fifth paid call — text-only, `claude-sonnet-5`, effort `low`, 20s timeout, metered like the other four (`FOLLOW_UP_QUESTIONS`).

It picks a **key** from a vocabulary this consult actually has — a per-run enum, so an invented question is not something the grammar can return — and writes the sentence and the option wording. Every option value is re-checked against that key's real options on the way back in; one that is not real throws the whole round away (Part 0 rule 11: the grammar cannot express "options depend on the sibling key", so it is stated in the description and enforced on the server).

### One home per vocabulary

🔴 An **INTAKE**-keyed answer goes to the INTAKE revision through `appendConsultIntakeRevision` — the same write boundary, locking, pack pinning and rerun request the intake step uses — because that is what `safetyFlags.ts` and `consult_analysis_payload_guard` read. A henna answer stored anywhere else is a henna answer the analysis cannot see.

The **follow-up pack's** own keys (`event_timing`, `budget`, `maintenance_tolerance`, `service_experience` — the ones P6's diet moved out of the intake and which have had no storage since) live on the round. Enforced in `consult_follow_up_round_guard`, not just in application code.

### The cap is the unique index

`(consultSessionId, planVersion, round)` is both *"at most three rounds per plan version"* and *"one call per answer burst"* as a database fact: a double-tap, a retried POST and two concurrent requests all lose the insert rather than each buying a paid call. Plan versions are capped at four, so the ceiling is 12 of these calls per consult.

The burst boundary is **structural** — a round closes when its last question is answered — not a timer. (The plan rerun uses a 90s debounce because "an input changed" has no natural end. This does.)

A round is also only bought once a **booking** exists, because the thread renders the whole prep tier inside its booking block: a round bought earlier would be a paid call whose questions nobody is ever shown.

### The fallback, and why the test has to force it

Never a generic list: the intake pack's **own remaining safety questions**, in the pack's own words, with a bubble saying what happened. No safety question left means no round at all.

⚠️ On hair colour this cannot be *waited for*: intake v3 requires all five safety questions before it can complete, and completion gates the analysis, so by the prep tier there is never an outstanding one. The integration test forces both halves — a failing provider **and** an unanswered question. Allergies are the real gap (the colour pack asks neither `known_allergies` nor `skin_sensitivity`, which is why `ALLERGY_HISTORY_UNKNOWN` is permanently required); closing it is P5g-2 by decision.

## Storage

`ConsultFollowUpRound` is a table, deliberately **not** a `ConsultRevision`. Every revision payload is keys and enums, and this artefact's whole content is a sentence a model wrote; putting prose through `consult_revision_requires_agreements` would mean widening a guard that protects five other kinds to admit the one thing they exist to exclude. Its own CHECKs carry the identity-word and secret-key regexes word-for-word, plus length caps.

Also widened: the inspiration payload guard's answer-array cap, 8 → 16. Hair colour has exactly eight attributes, so *"I love all of it"* sat precisely on the old ceiling. Both migrations are strictly expand-only.

## Found by running it

The first live call produced, for a client to read:

> *"You loved that cool, pale **lightestLevel:LEVEL_9** look…"*

It had been handed the pair and quoted it back. Fixed in three layers: the context now passes plain words (`how light it gets: light blonde`), the prompt forbids codes explicitly, and the sanitizer refuses one on any surface she reads — never on `evidence`, which a reviewer reads and where a code is what makes the question gradeable.

A browser screenshot then showed the picker rendering one and a half viewports tall on desktop, with boxes too faint to read as controls over a photograph. Both fixed; the width cap is on **width**, not height, because the boxes are percentages of that element.

## Verified

typecheck · lint · all 33 static guards · **11,255** unit tests · **19** integration tests against real PostgreSQL · **14** browser tests · the live contract test against the real model with a **required-success** fixture (Part 0 rule 10), asserting safety-first ordering and that no identity word reaches the output.

## Not verified

- The full flow end-to-end on prod data — the browser tests stub every route.
- `consult-intake-api.test.ts` fails identically on clean `origin/main` in this local environment (a fixture slug colliding with the seed). Pre-existing, not from this change.

**Deploy: not authorized.** Awaiting Tori's go-ahead as usual.

body:
# Agent detail summary strip, tracker tabs as collection panes, one shared range

Round 5, wave 3 of the 2026-09-05 UX review: items W3-4 (A5), W3-5 (C10) and
W3-6 (D8, D9, finding 32).

## Summary

Three pages stop inventing their own version of a pattern the console already
has. The agent detail overview card becomes the hairline summary strip DESIGN.md
describes. The tracker's Issues and Pull requests tabs become collection panes
with the shared list toolbar instead of cards inside tabs. API usage and the
model detail page drop their Filters cards for the shared time range control,
and every page that reports gateway usage now resolves its window through one
module, so "30 days" means the same 30 days everywhere.

## Changes

**1. Agent detail summary strip (`0b60d4b6`)**
- `views/authed/agent-detail-view.ts`: the `.agent-overview` card is replaced by
  a `.summary-strip` hairline row that states kind, source id, session
  reference, the status chips, estimated spend and the request count, with the
  range control at the right.
- The last bare range `<select>` on the page becomes `time-range-select`
  (24h/7d/30d/1y).
- Test: the strip states the agent's facts and its spend, and the card is gone.

**2. Tracker tabs as collection panes (`63ec239d`)**
- `views/authed/tracker-detail-view.ts`: the Issues and Pull requests tabs lose
  their cards and their repeated titles. Each is a full-width pane with a
  `list-toolbar` (search, the project and status selects, the bulk triage
  action, a count in `slot="count"`), and empty states are hairline rows rather
  than centred cards in a box.
- Per-row buttons become `resource-actions menu-only` kebabs.
- `components/list-toolbar.ts` gains `searchable`, so a collection the host
  returns unfiltered (pull requests) can take the shared bar without a search
  field that would do nothing.
- Tests: the empty Issues tab renders as a full-width pane; the GitLab tab says
  "1 open merge request" and no longer repeats the tab's name.

**3. One range control and one shared answer for "30 days" (`cc512088`)**
- New `utils/time-range.ts`: reads every range spelling the console grew
  (`day`/`week`/`month`/`year`, `24h`/`7d`/`30d`/`1y`, `last-30`) and resolves
  it to one window, plus the prior window for deltas and the "Aug 7 to Sep 6"
  label.
- Cost, the Overview Usage card, API usage and the model detail page all use it.
  Before this, the same account read 18.9K, 18,306, 18,504 and 18,419 requests
  for the same nominal month.
- API usage and the model detail page replace the Filters card (select + two
  date inputs + Apply + Reset) with `time-range-select`, the resolved window
  restated beside it, and a search field that answers as you type.
- API usage adopts Cost's stat vocabulary: "Requests · 30d" with the
  succeeded/failed split, "$ est. · 30d" with an arrow delta against the prior
  window, "Tokens · 30d" compact, "Success rate · 30d" with the failure count.
  A range change keeps the previous numbers at 60% instead of blanking the page.
- A session row is reduced to name, model and one short link to the run, instead
  of printing the same id three ways. Section titles are sentence case.

## Review follow-ups (V-W2)

The review returned 4 "should" items and 5 nits, all applied in five further
commits.

- **A search pause is one request, not four.** Only the captured interactions
  depend on the query, so both usage pages now have a loader that refreshes
  that one card, with its own busy state and its own error line. Measured in
  the browser: API usage 1 API call per pause in typing (was 4), the model
  detail page 1 (was 5).
- **The model detail page dims instead of blanking.** A range change or a
  search used to swap the whole page for a spinner card. It now keeps the
  numbers at 60% with `aria-busy`, the way API usage and Cost behave, while
  the 250 ms realtime refresh stays silent. A reload that arrives during
  another one is queued rather than dropped, so the range control cannot name
  a window whose data was never fetched.
- **The model detail page renders the interaction list its search promised.**
  The results were fetched on every load and never shown, on this branch and
  on main.
- **The tracker pane filters name themselves on screen** ("Project Alpha",
  "Status Open") instead of showing two unnamed dropdowns reading "Alpha" and
  "Open".
- **"All time" is back on both range controls.** The shared util already
  resolved it to a window with no bounds; API usage skips the comparison
  request for it and says "All recorded gateway spend" rather than printing a
  delta against itself.
- Nits: the agent strip shortens uuids to eight characters with the full value
  in the title and on the clipboard (DESIGN.md line 312); the render helpers
  and CSS rules that died with the overview card and the Filters cards are
  deleted; `utils/time-range.ts` documents why calendar and rolling comparison
  windows have different shapes.

## Tests

`cd frontend && npm ci && npm test`: **156 files, 1839 passed, 0 failed**
(baseline on main: 154 files, 1818 passed). 21 new tests, including
`utils/time-range.test.ts` for the math and
`views/authed/usage-range-agreement.test.ts`, which mounts Cost, API usage and
Models against one fixture and asserts they ask for the same window and print
the same total, plus 8 from the review follow-ups (the dim on a range change,
the one-request search on both pages, the queued reload, the named tracker
filters, "All time" on both pages, and the shortened strip ids). No backend
change, so no pytest. `npx tsc --noEmit` adds no errors to the touched files
(three pre-existing ones remain).

## Founder calls

1. The tracker Issues tab keeps a single-project select: issues are fetched per
   project, so an "All projects" option would need a fan-out or a new endpoint.
2. API usage and the model detail page keep "All time" but still have no custom
   date window. A custom mode belongs inside `time-range-select`, where all
   five pages would gain it at once, rather than two pages keeping their own
   date inputs.
3. The canonical 30 days is a rolling instant window (Cost's shipped
   behaviour), so the Overview's totals shift slightly now that it no longer
   steps back a calendar month.
4. The API usage search now runs 300 ms after the last keystroke instead of on
   Apply, and costs one server request per pause.

<!-- PRELOOP_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Low risk**
> UI-only consolidation onto shared console patterns; no backend, config, or API-surface changes, and the shared range math is heavily unit- and cross-page-tested. All previously flagged findings are now addressed.
>
> **Overview**
> Three pages stop inventing their own versions of existing patterns: the agent detail card becomes a summary strip, tracker tabs become collection panes with the shared list toolbar, and API usage / model detail adopt the shared `time-range-select` with one `utils/time-range.ts` resolving "30 days" identically everywhere. All three prior low findings (paginated PR count label, silent range-key fallback, and the search/range race) are now addressed.
>
> <sup>Written by [Preloop PR Reviewer](https://preloop.ai) for commit 519025f9. Updates automatically on new commits.</sup>

author: thedavidmeister
body:
First step of the library / deploy split (#552, rainix#296): the logic of the five deployed contracts moves into `src/abstract/BaseRainlang{Parser,Store,Interpreter,ExpressionDeployer,}.sol`, and `src/concrete/*` become thin bindings of the generated tables and Zoltu addresses over them. This is the shape the `.deploy` repo needs from the `rainlang` package: it will carry only the thin concretes plus the pins.

- `BaseRainlangInterpreter` binds `opcodeFunctionPointers()`; `BaseRainlangParser` binds `parseMeta()` / `operandHandlerFunctionPointers()` / `literalParserFunctionPointers()` (now `view` so a binding may read storage); `BaseRainlangExpressionDeployer` binds `parser()` / `integrityFunctionPointers()` / `describedByMetaV1()`; `BaseRainlangStore` and `BaseRainlang` bind nothing beyond `IRainlang`. `PARSE_META_BUILD_DEPTH` is a source constant on `BaseRainlangParser` rather than a value re-read from the generated file it parameterises.
- `test/concrete/Test*.sol` are the bases built from current source with no generated tables: the parser builds its parse meta from `LibAllStandardOps.authoringMetaV2()` at construction, the pointer tables are read from `LibAllStandardOps` at runtime. `test/lib/deploy/LibTestInterpreterDeploy.sol` places them at fixed test addresses.
- `RainlangExpressionDeployerDeploymentTest` types `I_*` as the bases and gets one hook, `deployRainlang()`, defaulting to the test concretes. The op / integrity / eval / parse tests now run against current source rather than the etched candidate record; the concrete-specific tests (`*.pointers`, `*.meta`, `deployCheck`, `extrospect`, `Rainlang.t`, `LibInterpreterDeploy.t`, `Build.t`, the deploy chain test) still exercise the real concretes and pins, and the deploy repo's `OpTest` will override the hook with `etchRainlang`.
- Generated: the parser, store and interpreter bytecode are unchanged. `RainlangExpressionDeployer` is 15 bytes longer (the `parser()` / `integrityFunctionPointers()` hooks are internal calls the legacy optimizer does not inline), so its candidate address moves `0xb90c299a…` → `0x146Fecd8…`, and `Rainlang`, which embeds it, moves with it. The live 0.1.9 deployments are untouched; the next release needs the `expression-deployer` and `rainlang` suites deployed before its cut, which is the documented flow.

## QA

- Discriminating tests: the full suite, 1518 passed, 7 failed, where the 7 are the fork tests needing `ARBITRUM_RPC_URL`, the same set that fails locally on `main`. `RainlangExpressionDeployer.meta.t.sol` now asserts against `new RainlangExpressionDeployer()` because `I_DEPLOYER` is the source-built test concrete, which is the discriminating case for the hook: with the old binding it read the generated hash back from itself.
- Mutations applied: n/a, a structural move with no new logic; the equivalence tests `RainlangParser.pointers`, `RainlangInterpreter.pointers` and `RainlangExpressionDeployer.pointers` pin generated tables == `LibAllStandardOps`-built tables for the concretes, and every op test now takes the `LibAllStandardOps` path directly through the test concretes.
- Oracle: `script/Build.sol` run to a fixed point; `src/generated/candidate/{RainlangParser,RainlangStore,RainlangInterpreter}.sol` byte-identical to `main`, the two moved records regenerated by the script.
- Category check: #552 asks for the deploy half split out; this PR is the library-side prerequisite (logic in `Base*`, thin concretes, test harness independent of pins). The deploy repo, the slim and consumer migration follow.

author: amund211
body:
Replaces the light/system/dark `ToggleButtonGroup` with a single toggle button, following [Lea Verou's *Dark mode toggles should be two-state*](https://lea.verou.me/blog/2026/dark-mode-toggles).

## The idea

Three modes are still stored, but only two are ever offered: the scheme you see, and its opposite.

| You see | Button offers | Press stores |
| --- | --- | --- |
| light (system default) | dark | `dark` |
| dark (override, OS is light) | light | `system` |
| dark (override, OS is dark) | light | `light` |

A press stores the opposite scheme explicitly — unless that scheme is the one the OS already asks for, in which case it stores `system` so the user keeps following the OS. The OS preference is read **only on press**, never to drop an override, so an OS that switches on a schedule cannot discard a pinned preference.

## Notes

- MUI only populates `systemMode` while the mode is `"system"`, so the OS preference comes from a `prefers-color-scheme` media query instead.
- The icon is the target (a moon while you are in light mode). The tooltip and `aria-label` read `Switch to dark mode`, gaining ` (system default)` when the press will clear the override — the disclosure the article floats as an option.

## Testing

- New `src/components/DarkModeSwitch.ui.test.tsx`: 5 cases covering both storage branches.
- The three layout tests that keyed off `.MuiToggleButtonGroup-root` / `[value="dark"]` now target the label, and assert visibility rather than presence — both layouts render a switch, and only one is visible at a time.
- `vitest.config.ts` pins the browser context to `colorScheme: "light"`. Every label depends on the OS preference, and the suite was relying on playwright's default for it.
- Labels are matched with `{ exact: true }`: `Switch to dark mode` is a substring of `Switch to dark mode (system default)`, and the two mean opposite things about what the next press stores.
- The OS-agrees-with-the-override branch is covered by pinned-light-on-a-light-OS, the mirror of pinned-dark-on-a-dark-OS.

`pnpm run tsc`, `lint:check` and the full suite (1197 tests) pass.

author: rockfordlhotka
body:
## Summary

Every schema change to RockBot's on-disk stores so far has been additive — a new optional property with a default, absorbed by the tolerant deserializer — so upgrading has never needed a data step. The next change that *can't* be expressed that way would have no answer for a deployment with accumulated memory on a PVC, and because RockBot ships as NuGet packages as well as an image, we can't gate that on an init container.

This adds the mechanism before we hit that wall.

**Contracts** (`RockBot.Host.Abstractions` — no new package; every store interface already lives there):
- `ISchemaMigration` — one forward step for one store
- `StoreSchemaDescriptor` — enrols a store: name, expected version, path resolver
- `StoreSchemaMarker` / `SchemaMigrationContext` / `SchemaMigrationOptions`

**Runtime** (`RockBot.Host`): `SchemaMigrationService` is registered as the first `IHostedService` in `AddRockBotHost`, so it runs before any store reads its data.

| On disk | Action |
| --- | --- |
| No marker, dir empty/absent | Stamp `CurrentVersion` — a new store |
| No marker, dir holds data | Assume `LegacyVersion`, run pending migrations |
| `marker < CurrentVersion` | Run migrations in order, re-stamp after **each** step |
| `marker > CurrentVersion` | Warn, leave untouched, continue |
| Marker names a different store | Warn, skip |

Forward-only. A gap or an ambiguity in the migration chain aborts startup — a store this build can't read safely is worse than one that won't boot. Stamping per step means an interrupted upgrade resumes rather than replaying.

**The marker filename is load-bearing.** `.rockbot-schema` is deliberately dot-prefixed and extension-less: `FileMemoryStore` and `FileSkillStore` build their indexes by enumerating `*.json` recursively beneath their root (and `FileFeedbackStore` does the same for `*.jsonl`), so a `_version.json` would have been picked up and reported as a corrupt entry. There's a test that proves the marker is invisible to the real `FileMemoryStore` index walk.

**Enrolled stores** — `memory`, `skills`, `feedback`, `wisp`, each from the `With*`/`Add*` extension that registers it, so a consumer who never opts into a store never gets a marker for it. All four at version 1 with **no migrations shipped**: the first boot after this change stamps four markers and changes nothing else.

**Consumer API:**
```csharp
builder.AddStoreSchema("my-store", currentVersion: 2, sp => "/data/my-store");
builder.AddSchemaMigration<MyV1ToV2>();
builder.ConfigureSchemaMigrations(o => o.DryRun = true);
```

**Docs:** `design/schema-migrations.md` — the additive-vs-destructive policy, the startup table, how to write and enrol one, and the hosted-service ordering caveat (constructors have already run, which is why migrations get a *path*, not a store service). Linked from `design/architecture.md`; short entry added to `CLAUDE.md`.

## Answers to the issue's open questions

- **Where does the registry live?** `RockBot.Host.Abstractions` — no new NuGet package to add to the release train.
- **CLI?** Not in this PR. `SchemaMigrationOptions.DryRun` lets an operator boot report-only, which covers the need without a new verb. `dotnet rockbot migrate` left open.
- **How to test end-to-end?** 14 unit tests here; fixtures of old on-disk state left open until there's a real migration to exercise them with.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet test RockBot.slnx` — 21 assemblies, 3147 passed, 0 failed
- [x] 14 new tests in `SchemaMigrationRunnerTests`: new store, legacy store, multi-step chain ordering, forward-compat, chain gap, ambiguous step, dry run, disabled, mid-chain failure leaves the marker at the last completed step, foreign marker, corrupt marker, multi-store
- [x] Marker invisibility verified against a real `FileMemoryStore`, not a stub
- [ ] First boot on the cluster should log four "no schema marker … a new store" lines (or "existing data" for the populated ones) and stamp v1; the second boot should be silent

Closes #308

## ENV2：新機器環境（MySQL 9.7.2）＋ `db/seeds.rb` 平台字典缺口

**對應規格／文檔**：`docs/handoff/2026-09-07-新機環境與seeds字典ENV2.md`（handoff ①②③④）、`docs/worklog/2026-09-07-新機環境與seeds字典ENV2.md`、`docs/dev/external-facts.md` §G56、`docs/specs/91-pit-register.md` §3.98、`docs/dev/m0-rails-skeleton.md`「Seeds 狀態」段、`docs/handoff/新機器接手-環境安裝.md`、接手指令第 1／3 步。

author: goshacodes
body:
Adds end-to-end coverage for the OIDC hybrid flow (`response_type=code id_token`), which was previously touched by only one negative test (`prompt=none` fragment error). Also documents two real implementation gaps found while verifying behavior against the code rather than assuming it.

## Tests added (3, `HybridFlowSpec`)
1. **Full interactive hybrid login** — code + id_token land in the URL **fragment** (not query); id_token `nonce` matches the sent value; `c_hash` == left-half-SHA256(fragment code) per OIDC Core §3.3.2.11; `iss`/`aud`/`sub`/`exp` are correct; the fragment code exchanges successfully at `/token` and the resulting access token's `userinfo.sub` matches the id_token's `sub`.
2. **Hybrid without `nonce` is accepted but the id_token omits the `nonce` claim** — documents actual (non-compliant) behavior; see findings below.
3. **A protocol error during hybrid (missing `code_challenge`) is returned in the fragment, never the query** — generalizes the sole pre-existing hybrid negative test beyond `login_required`.

## Implementation findings (please review)
- **Hybrid support is exactly `code id_token`.** `AuthorizeRequestParser` matches only the literal strings `"code"` and `"code id_token"` — `token`, `code token`, `code id_token token`, bare `id_token` are all `unsupported_response_type`.
- **⚠️ Nonce is not enforced for hybrid.** Parsed as `Option[Nonce]`, never validated as required; `UserInfoService` just omits the claim when absent. This is the same class of gap recently found and fixed in the unit-test analog (`AuthorizeEndpointServiceSpec`) — the server is OIDC-non-compliant here (OIDC Core requires nonce for the implicit/hybrid flows) but silently accepts the request instead of rejecting it. Test #2 locks down current behavior as a regression guard; **recommend filing a follow-up to make nonce mandatory for hybrid** in `AuthorizeRequestParser`/`AuthorizeEndpointService`.
- **No per-client response-type allow-list exists.** `OAuthClientRecord` has no such field and the parser never checks one, so "a client not registered for hybrid → unauthorized_client" (in the original task brief) does not correspond to any real behavior and was not written as a test — documented in the spec instead.

## `OAuthClient.scala` changes (additive only, ~24 lines)
- `authorizeRaw(...)`: one new optional trailing parameter `nonce: Option[String] = None`.
- `SubmitResult.assertFragmentRedirect`: new method (+ matching `Task[SubmitResult]` extension) mirroring the existing `assertFragmentErrorRedirect`, but extracting `code`+`id_token` on success instead of an error.
- No existing lines modified.

## Mutation checks (both reverted, production byte-identical to HEAD)
- Prefixed the nonce claim with `"MUTATED-"` in `UserInfoService` → test #1 failed with a clear diff. Reverted, re-ran → passed.
- Forced `redirectUriWithErrorParams` to always use the query instead of the fragment → test #3 AND the pre-existing `AuthorizeNegativeSpec` hybrid negative test both failed correctly. Reverted, rebuilt, re-ran both → 11/11 passed. `git diff` vs HEAD across `auth/`, `central/`, `edge/`, `util/` confirmed empty.

## Test results
`sbt e2e/test` run 3× against a live database: **97/97 passing** each time (94 pre-existing + 3 new).

author: kaeawc
body:
## Root cause

`test/features/observe/DetectIntentChooser.test.ts` constructed `DetectIntentChooser` without overriding its ADB dependency, so `BaseVisualChange`'s constructor built a **real** `AdbClient` via `defaultAdbClientFactory`.

`DetectIntentChooser.execute()` runs through `BaseVisualChange.observedInteraction()`, which (for an Android device) calls:

```ts
if (typeof this.adb.getDeviceTimestampMs === "function") {
  return this.adb.getDeviceTimestampMs();
}
```

That resolves to `AdbClient.getDeviceTimestampMs()`, which spawns a real `adb shell date +%s%3N` subprocess against the test's device id (`emulator-5554`), which does not exist in the unit-test environment. This real IO usually returns/fails fast enough to be invisible, but under parallel load (`turbo run test`) it occasionally took long enough to trip the per-test timeout (5s isolated / 20s under turbo), always surfacing on the first `execute()` test in the `describe` block even though every non-spied `execute()` test in the file was exposed to the same real-IO path.

All of the test's other collaborators (`observeScreen`, `window`, `awaitIdle`, `deepLinkManager`) were already faked — only `adb` (a public field on `BaseVisualChange`) was left pointing at the real client.

## Fix

Inject a `FakeAdbExecutor` as `detectIntentChooser.adb` in `beforeEach`, matching the existing pattern in `test/features/observe/Idle.test.ts` and other `BaseVisualChange`-derived feature tests. `FakeAdbExecutor.getDeviceTimestampMs()` resolves synchronously (from a configured value or `Date.now()`), so `observedInteraction()` never touches a real process.

## Validation

- `bun test test/features/observe/DetectIntentChooser.test.ts` — 5x isolated runs, all 9 pass in ~170ms total, no hangs.
- 3x concurrent parallel invocations of the same file (simulating turbo load) — all pass.
- `bun test test/features/observe/` — 2381 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bunx turbo run build` — all clean (only pre-existing baselined warnings).

Closes #6173
Closes #6174

author: fomotsar-commits
body:
## What this is

A new Anchor program, `programs/bayla-ladder`: the Solana port of `contracts/src/LighthouseLadder.sol`. Synthetix's reward engine with boosted weight as its divisor and multiplier, the 7d→4y / 0.40×→4.00× ladder (TOWELI parity), and **three exits** — matured, early (−25%, rewards paid), and an emergency hatch that declares **no reward vault** so nothing on the reward side can ever stop it.

Owner decisions encoded: **build the hatch** (the search for battle-tested code came up genuinely empty — 57 programs scanned, 18 refuted, and kfarms' penalty engine has never charged anyone in three years); **reload every 90 days, distribute per second** (`REWARDS_DURATION_SECS = 90d`, per-second `reward_rate`, Synthetix remainder fold-in).

## Why

The rented rail produced two distinct principal-hostage failures in a fortnight — Streamflow 6012 on a dry vault and 6000 when a position's cumulative counter passes u64::MAX (42.4% of all live entries on that program already had). Neither is fixable from outside. Owning the program makes THE PRINCIPAL PROMISE a property of the code.

## The invariants (the audit surface)

The venue's last custom staking contract failed on liability outrunning backing 4× (`docs/RESTAKING_BONUS_INSOLVENCY_2026_08_27.md`); four of five internal lenses missed it. Here that is four properties that **only hold together**:

- **I-1** `stake_vault.amount >= total_principal` after every principal move — `total_principal` is a tracked scalar, never derived from a vault a stranger can top up
- **I-2** `payable = min(owed, reward_vault)`; the remainder **stays owed** — never zeroed, never a revert (a revert here *is* Streamflow 6012)
- **I-3** a new period draws only on `reward_vault − (emitted − paid)` (AUDIT C2)
- **I-12** two vaults, always; no reward instruction is handed the stake vault; the hatch is never handed the reward vault

Plus I-5/6 (u128 everywhere, saturating, narrowed once at the transfer), I-7 (closed positions are **deleted** — every EVM critical began with a record that outlived its close), I-9 (`weight <= total_weighted` before the multiply — what makes the 1e12 headroom analysis true), I-10 (`received = post − pre`), I-11 (dust-divisor floor), I-13 (raise-only timelocked cap), I-14 (pay before close, AUDIT C1), I-15 (clocks aren't monotone). Full list in the `lib.rs` header.

**Deliberately absent:** `pause`, sweep-to-treasury, `recover_tokens`, `relock`, permissionless `decay`, `set_penalty`, `set_ladder`, `close_pool`. Penalty and ladder are compile-time constants.

## Verification status — read this before reviewing

**`math.rs` is proven on the host. The Anchor layer compiles green in CI. Nothing has run on a validator yet.**

`math.rs` is dependency-free and runs under bare `rustc --test`: **19 tests green**. Every test was **mutation-checked before being trusted** — penalty 25→20% (1 red), `payable` narrowing blindly (2 red), no dust floor (1), `fundable` ignoring what's owed (1), reload discarding the remainder (1), and `earned` wrapping instead of saturating — **which survived the first test** and forced a stronger one (now 1 red on either the multiply or the subtraction wrapping alone).

**`lib.rs`, `state.rs`, `token.rs` — CI is the only place they can compile** (Application Control blocks `anchor` and `cargo build-sbf` on the dev box, as tegridy-launch's header documents). History of that gate on this PR:

- **First run (`e8176769`)**: compiled clean; the build step's SBF stack-frame guard then fired — `Exit::try_accounts` at **4152 bytes against the 4096 frame, over by 56**. None of the three Anchor-macro shapes flagged as risky (position `init` seeded on an `init_if_needed` sibling's field, `token::token_program` on the vault inits, `address = … @ err` on a Signer) was a problem.
- **Second run (`5ee028c0`)**: every `Account`/`InterfaceAccount` in every Accounts struct boxed (44 fields — cp-swap's own idiom, and the migration-rehearsal job's own hint text). **`bayla-ladder` job green end to end**: math → `cargo build-sbf` (494,856-byte `.so`, artifact asserted) → layout and error-code pins. The hand-summed sizes (Pool 508, Position 141, UserStats 94) and error positions were right.

**What has NOT happened:** no instruction has executed against a validator; no integration test exists yet (needs the SBF toolchain — CI only); no human has read the Anchor layer end to end; no audit. Treat it accordingly. The CI job (`bayla-ladder`) mirrors `launch-curve`.

`token.rs` transfer helpers are cp-swap's, copied verbatim. The mint gate is an **allowlist** — exactly BAYLA's two inert metadata extensions; transfer-fee, hook, permanent-delegate and a freeze authority are refused at `initialize_pool`.

## Not in this PR

- A real program id (placeholder `GKwgTQtV…`, keypair outside the repo) and the deployer key (fail-closed System-program sentinel, same convention as tegridy-launch)
- Integration tests against a local validator with BAYLA's mint cloned — needs the SBF toolchain
- The upgrade authority decision (Squads + timelock, or immutable) — **must be settled before deploy**; the current BAYLA pool admin is a bare on-curve keypair
- Client wiring, the audit RFQ scope, devnet soak

Independent of #444 (no shared files); the two can merge in either order.

author: damiensy
body:
Implements `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-13-http-transport-and-token-admin.md` in full (all 8 tasks), so UnifiMCP can run as a persistent network service instead of only as a local stdio subprocess.

## What this adds

- **`TokenStore`** (`src/unifi_mcp/tokens.py`) — SQLite in WAL mode, shared by two processes. argon2 password hashes; tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes, so a raw token is visible exactly once at creation.
- **Streamable HTTP transport** (`src/unifi_mcp/server/_http.py`) — `POST/GET /mcp` behind `BearerAuthMiddleware`, plus an unauthenticated `GET /healthz` for the Docker healthcheck. Fails closed: an unreadable token DB rejects every request rather than allowing any.
- **`MCP_TRANSPORT` dispatch** — `stdio` remains the default, so existing Claude Desktop setups are untouched. `http` selects the new transport.
- **Token-admin service** (`src/unifi_mcp/admin/`) — a small Starlette + Jinja2 UI on port 8766. Root is env-var only with no `accounts` row, so it structurally cannot own a token; it exists to provision accounts, and each person mints and revokes their own.
- **Deployment** — both services run from one image separated only by `command:`, sharing a named volume for the token DB. Adds a QNAP compose file pinned to ghcr.io and a deployment guide.

## Two defects found while implementing

**1. Admin login 500'd whenever root was unconfigured.** `check_root_credentials` did `os.environ["ROOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD"]`, but `login_submit` calls it on *every* login attempt — including regular-account logins that have nothing to do with root. An unset root password raised `KeyError` and took down the login page. It now fails closed; `main()` still hard-fails at startup, which is the right layer for a required-config check.

**2. The container crash-looped on startup.** The Dockerfile ran `uv pip install -e .`, re-resolving dependencies at build time. With `mcp>=1.0.0` unpinned that pulled **mcp 2.1.1**, whose low-level `Server` API no longer exposes `list_tools`:

```
AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools'
```

starlette and uvicorn drifted the same way (1.6.0 / 0.52.4 against the tested 0.50.0 / 0.38.0). The image now installs from `uv.lock`, and `mcp` is pinned `<2`. Worth noting the test suite passed throughout — this was only visible by actually running the container.

## Verification

- **323 tests pass** (up from 277 on master); `ruff check .` clean; `ruff format --check .` reports 96 files already formatted.
- **Verified against a running container**, not just the test suite: 11/11 checks covering `/healthz`, 401 on missing/bogus/revoked tokens, root login, account provisioning, token minting, and an authenticated MCP `initialize` round-trip returning `serverInfo.name = unifi-mcp`.
- Image contents confirmed as the tested dependency set: mcp 1.28.1, starlette 0.50.0, uvicorn 0.38.0.
- Multi-arch build validated for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.

## Third defect: `/mcp` returned a 307 redirect

`Mount("/mcp")` only matches `/mcp/...`, so a bare `POST /mcp` — the URL documented for clients — returned `307 Temporary Redirect` instead of serving the request. Clients that don't follow redirects on POST fail outright; the rest pay an extra round-trip.

This survived the first round of tests because Starlette's `TestClient` follows redirects by default, so an in-process check reported 200 while `curl` against the container got 307. Only running the real container exposed it. Fixed with a small ASGI path-normalising middleware, and the new test disables redirect-following so it cannot go green falsely again.

## Not done

The image has **not** been pushed to ghcr.io and nothing is deployed to the NAS. Pushing needs a token with `write:packages`; the current `gh` OAuth token lacks it and ghcr.io rejects the push with `permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes`.

Deployment steps are in `docs/qnap-deployment.md`.

## Security note

Both ports serve plain HTTP, so admin passwords and freshly minted tokens cross the LAN in cleartext. This is an explicit non-goal of the accompanying spec, not an oversight. A valid token also grants every mutating tool the server exposes (device restarts, firewall changes) — there is no per-token scoping.

author: kvnlng
body:
Fixes #348.

## What

Relicenses Isocenter from AGPL-3.0-or-later to Apache-2.0, effective from the release after 0.9.2. Every place the license is named moves together, and the two contract tests now pin all of them:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `LICENSE` | Canonical Apache License 2.0 text, fetched from apache.org |
| `NOTICE` | New. Copyright line and the non-retroactivity statement. setuptools ships `NOTICE*` under its default `license_files`, and the built wheel carries both files (verified: `isocenter-0.9.2.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE` and `.../NOTICE`, `License-File:` for each in METADATA) |
| `setup.py` | `license="Apache-2.0"` and `License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License` |
| `.zenodo.json` | `apache-2.0`, verified against `zenodo.org/api/vocabularies/licenses/apache-2.0` on 2026-09-06 |
| `CITATION.cff` | `license: Apache-2.0` |
| `docs/developer_guide.md` | The Zenodo vocabulary note keeps its lesson with the new id as the example |
| `README.md` | New License section, since the README is the PyPI project page |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Unreleased entry with the reasoning and the non-retroactivity statement |
| `tests/test_packaging_contract.py` | Pins LICENSE text, the SPDX field, the classifier, and now `CITATION.cff` together; also asserts the AGPL text and classifier are gone |
| `tests/test_version_contract.py` | Pins the Zenodo id |

## Why

The reasoning is in #348 and in the CHANGELOG entry. Short form: a library is adopted by being imported, every dependency is MIT, BSD, or Apache, and AGPL only earns its adoption cost as the open half of a dual-licensing model that does not exist. Apache-2.0 over MIT for the patent grant institutional reviewers look for.

## What does not change

- **Copyright.** Sole author; the 138 empty-identity commits are MkDocs deploys on `gh-pages`, and GitHub lists one contributor. No consent needed.
- **Past releases.** 0.9.2 and earlier stay AGPL-3.0-or-later. The change is not retroactive and every artifact says so.
- **`pyproject.toml`.** Still build-system only, by the decision recorded in its comment, so the license goes out as the `License:` field plus classifier rather than a PEP 639 `License-Expression`. setuptools 84 warns that license classifiers are deprecated; it warned identically about the AGPL classifier, so nothing new.

## Testing

- TDD: both contract tests were rewritten first and failed for the right reason (`'agpl-3.0-or-later' == 'apache-2.0'`, AGPL text present), then went green after the change.
- Full suite on the committed state: see the checks on this PR; the local run is recorded in the final comment.
- Wheel built and inspected for the license files and METADATA lines above.

## For the merger

This is the outward-facing change in the promotion kit, so the merge is deliberately left to you. The next Zenodo record picks up the new id at the next GitHub Release; nothing to do there.
