author: bsletten
body:
## The defect

`ikigai-vocab` 0.1.66 could not be released. Its manifest claimed

```toml
ikigai-core = { path = "../ikigai-core", version = "0.1" }
```

while `crates/ikigai-vocab/src/lib.rs` calls `ikigai_core::escape_iri_fragment`
at `:78`, `:167`, `:232` and `:259` — a free function **added in 0.1.66 by #99**.
`^0.1` is satisfied by 0.1.65, which does not have it, so the release preflight's
packaging dry-run failed with `error[E0425]: cannot find function
escape_iri_fragment in crate ikigai_core`.

Constitution rule 5: a version pin states the true minimum API you use.

## Why every gate stayed green

The **path** dependency satisfies the call inside this workspace, so `fmt`,
`clippy`, `test`, the wasm check and CI were all green against a pin that cannot
resolve on crates.io. **A pin too HIGH fails locally and instantly; a pin too LOW
is invisible until release day.**

Worth stating because it bounds how far our newer instruments reach:
`resolve-drift.py` skips `ikigai-*` deps by design, and the ecosystem-drift
fresh-build resolves workspace members through their path deps. Neither can see
this class. Only the packaging dry-run can.

And it was about to get *more* hidden: once core 0.1.66 is on crates.io, `^0.1`
resolves to it and vocab builds again — while the pin stays a lie that breaks
anyone pinning core lower or resolving minimal versions.

## The change

- `ikigai-vocab` → `version = "0.1.66"`, with the trailing comment naming what it
  buys (`escape_iri_fragment`, the IRI-position escaping #99 added) and why it is
  a hard floor: a missing free function is E0425, not a silent behavior change.
- **Audited the other two intra-workspace pins instead of assuming them.**
  `ikigai-store`'s `ikigai-core = "0.1"` and its `ikigai-vocab = "0.1"` dev-pin
  are both **honest**, proven two ways: `git log -S` puts the introducing commit
  of every item either crate names from the other in the 0.0.0 pre-release era,
  and a standalone copy of the store lib compiles clean against
  `ikigai-core = "=0.1.0"`. Both pins now carry a comment recording the audit and
  its re-audit trigger, so the next reader does not repeat the archaeology.
- Those three are the whole set — no other member of this workspace depends on an
  ikigai crate.

No version bump: 0.1.66 is already on main and unpublished, so this rides it.

## Gates

- `just … gates` green: fmt · clippy · test, plus both extra CI commands
  (wasm `cargo check`, `tools/walkthrough/generate.py --check` — 40 anchors
  across 17 files).
- Acceptance gate is the release preflight for `ikigai-vocab` reaching READY;
  that is the only gate that can see this defect. It needs `ikigai-core` 0.1.66
  on crates.io first (Brian is publishing it now).

author: yemfan
body:
`title="…"` and `title={…}` are the same tooltip to the reader and two different shapes to a regex, and `COPY_ATTRS` only ever matched the first. A braced attribute was therefore somewhere English could sit inside a fully translated file and come back clean — which is how the five literals in #1596 shipped. They were not five.

This teaches `residualEnglish` to walk `attr={` to its partner brace and read the string literals inside. **40 findings across 18 internationalised files**, all now keys in both locales.

## What was English

| file | what the reader saw |
|---|---|
| `OutboundCallPanel`, `BulkCallPanel` | every search/loading placeholder, plus both call-purpose examples |
| `SalesOutreachComposer` | the three contact-search placeholders |
| `PlaybooksPanel` | the four task-button tooltips (select / deselect / mark complete / incomplete) |
| `ScriptGenerator` | `aria-label` on both copy buttons — what a screen reader announces |
| `AiEmailModal`, `AiSmsModal` | subject, body and both compose placeholders |
| `ShareReport`, `CustomerSupportChat`, `IdxLeadCaptureModal` | the input placeholders |
| `RevenuePanel`, `AccountantClient`, `SphereContactProfile` | KPI hints |
| `CalendarClient`, `AdCampaignWizard`, `ServiceAreasPicker`, `PlaybooksPageClient`, postcard animations | one tooltip / alt / label each |

`more.playbooks.cancel` already existed with exactly the right value, so that site reuses it rather than adding a duplicate.

## Three guards pay for the widening

Each is a real false positive from this app, not a hypothesis:

- **a comparison operand** — `status === "needs review"` is a database enum, and two lowercase words over six characters is indistinguishable from a label by any rule in `isCopy`;
- **a `cn(...)` argument** — Tailwind, not English;
- **a `defaultValue:`** — the documented way to ship a key ahead of its translation. `missingKeys` exempts the same shape by name, and both instances here (`assistants.actionsAria`, `ask_max_band.avatar_alt`) resolve in both locales, which is what makes them fallbacks rather than copy.

## Two notes on what the scan does not do

**It tokenizes rather than pattern-matches**, because a regex cannot do this. `'e.g. "How was your home tour?"'` is ONE single-quoted string containing two double quotes: a `"…"` rule reports its middle, and a `'…'` rule bolted alongside pairs the apostrophes in `"You've hit this period's cap."` and reports the code between them.

**Template literals are skipped whole.** They are copy too — I counted 48 — but they arrive spliced around their `${…}` holes and each needs a `t()` with interpolation rather than a swap. That is the next layer, not this one. The most visible are `SphereMonetizationPanel`'s `aria-label` and `ShowingDetailClient`'s card title.

The straight double quote had to join the accepted body characters for the tokenizer's sake, and it is scoped to **attribute literals only** via `ATTR_BODY`. In `BODY` itself it is a disaster: a JSX text node is bounded by `}` and `{` as well as by tags, so `} from "next"; import Link from "next/link"; import {` becomes copy and the scan goes from 40 findings to **1956** — every import line in the app. An attribute literal is already known to be a string, so a quote inside one is punctuation; inside a text node it is usually source.

## Verification

- i18n guards: 15 files / 82 tests pass. `residualEnglish` now carries 12 self-tests, 5 of them new — both ternary arms, the three excluded code shapes, the cross-quote cases, the template-literal skip, and the nested brace.
- Full `leadsmartai` suite: 2255 passed, 4 failed — all four in `lib/marketing-hub/`, untouched here and byte-identical to `origin/main`.
- Typecheck: errors confined to `lib/boss/runs/engine.ts`, `lib/boss/tools/types.ts`, `lib/marketing-hub/config.ts`, `lib/sanitizeHtml.ts` — same four, also identical to `origin/main`, all of the known local-worktree kind. None of the 18 edited components appears.

author: aviliof5
body:
## Qué es (y qué NO es)

**No es** "modo offline" completo — no hay sincronización bidireccional ni resolución de conflictos, y no es para "sin internet por días". **Sí es** resiliencia a la conexión intermitente/lenta real de un gimnasio con mal wifi/datos: el pedido concreto era que un cliente pueda seguir entrenando y que el staff pueda seguir viendo quién pagó, aunque la señal falle justo en ese momento.

## Núcleo nuevo — `src/offline.js`

- **`queueAction`/`flushQueue`**: una cola en localStorage para escrituras que fallaron por la red. Se reintentan solas, **en orden**, cuando vuelve la señal (evento `online`, al arrancar la app, y cada 20s en segundo plano — con mala señal el navegador no siempre dispara esos eventos).
- **`saveSnapshot`/`loadSnapshot`**: última copia buena de una lectura, para caer ahí en vez de romper la pantalla — siempre marcada como "puede estar desactualizada".

## Dónde se aplicó

| Dónde | Qué pasa sin señal |
|---|---|
| Modo entrenamiento (empezar, marcar series, terminar) | El ID de la sesión se elige en el celular (`newUuid()`) antes de saber si hay señal — se puede entrenar la sesión ENTERA sin conexión; todo se encola en orden y se sincroniza solo. |
| Check-in (manual y QR) | Se encola si falla, con el mismo "✓ Hoy" de siempre. |
| Confirmar un cobro **ya generado** (manual y QR del cliente) | Se encola igual — el pago ya tiene ID, no hace falta señal para eso. |
| Panel de dueño/admin (`enterOwnerDash`, de ahí sale "quién pagó") | Antes UN fallo tumbaba las 9 lecturas juntas. Ahora cada una cae a su última copia guardada por separado, con aviso "mostrando la última info guardada". |

**A propósito NO cubre** generar un cobro **nuevo** sin señal (el ID lo asigna el servidor — cambiar eso es más riesgo tratándose de dinero) ni el chequeo de "¿ya me aprobaron?" de un administrador (ese sí necesita señal real, no una copia vieja) — ver comentarios en el código.

## Verificación

Probado en el mock simulando "sin señal" (forzando que `BolaAPI` tire errores de red) y confirmando en la base simulada, no solo en el estado en memoria:
- Entrenamiento completo (sesión + varias series + cierre) encolado y sincronizado con el peso/ejercicio correctos — **incluso sobreviviendo una recarga de página** a mitad de camino.
- Check-in encolado y confirmado.
- Cobro confirmado por botón manual y por escaneo del cliente (con su validación de dueño/estado intacta).
- Panel de dueño abriendo con la última copia guardada cuando `clients.listForGym` falla, y volviendo a datos frescos apenas la red se restablece.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

- AC-4 scaffolding: `agentcore/` config pointing the `@aws/agentcore` CLI (0.28.1, devDependency) at the AC-1 agent service for AgentCore Runtime deployment — no changes to `src/agent-service/` or `src/agent-core/` (frozen per packet).
- Every field name was verified, not guessed: against the CLI's own zod schemas (`agent-env.js`, `agentcore-project.js`, `aws-targets.js`) and the pinned docs (get-started-cli, service-contract, http-protocol-contract). `npx agentcore validate` → **Valid**.
- Two packet assumptions were corrected by evidence and documented in the README provenance table: the field is `protocol: "HTTP"` (not `serverProtocol`), the entry field is `entrypoint` and the bundled file must be named `main.ts`; there is **no standalone `build` command** in 0.28.1 (packaging happens inside `deploy`; local credential-free validation is `agentcore validate`); microVM compute has no config field (the lifecycle timeout does).
- Deploy stays **manual (Joe, AC-5)**; CI never makes AWS calls. `aws-targets.json` carries a schema-valid **placeholder** account (`000000000000`) with the replace-before-deploy warning in its `description` field.

## Files

- `agentcore/agentcore.json` — `who_decides_agent`: CodeZip, NODE_22, HTTP, `networkMode PUBLIC`, `lifecycleConfiguration.idleRuntimeSessionTimeout 600`, `sessionStorage /mnt/data` (one-level mount rule; service uses `/mnt/data/agent` beneath it), non-secret `envVars` (`WD_AGENT_PORT=8080`, `WD_AGENT_DATA_DIR=/mnt/data/agent`, `WD_PROVIDER=bedrock` per RULING M4).
- `agentcore/aws-targets.json` — `who-decides-dev`, us-east-1, placeholder account.
- `agentcore/.env.local.example` — every env var the agent service reads (`server.ts`, `machine-auth.ts`, `provider.ts`), no secrets; `WD_MACHINE_TOKEN_HASH` generation command included.
- `agentcore/app/who-decides-agent/main.ts` — glue entry (the node CodeZip packager hard-codes `<codeLocation>/main.ts`); starts the exported AC-1 server on `0.0.0.0:8080` only if its own direct-run guard has not already started it. Nested under `agentcore/` to avoid the Next.js `app/` router dir.
- `agentcore/README.md` — file purposes, deploy sequence, field-provenance table, residual risks.
- Wiring: `.gitignore` negation for the env template (`.env.local` stays ignored), `tsconfig` include for the glue, `@aws/agentcore` devDependency + lockfile.

## Residual risks for AC-5 (recorded, not fixed — src/ frozen)

1. `/ping` returns `{ok:true,…}` not the documented `{"status":"Healthy"}` body — endpoints/port/status match; body schema may need a small service change if the platform validates it.
2. The node CodeZip packager esbuild-bundles the entry graph with no externals mechanism; `src/consumption/store.ts` imports `better-sqlite3` (native addon) — deploy-time packaging may fail until externalized.
3. `server.ts` loads `fixtures/patch-scenario.json` from CWD at import; the CodeZip zip ships only the bundle — deployed boot needs an env-overridable/lazy fixture path.
4. `aws-targets.json` account is a placeholder that MUST be replaced before deploy.

## Validation

- `npx agentcore validate` → `Valid` (exit 0), config-shape proof (no AWS creds needed).
- `JSON.parse` passes for both JSON files.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `npm test` → **100/100 pass, 0 fail** (nothing existing broke).
- `npm install` succeeded with the new devDependency.
- No AWS calls made; no deploy; no secrets committed (`git check-ignore` verifies `agentcore/.env.local` is refused).

Closes #20 scope item AC-4. PR targets `dev-agentcore` per packet.

## Summary by Sourcery

Prepare the repository for manually deploying the existing agent service to AWS AgentCore Runtime without changing the frozen service or core code.

New Features:
- Add AgentCore Runtime project scaffolding for deploying the existing who-decides agent service with HTTP, CodeZip, Node 22, session storage, and runtime environment configuration.
- Add an AgentCore CodeZip entry point that exposes the AC-1 service on the required runtime host and port.
- Provide deployment targets and a non-secret environment template for AgentCore setup.

Enhancements:
- Document AgentCore configuration field provenance, manual deployment workflow, validation commands, and known deployment risks.

Build:
- Add @aws/agentcore 0.28.1 as a development dependency and include the AgentCore glue entry point in TypeScript compilation.

Deployment:
- Add AgentCore runtime and AWS target configuration, including a schema-valid placeholder account that must be replaced before deployment.

Documentation:
- Add AgentCore scaffolding documentation covering file purposes, configuration decisions, deployment steps, and residual risks.

Tests:
- Validate the new AgentCore configuration and confirm TypeScript compilation and the existing test suite remain successful.

Chores:
- Preserve the existing agent service and core implementation while wiring them into the new deployment scaffold.

author: mastersingh24
body:
Two things the first real run of the dataplane pack on GKE found. Neither could have come from a unit test.

## 1. The pack could not be run whole at default flags

Every lease was 6m; `--subject-timeout` defaults to 10m. The harness refused the invocation:

```
error: these scenarios have faults shorter than --subject-timeout 10m0s:
  dataplane-latency-not-saturation (6m0s), dataplane-stress-real (6m0s), ...
```

It was right to. A lease that expires mid-investigation is cleared by the reaper and looks exactly like the subject having remediated it. The escape hatch is `--allow-short-faults`, which is precisely the flag that turns "the lease expired" into a score — and this is the pack most likely to be reached for with it, because its subjects are the slowest.

Six minutes was the wrong number anyway, for a reason specific to this pack. The gate alone can eat three of them: an SOT probe waits up to 60s for the substrate to prove it was healthy, the Settle probes up to 120s plus a dwell, and every one of them is a request rather than an object read. What is left has to cover a subject that cannot answer from `kubectl get` and has to go and measure traffic — which is the premise of the pack.

All six leases are now 12m, matching the scenarios in the other packs whose gates eat their lease. It costs a fast subject nothing: the lease is a ceiling, and chaos is cleared when the subject answers. `TestTheDataplanePackOutlastsTheDefaultSubjectTimeout` is the guard, deliberately scoped to this pack.

## 2. Deleted is not the same as gone, one layer further down

```
WARN harness: arena teardown failed scenario=dataplane-partition-one-way namespace=flow-payments
  error="arena: 1 simian-managed chaos resource(s) still active in \"flow-payments\"
  (NetworkChaos/simian-c6qdl); clear them first or pass --force"
```

`teardown` clears the faults and then destroys the arena. But `Clear` only issues a delete: the CR has a finalizer, and the controller has to undo what it did — take the iptables rules out, stop the stressors, put resolv.conf back — before the object leaves the API server. The arena refuses to be destroyed over live chaos, rightly. So the namespace was left standing, with a warning nobody reads until the next run collides with it.

Teardown now waits for the faults to actually be gone before destroying the arena, bounded at 30s. Bounded rather than patient: a controller that has not finished recovering in half a minute is not going to finish in the next two, and spending the whole teardown budget there would leave every *later* namespace behind as well. Better one warning than a suite's worth.

`TestTheArenaIsNotTornDownUntilTheChaosHasActuallyGone` reproduces it with a fake injector whose `Clear` returns before the object goes; `TestTeardownGivesUpOnAFaultThatWillNotClear` pins the other end.

## Floor run

```
harness
  scenarios        6
  manifested       6
  inject failures  0
  efficacy rate    1.00
```

Six scenarios, six manifested, every hand-written gate passing on a real GKE cluster — with the `noop:` subject, so the 0.00 scores are the floor and `hallucinated_fault 1.00` is a subject that invented nothing.

Side effect: `pkg/harness` tests went from 32s to 0.9s. `TestRemediationIsNotInferredFromSilence` was paying the full grace period, which is why it is a `Runner` field.

author: inso1337
body:
Closes #539

## Problem
`ownership.retention_summary` computes a monotone least fixpoint but drove it by recomputing **every** function body **every** round and rebuilding the whole visible-summary dict each round: O(F^2) per round over ~20 rounds x 553 bodies. The review measured it at 50-55% of check+lower on large inputs (1992ms on `selfhost/lower.rvl`).

## Change
Demand-driven **worklist** over the callee dependency graph:
- Precompute, per body, the module-fn callee names it depends on (`_callee_names` intersected with the fn set, minus names the body binds — the same shadowing `visible` applied).
- Each recompute reads a **shadow-view**: a copy holding only that body's callee summaries — exactly the keys `_summary_walk`/`_arg_retention` can look up. A missing key `.get()`s to `None` and defaults to "retains", identical to what the full `visible` dict did for a non-fn or shadowed callee.
- A body re-enters the worklist only when a callee it depends on gains retention.

A least fixpoint over a finite lattice is order-independent, so the summary reached is **byte-identical** to the round-based driver; only the evaluation schedule changed.

## Result
`selfhost/lower.rvl` (553 fns): **816ms -> 65ms, 12.5x** locally.

## Proof of identical output
`tests/test_retention_summary_worklist_539.py` keeps a **verbatim copy of the old round-based driver** as an oracle and asserts the shipping summary equals it on every function of the emit_py corpus + the self-host frontend (`lower.rvl` included) — 0 mismatches across 48 documents. A timing-sanity test guards against reverting to the quadratic form.

## Tests
- New equality/timing test: 38 passed.
- Ownership suites (`test_py_inplace_accumulation`, `test_ownership_f9_runtime_308`, `test_ownership_modes_308`, `test_selfhost_ownership_gap_308`, `test_swap_owner_abort`): 109 passed, 8 skipped.
- `test_selfhost_lower` + `test_selfhost_lower_ir`: passed (combined run exit 0).

No emitted-code (Rust/gate-crate) changes — the edit is confined to the Python analysis.

author: greenlemin
body:
⚡ Bolt: optimize lesson search index pre-computation and filtering

💡 What:
- Introduced a memoized `searchIndex` in `LearnClient.tsx` that pre-normalizes lowercased title, description, and category strings when lessons or locale change.
- Reordered filter logic to evaluate fast category (`activeCategory`) and difficulty (`activeDifficulty`) boolean matches first, short-circuiting before executing search query substring matching.

🎯 Why:
- Previously, filtering lessons on every keystroke executed `.toLowerCase()` on `title`, `description`, and `getCategoryLabel()` for every lesson in the array before checking category/difficulty filters.
- Pre-computing searchable strings avoids repeated lowercasing and label lookups on user keystrokes. Short-circuiting early prevents unnecessary string comparisons for lessons outside the active category or difficulty level.

📊 Impact:
- Reduces string allocations and CPU processing during real-time typing in the Learn catalog filter input.
- Eliminates redundant string operations when category or difficulty filters are active.

🔬 Measurement:
- Run `npm test` to verify `LearnClient.test.tsx` passes.
- Filter lessons by query in `/learn` and verify matching lessons render instantly without UI lag.

author: larszu
body:
Zwei Bedarfe, die an derselben Stelle zusammenlaufen: was eine `.mvr` trägt, und was sie nicht trägt.

---

## Bedarf 139 — Gruppen überleben die Übergabe

> MVR carries no fixture groups. Users „manually recreate complex grouping structures in each system they use". […] it „would significantly speed up the process of getting a console or a media server up and running quicker if you have a lot of complex groups on a rig".
>
> — belegt an [`mvrdevelopment/spec#295`](https://github.com/mvrdevelopment/spec/issues/295) (offen, 2026-01-13)

`FixtureGroup` steht seit jeher im Projekt — aber nur als **Auswahl-Bequemlichkeit auf der Zeichenfläche**. Die Gruppe hieß „Gruppe 3" (durchnummeriert, nie benannt), stand auf keinem Blatt, ging in keinen Export und war außerhalb des Canvas unsichtbar. Genau das beschreibt der Beleg: die Struktur ist da, sie überlebt nur die Übergabe nicht.

**Was dazukommt:** `src/core/fixtureGroups.ts`, ein Namensfeld je Gruppe im Ablauf-Dialog, das **Gruppen-Blatt (CSV)** (Gruppe, Kanal, Unit, Typ, Position — je Mitglied eine Zeile), und `npm run groups:check`.

**Die ehrliche Hälfte.** MVR kann Gruppen nicht tragen — das ist keine Lücke dieses Exports, sondern des Formats. Was sich schließen lässt, ist das Verschweigen. Dabei fiel eine zweite Sache auf: die Ehrlichkeit stand bisher für genau **einen** Fall im Dialog (die Traversen), weil den einmal jemand bemerkt hatte; Gruppen, Farbfolien, Zwecke und Notizen gingen daneben genauso verloren, ohne ein Wort. `mvrOmissions` **rechnet sie jetzt aus**. Jede Meldung nennt den Ausweg — eine Auslassung ohne Ausweg ist eine Entschuldigung —, und was **Absicht** ist (die Notizen bleiben nach Bedarf 71 im eigenen Projekt), liest sich nicht wie ein Mangel.

**Benannt statt leer:** „ohne Namen", ein Strich für einen fehlenden Kanal, und ein gelöschtes Mitglied verschwindet nicht still. Eine leere Gruppe steht trotzdem auf dem Blatt.

---

## Bedarf 144 — Austauschdateien, die an einer Umbenennung nicht zerbrechen

> Documented failure modes, all mundane and all silent: renaming the .vwx leaves the paperwork reading a stale .xml; **non-unique UIDs make a deleted fixture reappear**; „one undefined or corrupted character in a data field can invalidate the whole exchange .xml".
>
> — belegt am `showstack`-Datenblatt zu Lightwright (John McKernon Software, 2026-08-17), [`PeramatoG/Perastage#2157`](https://github.com/PeramatoG/Perastage/issues/2157) und `#2233`

**Zwei gemessene Defekte (2026-09-06):**

1. **Derselbe Plan ergab zweimal verschiedene UUIDs.** `fixtureXml` rief bei jedem Export `uuid()` neu auf. Wer eine geänderte `.mvr` nachimportiert, bekommt damit **keine** Aktualisierung, sondern lauter neue Objekte: die alten bleiben stehen, die neuen kommen dazu. Genau der Befund aus dem Beleg — „a deleted fixture reappears" —, nur von der anderen Seite.
2. **Zwei Typen, ein Dateiname.** „Source/Four" und „Source:Four" wurden beide zu `ETC_Source_Four.gdtf`; der Importer bekam für zwei Geräte denselben Bezug, ohne ein Wort. Dasselbe für Namen, die sich nur in der Groß-/Kleinschreibung unterscheiden — auf einem Mac-Dateisystem sind sie dieselbe Datei, und der Export überschreibt sich selbst.

**Was jetzt da ist:** `src/core/mvrIdentity.ts`. Die UUID wird aus Projekt- und Leuchten-id **abgeleitet** und überlebt damit Speichern, Neuladen und den Export von einem anderen Rechner. Der Projekt-Namensraum geht mit (sonst sieht ein Visualisierer, der zwei Pläne lädt, eine Leuchte statt zweier). GDTF-Dateinamen sind kollisionsfrei und deterministisch — der erste behält seinen Namen —, und die Kollision steht im Dialog. Das Archiv ist **reproduzierbar**: fester DOS-Zeitstempel statt der Uhr.

**Version 8, und das mit Absicht.** RFC 9562 hält Version 8 für herstellerdefinierte Layouts frei. Eine 4 hineinzuschreiben („zufällig erzeugt") wäre eine Aussage über die Herkunft dieser Bytes, die nicht stimmt: sie sind ausgerechnet, nicht gewürfelt.

---

## Geprüft

- `groups:check`, `identity:mvr` und die dreizehn übrigen Wächter grün, `tsc --noEmit` ohne Fehler, Lint ohne Fehler, Build grün
- **Gegenprobe 139: 20 eingespielte Defekte, alle rot** — u. a. das still verschwundene Mitglied, der als 0 gemeldete fehlende Kanal, die behauptete Auslassung ohne Anlass, der Template-i18n-Schlüssel
- **Gegenprobe 144: 15 eingespielte Defekte, alle rot** — u. a. die zurückgeholte Zufalls-UUID, die an der Reihenfolge statt an der Leuchte hängende Kennung, der Hash, der nur das untere Byte eines Zeichens sieht, die wieder eingebaute Uhr im Archiv, die still aufgelöste Namenskollision

body:
openssl ライブラリで、実 Ruby には存在するのに記載が無かった公開メソッドのドキュメントを追加します(refs #3548 の不足側・第 1 弾)。対象は `tools/method-coverage/` の実測で openssl の「文書済みクラスの公開メソッド不足」に挙がった 137 件と、ページはあるがメソッド記載が無かった `OpenSSL::PKey` のモジュール関数 5 件・`OpenSSL::OpenSSLError#errors` です。

## 追加したエントリ(137 メソッド・見出し 152 行・27 ファイル)

- `OpenSSL::PKey` モジュール関数 5(`read`・`generate_key`・`generate_parameters`・`new_raw_private_key`・`new_raw_public_key`)と `OpenSSL::PKey::PKey` 17(`sign_raw`/`verify_raw`/`verify_recover`・`encrypt`/`decrypt`・`derive`・`compare?`・`private_to_der`/`private_to_pem`/`public_to_der`/`public_to_pem`・`raw_private_key`/`raw_public_key`・`oid`・4.1 の `encapsulate`/`decapsulate`/`get_param`)
- `OpenSSL::PKey::RSA` 5(`set_key`・`set_factors`・`set_crt_params`・`sign_pss`・`verify_pss`)・`DSA` 2・`DH` 6・`EC.generate`・`EC::Point#add`/`#mul`/`#to_octet_string`
- `OpenSSL::SSL::SSLContext` 25(`add_certificate`・`alpn_protocols(=)`・`alpn_select_cb(=)`・`npn_*`・`ciphersuites=`・`sigalgs=`/`client_sigalgs=`・`ecdh_curves=`/`groups=`・`enable_fallback_scsv`・`keylog_cb(=)`・`min_version=`/`max_version=`・`security_level(=)`・`setup`・`tmp_dh=`・`verify_hostname(=)`)、`SSLSocket` 10(`alpn_protocol`・`npn_protocol`・`client_ca`・`close_read`/`close_write`・`export_keying_material`・`finished_message`/`peer_finished_message`・`ssl_version`・`tmp_key`)、`SocketForwarder` 10(`fileno`・`close_on_exec(=・?)`・`local_address`/`remote_address`・`timeout(=)`・`wait`/`wait_readable`/`wait_writable`)
- `OpenSSL.Digest`・`.fips_mode`・`.secure_compare`/`.fixed_length_secure_compare`、`OpenSSL::ASN1.EndOfContent`、`ASN1Data#indefinite_length(=)`(旧名 `infinite_length` と統合)、`BN` 6(`+@`・`-@`・`abs`・`mod_sqrt`・`get_flags`/`set_flags`)、`Buffering#getbyte`/`#readbyte`、`Cipher` 7(`auth_data=`・`auth_tag(=)`・`auth_tag_len=`・`authenticated?`・`ccm_data_len=`・`iv_len=`)、`Config.parse_config`、`Digest.digests`、`HMAC.base64digest`/`#base64digest`、OCSP 8(`BasicResponse#find_response`/`#responses`/`#to_der`・`CertificateId#hash_algorithm`/`#issuer_key_hash`/`#issuer_name_hash`/`#to_der`・`Request#signed?`)、`PKCS12#set_mac`、`PKCS7#to_text`、X509(`Certificate.load_file`/`#tbs_bytes`・`Extension#value_der`・`Name#to_utf8`・`Revoked#to_der`・4.1 の `CRL#by_serial`・`Store`/`StoreContext#flags`/`#clear_flags`)、`OpenSSLError#errors`

初出版が 3.0 より後のものは `#%since` で囲みました(3.1: openssl gem 3.0 / 3.2: 3.1 / 3.3: 3.2 / 3.4: 3.3 / 4.0: 4.0.0 / 4.1: master)。

## 既存記述の修正

- `OpenSSL::Config`: `#%until 3.1` のブロックに `[]`・`sections`・`to_s` が入っていましたが、これらは C 実装化後(Ruby 3.1 以降)も存在するのでゲート外に出しました。`section` の別名行と obsolete の注記だけ until を維持しています
- `OpenSSL::PKey::EC`: 正式名が未記載で別名だけ載っていた `generate_key!`(`generate_key`)・`private?`(`private_key?`)・`public?`(`public_key?`)の見出し行を既存エントリに追加。`to_pem` は正式名 `export` を追加し、「パスフレーズで暗号化できない」という記述を現行の `export(cipher = nil, pass = nil)` の仕様(SEC 1/RFC 5915 ECPrivateKey・cipher と pass で暗号化可)に書き換えました。`generate_key!` には OpenSSL 3.0 以降で利用できない旨を追記

## 対象外にしたもの

- `OpenSSL::SSL.verify_certificate_identity`/`verify_hostname`/`verify_wildcard`: 原典で `:nodoc:` のため
- `OpenSSL::Config#data`/`#set_section`/`.get_key_string`(3.0 のみの内部 API)・`OpenSSL::ASN1.take_default_tag`(3.4 のみの内部 API)

## 作業方法と検証

- 原典は openssl gem v4.0.0(4.1 分は master)の C ソースと lib/*.rb の rdoc・`History.md`。下書きは Claude のサブエージェントが作成し、実 Ruby 4.0.0 と master で全見出しの存在と引数の数を機械検証したうえで、原典と突き合わせて査読・修正しています
- lint 4 種 OK・3.0〜4.1 の 7 版で DB 生成+checklink 0 件・`#%since` の境界(例: `PKey.generate_key` 3.0 なし / 3.1 あり、`SSLContext#groups=` 3.4 なし / 4.0 あり、`OpenSSLError#errors` 3.4 なし / 4.0 あり)を lookup で確認

author: jakechampion
body:
Closes the first item of #8770. Two changes, one commit each, plus a doc entry.

## 1. `__fern_str_append_range` — the fusion

`acc = acc + slice_unchecked(s, lo, hi)` copied its bytes TWICE and allocated once: `__str_slice` built a fresh string block, then `__fern_str_append` memcpy'd it into the accumulator's slack and freed it. The new helper appends the range straight out of the source — one memcpy, no allocation.

It keeps every property of the plain in-place append:

- same eligibility guards on the accumulator, and the same CONSUMPTION of it, so the assignment's suppressed dec-on-overwrite still balances;
- the source is BORROWED, exactly as `__str_slice` borrowed it, and an owned-temp source (`slice_unchecked(f(x), lo, hi)`) keeps its stash-and-release;
- when the fast path is refused the fallback materialises the range through `__str_slice` and joins it as before, then releases both the accumulator and the slice — the refused case is byte-identical work;
- bounds are checked UP FRONT and trap through `__str_slice`'s own message. That is load-bearing: on the fast path no slice call is left to check them, so a range the unfused form rejected has to be rejected here, and the trap is tested on all four backends.

The source may BE the accumulator — `e = e + slice_unchecked(e, 0, 2)` passes one buffer as both operands — and that is safe without a `memmove` by construction rather than by luck: the range lies inside the accumulator's current length, which is exactly where the destination begins, so the two regions touch and never overlap.

Gated identically to `__fern_str_append` — wasm and native x86-64 only. Shapes that must NOT fuse, each with an ops-level test: arm64, which has no in-place append to fuse into and whose codegen is unchanged; a `Cell` read, which is owned only in the sense of carrying a retain on top of the reference the slot still holds (#8067); a join whose left operand is borrowed, which allocates its result anyway and so has no second copy to remove; a borrowed string parameter as the accumulator.

The SSA backends bump-allocate and never reclaim, so their lift expands the call back into the `__str_slice` + `__str_concat` pair — the same thing `ssaHelperName` already does for `__fern_str_append`. Without that a missing emitter there is a hard "call target the module never defines"; `TestX86_64SSABackendDifferential` still compares 217 programs against its floor of 215.

## 2. One size-class computation, not two

The grow-in-place guard asked whether the grown request classed the same as the old one and computed the capacity of BOTH. One suffices: the capacity function is monotone and idempotent, so `class(req_new) == class(req_old)` exactly when `req_new <= cap(req_old)`.

What that is worth depends on the tier, and the two ends are far apart. Below 2048 bytes the capacity IS the request, so a compare and a branch go. Above it — where an 8 KiB accumulator sits — a `bsr` plus seven more instructions on x86-64 and a whole `emitFreelistBin` expansion on wasm do. Measured: `examples/bench/string_build` never leaves the small tier and falls 0.27%, with exactly ten instructions off the emitted `.text` of every program that appends.

Proved rather than argued, in two places. `internal/codegen/x86_64/sizeclass_cap_test.go` checks the three properties the equivalence rests on over the whole 16-aligned request domain, densely either side of every large-tier grid point, then checks the equivalence itself at the two places it can break. And `TestX86_64StrAppendClassBoundary` pins the EMITTED guard: 2100 appends growing an accumulator across the 2048 tier change and through several large-tier classes, at its exact allocation count — which is the guard's decision sequence — with every byte verified by position.

## Measurements

x86-64, `-O`, this 4-core container, median of 9 runs, 8M iterations:

| probe | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `out = out + "$\n"` | 58 ms | 57 ms |
| `out = out + slice_unchecked(src, 0, 8)` | 183 ms | 101 ms |

So 10.2 ns off each slice append, against the 9.2 ns #8770 measured for the materialisation.

`coreutils/cat.fern` is not on main yet (it is in flight on the `coreutils-cat-tail-v2` branch), so `scripts/coreutils-bench cat` has nothing to run. I built that file with both compilers instead, over the same 8M-line 62 MiB input the issue used. Retired instructions, counted by callgrind on a 1M-line prefix, since wall time on this container has a σ of 4-60 ms per mode:

| mode | before | after | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | 142,367 | 142,108 | −0.2% |
| `-E` | 408,620,440 | 342,908,697 | **−16.1%** |
| `-v` | 509,596,765 | 457,452,933 | **−10.2%** |
| `-n` | 756,884,584 | 698,580,290 | **−7.7%** |
| `-s` | 85,257,108 | 85,257,631 | +0.0006% |

Wall time over the full 8M lines, hyperfine, mean ± σ: `-E` 300.6 ± 6.7 ms to 257.0 ± 3.4 ms, `-v` 395.1 ± 8.1 to 343.1 ± 4.9, `-n` 811.3 ± 53.9 to 630.2 ± 67.1. Output is byte-identical to GNU in every mode, before and after.

**cat is still well behind GNU and this does not change that.** `-E` goes from 4.4x to 3.8x GNU's time, `-v` from 4.3x to 3.7x, `-n` from 3.8x to 3.0x. The fusion removes about 5.5 ns of the roughly 28 ns per line `-E` spends — less than #8770 predicted, and worth saying why: cat's slices average under 8 bytes on this input, so `__str_slice` was already taking its inline path and the saving is the second copy and the call, not an allocation. Above the 7-byte threshold the allocation collapse is real — 500 appends of a 12-byte range go 633 to 266 allocations. Closing the rest needs a capacity-carrying builder type, which `docs/STRINGS-SOTA.md` §2.10 already names as the open question; `-s`, which does one append per RUN of lines rather than per line, is unmoved by design.

### The two advisory perf lanes warn, and none of it is this change

Both lanes report drift on this PR. I measured whether any of it is mine by running each bench in a worktree at `origin/main` and one at this branch, same container, same paths:

- **`selfhost-perf-x86_64`** warns `x86_64/checker.allocs` +7.53% and `.frees` +10.87%. The A/B says this change moves them by **−15 and −15** — 16,495,783 → 16,495,768 allocs, 13,468,253 → 13,468,238 frees, peak RSS identical to the byte. That baseline was last re-pinned 396 commits ago (70761c88c, 2026-09-05); the +7.5% is main's accumulated drift, and my merge base measures it too.
- **`perf-x86_64`** warns on `string_slice.ir`, `tokenize.{text,ir}` and the four `utf8_ingest_*` rows. `string_slice` and `tokenize` measure **identically** before and after here, so they are main's. The `utf8_ingest_*` rows this change moves by exactly **ten `.text` instructions** each — the one dropped size-class expansion — against a total drift of −1722 and −1732.

So I have deliberately NOT re-banked either baseline. Both lanes warn rather than fail (`ci-check-perf` exits 0 by design); re-banking here would put 396 commits of main's drift under this PR's name, and the `.ir` half does not reproduce across hosts in any case — three `string_*_byte.ir` rows differ ~50% between this container and the runner at the *merge base*, and CI does not flag them at all. Re-banking is a whole-file job against the merged head.

## Self-host

**Native-only, deliberately.** The self-host compiler has no in-place string append at all — its concat is always `op_str_concat`, allocate-and-copy — so there is no fused form for it to mirror; porting `__fern_str_append` first is goal-2 work, not this PR's. What IS mirrored is the one thing the parity gate requires: `examples/self_host/irverifyrc.fern`'s rc release set, which `TestSelfHostIRVerifyRcReleaseSetMatchesNative` compares entry-for-entry against `internal/ir/rcsigs.go`. `TestSelfHostFeatureCensus` and `TestSelfHostIRKindRegistry` are unmoved. Referencing #4451 for the native-only surface.

## Gates — all green locally

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `internal/ir` (whole package) | ok, 305 s |
| `internal/

author: peters
body:
## Purpose

Provide a complete, immutable local file bundle for the exact-base, two-layer
repository overlay model. This is a focused prerequisite for #383, not completion
of repository capture, transfer or remote checkpointing.

## Behavior

- Hash actual owned file bytes using the existing locked SHA-256 library; retain
  no spare vector allocation. Limit each file to 64 MiB and distinct payloads to
  128 MiB at this in-memory boundary.
- Require exactly one verified payload per distinct planned file hash. Reject
  missing, extra, duplicate, length-inconsistent or oversized content.
- Preserve staged versus working-tree contents, executable bits, literal links
  and removals; shared contents use one owned payload.
- Fingerprint repository identity, exact commit, optional branch and both ordered
  layers with a fixed version 1 canonical encoding. Debug/errors omit content,
  paths and identities.

No filesystem, Git, provider, network or configuration operation is added. A
fingerprint is not export approval, a signature, secret detection, an atomic
snapshot or safe materialization. Hashing belongs off the UI thread. Larger
overlays need a separate streaming boundary. The explicit SHA-256 dependency was
already resolved at the same version; the lockfile gains only one dependency edge.

## Validation

- 15 bundle regressions, including spare capacity, byte limits, membership,
  shared contents, canonical encoding and all fingerprinted semantics.
- Independent known SHA-256 vectors and a separately recomputed golden manifest.
- Full repository matrix, full-diff self-review and independent local review.
- Standalone Linux public-API smoke: confined selected files/literal links feed
  distinct overlay layers; excluded paths fail; later local edits cannot replace
  immutable bundle bytes or its fingerprint. Only synthetic fixture data is used.

Native UI and paid-cloud smoke are not applicable to this local data-only slice.

author: dgmlnr
body:
## El síntoma que motivó la investigación

El panel de admin (`apps/admin`) salió con título, etiquetas e identificadores **invisibles**: `text-foreground` (`--gx-color-on-surface`, `#1a1a1a`) sobre `bg-background` (`--gx-color-surface`, `#14231d`), contraste medido **1,07:1**. Ese bug ya está arreglado en `main` (slice 14, `theme-contrast-fence.test.ts`) — el arreglo local en `apps/admin` y la valla que lo fija **no se tocan en este PR**.

La consigna era: confirmar o refutar la hipótesis de que el defecto real es de **contrato** (qué pares de tokens son legibles juntos) y no de **valores**, y cerrar el hueco para que ningún otro componente repita el error.

## Conclusión sobre la hipótesis: CONFIRMADA, con evidencia nueva

Ningún color cambia en este PR. `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS["--gx-color-surface"] = #14231d` y `["--gx-color-on-surface"] = #1a1a1a` quedan intactos, y son correctos **en los términos en los que cada uno se usa realmente** (ver mapa abajo).

Lo que faltaba no era otro valor: era que **nada en el repo declaraba qué pares de tokens están garantizados como legibles**. `validateThemeContrast` (`widget-protocol/theme-tokens.ts`) valida el payload de un tenant contra 4 `CONTRAST_RULES`, entre ellas `on-surface/surface` — pero **nunca se corre contra `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS`**, y no tiene forma de ver qué token bridgea un componente en su propio CSS/markup. `apps/admin` bridgeó `--background`/`--foreground` de shadcn directamente sobre ese par, asumiendo que dos tokens nombrados eran automáticamente un par seguro. No lo eran.

**Y el mismo error ya estaba reproducido, en silencio, dentro del propio widget** (ver "el bug nuevo" abajo) — no hacía falta imaginar un componente futuro repitiéndolo: ya había uno.

### El "contradicción" entre embed-shell.ts y chrome-styles.ts: NO es tal

- `packages/widget-frontdoor/src/embed-shell.ts:56` → `var(--gx-color-surface, #ffffff)`: fallback del `html, body` antes de la hidratación (y para siempre, si el tenant no configura tema — `applyThemeToRoot` nunca escribe `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS` al DOM, solo lo que el tenant/host realmente mandan). Blanco es la elección correcta para "no dejar ver la página del host".
- `apps/widget-app/src/chrome-styles.ts:765` → `color-mix(in srgb, var(--gx-color-surface, #14231d) 88%, #fff)`: un blend de hover, evaluado solo **dentro** del widget ya montado, donde el paño (felt) es la superficie real.

Verificado con `applyThemeToRoot(document.documentElement, ...)` (`apps/widget-app/src/main.ts:100`): el custom property se escribe en `<html>`, así que `embed-shell.ts` sí hereda cualquier tema real aplicado — el `#ffffff` es exclusivamente el piso para el tenant sin tema. Dos literales independientes, elegidos por contexto, sin promesa cruzada entre sí. **No se tocó ningún valor acá.**

## El bug nuevo encontrado mapeando consumidores

Mapeando **todos** los usos reales de `--gx-color-surface`/`--gx-color-on-surface` (no solo los de `apps/admin`), cuatro reglas de `apps/widget-app/src/chrome-styles.ts` leían `--gx-color-on-surface` sin blend:

- `.hexdev-chrome-empty` / `.hexdev-chrome-loading` (mensaje de catálogo vacío / placeholder de carga)
- `.hexdev-about-toggle` (borde y texto del botón "i" de créditos)
- `.hexdev-about-panel` (texto del panel de créditos/licencia)

Ninguna de las cuatro pinta sobre la superficie cruda: las cuatro se sientan sobre `.convite-chrome`, el **paño** — `--hx-cloth-lit`/`-cloth`/`-cloth-deep` teñido por a lo sumo 14% de `--gx-color-surface` (`--hx-felt-tint`). Medido con el mismo `contrastRatio` que usa `widget-protocol`, contra cada parada del degradé:

| Fondo real | Ratio on-surface (#1a1a1a) |
|---|---|
| `--hx-cloth-lit` (el más claro) | 2.67:1 |
| `--hx-cloth` | 1.47:1 |
| `--hx-cloth-deep` (el más oscuro) | 1.26:1 |

Nunca 4.5:1 — para **ningún** tema de tenant, porque ningún `--gx-color-surface` que un tenant elija puede aclarar el paño lo suficiente (el blend tapa como máximo el 14%). Es el mismo modo de falla exacto del panel de admin, reproducido de forma independiente en el propio widget, sin ningún test ni captura que lo hubiera visto — `chrome-contrast.browser.test.ts` solo cubría el botón de status/retry/back-to-lobby.

**Arreglo**: las cuatro reglas pasan a leer `--hx-felt-ink`, el token que ya usa el resto de la copia de cuerpo sobre el paño (la tarjeta de estado, la copia discreta del lobby) — el mismo token al que ya había migrado `.convite-chrome button` en un refactor anterior (PR-EST2, "the surface is ours"), que dos comentarios en `chrome-styles.ts`/`chrome-contrast.browser.test.ts` seguían describiendo con el token viejo. Corregidos también.

## Mapa completo de consumidores de los dos tokens

| Archivo | Uso | ¿Correcto? |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/widget-protocol/src/theme-tokens.ts` | `THEME_TOKEN_NAMES`, `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS`, `CONTRAST_RULES` (valida el par para overrides de tenant) | Sí — valores y regla son correctos en sus propios términos |
| `apps/admin/src/ui/theme-bridge.css` | `--background: var(--gx-color-surface)`, `--foreground: var(--gx-color-on-surface)` | Ya arreglado (slice 14): componentes usan `text-primary-foreground`, no `text-foreground`, sobre ese bridge |
| `apps/widget-app/src/theme.ts` (`applyThemeToRoot`) | Nunca aplica `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS` al DOM — solo lo que el tenant/host mandan | Correcto, y es la razón por la que ningún fallback en stylesheet es "el" default real |
| `packages/widget-frontdoor/src/embed-shell.ts:56` | `var(--gx-color-surface, #ffffff)` en `html, body` | Correcto (ver arriba) |
| `apps/widget-app/src/chrome-styles.ts` (felt, blends) | `color-mix(... var(--gx-color-surface, #14231d) ..., ...)` en 3 sitios (background del paño, hover de card) | Correcto — son blends, nunca el par crudo |
| `apps/widget-app/src/chrome-styles.ts` (4 sitios) | `var(--gx-color-on-surface, #1a1a1a)` como texto/borde sobre el paño | **Arreglado en este PR** → `--hx-felt-ink` |
| `packages/games/truco-ui/src/table-styles.ts` (4 sitios) | `background: var(--gx-color-surface, ...)`, `color: var(--gx-color-on-surface, ...)` — el par crudo, de verdad, foreground sobre background | Correcto — es exactamente el caso que `CONTRAST_RULES` protege para overrides de tenant, y los literales propios (`#1c1c1c`/`#f2f2f2`, etc.) son un par seguro por default |
| `packages/games/escoba-ui/src/rail-styles.ts`, `match-over-styles.ts` | Mismo patrón que table-styles.ts | Correcto, mismo motivo |

## Qué decidí NO tocar, y por qué

- **`DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS`**: los valores son correctos en sus propios términos (ver mapa). Cambiarlos arreglaría el panel de admin (ya arreglado de otra forma) y rompería `table-styles.ts`/`escoba-ui`, que sí dependen del par crudo.
- **`embed-shell.ts`**: no hay contradicción real que resolver (ver arriba).
- **`validateThemeContrast`/`CONTRAST_RULES`**: no se extiende. Valida un payload de tenant; no tiene (ni debería tener) forma de ver qué token bridgea un componente en su propio CSS — eso convertiría un chequeo pairwise enfocado en un registro de todo el markup de cada consumidor. Documentado como "THIRD KNOWN LIMIT" en `theme-tokens.ts`.
- **Las 4 baselines visuales de `packages/games/truco-ui/src/__screenshots__/`**: no se tocaron (`git status` confirma cero cambios ahí; el fix vive enteramente en `chrome-styles.ts` de `widget-app`).

## Cómo queda impedido que esto se repita

1. `chrome-contrast.browser.test.ts` gana un `describe` que renderiza el lobby real (`renderGameSelection`) y mide contraste en los 4 casos que fallaban, con la misma lógica de `ratioFor` ya probada en el resto del archivo.
2. `design-token-parity.test.ts` gana una guarda negativa: si `--gx-color-on-surface` vuelve a aparecer en `chrome-styles.ts`, el test avisa antes de que salga otro screenshot roto.
3. `theme-tokens.ts` documenta explícitamente, junto a las dos "KNOWN LIMIT" que ya tenía `validateThemeContrast`, que `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS` nunca se valida contra sí mismo y que el patrón correcto para u

author: bohdankhrystov
body:
The mechanism behind `ADR-0120`'s two-second hold — the last architect decision `STORY-1411` was
waiting on.

**A beat carries its kind, never its length.** `RevealStep` gains `hold: "step" | "read"`, set once
in `layOutReveal` from `ADR-0120` §3's own predicate over `PlayerView.viewerSeat` and
`SeatView.holeCards`. The milliseconds stay where `ADR-0102` §4 put them — named once at the boot
seam, `REVEAL_READ_MS = 2000` beside `REVEAL_STEP_MS = 600` — which is the whole reason kind and
length are separated.

The classification is **a pure function of one frame**: no `state.mySeat`, no `null` case, no memory
of a previous view. So a hand-ending `Snapshot` that was *queued* behind another one still classifies
itself correctly on drain. `advanceReveal` is byte-unchanged and no component learns the field, so the
DOM is byte-identical at 600 ms and at 2,000 ms.

**`stepMillis === 0` silences every beat**, gated before the kind is read. So `drive-duel.tsx` is
**not edited**, no e2e file is, and nothing is re-recorded — and it is deliberately *not* given a
redundant `readMillis: 0`, because a redundant zero can drift out of agreement with the gate that
makes it redundant. Neither horn of the dilemma bites: the driver never waits, and it does not
"ignore" a hold it was never evidence about. The hold is proved where a duration is observable — by
asserting the injected `schedule`'s **`delayMillis` arguments** (`[600, 600, 600, 2000]` vs `[600]`),
never a call count.

**The failure mode of getting this wrong is not slowness**, and the ADR says so: the reveal's timer is
what drains the queue, so a `readMillis` reachable at `stepMillis: 0` would stop the next hand ever
reaching the screen inside its `act()` — and it would read like a flake.

**Nothing crosses the socket.** The predicate reads two fields that already ship and are already
filtered per recipient by `PlayerView.of`'s `showCards`, so `ADR-0047` §2's fingerprint cannot move
and `STORY-1411`'s ticket is **not** `atomic:`. The non-negotiable is met head on rather than by
silence: the client reads hole cards to pick a schedule, cannot see more than the projection sent, and
the worst this mechanism can do wrong is stand a beat for the wrong length.

Two things flagged without registering, per `ADR-0105` §6: a preflop showdown runs **3.8 s**, not 4.4
— `ADR-0120` §3's last beat *is* the held one — and the **deciding hand of a duel holds too**, so the
result screen arrives 2 s later. Both follow from applying §3 as written.

## Gates

- `DEC-146` appears in no open table; struck in all three registers and standing in each *Answered*.
- `## Consequences` names a cost.
- `python3 .github/scripts/lint_tickets.py` → `backlog ok — 11 epics, 99 stories, 1098 tasks`

`EPIC-14` now has **one** architect decision open (`DEC-150`, which blocks nothing) and one product
decision (`DEC-145`, which blocks nothing).

author: gcanino-wq
body:
A verification pass over the guideline engine, a `VERIFICATION.md` recording what has been checked and what has not, and a CI workflow so the tests actually run.

## Read this first: nothing here was checked against the Manual

All outbound HTTPS from the environment this was written in is refused by the egress proxy — `ussc.gov` returns 403 on CONNECT, and so does every other host tried. Only summarized web-search snippets were reachable, which is not a basis for rewriting guideline tables.

So **every finding below rests on internal consistency, arithmetic, and the app's own citations** — enough to find contradictions, not enough to confirm that a correctly-self-consistent number matches the published text. `VERIFICATION.md` marks the difference throughout. The sentencing table change in particular deserves a human eye against the printed table. CI passing does not close that gap: it proves the code is self-consistent, not that 77 is what the Manual prints.

## Fixes

**Sentencing table, level 21 / Cat. VI and level 22 / Cat. V read 78 months.** Categories IV, V and VI climb one shared run of minimums — 63, 70, 77, 84, 92, 100, 110 — each reaching it earlier than the last, and diverge only above 110, where IV coarsens to 121, 135 while V and VI keep the finer 120, 130, 140. Every cell in that run agreed across the three columns except these two, and Category IV already read 77. Both now read 77, pinned by tests that assert the column structure rather than the individual cells.

**Mass-marketing was counted twice.** §2B1.1(b)(2)(A) is a single 2-level increase reached by any of three alternatives, and the wizard already cited mass-marketing to `(b)(2)(A)(ii)` — but `socAdjustment` added a second 2 levels on top. A case with ten or more victims *and* mass-marketing came out two levels high. It is now scored once, on Worksheet A line 2(c).

**Worksheet C did not foot.** The §4A1.1(e) status point was added to the total while the status line always printed `+0`. Criminal history is now returned broken out as priors / status point / total, and the line reports the point it contributes.

**Prior sentences were all cited to §4A1.1(b)** whatever their score; a 3-point prior belongs under (a) and a 1-point prior under (c). The cite now follows the points.

**Worksheet A hardcoded the demo facts into its citations and excerpts.** Line 2(b) cited `(b)(1)(H)` and read "more than $550,000" at any loss; line 1 cited `(a)(1)` even at a base of 6; line 2(c) read "10 or more" with 3 victims. All four lines now derive from the facts.

**The §4C1.1 line printed `−2`** in the value column of a criminal-history sheet whose total excludes it. It is a 2-level offense-level reduction, not a criminal history point, and is not applied at all — the line now reads `eligible`.

## CI

The repository had no CI — pull requests reported no checks, so the suite only ever ran locally. The second commit adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, running the three commands a contributor runs before pushing, from a lockfile install:

```
npm ci → npm run typecheck → npm test → npm run build
```

On every `pull_request` and on pushes to the default branch, Node 22 (Vite 6 and Vitest 3 both need `^20.19 || >=22.12`), with `cancel-in-progress` concurrency and `permissions: contents: read`.

One caveat: the push trigger names `claude/artifact-rebuild-ohljzm` literally, since that is the default branch and the repo has no `main`. There is a comment on that line; it needs updating if the default branch is renamed. PR runs are unaffected either way.

## Verified as internally consistent

§2B1.1(b)(1) loss table structure, §2B1.1(a) base level, the §4A1.1(e) 7-point threshold (post-Amendment 821 form), the criminal history category boundaries, the range construction (top = greater of min+6 and 125% of min), and the §5C1.1 zone cutoffs.

## Deliberately not changed

`EDITION_LABEL` still reads "Guidelines Manual, Nov. 2024". That is currently accurate; relabelling it 2025 without being able to verify the data against the 2025 Manual would turn a true statement into a false one.

## Out of scope, and worth knowing

**§2B3.1, §2K2.1 and §2D1.1 compute nothing in this codebase.** `§2K2.1` exists only as a display tag string on a sample matter; the other two appear nowhere. There is no drug quantity table and no robbery guideline. The Nov. 1 2025 amendments to those sections have nothing here to apply to — implementing them is new work that should start from the Manual, not from this app.

Also still unimplemented: the §2B1.1(b)(9) floor (offense level raised to 10) and the §2B1.1(b)(10) floor (raised to 12). Neither binds on the default facts, but both will on a small-loss case.

## Testing

39 tests pass, up from 28; typecheck and build clean. New coverage: the table column invariants, the mass-marketing single count, the status-point line, and the fact-derived citations. All of it now runs in CI on this PR rather than only locally.

author: sehkone
body:
Corrects two statements in `docs/rfcs/0001-install-update-state-schema.md` that `origin/main` contradicts. Documentation only — no decision changes.

## 1. The column-family count conflated two numbers

- `MAP_NAMES` (`src/tables.rs:161`) is `[&str; 39]`, so this change adds **five** names (39 → 44).
- `MAP_NAMES_V0_43_TO_V0_46` (`src/migration.rs`) is `[&str; 36]`, so a `0.46.0` store lacks **eight**: those five plus `core_component`, `operation_attempt` and **`customer deletion jobs`**, all registered by earlier `0.47.0` alpha slices.

The RFC said "seven" for both, and separately claimed the pre-bump open does not create `core_component`/`operation_attempt` — which are already registered at `alpha.2`. As written the acceptance criterion **fails a correct implementation** or passes one that never exercises the real `0.46` path.

## 2. The owed-cleanup premise was the reverse of the shipped code

The RFC argued the one-cleanup-owed-row-per-triple invariant was already enforced, "because the owed-teardown index is keyed `(target, host, instance)` with no discriminator, so a second row would **overwrite** the first". In `src/tables/operation_attempt.rs`:

- `owed_cleanup_key` **appends the `idempotency_key`** after the triple, and its doc comment says "several attempts may owe a cleanup for one triple";
- `attempts_owing_cleanup` returns a **`Vec<OperationAttempt>`**;
- tests assert the plural case.

A second row **queues** rather than overwriting, and nothing refuses it. The invariant is therefore a **code change** — drop the discriminator, narrow the read to at most one, retire the tests asserting several — and the RFC now says so. Without it, an implementation lays the new latest-pointer lookup over an index that still holds several rows and the lookup second step has no single row to return.

## Verification

Linted with this repository own `.markdownlint.yaml` at `markdownlint-cli2` 0.23.2 — 0 issues.

Closes #876

author: abhishek-chohan
body:
## Issue

Two gaps in the trust model at the boundary this product exists to defend:

1. **`execute` meant both "invoke tools" and "be a provider."** Any session key could register a machine, claim queued work, and submit results — the structural hole behind the result-forgery finding. Lease fencing narrowed it; nothing closed it.

2. **Machine identity was self-asserted.** `RegisterMachine` accepted a caller-chosen ID and silently updated the existing record — SDK version, IP, tools — so any execute-capable key could take over a machine, steal its tool names, and inherit its workload. No credential, no attestation, no conflict.

## Contract changes (additive)

- Capability values are now `read`, `invoke`, `provide`, and `admin`. `execute` remains a **legacy alias**: still accepted anywhere capabilities are parsed (existing keys, database rows), expanding to `invoke`+`provide`. Do not mint new keys with it.
- The authz policy table is repartitioned: 12 provide-scoped RPCs (register machine/tool, pings, claim, submit result, append chunks, renew lease, drain, unregister, update request) and 7 invoke-scoped RPCs (execute tools, stream/resume, create request, cancel request/task). Reads and admin entries unchanged.
- `Machine` message gains `machine_token`: the per-machine credential, returned exactly once by `RegisterMachine` on the registration that minted it, empty otherwise. Stored server-side only as a SHA-256 (`machines.token_hash`, idempotent migration).
- All four SDK proto stacks regenerated from the canonical `server/proto/service.proto` with the pinned toolchain; `make check-proto-drift` passes.

## Server

- `RegisterMachine` mints `toolplane_machine_<uuid>`; the cached and persisted machine keeps only the hash, and the plaintext travels to the caller exactly once.
- Provide-scoped RPCs must present the credential via `x-toolplane-machine-token` metadata when session-key auth is active (`WithMachineTokenAuth` hook on the authorizer, validated after capability+session checks). The JSON proxy and MCP gateway forward `X-Toolplane-Machine-Token`.
- Re-registering an existing machine ID requires its credential (`PERMISSION_DENIED` on mismatch or absence) — the silent-takeover path is removed. Machines registered before this change have no stored hash and bind the first credential presented.
- Fixed mode and auth-disabled mode are exempt from the machine-token gate; production refuses both, so the gate covers exactly the multi-credential deployments where hijacking matters.

## SDKs

- Python (gRPC and HTTP) and TypeScript capture `machine_token` from the registration response automatically and attach it to every call (`get_metadata()` / `createMetadata()` / HTTP headers). Provider authors change nothing.
- Go client: regenerated protos (no provider surface exists there).

## Tests

- `server/cmd/server/auth/machine_token_test.go` — capability normalization (execute → invoke+provide), policy-table partition by role, legacy-execute key passes both roles, machine-token gate (missing/wrong/right credential → PERMISSION_DENIED/PERMISSION_DENIED/OK), fixed-mode and invoke-RPC exemptions.
- `server/pkg/service/machine_identity_test.go` — mint-once (cached copy has no plaintext), re-registration requires the credential (no credential and forged credential rejected; legitimate one succeeds and does not re-reveal), legacy binding.
- Postgres storage suite green with the new `token_hash` column; conformance `api_key_lifecycle` now mints a `read`+`invoke` key with the new values.

## Verified

- Full Go suite in memory mode and against Postgres 16 (storage + service + cmd); race-clean packages under `-race`; golangci-lint (gosec+staticcheck) clean on both Go modules.
- Python conformance full leg (36 passed) and MCP leg (3 passed) in fixed auth; black/isort/flake8 clean.
- TypeScript build, 34 unit tests, eslint.
- `make check-proto-drift`.

## Migration

- Keys minted with `execute` keep working (expand to invoke+provide). Rotate to explicit lists at your leisure.
- Custom provider clients not using the maintained SDK runtimes must capture `machine_token` from `RegisterMachine` and send it on provide-scoped RPCs, or those calls fail with `PERMISSION_DENIED` in session-key mode.
- Operators: no action; `machines.token_hash` migrates idempotently at startup, and existing machine rows bind a credential on the first provide call that presents one.

## Known limits

Machine credentials are bearer secrets held in provider process memory; there is no per-machine expiry or rotation RPC yet (a machine recovers by re-registering with a new ID, which mints a fresh credential). Tool-name ownership remains single-owner per session.

body:
The campaign UI needs a shared, schema-checked transport so frontend work can proceed against the frozen HTTP and live contracts without an engine or model provider.

This implements #49:
- Generate HTTP types, live message unions and operation metadata from the committed v1 schemas; provide an openapi-fetch client and a bounded, validated WebSocket iterator.
- Implement MSW handlers for all 17 frozen HTTP operations plus live authentication, atomic snapshots, scripted replay, disconnects, duplicate/out-of-order frames, revocation and narration. Exact retries preserve command receipts and reject changed payloads.
- Add 20 named scenarios covering campaign join, legal/illegal character previews, actions/clarification, item use, encounters, split/capture/rescue, reconnect, endings and errors. These select preauthored projections and outcomes; they do not implement game rules or invent proposed endpoints.
- Route the existing browser sample mode through NetworkPlayTransport and MSW. Real connections use the same facade. Preserve the direct fixture double for focused store tests.
- Add schema validation, generated artifact/worker drift checks, a PR-base compatibility guard and a documented major-version migration path. Preserve the existing TypeScript 7 compiler and locked pnpm toolchain.

Validation:
- 52 unit/schema/network tests and 4 compatibility-gate tests passed.
- Typecheck, ESLint, formatting, generated checks, normal build and sample-mode build passed.
- Deliberately modified generated output was rejected by the drift check; Git-backed compatibility tests reject breaking edits/removal and require migration records for new majors.
- Offline validators passed for 17 HTTP operations/45 examples and 28 live messages/12 recovery scenarios.
- Local Playwright execution could not start Chromium. Installing the browser failed after repeated CDN download timeouts. The existing 33 phone/tablet/desktop browser tests remain enabled in CI; they have not been verified locally with this transport.

Backend runtime/auth integration remains #50. Automatic reconnect and cache reconciliation policy remain #54; the wire client supports resume inputs and refuses inconsistent snapshot handoffs. Proposed-domain scenarios use frozen projections and do not claim live engine acceptance.

Closes #49

author: kleyson-carreira
body:
## What this changes, and why

`release.yml` builds its changelog from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 "${TAG}^"` — the previous tag, of whatever kind.

For a candidate that is correct, and this PR leaves it alone: rc.3 announcing "changes since rc.2" is what someone tracking candidates wants.

For a stable release it is wrong. The tag immediately before `v0.2.0` is `v0.2.0-rc.N`, so a whole release cycle gets announced as the handful of commits that happened to land after the final candidate.

**Concretely, today.** Cutting `v0.1.0` from `main` right now would publish this as the 1.0 announcement page:

```
## v0.1.0

Changes since v0.1.0-rc.3:

- docs: the image example named a candidate two releases old
- docs(security): the reporting policy offered two channels and neither one worked
- docs(github): the templates ask for what triage actually needs, not what is easy to type
- docs(contributing): the first thing a contributor reads asks for a CLA that does not exist
- ci(security): the advisory gate tells an outage apart from a vulnerability
- docs: the release docs name rc.3, the candidate carrying the design pass
```

Six housekeeping commits, all of them docs and CI, for a release that delivers 224. Meanwhile `latest` — which the shipped `compose.yaml` pulls by default — would move to an image whose release page describes nothing about it.

**Why it was never caught:** the branch that gets this wrong has never executed. `release.yml` only runs on a tag, and every tag so far has been an `-rc`. The stable path's first run would have been the first stable release itself.

## The rule now

| tag | range | reader |
|---|---|---|
| candidate | previous tag, any kind — **unchanged** | someone tracking candidates |
| stable, with a stable predecessor | since the previous **stable** tag | an operator deciding whether to upgrade |
| stable, first of its kind | since the **first candidate** of the same version | same, and those candidates are the only thing anyone outside could already be running |

The third row is a judgement call, not a calculation: there is no predecessor, so the alternatives were the full 224-commit history or a hand-written page. The candidate cycle was chosen because it is bounded and it describes the period during which this software was actually installable by someone else.

## Evidence

A clone was tagged with `v0.1.0`, `v0.2.0-rc.1`, `v0.2.0-rc.2` and `v0.2.0` to create the situations that do not exist yet, and the resolution checked against all four cases — first stable release, later stable release, candidate, and the very first tag (which correctly resolves to nothing):

```
PASS  v0.1.0       stable=true   expected=v0.1.0-rc.1  got=v0.1.0-rc.1
PASS  v0.2.0       stable=true   expected=v0.1.0       got=v0.1.0
PASS  v0.2.0-rc.2  stable=false  expected=v0.2.0-rc.1  got=v0.2.0-rc.1
PASS  v0.1.0-rc.1  stable=false  expected=<empty>      got=<empty>
```

Four passes prove nothing on their own, so the old logic was run over the same cases to confirm the change is not inert — and that it does not touch candidates:

```
v0.1.0       fixed=v0.1.0-rc.1  current=v0.1.0-rc.3  DIFFER
v0.2.0       fixed=v0.1.0       current=v0.2.0-rc.1  DIFFER
v0.2.0-rc.2  fixed=v0.2.0-rc.1  current=v0.2.0-rc.1  same, as intended
```

Finally the `run:` body was **extracted from this file** and executed against that clone, so what was exercised is the shipped text rather than a reconstruction of it. It emitted `Changes since v0.1.0-rc.1` for the stable tag and left the candidate's output identical.

`TAG` and `STABLE` reach the script through `env:`, never interpolated into the shell — the pattern this file already documents, since a tag name is attacker-chosen the moment anyone can push one. `grep -vFx` keeps the tag a fixed string rather than a pattern. The step body contains zero `${{ }}` expansions.

author: loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]
body:
## Summary

`.loom/scripts/dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh operator-premise` could compute two
different `CONCLUSION_HASH` values for a reference whose real-world state
hadn't changed at all, because `_fetch_operator_premise_json` can resolve a
reference either via `gh issue view` (which reports a merged PR's generic
state as `CLOSED`) or fall back to `gh pr view` (which reports `MERGED` for
the identical PR). Since the raw state string was hashed directly, this
produced spurious "still stale" heartbeat comments under `curator.md`'s
idempotency rule, which treats any hash change as a real conclusion change.

## Changes

- `.loom/scripts/dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh`: `_operator_premise_refs` now
  normalizes any non-`OPEN` state to a single canonical `CLOSED` marker
  before it is folded into the `"<ref#>:<state>"` hash-input line. This
  loses no information the caller uses for its decision —
  `_run_operator_premise` (VERDICT) already only distinguishes `OPEN` from
  not-`OPEN`.
- `.loom/scripts/tests/test-dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh`: added T14
  regression test, stubbing `gh` so the same reference (`#102`, mirroring
  the issue's own repro against this repo) resolves once via the
  `gh issue view` path (`CLOSED`) and once via the `gh pr view` fallback
  path (`MERGED`), asserting both produce an identical `CONCLUSION_HASH`.

`_dep_recheck_verdict` (the `dep-recheck` subcommand, which already
distinguishes `OPEN` from other states for its own, unrelated purpose) is
untouched — the fix is scoped entirely to `_operator_premise_refs`, used
only by the `operator-premise` subcommand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `operator-premise`'s state normalization treats a merged PR
      consistently regardless of which lookup path resolved it.
- [x] Regression test added to
      `.loom/scripts/tests/test-dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh` (T14a/b/c).
- [x] Confirmed `dep-recheck`'s existing `OPEN`/other-state distinction
      (`_dep_recheck_verdict`) is unaffected — no changes to that function
      or its call path; all pre-existing T0-T13 tests still pass.

## Test Plan

- `./.loom/scripts/tests/test-dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh` — 41/41 passed
  (37 pre-existing + 4 new T14 assertions).
- Manual verification (per issue Test Plan): ran
  `./.loom/scripts/dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh operator-premise --refs 102`
  against this repo after the fix — emits `CONCLUSION_HASH=bd1c33f4dc932e26`,
  which matches `sha256("stale-premise\n102:CLOSED")` and the historical
  marker already posted on issue #101, confirming the fix eliminates the
  churn rather than just moving it.
- `shellcheck` clean on both changed files.
- TDD: wrote T14a/b/c (asserting the CLOSED-vs-MERGED hash must match)
  against the pre-fix `_operator_premise_refs`, confirmed the underlying bug
  mechanism via the manual `--refs 102` repro producing
  `CONCLUSION_HASH=78857fe5c1c6909e` (the `MERGED`-based hash) before the
  fix, then implemented the normalization to green.

Closes #170

author: adnanelassadi
body:
**Client.** Three changes to `LLM.chat`, each matching a maintained library.

- No output cap unless the caller sets one, as in LangChain. A cap also counts a reasoning model's thinking, so a small cap can return an empty answer that the judge would score as a parse failure.
- When a cap is set it is sent as `max_completion_tokens`, as in lm-eval and LangChain. Every OpenAI model since gpt-5 refuses `max_tokens`; older OpenAI models, vLLM, OpenRouter and the SDK accept the newer name.
- When a model still answers 400 naming a parameter (models that always reason take no temperature), the client drops that parameter, remembers it, and logs one warning. Every surveyed library adjusts the temperature for such models; they do it from a table of model names, which cannot cover a model released after the table was written, so here the server is the authority. Models that accept the parameters keep the pipeline's 0.7 for generation and 0 for judging. One test with a stub client: learned once, never re-sent.

**Quickstart.** `gpt-5.4` as judge, `gpt-5.4-mini` as generator: the current generation, and both accept sampling parameters when no reasoning effort is set. Shell line and output tree match.

**README.** Usage says what a user does. The two temperatures are stated under How it works, where the method is described. No vendor or model family is named.

Not run against the live API from this machine (no key here). Whoever merges should paste the quickstart once.
